title: [rtl,pmp] Allow all accesses to Debug Module in debug mode
body:
The RISC-V Debug Specification ([current release 1.0.0-rc4](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-debug-spec/releases/tag/1.0.0-rc4)) in Section A.2 states that the PMP must not disallow accesses to addresses of the Debug Module when the hart is in debug mode, regardless of how the PMP is configured.  This commit changes the PMP accordingly.

This PR doesn't contain the verification, which is tracked by #2233.

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[controller] Add assertion on pipeline flush when entering debug mode

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

[rtl,pmp] Allow all accesses to Debug Module in debug mode

The RISC-V Debug Specification (current release 1.0.0-rc4) in Section
A.2 states that the PMP must not disallow accesses to addresses of the
Debug Module when the hart is in debug mode, regardless of how the PMP
is configured.  This commit changes the PMP accordingly.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [dv] Verify access to Debug Module in debug mode even if disallowed by PMP
resolved_issues.body:
Verify the feature implemented in #2232; specific tasks are:
- [ ] (P1) Minimal smoke test that verifies the feature works (i.e., read, write, and fetch a couple of addresses in the Debug Module address space while debug mode is enabled but the PMP doesn't allow the accesses).
- [ ] (P2) Extensive testing that verifies the feature cannot be used for accesses outside the Debug Module address space that are disallowed by the PMP.
- [ ] (P3) Extensive testing that verifies the feature works (close coverage over all addressing cases cross access types cross relevant states).

problem_statement: The Physical Memory Protection (PMP) logic in Ibex still rejects accesses to the RISC-V Debug Module address range even when the processor core is already in debug mode. If the active PMP rules would normally deny the access, a load, store, or instruction fetch to an address inside the Debug Module range can incorrectly raise a PMP access error. The correct behavior is that, while debug mode is active, PMP must allow loads, stores, and instruction fetches within the Debug Module address range even when those same accesses would otherwise be blocked by PMP. At the same time, accesses outside the Debug Module address range must continue to follow normal PMP checks and must still fault when PMP denies them. This bug affects the PMP permission-check path for debug-mode accesses and is triggered when the core, while in debug mode, accesses an address in the Debug Module range under PMP rules that would otherwise deny the access.

title: [rtl] Protect core_busy_o with a multi-bit encoding
body:
This PR protects the `core_busy_o` signal using a multi-bit encoding to reduce the chances of an adversary for glitching this signal to low, thereby putting the core to sleep and e.g. not handling an alert.

Without this change, the glitch would only be detected once both the main core and the shadow core wake up again and the comparison of the core_busy_o signals continues.

This resolves lowRISC/Ibex#1827.

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[rtl] Protect core_busy_o with a multi-bit encoding

This commit protects the core_busy_o signal using a multi-bit encoding
to reduce the chances of an adversary for glitching this signal to low,
thereby putting the core to sleep and e.g. not handling an alert.

Without this commit, the glitch would only be detected once both the
main core and the shadow core wake up again and the comparison of the
core_busy_o signals continues.

This resolves lowRISC/Ibex#1827.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: `core_busy_o` not protected by lockstep
resolved_issues.body:
## Observed Behavior
The `core_busy_o` output signal of the non-lockstep core is used to gate the core clock, which is used by the regular Ibex core and its lockstep counterpart.
https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/3943a4eca3917d0a00406abb36f4951304c0b394/rtl/ibex_top.sv#L211-L219
https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/3943a4eca3917d0a00406abb36f4951304c0b394/rtl/ibex_top.sv#L286-L287
https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/3943a4eca3917d0a00406abb36f4951304c0b394/rtl/ibex_top.sv#L927-L928

This means that the lockstep core gets gated in the same clock cycle as the regular core, even though the lockstep core is a few cycles delayed. **A low-glitch in the `core_busy_o` output of the non-lockstep core thus does not lead to a comparison mismatch and a major alert because the lockstep core is already clock-gated when it would produce the value of `core_busy_o` that is used in the comparison.**
https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/3943a4eca3917d0a00406abb36f4951304c0b394/rtl/ibex_lockstep.sv#L453-L454

<!--
Please describe the problem you saw. Include waveforms (in VCD or Verilator/GtkWave FST format only please) and log files if possible.
-->

## Expected Behavior

A low-glitch/mismatch in the `core_busy_o` output signal of the non-lockstep core should lead to a major alert by the lockstep core.

## Steps to reproduce the issue
Run the `chip_sw_ibex_lockstep_glitch` test in OpenTitan (currently in https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/15221) and override `port_idx` to the index of `core_busy_o` in `output_ports`.

> estimate 2

problem_statement: In lockstep mode, the main Ibex core and its delayed shadow core share the same gated core clock, but the lockstep logic compares the shadow core's delayed `core_busy_o` value against the main core's `core_busy_o`. If the main core's `core_busy_o` has a transient low glitch while the core is still busy, both cores can be clock-gated in the same cycle before the delayed shadow core reaches the corresponding busy state. That masks the `core_busy_o` mismatch, can spuriously put the core to sleep, and prevents the lockstep logic from reporting the error. A transient low glitch on `core_busy_o` while the core is still busy must not gate off the shared core clock in that cycle; the delayed shadow core must continue running long enough for the lockstep comparison to observe the mismatch and raise a major alert.

title: [rtl] Change how we record debug causes
body:
This commit changes when we catch the debug causes. Since `debug_cause_o` only gets saved when `csr_save_cause_o` is high, it would work if we change the cause with a mux that is connected to the input signals.

Resolves #1772

Signed-off-by: Canberk Topal <ctopal@lowrisc.org>

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[rtl] Change how we record debug causes

This commit changes when we cath the debug causes. Since debug_cause_o
only gets latched when `csr_save_cause_o` is high, it would work if
we change the cause with a mux that is connected to the input signals.

Resolves #1772

Signed-off-by: Canberk Topal <ctopal@lowrisc.org>
Fixup signal used when checking for ebreak cause

resolved_issues.title: Cosim mismatch when reading DCSR.cause
resolved_issues.body:
## Observed Behavior
Test failures with the following error : 
```
UVM_FATAL ibex_cosim_scoreboard.sv(138) @ 4049807: Cosim mismatch Register write data mismatch to x22 DUT: 40000100 expected: 400000c0
```

This fails upon reading from `DCSR.cause`
In this case : 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102029880/184605611-4f106a6b-a987-4952-b636-760647e12afe.png)
(IBEX)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102029880/184605563-b1bd1eb8-b8c3-47c2-b263-3c84427153f3.png)
(SPIKE)

Observing the waveform below, we can see that `debug_req_i` is de-asserted shortly after `debug_mode_i` goes low due to leaving debug mode from a dret. We do re-enter debug mode, but the cause can be seen to be recorded as `DBG_CAUSE_STEP`. In spike, we read back `DBG_CAUSE_HALTREQ` at the same instruction, hence the mismatch.

## Expected Behavior

Ibex should record `DCSR.cause` as DBG_CAUSE_HALTREQ.

I think this might be due to the [ibex_controller.sv ](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/2f8dfa9dfe2d938228118ed8ab6a543804d0c9ae/rtl/ibex_controller.sv#L662)state machine sampling the `debug_req_i` signal to determine the correct `cause` one cycle later than the decision to enter debug_mode.

## Steps to reproduce the issue
```
cd dv/uvm/core_ibex/
make TEST=riscv_debug_basic_test ITERATIONS=1 WAVES=1 SEED=9892 -j12 -ik
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102029880/184603232-ef1a9397-1cd2-4a0b-828b-1b2eb4e1745a.png)

> estimate 8
> remaining 2022-09-27 4
> remaining 2022-10-12 1

problem_statement: Reading the `cause` field of the RISC-V Debug Control and Status Register (`DCSR.cause`) can report the wrong reason for entering debug mode. In the failing behavior, Ibex records a single-step cause (`DBG_CAUSE_STEP`) even though debug mode was entered because of an external debug request (`debug_req_i`), which should be reported as `DBG_CAUSE_HALTREQ`. This affects the debug-entry cause recording logic in `ibex_controller`. The bug is triggered when the core decides to enter debug mode because `debug_req_i` is asserted, but `debug_req_i` is de-asserted before the later cycle that saves the cause into `DCSR.cause`; the issue was observed after a debug return instruction (`dret`) followed by immediate re-entry into debug mode. In that situation, `DCSR.cause` must still read back as `DBG_CAUSE_HALTREQ`, because the debug entry was caused by the halt request rather than by single-step execution.

title: [rtl] Cannot add M mode executable PMP regions when MML = 1
body:
A rule that allows M mode execution (either M mode only or shared M/U
mode) cannot be added when MML is set, unless RLB is also set.

Fixes #1740

resolved_issues.title: [rtl,epmp] Prevent addition of executable regions as required by the specification
resolved_issues.body:
The Smepmp specification states:

> Adding a rule with executable privileges that either is M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region is not possible and such pmpcfg writes are ignored, leaving pmpcfg unchanged. This restriction can be temporarily lifted e.g. during the boot process, by setting mseccfg.RLB.****

This was overlooked during the original epmp implementation and must be added.

> estimate 2
> remaining 2022-18-08 1

#!/bin/bash

set -uo pipefail

cd /home/ibex

TEST_NAME="pmp_mml_exec_cfg_write_suppression"
TB_DIR="/home/ibex/.tb_${TEST_NAME}"
BUILD_DIR="/home/ibex/build/lowrisc_ibex_${TEST_NAME}_0"
SIM_LOG="${TB_DIR}/sim.log"

finish_test() {
  local status="$1"
  local rc=1

  if [ "${status}" = "PASS" ]; then
    rc=0
  fi

  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... ${status}"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit "${rc}"
}

rm -rf "${TB_DIR}" "${BUILD_DIR}"
mkdir -p "${TB_DIR}"

cat > "${TB_DIR}/${TEST_NAME}.sv" <<'EOF'
module pmp_mml_exec_cfg_write_suppression (
  input  logic clk_i,
  input  logic rst_ni,
  output logic test_done_o,
  output logic test_passed_o
);
  import ibex_pkg::*;

  typedef enum logic [2:0] {
    StWriteMseccfg,
    StWaitMseccfg,
    StCheckMseccfg,
    StWritePmpcfg,
    StWaitPmpcfg,
    StCheckPmpcfg,
    StDone
  } tb_state_e;

  tb_state_e state_q;

  logic               csr_access_i;
  csr_num_e           csr_addr_i;
  logic [31:0]        csr_wdata_i;
  csr_op_e            csr_op_i;
  logic               csr_op_en_i;
  logic [31:0]        csr_rdata_o;
  logic               illegal_csr_insn_o;
  pmp_cfg_t           csr_pmp_cfg_o [4];
  logic [33:0]        csr_pmp_addr_o[4];
  pmp_mseccfg_t       csr_pmp_mseccfg_o;

  logic cfg_write_blocked;

  assign cfg_write_blocked = !csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].lock  &&
                             (csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].mode == PMP_MODE_OFF) &&
                             !csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].exec  &&
                             !csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].write &&
                             !csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].read;

  always_comb begin
    csr_access_i = 1'b0;
    csr_addr_i   = CSR_MSECCFG;
    csr_wdata_i  = 32'h0;
    csr_op_i     = CSR_OP_WRITE;
    csr_op_en_i  = 1'b0;

    unique case (state_q)
      StWriteMseccfg: begin
        csr_access_i = 1'b1;
        csr_addr_i   = CSR_MSECCFG;
        csr_wdata_i  = 32'h1;
        csr_op_en_i  = 1'b1;
      end

      StWritePmpcfg: begin
        csr_access_i = 1'b1;
        csr_addr_i   = CSR_PMPCFG0;
        csr_wdata_i  = 32'h0000_0084;
        csr_op_en_i  = 1'b1;
      end

      default: begin
      end
    endcase
  end

  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
    if (!rst_ni) begin
      state_q        <= StWriteMseccfg;
      test_done_o    <= 1'b0;
      test_passed_o  <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
      unique case (state_q)
        StWriteMseccfg: begin
          state_q <= StWaitMseccfg;
        end

        StWaitMseccfg: begin
          state_q <= StCheckMseccfg;
        end

        StCheckMseccfg: begin
          if (illegal_csr_insn_o || !csr_pmp_mseccfg_o.mml) begin
            $display("SIM_RESULT: FAIL mseccfg write did not latch mml=1");
            test_done_o   <= 1'b1;
            test_passed_o <= 1'b0;
            state_q       <= StDone;
          end else begin
            state_q <= StWritePmpcfg;
          end
        end

        StWritePmpcfg: begin
          state_q <= StWaitPmpcfg;
        end

        StWaitPmpcfg: begin
          state_q <= StCheckPmpcfg;
        end

        StCheckPmpcfg: begin
          if (illegal_csr_insn_o) begin
            $display("SIM_RESULT: FAIL pmpcfg write raised illegal_csr_insn_o");
            test_done_o   <= 1'b1;
            test_passed_o <= 1'b0;
            state_q       <= StDone;
          end else if (cfg_write_blocked) begin
            $display("SIM_RESULT: PASS disallowed executable locked config was suppressed");
            test_done_o   <= 1'b1;
            test_passed_o <= 1'b1;
            state_q       <= StDone;
          end else begin
            $display("SIM_RESULT: FAIL pmpcfg0 lock=%0d mode=%0d exec=%0d write=%0d read=%0d",
                     csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].lock,
                     csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].mode,
                     csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].exec,
                     csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].write,
                     csr_pmp_cfg_o[0].read);
            test_done_o   <= 1'b1;
            test_passed_o <= 1'b0;
            state_q       <= StDone;
          end
        end

        default: begin
          state_q <= StDone;
        end
      endcase
    end
  end

  ibex_cs_registers #(
    .DbgTriggerEn     (1'b0),
    .ICache           (1'b0),
    .MHPMCounterNum   (0),
    .MHPMCounterWidth (40),
    .PMPEnable        (1'b1),
    .PMPGranularity   (0),
    .PMPNumRegions    (4),
    .RV32E            (1'b0),
    .RV32M            (ibex_pkg::RV32MFast),
    .RV32B            (ibex_pkg::RV32BNone)
  ) dut (
    .clk_i                   (clk_i),
    .rst_ni                  (rst_ni),
    .hart_id_i               (32'h0),
    .priv_mode_id_o          (),
    .priv_mode_lsu_o         (),
    .csr_mstatus_tw_o        (),
    .csr_mtvec_o             (),
    .csr_mtvec_init_i        (1'b0),
    .boot_addr_i             (32'h0),
    .csr_access_i            (csr_access_i),
    .csr_addr_i              (csr_addr_i),
    .csr_wdata_i             (csr_wdata_i),
    .csr_op_i                (csr_op_i),
    .csr_op_en_i             (csr_op_en_i),
    .csr_rdata_o             (csr_rdata_o),
    .irq_software_i          (1'b0),
    .irq_timer_i             (1'b0),
    .irq_external_i          (1'b0),
    .irq_fast_i              (15'h0),
    .nmi_mode_i              (1'b0),
    .irq_pending_o           (),
    .irqs_o                  (),
    .csr_mstatus_mie_o       (),
    .csr_mepc_o              (),
    .csr_mtval_o             (),
    .csr_pmp_cfg_o           (csr_pmp_cfg_o),
    .csr_pmp_addr_o          (csr_pmp_addr_o),
    .csr_pmp_mseccfg_o       (csr_pmp_mseccfg_o),
    .debug_mode_i            (1'b0),
    .debug_cause_i           (ibex_pkg::DBG_CAUSE_NONE),
    .debug_csr_save_i        (1'b0),
    .csr_depc_o              (),
    .debug_single_step_o     (),
    .debug_ebreakm_o         (),
    .debug_ebreaku_o         (),
    .trigger_match_o         (),
    .pc_if_i                 (32'h0),
    .pc_id_i                 (32'h0),
    .pc_wb_i                 (32'h0),
    .data_ind_timing_o       (),
    .dummy_instr_en_o        (),
    .dummy_instr_mask_o      (),
    .dummy_instr_seed_en_o   (),
    .dummy_instr_seed_o      (),
    .icache_enable_o         (),
    .csr_shadow_err_o        (),
    .csr_save_if_i           (1'b0),
    .csr_save_id_i           (1'b0),
    .csr_save_wb_i           (1'b0),
    .csr_restore_mret_i      (1'b0),
    .csr_restore_dret_i      (1'b0),
    .csr_save_cause_i        (1'b0),
    .csr_mcause_i            (ibex_pkg::ExcCauseIrqSoftwareM),
    .csr_mtval_i             (32'h0),
    .illegal_csr_insn_o      (illegal_csr_insn_o),
    .double_fault_seen_o     (),
    .instr_ret_i             (1'b0),
    .instr_ret_compressed_i  (1'b0),
    .instr_ret_spec_i        (1'b0),
    .instr_ret_compressed_spec_i(1'b0),
    .iside_wait_i            (1'b0),
    .jump_i                  (1'b0),
    .branch_i                (1'b0),
    .branch_taken_i          (1'b0),
    .mem_load_i              (1'b0),
    .mem_store_i             (1'b0),
    .dside_wait_i            (1'b0),
    .mul_wait_i              (1'b0),
    .div_wait_i              (1'b0)
  );

endmodule
EOF

cat > "${TB_DIR}/${TEST_NAME}.cc" <<'EOF'
#include "Vpmp_mml_exec_cfg_write_suppression.h"
#include "sim_ctrl_extension.h"
#include "verilated_toplevel.h"
#include "verilator_sim_ctrl.h"

class PmpMmlExecCfgWriteSuppressionTB : public SimCtrlExtension {
 public:
  explicit PmpMmlExecCfgWriteSuppressionTB(
      pmp_mml_exec_cfg_write_suppression *top)
      : top_(top) {}

  void OnClock(unsigned long sim_time) override {
    (void)sim_time;
    if (top_->test_done_o) {
      VerilatorSimCtrl::GetInstance().RequestStop(top_->test_passed_o);
    }
  }

 private:
  pmp_mml_exec_cfg_write_suppression *top_;
};

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  pmp_mml_exec_cfg_write_suppression top;

  VerilatorSimCtrl &simctrl = VerilatorSimCtrl::GetInstance();
  simctrl.SetTop(&top, &top.clk_i, &top.rst_ni,
                 VerilatorSimCtrlFlags::ResetPolarityNegative);

  PmpMmlExecCfgWriteSuppressionTB extension(&top);
  simctrl.RegisterExtension(&extension);

  return simctrl.Exec(argc, argv).first;
}
EOF

problem_statement: The bug is in the CSR write path for Physical Memory Protection (PMP/ePMP). After the Machine Security Configuration CSR (`mseccfg`) enables Machine Mode Lockdown (`mseccfg.MML`) and Rule Locking Bypass (`mseccfg.RLB`) remains clear, a write to a PMP configuration CSR (`pmpcfg`) that would create a locked executable region for M-mode only is still accepted and changes the PMP entry. The expected behavior is that this write is ignored: the existing PMP entry must remain unchanged, and the CSR access must not raise an illegal-instruction error.

title: [rtl] Do not register instruction fetch errors
body:
Registering instruction fetch errors causes problem in the case of seeing
a PMP execution access block. ID/EX stage learns about
the instruction that it executed should be blocked a
cycle late. This commit fixes that.

Found this one while working on fixing https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/issues/1720. However it does not fully solves the issue because we are still seeing some mismatches because of some self modifying code problems.

Signed-off-by: Canberk Topal <ctopal@lowrisc.org>

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[rtl] Flush controller in PMP CSR write ops

As Greg pointed out:

When we have an instruction in ID/EX that writes a PMP register that
update gets written to the CSR the same cycle the next instruction
moves from IF to ID/EX with it's PMP check done with the old value.

The solution is to flush the pipeline when we get a PMP CSR write.

Signed-off-by: Canberk Topal <ctopal@lowrisc.org>

problem_statement: Ibex can apply a Physical Memory Protection (PMP) update one instruction late. When software writes a PMP address or configuration CSR so that the next instruction address becomes non-executable, the core may still fetch that next instruction and let it execute instead of faulting immediately. The expected behavior is that the updated PMP permissions take effect for the very next instruction fetch: if the next program counter is now blocked for execution, that instruction must not execute and the core must raise an instruction access fault at that program counter. This bug affects PMP-based instruction-fetch permission checking, and it is triggered by a PMP CSR write immediately followed by a fetch from the newly blocked address.

title: [rtl,doc] Add double fault detection.
body: Fixes #1117

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[rtl,doc] Add double fault detection.

Fixes #1117

resolved_issues.title: [rtl] Double fault handling
resolved_issues.body:
Consider the case where an exception occurs on the first instruction of an exception handler (e.g. due to a bus fault or PMP access fault), what should happen?

I suspect Ibex currently enters some kind of infinite loop or deadlocks.

We need to define and document a sensible behaviour here.

I would suggest some kind of double fault detection that causes the core to halt and assert a top-level signal e.g. `double_fault_o`. System implementers are then left with the choice of what to do (e.g. immediately reset the core). I don't think Ibex should perform a reset itself, simply halt and let the system decide what to do.

problem_statement: Ibex does not correctly detect and record double faults in its synchronous-exception handling state. In this context, a double fault means that a second synchronous exception is taken before the core has returned from a previous synchronous exception, for example when the first instruction of the exception handler itself raises a bus fault or a Physical Memory Protection (PMP) access fault. The current behavior can leave the core looping or deadlocked without exposing the condition through machine-visible control/status state. The expected behavior is that taking any synchronous exception records that a synchronous exception is in progress in a machine-visible control/status register, and taking another synchronous exception while that state is still set records a separate double-fault condition. Executing the RISC-V `mret` return-from-exception instruction must clear only the "synchronous exception in progress" state and must not clear the recorded double-fault condition. This bug affects the exception/CSR control logic that tracks synchronous exceptions across handler entry and return.

title: Introduce internal interrupt concept
body:
As we have another potential fix in OpenTitan for this see https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/11622 and https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/11571 so may need this after all. I'm pushing as a draft for now, some tidy up may be needed and documentation should be added (skipping doing this for now if we decide not to make the change).

The main reason to make this change, even if we don't need it as a timing fix, is the current timining feedthrough from data to request is a bit awkward, we may prefer not to have it.

An internal interrupt triggers an NMI. A single one is implemented, one
on integrity errors being seen in load data. This replaces a synchronous
exception on an integrity error which caused timing issues.

problem_statement: When memory-data integrity checking is enabled through MemECC, Ibex currently handles a load response with bad integrity/ECC bits through the normal synchronous exception path. Instead, a load-data integrity failure must be treated as an internal interrupt that enters the Non-Maskable Interrupt (NMI) vector rather than the standard exception vector. The affected behavior spans the load/store unit's handling of load-data integrity failures and the controller logic that selects between exception and interrupt entry. The bug is triggered when a load completes and the returned data fails the integrity check.

title: Move not-taken, predicted taken branch address calculation to ID stage
body:
Currently, the not-taken address of a branch is registered in flops in the prefetch buffer or instruction cache when ever a branch prediction is lodged with these modules. However, as discussed in https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/issues/1462, there is an issue with this address being overridden by a second predicted branch when the an instruction moves from the prefetch to the IF stage skid buffer. If the instruction in the skid buffer was mispredicted taken, the prefetch will replay from the stored address of the second predicted branch, not the first one.

To solve this without adding extra flops in the IF stage to store the not-taken address of the instruction in the skid buffer, we can get rid of these flops entirely and calculate the not-taken address in the ID stage. This would be fed back along with the existing not-taken mispredict signal `nt_branch_mispredict_i` used to clear the prefetch and allows it to resume fetching on the correct path.

As a code refactoring bonus, we do not need to consider the existence of the branch predictor in the prefetch buffer, instruction cache and fetch FIFO modules any more. Previously, the next address of the fetch FIFO would be registered in flops as the not-taken address using an `if generate` block based on the `BranchPredictor` parameter, but these flops do not exist anymore as of this PR.

Though not specifically relevant to this change, we now also suppress the validity of the skid buffer content by `nt_branch_mispredict_i` which prevents mispredicted instructions in the skid buffer from entering the ID stage. This is required as part of fixing the aforementioned bug.

resolved_issues.title: [Bug] Branch prediction on predicted branches causes bad behaviour
resolved_issues.body:
<!--
Thank you for your interest in Ibex. We are continuously improving Ibex, and your bug report will help us with that. To help us understand and reproduce your problem as quickly as possible we have prepared a little template below.

No text in blocks starting with < !-- will be shown in the final bug report.

You can also copy/paste images into the bug report, and you can attach files to it by simply dragging them into the issue window.
-->

## Steps to reproduce the issue
<!--
Please help us to reproduce the issue you're seeing by including a detailed description of what you did to get to the problem.

For example:
* What command did you run? (Also include the output of the command.)
* What parameters/defines did you set?
* Did you make modifications to the source code?
-->
Consider the following code:
```
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    static int x = 25;
    int* x_addr = (int*)&x;
    __asm__ (
        "j skip\n\t"

        "predict_to_here:\n\t" // we shouldn't branch here but even if we do, just finish
        "j finish\n\t"
        "wfi\n\t" // this will kill things if hit

        "skip:\n\t"
        "lw t0, 0(%0)\n\t"
        "beqz t0, predict_to_here\n\t" // clearly this branch is not meant to be taken but is predicted taken
        "j finish\n\t"

        "finish:\n\t"
        "nop\n\t"
        :
        :"r" (x_addr)
        : "t0"
    );
    return 0;

}
```
We would expect the following branch pattern in general: `-> skip -> finish`
Building ibex_simple_system with the following parameters works correctly:
`fusesoc --cores-root=. run --target=sim --setup --build lowrisc:ibex:ibex_simple_system --RV32E=0 --RV32M=ibex_pkg::RV32MFast --BranchTargetALU=1 --WritebackStage=1 --BranchPredictor=0`

Building with these parameters causes the core to seemingly "lock up":
`fusesoc --cores-root=. run --target=sim --setup --build lowrisc:ibex:ibex_simple_system --RV32E=0 --RV32M=ibex_pkg::RV32MFast --BranchTargetALU=1 --WritebackStage=1 --BranchPredictor=1`

## Observed Behavior
<!--
Please describe the problem you saw. Include waveforms (in VCD or Verilator/GtkWave FST format only please) and log files if possible.
-->
Ibex overrides `branch_mispredict_addr` by predicting on a predicted branch. This means when a mispredict fires on `beqz t0, predict_to_here` the PC fetched next is at `wfi`.

[waves.zip](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/files/7384667/waves.zip)

## Expected Behavior
<!-- Please describe the behavior you expected to see instead. -->
I honestly don't know. In the prefetch buffer configuration, there is only one `branch_mispredict_addr_q` present so there is no practical way to nest branch predictions as far as I can tell. It seems like branches should just be predicted not taken when we are already on a predicted path.

## My Environment

<!--
Let us know how you're using Ibex. This helps us to better understand your problem and find a solution more quickly.
-->
**Compiler:**
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc (GCC) 8.2.0

**EDA tool and version:**
<!--
If you are using an EDA tool to work with Ibex let us know which tool and which version you're using.
For example, "Xilinx Vivado 2020.1" or "Synopsys VCS 2020.03-SP1"
-->
Verilator 4.210 2021-07-07 rev v4.210

**Operating system:**
<!--
Please let us know the operating system/Linux distribution you're using.
For example "Ubuntu Linux 18.04" or "CentOS 7.3".
-->
Ubuntu 21.04

**Version of the Ibex source code:**
<!--
Which version of the Ibex source code are you using?
You can call `git rev-parse HEAD` in your Ibex source directory to get this information.
Please also let us know if you have made changes to the code.
-->
cfeef7e864926cf4d30e271a3e2aa5d95e0c141f

  static int x = 25;
  int *x_addr = (int *)&x;

  puts("START\n");

  __asm__ volatile(
      "j skip\n\t"
      "\n\t"
      "predict_to_here:\n\t"
      "j finish\n\t"
      "wfi\n\t"
      "\n\t"
      "skip:\n\t"
      "lw t0, 0(%0)\n\t"
      "beqz t0, predict_to_here\n\t"
      "j finish\n\t"
      "\n\t"
      "finish:\n\t"
      "nop\n\t"
      :

      : "t0", "memory");

  return 0;
}
EOF

cat > "${TEST_DIR}/Makefile" <<'EOF'

PROGRAM_DIR := $(shell dirname $(realpath $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))

make -C "${TEST_DIR}"
sw_rc=$?
if [ ${sw_rc} -ne 0 ]; then
  report_and_exit "FAIL" "${sw_rc}"

fusesoc --cores-root=. run --target=sim --tool=verilator --setup --build \
  lowrisc:ibex:ibex_simple_system \
  --RV32E=0 \
  --RV32M=ibex_pkg::RV32MFast \
  --BranchTargetALU=1 \
  --WritebackStage=1 \
  --BranchPredictor=1
build_rc=$?
if [ ${build_rc} -ne 0 ]; then
  report_and_exit "FAIL" "${build_rc}"
fi

timeout 20s "${SIM_BIN}" --meminit=ram,"${TEST_DIR}/${TEST_NAME}.elf" | tee "${SIM_STDOUT}"
sim_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

if [ -f "${UART_LOG}" ]; then
  cat "${UART_LOG}"
fi

if [ ${sim_rc} -eq 0 ] && [ -f "${UART_LOG}" ] && grep -q "DONE" "${UART_LOG}"; then
  report_and_exit "PASS" 0
fi

report_and_exit "FAIL" 1

problem_statement: When `BranchPredictor=1`, Ibex can mis-handle recovery from a branch that was predicted taken but later resolves as not taken if that branch is still unresolved while fetch continues down the predicted path. In the reported failing case, a preceding load delays resolution of the first branch, a later branch or jump on the speculative path is also predicted, and the recovery state for the earlier branch is replaced by the later prediction. Instructions from the wrong path can also remain buffered in the instruction fetch pipeline. When the earlier branch is finally resolved as not taken, the core can resume from the wrong PC and continue with wrong-path instructions, which can send execution into an unintended instruction stream and make the core appear to lock up. The expected behavior is that a predicted-taken branch that resolves as not taken must restart execution from the instruction immediately following that branch, independent of any later predictions, and any buffered instructions from the wrong predicted path must be discarded. This affects the instruction-fetch branch prediction and not-taken mispredict recovery logic.

title: Various fixes for known simulation issues
body: Small fixes to the RTL and testbench to fix issues seen in nightly runs

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[rtl] Add reset to lockstep delayed inputs

In tests with multiple resets, these signals could hold onto spurious
values through reset (since the clock is also gated) which caused
assertion failures on resumption.

Fixes #1368

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

[rtl] Fix decode values for B Operand mux select

With data-independent timing enabled and BranchTargetALU configured,
branches will stall for a cycle causing an illegal value to be decoded
for the B Operand. No functional impact of this, but an assertion fires
so we might as well tie it off properly.

Fixes #1367

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

[dv/uvm/core_ibex] Update CSR description file

The CSR tests don't currently support multiple configurations
(see #1333). Since the OpenTitan configuration is the only one currently
being run, update this file to pass with that for now.

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

[dv/uvm/core_ibex] Pass ISA from Makefile

This allows run.py to pass ISA options through to Spike. This relates to
the failure in #1369 (test inserts a bitmanip instruction which Spike
interprets as valid but the core treats as invalid depending on config).

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

problem_statement: In `ibex_decoder`, a taken branch can remain in decode for a second cycle while the optional dedicated branch-target path (`BranchTargetALU`) is enabled; this is the state reached when data-independent timing keeps the branch in decode for an extra cycle. In that non-first decode cycle, the decoder incorrectly drives the main ALU B-operand selection as if the main ALU should use the branch-offset immediate, even though branch target generation is supposed to come from the dedicated branch-target path. This creates an illegal decode combination and causes simulation assertion failures. For any taken branch that remains in decode on a non-first cycle with `BranchTargetALU` enabled, the decoder must keep its operand-select outputs legal and must not route the branch-offset immediate onto the main ALU B operand.

export PATH="/opt/micromamba/envs/ibex/bin:/opt/micromamba/condabin:$PATH"

mkdir -p "${TB_DIR}"

timeout 1200s fusesoc --cores-root=. run --target=sim --setup --build \
  lowrisc:ibex:ibex_simple_system > "${BUILD_LOG}" 2>&1
build_rc=$?

cat > "${TB_DIR}/ibex_pkg_unused_only.vlt" <<'EOF'
`verilator_config
lint_off -rule UNUSED -file "*rtl/ibex_pkg.sv"
EOF

verilator -E -P -sv rtl/ibex_tracer_pkg.sv | \
  sed '/verilator[[:space:]]\+lint_/d' > "${TB_DIR}/ibex_tracer_pkg_stripped.sv"
pp_pkg_rc=$?
verilator -E -P -sv rtl/ibex_tracer.sv | \
  sed '/verilator[[:space:]]\+lint_/d' > "${TB_DIR}/ibex_tracer_stripped.sv"
pp_tracer_rc=$?

if [ "${pp_pkg_rc}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${pp_tracer_rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  timeout 300s verilator --lint-only -Wall -Werror-UNUSED -Wno-DECLFILENAME \
    --top-module ibex_tracer \
    "${TB_DIR}/ibex_pkg_unused_only.vlt" \
    rtl/ibex_pkg.sv \
    "${TB_DIR}/ibex_tracer_pkg_stripped.sv" \
    "${TB_DIR}/ibex_tracer_stripped.sv" \
    > "${TRACER_LOG}" 2>&1
  tracer_rc=$?
else
  tracer_rc=1
  {
    echo "Failed to preprocess tracer sources."
    echo "ibex_tracer_pkg.sv rc=${pp_pkg_rc}"
    echo "ibex_tracer.sv rc=${pp_tracer_rc}"
  } > "${TRACER_LOG}"
fi

if [ "${build_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
  cat "${BUILD_LOG}"
fi

if [ "${tracer_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
  cat "${TRACER_LOG}"
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [ "${build_rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_BUILD} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_BUILD} ... FAIL"
fi

if [ "${tracer_rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_TRACER} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_TRACER} ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

if [ "${build_rc}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${tracer_rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

exit 1

In the baseline, the build emits `UNUSED` warnings from `rtl/ibex_tracer_pkg.sv` and `LATCH` warnings from `shared/rtl/bus.sv`, then exits with an error instead of completing. body:

commits.message:
[rtl] Fix performance counter bug

- Make sure performance counters only count retired, non-trapping
  instructions excluding ebrk/ecall
- Rewire some signalling through the writeback stage to allow
  instruction retire to be signalled from one place
- Relates to #1132

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: Illegal Instruction Retires
resolved_issues.body:
####  RISC-V Specification

> 3.1.11: "The minstret CSR counts the number of instructions the hart has retired. The mcycle and minstret registers
have 64-bit precision on all RV32 and RV64 systems.

> The counter registers have an arbitrary value after system reset, and can be written with a given value. Any CSR write takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed."

> The counter-inhibit register mcountinhibit is a 32-bit WARL register that controls which of the hardware performance-monitoring counters increment. The settings in this register only control whether the counters increment; their accessibility is not affected by the setting of this register.

> When the CY, IR, or HPMn bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the cycle, instret, or hpmcountern register increments as usual. When the CY, IR, or HPMn bit is set, the corresponding counter does not increment.

####  Issue Description
An illegal instruction increments the minstret counter as if it was a legal one.

#### Steps to Reproduce

As shown below, the minstret counter is incremented for the illegal instruction csrrw x8, 0x010, x3, knowing that IR bit of mcountinhibit is set to '0 and thus allowing for the minstret to be incremented.  

![minstret_ill](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/54367010/95972699-0e2e1280-0e13-11eb-87f8-9621c1352d6b.PNG)

---
Product: OneSpin 360 DV-Verify
App: Processor Verification App
Tool's version: 2020.2.0

@@ -246,6 +247,7 @@ module ibex_core #(
   logic        ex_valid;
 
   logic        lsu_resp_valid;
+  logic        lsu_resp_err;
 
   // Signals between instruction core interface and pipe (if and id stages)

@@ -298,9 +300,10 @@ module ibex_core #(
   // signals relating to instruction movements between pipeline stages
   // used by performance counters and RVFI

-  logic        instr_id_done_compressed;

problem_statement: The Ibex instruction-retirement counter path can count a trapping instruction as if it had retired normally. With retired-instruction counting enabled (`mcountinhibit.IR = 0`), `minstret` is observed to increment for an illegal instruction, and the same bug appears for `ECALL` (the RISC-V environment-call instruction): if software reads `minstret`, executes `ECALL`, and the trap handler reads `minstret` on entry, the second value should be exactly one count higher because only the earlier read instruction retired, but the trapping `ECALL` is currently counted as well. The affected logic is the instruction-retirement/performance-counter path between the core pipeline and the CSR counter block. The correct behavior is that `minstret` increments only for instructions that complete and retire normally; instructions that raise a synchronous exception, including illegal instructions and `ECALL`, must not contribute to the retired-instruction count.

title: [rtl] Various security feature bugfixes
body:
- Document that SecureIbex cannot be used without a multiplier and add
  an assertion in the rtl. This fixes #1080.
- Move the PC checking hardware onto its own parameter to match all the
  other individual security features.
- Make the PC increment behavior more sensible on fetch errors (and make
  it match the icache behavior). Factor this into the PC increment check
  to prevent false triggering, fixes #1094.
- Stop the PC mismatch checker firing on dummy instructions, fixes
  #1095.

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

repo.name: ibex

resolved_issues.title: [RTL] Illegal Instructions occur when dummy instructions are enabled and RV32M = 0
resolved_issues.body:
Bug conditions:
- parameter bit               RV32M                    = 1'b0,
- parameter bit               SecureIbex              = 1'b1,
- Bit 2 of cpuctrl register (dummy_instr_en)  is set 

Description:
When a dummy instruction is executed, an illegal opcode is set when the dummy instruction opcode corresponds to a MUL or DIV.

I would recommend to remove MUL and DIV from dummy opcodes.

![illeg_instr](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51697819/90790308-32d0a700-e308-11ea-8109-f09dbb03e427.PNG)

resolved_issues.body:
Hi,

The PC mismatch alarm fires when a dummy instruction is inserted.

conditions:

- parameter bit SecureIbex = 1'b1,
- Bit 2 of cpuctrl register (dummy_instr_en) is set

![pc_mismartch_instr_err](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51697819/91045760-a976e880-e617-11ea-9a9f-226ad9590340.PNG)

May I suggest following change in ibex_if_stage.sv : 

    // Check that the address equals the previous address +2/+4
    assign pc_mismatch_alert_o = prev_instr_seq_q & (pc_if_o != prev_instr_addr_incr) **& ~dummy_instr_id_o**;

problem_statement: An instruction bus error in the Ibex instruction-fetch path can be misclassified when it occurs on a 32-bit instruction that starts at a half-word-aligned address, so the instruction spans two 16-bit halves across fetch words. In that case, the fetch logic may treat the faulting instruction as if the first half were a completed 16-bit RISC-V compressed instruction, advance the instruction stream by 2 bytes, and, when SecureIbex's sequential program-counter check is enabled, raise a spurious PC mismatch alarm. The correct behavior is that a fetch error must not cause that unaligned 32-bit instruction to be treated as compressed: the instruction must remain incomplete until both halves are available, and the next sequential PC tracked by the fetch path must advance by 4 bytes rather than 2. This affects the instruction fetch FIFO/front-end and is triggered by a sequential instruction bus error during an unaligned 32-bit instruction fetch.

problem_statement: `fetch_enable_i` is the input that allows the Ibex core to fetch instructions. When the core comes out of reset with `fetch_enable_i` low, the gated core clock can still toggle during the startup idle window instead of staying off. If `fetch_enable_i` is later asserted for only a single cycle, that start request can be missed. The affected reset/startup path is the logic that keeps the core quiescent until fetch is enabled. Correct behavior is that no gated core clock activity should occur while `fetch_enable_i` is low after reset, and even a one-cycle assertion of `fetch_enable_i` must be enough for the core to wake up and issue an instruction fetch request.

title: [rtl] prefetch buffer performance fix
body:
- The prefetch buffer needs to know when space is available in the fetch
  FIFO to accept a new external request.
- This change updates that logic to look at what is in the FIFO and what
  is outstanding on the bus to decide when space is available rather
  than always assuming the maximum number of requests are outstanding.
- This improves the usage efficiency of the FIFO and fixes #574

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[rtl] prefetch buffer performance fix

- The prefetch buffer needs to know when space is available in the fetch
  FIFO to accept a new external request.
- This change updates that logic to look at what is in the FIFO and what
  is outstanding on the bus to decide when space is available rather
  than always assuming the maximum number of requests are outstanding.
- This improves the usage efficiency of the FIFO and fixes #574

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: Fetch FIFO blocks instruction request when full.
resolved_issues.body:
Hi everyone, 

I may have found an issue with the prefetch buffer. The situation: I have implemented a second memory port in the simple system example (PR #571) and run both the hello_test example and coremark on it. Since I would expect no memory contention on the instruction line, i would expect to record less IFetch waits with coremark. however the opposite was the case: Using the separated data and instruction ports, coremark recoreded around 200 more IFetch wait than using a single memory port.
For the hello_test example, I have found that the new implementation takes two more cycles than the baseline, which already is unexpected. So I have analyzed the situation using this simulation. By comparing the traces of the two hello_test runs, I think I can pinpoint exactly where the problem is:


The top level instruction request signal `instr_req_o` is set in `prefetch_buffer.sv` lines 108-111 by the signal `valid_req`:  
``` 
// Make a new request any time there is space in the FIFO, and space in the request queue
assign valid_new_req = req_i & (fifo_ready | branch_i) & ~rdata_outstanding_q[NUM_REQS-1];
assign valid_req = valid_req_q | valid_new_req;
```
So if we re not branching, a memory request can only be issued when the fifo is ready. The fifo ready signal is set in `ibex_fetch_fifo.sv` line 155:
```
assign in_ready_o = ~valid_q[DEPTH-NUM_REQS]; // DEPTH = 3, NUM_REQS=2
```
Now, by comparing the traces I have found that the delay is introduced around 154ns into the hello_test simulation. The waveform for the baseline implementation is here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47077581/73343178-679fe280-4280-11ea-97b8-4cb615f7b814.png)

The waveform for the implementation with dual port memory is here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47077581/73343091-3e7f5200-4280-11ea-95ef-6e16d835b118.png)


At 143ns you can see that the pipeline is stalled due to the `id_stage` being busy. This is a store-word instruction, so it makes a data request. In the baseline implementation the data and instruction line is shared, so in the meantime no instruction can be fetched. However for the dual-port implementation a new instruction is fetched, and the fetch-fifo after that has stored two memory words. therefore the fifo ready signal will be low, and no new memory request will be made (`instr_req_o`).  
The first instruction (`PC=001003B4`) in the FIFO is compressed. So, after that the word can not be popped and the fifo is still full. Here is content of the fifo at that point (at 149ns):
```
             | 31             16 | 15              0 |
FIFO entry 0 | PC001003B6 [15:0] | PC001003B4 [15:0] |
FIFO entry 1 | PC001003BA [15:0] | PC001003B6 [31:16]| 
```
So instruction `001003B6` is fetched and in the next cycle the fifo is not full anymore. 
```
             | 31             16 | 15              0 |
FIFO entry 0 | PC001003BA [15:0] |                   | 
FIFO entry 0 |                   |                   |
```
So  `instr_req_o` is raised again (at 151ns), but `instr_rvalid_i` is only received in the cycle after that, leading to a 1 cycle stall, since the instruction in the fifo is incomplete.

For the baseline implementation the fifo does not get full and therefore `instr_req_o` is never lowered and we never have to wait for `instr_rvalid_i`. That's the reason why the single-port implementation finishes faster.

So, as far as I can tell, at least while there are unaligned, uncompressed instructions in the fetch fifo, it can never remain full. Thus there is always a stall while waiting for `instr_rvalid_i`. 


I think the fundamental problem is that no simultaneous pop and push is possible while the FIFO is full. If we would take into account the anticipated next-cycle occupancy when setting the fifo `in_ready_o` signal, i. e. change line 155 `ibex_fetch_fifo.sv` to
```
assign in_ready_o = ~valid_d[DEPTH-NUM_REQS]; 
```
the memory request could be done one cycle earlier and the valid signal will arrive only once there is space in the fetch FIFO. 

I have run the hello_test and coremark programs using this fix. The number of IFetch waits for coremark using the fix on the baseline (single-port) implementation decreases from 14968 to 5215. Total ticks decrease from 423620 to 416639.  

Executing the hello_test program, there is no improvement for the single-port implementation. However the additional two cycles of latency that were observed for the dual-port implementation disappear. 

Also coremark now executes with exactly the same statistics for single- and dual-port implementation. This is disapointing, but I think very well possible for non-data intensive workloads. 

I do not know if my fix is fully correct, since there are some parts in the Prefetch Buffer and the Fetch FIFO, that I don't yet completely understand. But I hope that my account may help somebody investigate and fix the problem.

I will attatch the output of my simulation runs. For coremark I will omit the trace_core log and waveforms, since those are huge files. If you are interested in them let me know.

[edit: changed this file, since I have mixed up waveform files. ]
[prefetch-buff-issue_sim-out_new.zip](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/files/4127676/prefetch-buff-issue_sim-out_new.zip)




Nomenclature of the folders: master = single-port implementation, perf-eval = dual-port implementation

In perf-eval_hello_test-out, there is a gtkwave save-file `waveconfig.gtkw which you can use with all the simulation waveforms to directly display the waveforms as they are in my screenshots.

cheers, Noam

   // FIFO management //
diff --git a/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv b/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv
index 067867e82e..9343fc0355 100644
--- a/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv
+++ b/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv
@@ -51,6 +51,7 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (
   logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] rdata_outstanding_n, rdata_outstanding_s, rdata_outstanding_q;
   logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] branch_discard_n, branch_discard_s, branch_discard_q;
   logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] rdata_pmp_err_n, rdata_pmp_err_s, rdata_pmp_err_q;
+  logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] rdata_outstanding_rev;

@@ -62,6 +63,7 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (

@@ -82,6 +84,16 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (

+  // Reversed version of rdata_outstanding_q which can be overlaid with fifo fill state

problem_statement: In the instruction fetch path, the interaction between `ibex_prefetch_buffer` and the fetch FIFO can deassert `instr_req_o` too early when the FIFO is full on a non-branch path and contains a 16-bit compressed instruction followed by a 32-bit instruction that starts in the upper half of one fetched word and completes in the next fetched word. In that state, the next word is requested one cycle late, so after the compressed instruction is consumed the following 32-bit instruction is still incomplete and the core incurs an extra instruction-fetch stall. The expected behavior is that the prefetch buffer must keep requesting the next word needed to complete that spanning 32-bit instruction while the FIFO still holds the compressed instruction and the partial 32-bit instruction, so that once the compressed instruction is consumed the 32-bit instruction is available immediately without an extra fetch bubble.

title: [rtl] Various small icache bugfixes
body:

  accept data when the core is not ready
- Tighten-up behaviour around invalidations and cache enable/disable

problem_statement: `ibex_icache` violates its documented core-side instruction response handshake: `valid_o` can depend on `ready_i`, so the cache may withhold an instruction response that is already available internally until the core raises `ready_i`. The expected behavior is concrete and testable: once the cache has assembled a response for the current fetch, it must assert `valid_o` even while `ready_i` is low; `ready_i` should only control when the core consumes that response. This affects the icache output path back to the core and is exposed when fetch is redirected to a half-word-aligned address. In a design that supports 16-bit compressed instructions, a 32-bit instruction can start on a 16-bit boundary and must then be assembled from two fetch words; that completed 32-bit response must still be presented with `valid_o` independent of `ready_i`.

title: Fix behavior of exceptions in debug mode, document debug CSRs
body:
This PR consists of three small commits which implement the following changes:
- Exceptions in debug mode shall not modify any CSRs. This resolves #168 and is related to #365.
- Document debug CSRs. This resolves #307.
- Update documentation of `mhartid` CSR. Previously, the doc was still describing the cluster and core ID bit fields.

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[rtl] Do not update CSRs upon exceptions in debug mode

In debug mode, exceptions shall not update any CSRs including `mcause`,
`mepc`, `mtval`, `dpc` and `mstatus`, see Debug Spec v0.13.2, p.39.

This resolves lowRISC/ibex#168.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

[doc] Document debug CSRs

This resolves lowRISC/ibex#307.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

[doc] Update `mhartid` CSR description

This commit removes outdated bit-field descriptions for `mhartid` CSR.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: Check behavior of exceptions and special instructions related to debug mode
resolved_issues.body:
Currently, exceptions and special instructions are handled independent of whether the core is in debug mode or not. This is not correct for a couple of cases. For example, the Debug Spec v0.13.2 states on p.39 that while in debug mode:
- ~~WFI acts as a NOP. Currently the core just goes to sleep anyway.~~
- Exceptions do not update any registers such as `mcause`, `mepc`, `mtval`, `dpc` and `mstatus`. Currently, exception handling does not depend on debug mode.

~~Similarly, the DRET instruction must lead to an illegal instruction exception when the core is not in debug mode (p.41). Currently, DRET always restores the PC in dpc even if the core is not in debug mode, thus silently messing up the processor state.~~

resolved_issues.title: Document debug CSRs
resolved_issues.body: Document dscratch0, dscratch1 and dpc CSRs in the CSR documentation, and link them from the debug documentation page.

problem_statement: When Ibex takes an exception while the core is already in Debug Mode, the exception-handling path still overwrites machine Control and Status Registers (CSRs) that record trap state. As a result, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, and `mstatus` can be modified even though the core is already in Debug Mode. The affected functionality is the Debug Mode exception/CSR handling logic. The correct behavior is that an exception taken in Debug Mode must leave those CSRs unchanged; in particular, it must not clear the interrupt-enable state in `mstatus` or replace the existing trap information in `mepc`, `mcause`, and `mtval`. This is triggered whenever an exception is taken after `debug_mode` is already active.

resolved_issues.body:
Hi all,
I'm executing some tests after booting Ibex into User-Mode, and asserting debug stimulus, and I see the following:
![Screenshot from 2019-11-12 17-28-49](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/68725023-01090380-0572-11ea-86a8-d11f863ff425.png)
In this test, our debug ROM is located at `0x80004f88`.
We can see that the core's privilege level stays at `PRIV_LVL_U` even after the core has jumped to the debug ROM and `debug_req` has dropped, while the Debug-Mode Spec says that all operation in debug mode should be taken at machine mode. As a result of the current Ibex behavior, illegal instruction exceptions are thrown when we access D-mode CSRs inside of the debug ROM.
However, `dcsr.prv` is being updated properly, and stores the value of `PRIV_LVL_M` after trapping to debug mode, it is just the current privilege mode that is being calculated incorrectly.
Best,
Udi

problem_statement: When Ibex takes a debug request while the core is executing in RISC-V User mode (U-mode), it can jump to the debug ROM while still treating the current execution privilege as U-mode instead of RISC-V Machine mode (M-mode). This affects the debug-entry privilege handling in the core's control and CSR logic. The observed consequence is that code running from the debug ROM can raise illegal-instruction exceptions when it accesses debug control and status registers (CSRs), because those accesses are still being checked as if the core were in U-mode. The expected behavior is that once debug mode is entered, all execution in the debug ROM must run with the core's current privilege level set to M-mode, regardless of the privilege level from which debug was entered.

title: [RTL LSU] Change unaligned error behaviour
body:
- If an error is signalled in the first part of an unaligned
  transaction, the second part is issued anyway (to avoid a
  timing loop from data_err_i -> data_req_o)
- Previously, the error was signalled and an exception was taken
  as soon as the first transaction completed. This commits makes
  the core wait until both transactions have completed.
- This prevents strange behaviour caused by the lsu and controller
  being out of sync (fixes #374).

repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[RTL LSU] Change unaligned error behaviour

- If an error is signalled in the first part of an unaligned
  transaction, the second part is issued anyway (to avoid a
  timing loop from data_err_i -> data_req_o)
- Previously, the error was signalled and an exception was taken
  as soon as the first transaction completed. This commits makes
  the core wait until both transactions have completed.
- This prevents strange behaviour caused by the lsu and controller
  being out of sync (fixes #374).

Hi all,
When running this set of instructions:
![Screenshot from 2019-10-04 16-43-38](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/66245995-26c70100-e6c6-11e9-8347-b284c658e62c.png)

![Screenshot from 2019-10-04 16-47-11](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/66246078-a1901c00-e6c6-11e9-839a-a188fce292f5.png)
The `sw` instructions at `PC=0x800058d0` has a misaligned memory address, and is thus split into two internal memory transactions. In the waves, around 395,800,000ps corresponds to the memory response to the first of these two transactions, which is when the testbench randomly asserts a memory fault here. According to Ibex documentation for this situation, the second memory transaction should continue as normal, ignoring the response data, and then the core needs to also jump to the corresponding fault handler (located at `PC=0x80014000` in our case). The LSU's FSM transitions to it's error handling states from the misaligned transaction states, and the core jumps to `0x80014000` (which encodes the instruction `j 80014080`) directly after `0x800058d0`, but while executing this jump instruction, the core jumps to `0x8001e112` instead, throwing an illegal instruction exception, and then proceeds to wait for the `rvalid` corresponding to the second part of the original misaligned transaction. This occurs around 395,835,000ps, and after this, the core jumps back to the fault handler, and fully executes it. This intermediate PC of `0x8001e112` is calculated as the incorrect jump address from load address data that's already in the execution pipeline, and is muxed through due to `lsu_addr_incr_req_i` going high while waiting for the second half of the misaligned memory transaction to complete. Maybe a potential solution for this would be to only jump to the fault handler after the second part of the misaligned transactions has completed?
Best,
Udi

resolved_issues.title: Incorrect `mepc` value after irq is taken
resolved_issues.body:
Hi all,
During a test, this segment of code is running on the core:
![Screenshot from 2019-09-16 11-19-14](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/64982799-e406cb80-d873-11e9-8d8e-19d60156213b.png)
At `PC=0x80000276` (a `nop` instruction), our testbench asserts a software interrupt, as shown from the waves below:
![Screenshot from 2019-09-16 11-23-43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/64983038-74dda700-d874-11e9-8709-7f0dfce5636f.png)
However, we see that `mepc_q` gets set to `0x80000274` after this interrupt is detected and handling begins, meaning that after the interrupt handler has ended, the core will jump back to this address, but as you can see from the code snippet, this is a misaligned address, so Ibex immediately takes an illegal instruction exception, and fails the test.  This address comes from the `exception_pc`, which is muxed to the value of `pc_if_i`, which for some reason is set to this misaligned address, and is less than the `pc_id_i`.

resolved_issues.title: Instruction address changes before a request/grant handshake
resolved_issues.body:
The instruction interface of Ibex allows to change the address while asserting request and waiting for a grant. This behavior is inherited from RI5CY. If I remember correctly, the primary reason for having this in RI5CY is that in multi-core configurations (PULP) with a shared instruction cache, it allows to reduce contention on the cache and leads to notable performance gains. This can also be beneficial for performance in Ibex (e.g. in case the core takes a branch while the instruction interface is still waiting for the grant of a previous request) but has over and over again confused people.

There were several GitHub issues where we needed to explain this to users, but the problem was usually something else. However, we never had an issue to discuss if we want to change this behavior or keep it.

I think we should remove it. Ibex is a different core that does not target multi-core configs with shared I-caches, so the actual performance benefit is probably relatively low. Instead, it is confusing and complicates translation into popular protocols such as AXI/AHB (it is however legal for TileLink interconnects) as mentioned in pulp-platform/riscv#128.

WDYT?

resolved_issues.title: Instruction fetch error execution
resolved_issues.body:
Hi all,
![Screenshot from 2019-09-19 16-18-58](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/65288479-d06d9600-dafb-11e9-8060-11e8c25877e0.png)
![Screenshot from 2019-09-19 16-23-24](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/65288484-d2cff000-dafb-11e9-8ed2-266b8f6eac41.png)
Above is a snippet of disassembled code I was running on Ibex, and the associated section in the core tracer. At `PC=0x8000087c`, there should be a `nop` instruction, but Ibex shows execution of `lui x19, 0xabd6c000` at this PC.
![Screenshot from 2019-09-19 16-34-44](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/65288550-10cd1400-dafc-11e9-8a99-2d01a2d3525b.png)
At the location in the waves where the cursor is, the active `instr_grant` and `instr_rvalid` are responding to the `request` corresponding to the address `0x8000087c`. At the same time, the testbench randomly asserts an `instr_error` during the instruction fetch response, and randomizes the returned `instr_rdata`, as the request has returned with an error response. The random data here happens to be the value `0xabd6c9b7`, which Ibex decodes as the same exact `lui` instruction from above.  We should expect that this should not be executed then, since an error was returned to the core, but we can see that at time 4,113,000ns, Ibex raises the register file `we_a_i` write enable signal, and writes the data `0xabd6c000` to register `0x13`, effectively completing execution of this random instruction data even though there was an instruction fetch error associated with this response. Immediately after completing execution of the randomly generated data at `PC=0x8000087c`, the core jumps to the instruction fetch exception handler at `PC=80014000`, and runs the handler code.
This issue only exists for the instruction fetch interface; for similar situations involving load/store errors that the testbench generates, Ibex will not commit load data to the regfile, or write store data to our memory model, and will only run the faulty memory instruction to completion once it has finished executing the associated exception handler code.

problem_statement: The Ibex instruction-fetch prefetch buffer can change the address on the external instruction request interface before the current request has completed its request/grant handshake. When an instruction fetch request is still pending and a branch redirects fetching to a different address, `instr_req_o` remains asserted but `instr_addr_o` can incorrectly switch from the original fetch address to the branch target before `instr_gnt_i` arrives. This affects the prefetch buffer and instruction-side request path. The correct behavior is that, once an instruction fetch request is pending, the corresponding `instr_addr_o` must remain stable until the `instr_req_o`/`instr_gnt_i` handshake completes.

problem_statement: Recent instruction-side logic and prefetch-buffer changes broke the instruction fetch handshake in Ibex. The instruction-side prefetch buffer issues fetches through a request/grant/response interface: `instr_req_o` requests an instruction fetch, `instr_gnt_i` accepts that request, and the returned instruction data arrives later. In the failing behavior, if a fetch request is made and the grant does not arrive immediately, the prefetch buffer can stop treating that fetch as pending and can advance to a different address before the original request has been accepted. This can desynchronize instruction fetches and cause execution to stop early in the tracing example. The affected logic is the instruction-side prefetch buffer and its request/address tracking. When a fetch is pending but has not yet been granted, including the sequential fetch immediately after a granted branch fetch, `instr_req_o` must remain asserted and `instr_addr_o` must remain at the same word-aligned address until `instr_gnt_i` acknowledges that request.

problem_statement: In the instruction-side fetch path, the instruction request output (`instr_req_o`) has a combinational dependency on the instruction return-valid input (`instr_rvalid_i`). When the prefetch buffer already has a granted fetch outstanding and is deciding whether it can issue the next instruction fetch request, a change on `instr_rvalid_i` can immediately change `instr_req_o`, creating a slave-to-master-to-slave timing path on the instruction interface in systems that do not pipeline these signals. The correct behavior is that `instr_req_o` must not change combinationally in response to `instr_rvalid_i` within the same cycle; receipt of an instruction return-valid may only affect request generation in a later cycle.

problem_statement: `ibex_load_store_unit` has a data-interface timing bug. The outgoing request signal `data_req_o` is coupled to the current response/error inputs `data_rvalid_i` and `data_err_i`, creating a slave-to-master-to-slave combinational path on the Load-Store Unit (LSU) interface. In the misaligned access path, where one load or store that crosses a word boundary is split into two word-aligned memory transactions, this also changes visible behavior: the second transaction can be held off until the first transaction returns a response. The expected behavior is concrete: once the first part of a misaligned access has been granted, the LSU must be able to issue the second request before the first response arrives, independent of the current values of `data_rvalid_i` and `data_err_i`. If the first response later reports an error after that second request has already been issued, the LSU must report the error for the original access, remain busy until the already-issued second response is received, ignore that abandoned second response for architectural completion, and only then return to idle. The bug is triggered when a misaligned data access has its first transfer granted and the first response returns with `data_err_i` asserted while the LSU still needs to manage the second transfer.

commits.message:
ID stage: make single-cycle instr clear `instr_multicycle_done_q`

Previously, this signal was only cleared when starting the next
multi-cycle instruction.

ID stage: only eval `instr_multicycle_done_q` for multi-cycle instr

This signal should only be evaluated if the ID/EX stage currently
executes a multi-cycle instruction. Without this commit, the signal
is also evaluated for single-cycle instructions and can for example
cause the register file write enable to not be de-asserted in case of
stalls in the IF stage.

resolved_issues.title: instr_multicycle_done is not asserted, continuous register writes
resolved_issues.body:
While executing the code shown below:
![Screenshot from 2019-08-05 18-14-11](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/62504340-e2de7b00-b7ac-11e9-8b26-0cc4090ccec3.png)
We see this incorrect behavior in the core:
![Screenshot from 2019-08-05 18-13-52](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/62504356-ee31a680-b7ac-11e9-8d28-748683269f7e.png)

As shown, the `addi` instruction at PC `0x80000088` appears to correctly load register `x13` with the value `0xa5a5a5a5`, but at the very next instruction (PC: `0x8000008c`), we can see from the trace log that `x13` now has the value `0xa5a5de17`. 
![Screenshot from 2019-08-05 18-12-33](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/62504456-76b04700-b7ad-11e9-94ab-524900644a48.png)

From the waveform, `rf_reg[13]` is written correctly by the `addi` after adding the immediate value `0x5a5` (`alu_operand_b_i`), and becomes `0xa5a5a5a5`. After this, the testbench does not assert the `instr_gnt_i` for a number of cycles, leading the core to stay in the DECODE phase while waiting for the next instruction fetch. However, we see that `rf_reg[13]` keeps getting written with the incremented values of `alu_result` in every consecutive cycle that the core waits, as `instr_multicycle_done_q` in the ID stage does not go high after the `addi` finishes. This keeps `regfile_we` at 1, causing the continuous writes.

problem_statement: When a single-cycle instruction such as `addi` completes in Ibex and the next instruction fetch is stalled because the instruction-fetch grant signal (`instr_gnt_i`) stays low, the core can remain in the instruction-decode (ID) stage with the register-file write-enable signal (`regfile_we`) still asserted. During those stalled cycles, the destination register of the completed instruction may be written again even though no new instruction has arrived. The affected functionality is the ID-stage logic that determines when the current instruction has finished and whether register-file writes remain enabled while the instruction-fetch interface is stalled. Once the single-cycle instruction has committed its result, `regfile_we` must be deasserted on every cycle while the core waits for the next instruction-fetch grant, and the destination register must retain its committed value throughout that stall.

title: Rework CSR-related pipeline flushes
body:
This commit clarifies why CSR-related pipeline flushes are needed (e.g. when enabling interrupts), only introduces them when doing the critical modifications (write/set bits in `mstatus` and `mie` CSRs
for enabling interrupts, reads and clears are uncritical for these CSRs), and makes sure the controller is actually able to start handling interrupts while doing a CSR-related pipeline flush.

This resolves lowrisc/ibex#6.

(e.g. when enabling interrupts), only introduces them when doing the

for enabling interrupts, reads and clears are uncritical for these
CSRs), and makes sure the controller is actually able to start

fix_patch:
diff --git a/rtl/ibex_controller.sv b/rtl/ibex_controller.sv
index 1e03adf789..4cf6871202 100644
--- a/rtl/ibex_controller.sv
+++ b/rtl/ibex_controller.sv
@@ -38,7 +38,7 @@ module ibex_controller (
     input  logic                  dret_insn_i,           // decoder has DRET instr
     input  logic                  wfi_insn_i,            // decoder has WFI instr
     input  logic                  ebrk_insn_i,           // decoder has EBREAK instr
-    input  logic                  csr_status_i,          // decoder has CSR status instr
+    input  logic                  csr_pipe_flush_i,      // do CSR-related pipeline flush
 
     // from IF-ID pipeline stage
     input  logic                  instr_valid_i,         // instr from IF-ID reg is valid
@@ -158,7 +158,7 @@ module ibex_controller (
   assign exc_req_lsu = store_err_i | load_err_i;
 
   // special requests: special instructions, pipeline flushes, exceptions...
-  assign special_req = mret_insn_i | dret_insn_i | wfi_insn_i | csr_status_i |
+  assign special_req = mret_insn_i | dret_insn_i | wfi_insn_i | csr_pipe_flush_i |
       exc_req | exc_req_lsu;
 
   ////////////////
@@ -512,7 +512,7 @@ module ibex_controller (
           end
 
         end else begin
-          // special instructions
+          // special instructions and pipeline flushes
           if (mret_insn_i) begin
             pc_mux_o              = PC_ERET;
             pc_set_o              = 1'b1;
@@ -526,6 +526,9 @@ module ibex_controller (
             debug_mode_d          = 1'b0;
           end else if (wfi_insn_i) begin
             ctrl_fsm_ns           = WAIT_SLEEP;
+          end else if (csr_pipe_flush_i && handle_irq) begin
+            // start handling IRQs when doing CSR-related pipeline flushes
+            ctrl_fsm_ns           = IRQ_TAKEN;
           end
         end // exc_req
 
diff --git a/rtl/ibex_decoder.sv b/rtl/ibex_decoder.sv
index d472c50979..753ee39796 100644
--- a/rtl/ibex_decoder.sv
+++ b/rtl/ibex_decoder.sv
@@ -82,7 +82,7 @@ module ibex_decoder #(
     // CSRs
     output logic                 csr_access_o,          // access to CSR
     output ibex_pkg::csr_op_e    csr_op_o,              // operation to perform on CSR
-    output logic                 csr_status_o,          // access to xstatus CSR
+    output logic                 csr_pipe_flush_o,      // CSR-related pipeline flush
 
     // LSU
     output logic                 data_req_o,            // start transaction to data memory
@@ -159,6 +159,32 @@ module ibex_decoder #(
     end
   end
 
+  /////////////////////////////////
+  // CSR-related pipline flushes //
+  /////////////////////////////////
+  always_comb begin : csr_pipeline_flushes
+    csr_pipe_flush_o = 1'b0;
+
+    // A pipeline flush is needed to let the controller react after modifying certain CSRs:
+    // - When enabling interrupts, pending IRQs become visible to the controller only during
+    //   the next cycle. If during that cycle the core disables interrupts again, it does not
+    //   see any pending IRQs and consequently does not start to handle interrupts.
+    // - When modifying debug CSRs - TODO: Check if this is really needed
+    if (csr_access_o == 1'b1 && (csr_op_o == CSR_OP_WRITE || csr_op_o == CSR_OP_SET)) begin
+      if (csr_num_e'(instr[31:20]) == CSR_MSTATUS   ||
+          csr_num_e'(instr[31:20]) == CSR_MIE) begin
+        csr_pipe_flush_o = 1'b1;
+      end
+    end else if (csr_access_o == 1'b1 && csr_op_o != CSR_OP_READ) begin
+      if (csr_num_e'(instr[31:20]) == CSR_DCSR      ||
+          csr_num_e'(instr[31:20]) == CSR_DPC       ||

problem_statement: When software uses RISC-V Control and Status Register (CSR) instructions to enable interrupts through the `mie` (machine interrupt-enable) and `mstatus` (machine status) CSRs while an interrupt is already pending, Ibex can perform the CSR-related pipeline flush and then resume normal instruction execution instead of entering the interrupt handler. The failing case is a back-to-back sequence that first enables the relevant source in `mie`, then sets the global interrupt-enable bit in `mstatus`, and then immediately clears that bit again: the pending interrupt can be lost and a following non-interrupt instruction can retire. The affected logic is the CSR-related pipeline-flush and interrupt-entry path around updates to `mie` and `mstatus`. Correct behavior is that once those CSR write/set operations make a pending interrupt eligible for service, the core must take the interrupt before normal execution resumes, even if the next instruction would disable interrupts again.

body:

1. For illegal branch condition selections, the illegal instruction
condition must be signaled as long as the instruction is being executed
and not just during the first cycle, as the controller cannot interrupt
multicycle instructions.

for register-register ALU operations. Previously, these were not
signaled as the original design used `instr[28]` to encode custom bit-
manipulation instructions.

resolved_issues.body: As reported in https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/issues/147 the tracer, which is based on the RVFI signals is not working correct. problem_statement:
The Ibex RISC-V Formal Interface (RVFI) used by the execution tracer is not aligned with instruction retirement. In the current behavior, `rvfi_valid` can become true only after a later program-counter change, so the RVFI record for a retired instruction is emitted one cycle late and may be paired with the PC and instruction data of a different instruction. This affects the RVFI/tracer path that records retired instructions.

Expected behavior is that every retired instruction becomes visible to RVFI immediately when it retires, without waiting for a later PC update, and that each RVFI record corresponds to exactly one retired instruction in retirement order. The instruction value in that record, the PC of the retired instruction, and the next PC or branch target must all describe the same instruction. This must also work for 16-bit RISC-V compressed instructions, including consecutive compressed instructions: they should appear as separate retire records with 2-byte PC advances and a usable instruction value for tracing, rather than being delayed, merged into a later record, or shown as invalid.

title: Fix LSU + lint errors
body:
I prepared this PR to get urgent stuff fixed before the bigger changes for the controller and interrupts/exceptions.

This PR contains two commits:
- The first one is a cleanup of the LSU that also fixes a critical error. Previously, misaligned loads/stores were broken as the byte enable generation and read data alignment for the second transaction part were not working. These operations rely on the updated input address having the same alignment as the original address, whereas the LSU provided the aligned output address to the AGU.
- The second one fixes recently introduced linting errors.

2. Misaligned operations are again working correctly. Previously,
