problem_statement: In Caliptra's AES control finite-state machine, AES-GCM manual operation is not correctly enforced during the GCM TAG phase. When AES-GCM is configured for manual start, the controller is in the TAG phase, and software has already written a complete input block for tag processing, the block can leave its idle state and begin the GHASH (Galois hash) side of tag handling before software issues the explicit START command. The correct behavior is that manual mode must keep the AES-GCM TAG phase idle until START is asserted; loading the full tag input block alone must not consume that input or begin tag processing. This bug affects the AES subsystem's GCM control path under the trigger condition of manual operation plus a fully loaded TAG-phase input block.

problem_statement: In the Caliptra SHA-512 accelerator, the generate Platform Configuration Register (PCR) hash flow can leave the message-block lock state stuck after the operation finishes. If software runs a generate-PCR-hash command, waits for completion, issues a zeroize, and then starts a normal SHA-512 hash, the SHA-512 block registers can still behave as locked and fail to accept the newly written message block. The following standard SHA-512 command can therefore return an incorrect digest. Zeroize is expected to fully clear any lock state created by the generate-PCR-hash flow so that the next standard SHA-512 command behaves like a fresh operation: newly written block data must be accepted and the digest must match that data. The affected subsystem is the SHA-512 block, specifically the interaction between the generate-PCR-hash path and zeroize recovery.

problem_statement: Caliptra integrates a VeeR RISC-V core and exposes its debug path through a JTAG Test Access Port (TAP). In the affected VeeR TAP, when an external debugger resets the TAP and performs the default post-reset data-register scan, the TAP can return a legacy VeeR-specific IDCODE. In a larger system JTAG chain, that makes the Caliptra block appear to be a standalone VeeR device instead of a Caliptra submodule. The incorrect behavior is in the VeeR JTAG TAP used by Caliptra's RISC-V debug interface. The expected behavior is that after TAP reset, the default data-register scan must not expose that legacy IDCODE, while standard debug transport access remains available, such as a valid Debug Transport Module Control and Status (DTMCS) read.

5) Stop faulty ECC from continuing before zeroize (found by FPV): When the error happens for the first time, the error flag goes high and will remain high until zeroize. We expect that uC issues zeroize if there is an error in ECC. In this scenario, although the second command will be performed, the results should not be used since error flag is kept high. However, this PR stops faulty ECC from continuing before zeroize.

6) removed one cycle delay for hmac_drbg ready (found by FPV)
This PR synchronizes hmac_drbg READY to VALID by removing one cycle delay

7) add all_1 protection for LFSR
This PR has protection for the LFSR to stuck to be all 1.

8) Remove zeroize for the counter used as countermeasure (found by IOActive)

9) Remove one extra iteration in ecc_scalar_blinding (found by FPV)
In line 300 of scalar_blinding, we have a loop of 20 iterations (0 to 19). However, when we enter the last round, the scalar blinding flag changes to done and we don't perform the last iteration. This PR reduces the iteration by one by updating FULL_DIG_NUM.

problem_statement: In Caliptra's ECC modular add/subtract helper `ecc_add_sub_mod_alter`, a request is not fully captured when `add_en_i` is pulsed. If software or surrounding logic starts an operation with a single-cycle `add_en_i` pulse and then changes `sub_i`, the operands, or the modulus before `ready_o` asserts, the block can raise `ready_o` while `res_o` reflects the newer input values instead of the original transaction. The correct behavior is that each launched operation is self-contained: after a single `add_en_i` pulse, `ready_o` must indicate that `res_o` is valid for the operation mode, operands, and modulus that were present when the request was accepted, and callers should not need to keep those inputs fixed until completion as long as no new operation is issued before `ready_o`.

resolved_issues.title: RTL Bug: Missing async reset for mbox_rd_valid_f
resolved_issues.body:
mbox_rd_valid_f is a control signal used to qualify the population of mailbox SRAM read data into the mbox_dataout register.

Previously this signal was reset by the state machine due to assertion of the rst_rd_ptr signal on entry to a new mailbox flow, but mbox_rd_valid_f does not have an async reset.
Recent bug fixes for that rst_rdptr signal exposed the missing async. This will result in X values propagating into the mbox_dataout register if the first mailbox flow out of reset has a DLEN=0. 

Impact: The X value will still not be exposed to SoC or uC because the read data is masked for a dlen=0.

Proposed fix: Add mbox_rd_valid_f to noncore rst domain in mbox.sv

problem_statement: In the mailbox controller of Caliptra's SoC interface (`soc_ifc`), clearing `MBOX_EXECUTE` at the end of a mailbox command incorrectly resets the mailbox read pointer even when the Caliptra-side consumer has already consumed data from the mailbox SRAM during execution. After the mailbox transitions from EXECUTE back to IDLE, the read-pointer field reported in mailbox status jumps back to 0 instead of preserving the amount of data already consumed. This makes the mailbox appear to still contain unread data starting at dword 0 and can lead to repeated or unnecessary reads from the beginning of the mailbox buffer. The correct behavior is to preserve the current read pointer across the normal EXECUTE-to-IDLE transition and only reinitialize mailbox pointers when a new mailbox transaction begins. For example, if a command has 8 bytes of payload and two 32-bit words have already been consumed while `MBOX_EXECUTE` is asserted, then clearing `MBOX_EXECUTE` should leave the reported read pointer at 2, not reset it to 0. The bug is triggered when a mailbox transaction enters EXECUTE, one or more data words are consumed during command processing, and `MBOX_EXECUTE` is then deasserted before a new mailbox transaction starts.

title: [entropy_src] Keep applying fw_ov_rd_fifo_overflow
body:
Keep applying fw_ov_rd_fifo_overflow instead of pulsing. This commit is a manual port of the following Opentitan commit:

b454878f2528b49318ff2b604cb8d59a6e59b0ea

Which is associated with
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/21640.

Original commit description:

This commit applies the fw_ov_rd_fifo_overflow signal in case of an overflow. It used to only send a pulse through the register but now the signal is applied until the FIFO has been emptied once and is receiving contiguous data again.
This commit also aligns the documentation for the FW_OV_RD_FIFO_OVERFLOW register. The register is now not clearable by software. It instead is cleared by hardware.

Fixes: https://github.com/chipsalliance/caliptra-rtl/issues/503

resolved_issues.title: sfifo_observe_gate_q is stuck at reset in entropy_src
resolved_issues.body: This register sfifo_observe_gate_q never gets out of reset because the set condition can't ever be true. The observe push is qualified by the observe full already, so we never detect when there was an attempt to push the fifo while it was full.

problem_statement: In Caliptra's `entropy_src` block, the firmware-override observe FIFO overflow indicator is not held in a stable, software-visible state. The observe FIFO is the buffer that lets firmware read raw entropy samples through `FW_OV_RD_DATA`. When firmware override mode is enabled and new entropy samples keep arriving after that FIFO has become full, `FW_OV_RD_FIFO_OVERFLOW` can appear only as a pulse instead of staying asserted. As a result, firmware can miss the fact that samples were dropped and cannot reliably tell whether the data it reads from `FW_OV_RD_DATA` is still a contiguous stream of samples. The expected behavior is that once the firmware-override observe FIFO overflows, `FW_OV_RD_FIFO_OVERFLOW` remains asserted on repeated reads until the observe FIFO has been completely drained and sampling has restarted with contiguous data again; only then should the status clear.

problem_statement: In Caliptra's `soc_ifc` mailbox block, the direct mailbox SRAM read path can incorrectly turn a read into a write when the targeted mailbox word has a correctable single-bit Error Correction Code (ECC) error. The mailbox is an SRAM-backed message buffer, so this means a requester that has already acquired the mailbox lock can perform a direct read and unexpectedly modify mailbox storage during what should be a non-destructive access. The correct behavior is that a direct read encountering a correctable ECC error remains read-only: it may return the read data for that transaction, but it must not write the corrected word back into mailbox SRAM or otherwise change the stored mailbox contents. This bug is triggered during the locked direct-access flow when the mailbox owner reads a word that contains a correctable ECC fault.

problem_statement:
Caliptra is a hardware Root of Trust IP. Its `caliptra_top` module includes an optional internal Quad Serial Peripheral Interface (QSPI) host interface controlled by `CALIPTRA_INTERNAL_QSPI`. With that option enabled, `caliptra_top` exposes the QSPI data bus as one bidirectional `inout` port, `qspi_d_io`. That interface is awkward for integrations that use standard pad-cell style wiring, where pad input, pad output, and output-enable are separate signals. Those integrations cannot connect the QSPI data bus cleanly because `caliptra_top` does not provide separate top-level data input, data output, and output-enable ports.

The affected block is the `caliptra_top` QSPI/SPI host top-level interface and any top-level testbench or wrapper that instantiates it. The problem is triggered when `CALIPTRA_INTERNAL_QSPI` is defined and the integration connects QSPI through split pad signals instead of a single bidirectional SystemVerilog wire.

The QSPI clock and chip-select signals should remain ordinary outputs. The QSPI data bus should be exposed at the top level as separate per-bit input, output, and output-enable signals, matching the issue's proposed shape of `qspi_d_i`, `qspi_d_o`, and `qspi_d_oe`, or an equivalent Caliptra output-enable naming convention. There should be no on-chip tristate on `caliptra_top`'s data port; external pad logic can combine the split signals into a bidirectional pad. Under this configuration, a wrapper that instantiates `caliptra_top` with separated QSPI input, output, and output-enable signals should elaborate successfully.

title: Moving tool installation to step prior to matrix generation
body:
Moving tool installation to step prior to matrix generation.  

If the tools haven't been cached in a new branch, each test will clobber the cache, causing the tests to install the tools every time.  This re-arranges the order so that we ensure tools are installed prior to creating the test matrix.

This also modified the watchdog timer from always_comb to generate as discussed in https://github.com/chipsalliance/caliptra-rtl/issues/71

problem_statement: Caliptra's SoC interface (`soc_ifc`) includes watchdog timers that firmware programs through memory-mapped registers. In Verilator-based runs, watchdog Timer1 can report a timeout much too early: after firmware writes a large timeout value to `CPTRA_WDT_TIMER1_TIMEOUT_PERIOD_0/1`, enables Timer1, and issues a restart, the Timer1 timeout status in `CPTRA_WDT_STATUS` and the corresponding watchdog notification status can become asserted during a short polling delay even though the programmed timeout window should still be far in the future. The correct behavior is that, for this sequence, Timer1 must remain inactive during that bounded delay and must not indicate a timeout until the configured timeout period has actually elapsed.

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in the page-table walker (PTW), an S2 PTE-cache hit during hypervisor two-stage translation can leave `r_pte` with an unexpected stale value. `r_pte` is the PTW state that carries the current/root page-table entry for the walk. When Hypervisor is enabled, the address-translation mode is not Bare, and `hgatp` and `vsatp` are in different 512 GB regions, the PTW can return the wrong `r_pte` value after an S2 PTE-cache hit, especially if the walk aborts or faults immediately afterward. Expected behavior: after an S2 PTE-cache hit under these conditions, the PTW should return the correct `r_pte`/root PTE for the current translation instead of a stale value. Affected function: the PTW hypervisor two-stage translation path, specifically behavior after an S2 PTE-cache hit. Trigger condition: Hypervisor enabled, MODE not Bare, `hgatp` and `vsatp` in different 512 GB regions, and a walk that encounters an S2 PTE-cache hit.

title: Hypervisor: drive mtinst/htinst
body:
**Related issue**:

Doing this feature as required by the architecture:
> For guest-page faults, the trap instruction register is written with a special pseudoinstruction value if:
> (a) the fault is caused by an implicit memory access for VS-stage address translation, and
> (b) a nonzero value (the faulting guest physical address) is written to `mtval2` or `htval`.
> If both conditions are met, the value written to `mtinst` or `htinst` must be taken from the table below; zero is not allowed.

Paying off this tech debt from https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/pull/2841
> The `mtinst` and `htinst` CSRs are hardwired to 0, placing additional onus on hypervisor software to use the HLVX instruction.

**Type of change**: bug report | feature request

**Impact**: functional addition

**Development Phase**: implementation

**Release Notes**
Guest-page faults caused by an implicit memory access for VS-stage address translation write the architecturally-defined pseudo-instruction to `mtinst` or `htinst` because a nonzero value (the faulting guest physical address) is written to `mtval2` or `htval`.

resolved_issues.title: Add hypervisor extension
resolved_issues.body:
This PR implements v0.6.2 of the RISC-V Hypervisor Extension.

The implementation was inspired by José Martins' and colleagues' work
described in [1].  Much of the microarchitecture and essentially all of
the code is new, but their implementation served as our baseline.
We thank them for trailblazing hypervisor support in rocket-chip.

Note that this PR only includes the mechanisms to virtualize the hart
itself.  Virtualized interrupt controllers, IOMMUs, etc. are future work.
Lots of future work.

Note also that some features are (legally) not implemented.  Currently,
misa.H is not writable, something we may or may not choose to fix.
The mtinst and htinst CSRs are hardwired to 0, placing
additional onus on hypervisor software to use the HLVX instruction.

[1] "A First Look at RISC-V Virtualization from an Embedded Systems Perspective", https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14951

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in a Rocket core built with the hypervisor extension, the machine-level hypervisor trap-instruction CSR `mtinst` behaves as if it is hardwired to zero. If software writes a legal WARL value to `mtinst` and then reads it back, the read still returns zero. Expected behavior: `mtinst` must behave like an implemented hypervisor trap-instruction CSR, so a legal WARL write should be readable as a supported nonzero value instead of always reading as zero. Affected function: hypervisor trap-state and CSR handling for the `mtinst` trap-instruction register. Trigger condition: any hypervisor-enabled configuration where software directly accesses `mtinst`.

resolved_issues.title: Spurious data dependency in aes64ks1i instruction
resolved_issues.body:
<!-- THIS REPOSITORY'S ISSUES ARE RESERVED FOR FEATURE REQUESTS AND BUG REPORTS. -->
<!-- For support questions related to Rocket Chip, please use [Stack Overflow [rocket-chip]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/rocket-chip). -->
<!-- For support questions related to Chisel, please use [Stack Overflow [chisel]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/chisel). -->
<!-- Please select the item best describing the issue in each category and delete the other items. -->

<!-- choose all that apply -->
**Type of issue**: bug report

<!-- choose one -->
**Impact**: performance impact

**Other information**
 <!-- include detailed explanation, stacktraces, related issues, suggestions how to fix, links for us to have context, eg. Stack Overflow, gitter, etc -->
During formal verification with the BitManipCryptoConfig, we see the instruction in question being needlessly replayed. Consider the code sequence

        ld x19,256(x2)
        addi x8,x2,260
        aes64ks1i x11,x25,0x3

where the initial load has a cache miss. This is causing the aes64ks1i to replay without any actual dependency on the load. Apparently, the core thinks that aes64ks1i is using the rs2 field (encoding is actually 00 11000 1 rnum[3:0] rs1 001 rd 0010011), meaning a spurious dependency on x19 in this case with rnum=3.
I assume this is also causing needless stalls in decode.

This has been identified by running the Siemens Processor Verification App on the generated RTL.

#!/bin/bash

  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
}

fail_and_exit() {

  emit_result "FAIL"

if [ ! -x ./mill ]; then
  curl -fsSL -o ./mill https://github.com/com-lihaoyi/mill/releases/download/0.10.11/0.10.11 || \
    fail_and_exit "failed to download mill launcher"
  chmod +x ./mill || fail_and_exit "failed to make mill executable"
fi

mkdir -p src/test/scala/rocket || fail_and_exit "failed to create test directory"
cat > src/test/scala/rocket/AES64KS1IDecodeSpec.scala <<'EOF' || fail_and_exit "failed to write Scala test"
package freechips.rocketchip.rocket

import chisel3.util.BitPat
import freechips.rocketchip.config.Parameters
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.should.Matchers

class AES64KS1IDecodeSpec extends AnyFlatSpec with Matchers {
  implicit val p: Parameters = Parameters.empty

  private val rxs2Index = 6
  private val selAlu2Index = 12
  private val selImmIndex = 14

  "AES64KS1I decode" should "use the rnum field as an immediate and not as rs2" in {
    val ks1Entry = new ZKND64Decode().table.collectFirst {
      case (pattern, signals) if pattern == Instructions.AES64KS1I => signals
    }.getOrElse(fail("missing AES64KS1I decode entry"))

    ks1Entry(rxs2Index) shouldBe N
    ks1Entry(selAlu2Index) shouldBe BitPat(A2_IMM)
    ks1Entry(selImmIndex) shouldBe BitPat(IMM_I)
  }
}
EOF

# Mill caches task outputs in out/, and the build's Chisel version is derived
# from environment variables that are not tracked in those task hashes.
rm -rf out || fail_and_exit "failed to clear mill output cache"

test_rc=0
if env chisel3Version=3.6.0 "chisel3-pluginVersion=3.6.0" \
  ./mill --no-server rocketchip.test.testOnly freechips.rocketchip.rocket.AES64KS1IDecodeSpec; then
  emit_result "PASS"
else
  test_rc=$?
  emit_result "FAIL"
fi

problem_statement: Observed behavior: Rocket decodes the `AES64KS1I` instruction as if instruction bits 24:20 were an `rs2` register index, even though those bits encode the 4-bit round-number immediate (`rnum`). This gives `AES64KS1I` a spurious `rs2` dependency and can cause unnecessary stalls or replays when the encoded `rnum` happens to match the destination register number of an older in-flight instruction, such as a cache-missing load. Expected behavior: `AES64KS1I` must be decoded as an `rs1` plus immediate operation, with bits 24:20 interpreted as the round-number immediate rather than a second source register, so it does not wait on an unrelated `rs2` producer. Affected function: decode and operand selection for the `AES64KS1I` crypto instruction in Rocket. Trigger condition: a BitManipCrypto-enabled Rocket configuration executes `AES64KS1I` with an `rnum` value whose encoding aliases a pending destination register number.

1. The PTE Cache is supposed to cache the address being requested from memory.
2. The RISC-V Privileged ISA spec states that, for _every_ Stage-2 walk at _every level_ of Stage-1 walk, we need to check

  ptwVisibilityNode := ptwVisibilitySource
  ptwVisibilitySink := ptwVisibilityNode

  private val ptwP = p.alterPartial { case TileVisibilityNodeKey => ptwVisibilityNode }

  private val edge: TLEdgeOut = new TLEdgeOut(
    TLMasterPortParameters.v1(Seq(TLMasterParameters.v1(name = "pr3600-ptw-test"))),
    TLSlavePortParameters.v1(
      Seq(TLSlaveParameters.v1(
        address = Seq(AddressSet(0x0, (BigInt(1) << visiblePAddrBits) - 1)),
        regionType = RegionType.IDEMPOTENT,
        executable = true,
        supportsGet = TransferSizes(1, xLen / 8),
        supportsPutFull = TransferSizes(1, xLen / 8),
        supportsPutPartial = TransferSizes(1, xLen / 8),

      beatBytes = xLen / 8,
      minLatency = 1,

  )

  val ptw = Module(new PTW(1)(edge, ptwP))

  ptw.io.mem.req.ready := true.B
  ptw.io.mem.resp.valid := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.resp.bits := zeroOf(ptw.io.mem.resp.bits)
  ptw.io.mem.s2_nack := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_nack_cause_raw := false.B

  ptw.io.mem.ordered := true.B
  ptw.io.mem.perf := zeroOf(ptw.io.mem.perf)

  ptw.io.dpath.vsatp := zeroOf(ptw.io.dpath.vsatp)
  ptw.io.dpath.hgatp := zeroOf(ptw.io.dpath.hgatp)
  ptw.io.dpath.status := zeroOf(ptw.io.dpath.status)
  ptw.io.dpath.hstatus := zeroOf(ptw.io.dpath.hstatus)
  ptw.io.dpath.gstatus := zeroOf(ptw.io.dpath.gstatus)
  ptw.io.dpath.pmp := zeroOf(ptw.io.dpath.pmp)
  ptw.io.dpath.customCSRs.csrs.foreach { csr =>
    csr.ren := false.B
    csr.wen := false.B

  }
  ptw.io.dpath.sfence.valid := false.B
  ptw.io.dpath.sfence.bits := zeroOf(ptw.io.dpath.sfence.bits)

  val rootMode = (if (xLen == 32) 1 else pgLevels + 5).U
  val invalidRootPpn = (BigInt(1) << (pgLevels * pgLevelBits + maxHypervisorExtraAddrBits)).U(ptw.io.dpath.vsatp.ppn.getWidth.W)
  ptw.io.dpath.vsatp.mode := rootMode
  ptw.io.dpath.vsatp.ppn := invalidRootPpn
  ptw.io.dpath.hgatp.mode := rootMode
  ptw.io.dpath.hgatp.ppn := 0.U

  val issued = RegInit(false.B)

problem_statement: In Rocket Chip's hypervisor two-stage address translation, the page-table walker (PTW) should validate the initial stage-2 guest physical address taken from the guest `vsatp` page-table base against the address-width rules implied by `hgatp.mode`. In the verified case, when that root guest physical address has non-zero upper bits above the range allowed by the active Sv39x4/Sv48x4/Sv57x4 mode, the PTW continues the walk instead of raising a guest-page fault. The affected logic is PTW validation of the stage-2 root address at the start of a virtualized translation request, and the expected behavior is to stop immediately with a guest-page fault whenever that root GPA is out of range.

title: PTW: traverse check GPA bits higher than HGATP mode only if leaf
body:
**Related issue**: This is a similar bug as https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/pull/3625: different bits for a valid-but-table entry in the same last-level FSM state.

**Type of change**: bug report

**Impact**: functional fix

**Development Phase**: implementation

**Release Notes**
 PTW: qualify `invalid_gpa` with `pte.leaf()` instead of just `pte.v`.

**Related issue**: follow-on to https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/pull/3591

**Type of change**: bug report

**Impact**: functional fix

PTW: qualify `invalid_gpa` with `pte.v` and all the other terms from `pf` (page fault) in `gf` (guest page fault).

fix_patch:
diff --git a/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala b/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
index a4262843f99..872b143e24c 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
@@ -695,7 +695,7 @@ class PTW(n: Int)(implicit edge: TLEdgeOut, p: Parameters) extends CoreModule()(
       when (do_both_stages && !stage2) { do_switch := true.B }
       count := count + 1.U
     }.otherwise {
-      val gf = (stage2 && !stage2_final && !pte.ur()) || (pte.v && pte.reserved_for_future === 0.U && invalid_gpa)
+      val gf = (stage2 && !stage2_final && !pte.ur()) || (pte.leaf() && pte.reserved_for_future === 0.U && invalid_gpa)
       val ae = pte.v && invalid_paddr
       val pf = pte.v && pte.reserved_for_future =/= 0.U
       val success = pte.v && !ae && !pf && !gf
@@ -723,7 +723,7 @@ class PTW(n: Int)(implicit edge: TLEdgeOut, p: Parameters) extends CoreModule()(
         }
 
         resp_ae_ptw := ae && count < (pgLevels-1).U && pte.table()
-        resp_ae_final := ae
+        resp_ae_final := ae && pte.leaf()
         resp_pf := pf && !stage2
         resp_gf := gf || (pf && stage2)
         resp_hr := !stage2 || (!pf && !gf && pte.ur())

import chisel3.util._
import chisel3.simulator.EphemeralSimulator._

import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters

class DummyTLManager(address: AddressSet)(implicit p: Parameters) extends LazyModule {

class PTWGuestFaultDUT(implicit p: Parameters) extends LazyModule {
  private val tileParams = RocketTileParams(
    core = RocketCoreParams(
      useHypervisor = true,
      nPMPs = 0,
      nL2TLBEntries = 0,

  val manager = LazyModule(new DummyTLManager(AddressSet(0x0, (BigInt(1) << 40) - 1)))
  manager.node := visibilityNode

  val ptwP: Parameters = p.alterMap(Map(

class PTWGuestFaultDUTModule(outer: PTWGuestFaultDUT) extends LazyModuleImp(outer) {
  override implicit val p: Parameters = outer.ptwP

  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val done = Output(Bool())
  })

  val ptw = Module(new PTW(1)(outer.visibilityNode.edges.out.head, outer.ptwP))
  ptw.io.requestor(0) := DontCare
  ptw.io.mem := DontCare
  ptw.io.dpath := DontCare

  def tablePte(ppn: BigInt): UInt = ((ppn << 10) | 0x1).U(64.W)

  def leafPte(ppn: BigInt, user: Boolean): UInt = {
    val lowBits = if (user) 0x53 else 0x43
    ((ppn << 10) | lowBits).U(64.W)
  }

  val stage2RootLeaf = leafPte(ppn = BigInt(1) << 18, user = true)
  val stage1Level0Table = tablePte(ppn = 0x234)
  val stage2MidLeaf0 = leafPte(ppn = BigInt(2) << 18, user = true)
  val stage1Level1Table = tablePte(ppn = 0x345)

    stage1Level0Table,
    stage2MidLeaf0,
    stage1Level1Table,
    stage2MidLeaf1,
    stage1Level2BadTable
  ))

  val requestPending = RegInit(true.B)
  when (ptw.io.requestor(0).req.fire) {
    requestPending := false.B
  }

  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.valid := requestPending
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.valid := requestPending
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.bits.addr := 0.U
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.bits.need_gpa := false.B
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.bits.vstage1 := true.B
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.bits.stage2 := true.B

  val ptbr = 0.U.asTypeOf(new PTBR)
  ptbr.mode := 0.U
  ptbr.asid := 0.U
  ptbr.ppn := 0.U

  val vsatp = 0.U.asTypeOf(new PTBR)
  vsatp.mode := vsatp.pgLevelsToMode(3).U
  vsatp.asid := 0.U
  vsatp.ppn := 0x80.U

  val hgatp = 0.U.asTypeOf(new PTBR)
  hgatp.mode := hgatp.pgLevelsToMode(3).U
  hgatp.asid := 0.U
  hgatp.ppn := 0.U

  ptw.io.dpath.ptbr := ptbr
  ptw.io.dpath.vsatp := vsatp
  ptw.io.dpath.hgatp := hgatp
  ptw.io.dpath.sfence.valid := false.B
  ptw.io.dpath.sfence.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new SFenceReq)
  ptw.io.dpath.status := 0.U.asTypeOf(new MStatus)
  ptw.io.dpath.hstatus := 0.U.asTypeOf(new HStatus)
  ptw.io.dpath.gstatus := 0.U.asTypeOf(new MStatus)
  ptw.io.dpath.pmp := 0.U.asTypeOf(ptw.io.dpath.pmp)
  ptw.io.dpath.customCSRs := DontCare

  val reqCount = RegInit(0.U(3.W))
  val respDelay1Valid = RegInit(false.B)
  val respDelay2Valid = RegInit(false.B)
  val respDelay1Data = Reg(UInt(64.W))
  val respDelay2Data = Reg(UInt(64.W))

  when (ptw.io.mem.req.fire) {
    assert(reqCount < responseData.length.U, "PTW issued more memory requests than expected")
    respDelay1Valid := true.B
    respDelay1Data := responseData(reqCount)
    reqCount := reqCount + 1.U
  }.otherwise {
    respDelay1Valid := false.B
  }
  respDelay2Valid := respDelay1Valid
  respDelay2Data := respDelay1Data

  ptw.io.mem.req.ready := true.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_nack := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_nack_cause_raw := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_uncached := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_paddr := 0.U
  ptw.io.mem.resp.valid := respDelay2Valid
  ptw.io.mem.resp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new HellaCacheResp)
  ptw.io.mem.resp.bits.data := respDelay2Data
  ptw.io.mem.replay_next := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_xcpt := 0.U.asTypeOf(new HellaCacheExceptions)
  ptw.io.mem.s2_gpa := 0.U
  ptw.io.mem.s2_gpa_is_pte := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.ordered := true.B
  ptw.io.mem.store_pending := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.perf := 0.U.asTypeOf(new HellaCachePerfEvents)
  ptw.io.mem.clock_enabled := true.B

  val done = RegInit(false.B)
  when (ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.valid) {
    printf(p"PTW resp reqCount=${reqCount} gf=${ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.gf} ae_final=${ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.ae_final} gpa_is_pte=${ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.gpa_is_pte}\n")
    assert(reqCount === 6.U, "PTW responded after an unexpected number of memory requests")
    assert(ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.pte.table(), "Final PTW response should contain a valid table PTE")
    assert(ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.gpa_is_pte, "Final PTW response should still be marked as a GPA PTE")
    assert(!ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.gf, "PTW incorrectly raised guest fault on a valid table PTE")
    assert(!ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.ae_final, "PTW incorrectly raised ae_final on a valid table PTE")
    done := true.B
  }

  io.done := done
}

object PTWGuestFaultRepro extends App {
  implicit val p: Parameters = new BaseSubsystemConfig
  simulate(LazyModule(new PTWGuestFaultDUT).module) { dut =>
    dut.reset.poke(true.B)
    dut.clock.step(2)
    dut.reset.poke(false.B)
    dut.clock.stepUntil(dut.io.done, 1, 80)
    dut.io.done.expect(true.B, "timed out waiting for PTW response")
  }
}
EOF
}

problem_statement: Observed behavior: In Rocket's page-table walker (PTW), a hypervisor two-stage translation can incorrectly treat a valid non-leaf PTE (a page-table entry that points to the next page table) as a faulting final result when that entry's guest physical address contains bits above the range allowed by the active `hgatp` mode. In this case the PTW may return guest-page-fault and final access-error indications instead of returning the PTE as a valid table entry. Expected behavior: A valid non-leaf PTE in this situation must be returned as a table/page-pointer PTE, with no guest-page-fault and no final access error. The high-bit check against `hgatp` mode should affect leaf mappings, not table entries. Affected function: Rocket PTW handling of guest-physical-address validity during hypervisor VS-stage plus G-stage address translation. Trigger condition: A VS-stage plus G-stage walk reaches a valid table PTE in the final traversal step, and that PTE encodes guest-physical-address bits above the width permitted by the current `hgatp` mode.

resolved_issues.body:
**Type of issue**: bug report
**Impact**: unknown
**Development Phase**: proposal
**Other information**
The following dut was generated with RV32E, H ext, none FPU, the value in misa also proves this. We happened to find this problem because the next instruction accessed register x16, and since mtvec was not set, the simulation stalled.

```
[rocket] 3 0x00080000000 (0x0480006f)
[spike]   core   0: 0x0000000080000000 (0x0480006f) j       pc + 0x48
[rocket] 3 0x00080000048 (0x301022f3) x 5 0x8000000000941095  -> "XUSMHECA"
[spike]   core   0: 0x0000000080000048 (0x301022f3) csrr    t0, misa
[rocket] 3 0x0008000004c (0x20001073)
[spike]   core   0: 0x000000008000004c (0x20001073) csrw    vsstatus, zero
[rocket] 3 0x00080000050 (0x200022f3) x 5 0x0000000200000000
[spike]   core   0: 0x0000000080000050 (0x200022f3) csrr    t0, vsstatus
...
[rocket] 3 0x0008000008c (0x00000793) x15 0x0000000000000000
[spike]   core   0: 0x000000008000008c (0x00000793) li      a5, 0
```

[rocket-8.zip](https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/files/8691872/rocket-8.zip)


The specification says that the H extension depends on the I set instead of E set, which rocket does not check at generation time:
> The hypervisor extension depends on an “I” base integer ISA with 32 x registers (RV32I or RV64I), not RV32E, which has only 16 x registers.

**Please tell us about your environment:**
    - version: edc8d40

fix_patch:
diff --git a/src/main/scala/rocket/RocketCore.scala b/src/main/scala/rocket/RocketCore.scala
index 90896d37a5e..f7d6836f5a7 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/rocket/RocketCore.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/rocket/RocketCore.scala
@@ -269,6 +269,7 @@ class Rocket(tile: RocketTile)(implicit p: Parameters) extends CoreModule()(p)
 
   require(decodeWidth == 1 /* TODO */ && retireWidth == decodeWidth)
   require(!(coreParams.useRVE && coreParams.fpu.nonEmpty), "Can't select both RVE and floating-point")
+  require(!(coreParams.useRVE && coreParams.useHypervisor), "Can't select both RVE and Hypervisor")
   val id_ctrl = Wire(new IntCtrlSigs()).decode(id_inst(0), decode_table)
   val lgNXRegs = if (coreParams.useRVE) 4 else 5
   val regAddrMask = (1 << lgNXRegs) - 1

problem_statement: Rocket currently allows configuration elaboration to succeed when both the hypervisor extension and RVE are enabled in the same core, including the no-FPU case where no other incompatibility blocks elaboration. This is an invalid ISA combination because the hypervisor extension requires the full base integer register set, while RVE uses the reduced 16-register mode. Expected behavior is that Rocket core ISA/configuration validation rejects any configuration that combines hypervisor support with RVE during elaboration instead of generating the design. The affected area is Rocket core parameter validation at configuration/elaboration time, and the trigger is enabling both hypervisor and RVE for one Rocket core.

...

[rocket] 1 0x000800001c0 (0x00000613) x12 0x0000000000000000
[spike]  core   0: 0x00000000800001c0 (0x00000613) li      a2, 0
[rocket] 3 0x00080000004 (0x34302f73) x30 0x000000000000700b
[spike]  core   0: 0x00000000800001c4 (0x0000700b) custom0.rd.rs1.rs2 (args unknown)
[error] PC SIM 00000000800001c4, DUT 0000000080000004
[error] INSN SIM 0000700b, DUT 34302f73

We believe there is a typo in the rocc_illegal signal, where the `.vs` should be `.xs`:

-        if (usingRoCC) reg_vsstatus.xs := Fill(2, new_vsstatus.xs.orR)

@@ -1484,6 +1483,7 @@ class CSRFile(

+  reg_vsstatus.xs := (if (usingRoCC) UInt(3) else UInt(0))

package hwebench

import chisel3._
import chisel3.stage.ChiselStage

import freechips.rocketchip.config.Parameters
import freechips.rocketchip.diplomacy.LazyModule
import freechips.rocketchip.rocket.{CSR, CSRs, CSRFile, EventSet, EventSets}
import freechips.rocketchip.subsystem.WithHypervisor
import freechips.rocketchip.system.{ExampleRocketSystem, RoccExampleConfig}

object VsstatusXsHarnessParams {
  private val config = new WithHypervisor ++ new RoccExampleConfig
  private val system = LazyModule(new ExampleRocketSystem()(config))
  implicit val params: Parameters = system.rocketTiles.head.p
}

class VsstatusXsHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val writeEnable = Input(Bool())
    val writeData = Input(UInt(p(freechips.rocketchip.tile.XLen).W))
    val xs = Output(UInt(2.W))
  })

  private val dummyEventSets = new EventSets(Seq(
    new EventSet(
      (_: UInt, _: UInt) => false.B,
      Seq("never" -> (() => false.B))
    )
  ))

  val csr = Module(new CSRFile(dummyEventSets))

  csr.io.ungated_clock := clock
  csr.io.interrupts := 0.U.asTypeOf(csr.io.interrupts)
  csr.io.hartid := 0.U
  csr.io.rw.addr := Mux(io.writeEnable, CSRs.vsstatus.U(CSR.ADDRSZ.W), 0.U(CSR.ADDRSZ.W))
  csr.io.rw.cmd := Mux(io.writeEnable, CSR.W, CSR.N)
  csr.io.rw.wdata := io.writeData
  csr.io.decode.foreach(_.inst := 0.U)
  csr.io.exception := false.B
  csr.io.retire := 0.U
  csr.io.cause := 0.U
  csr.io.pc := 0.U
  csr.io.tval := 0.U
  csr.io.htval := 0.U
  csr.io.gva := false.B
  csr.io.fcsr_flags.valid := false.B
  csr.io.fcsr_flags.bits := 0.U
  csr.io.set_fs_dirty.foreach(_ := false.B)
  csr.io.rocc_interrupt := false.B
  csr.io.counters.foreach(_.inc := 0.U)
  csr.io.inst.foreach(_ := 0.U)
  csr.io.vector.foreach { vector =>
    vector.set_vs_dirty := false.B
    vector.set_vconfig.valid := false.B
    vector.set_vconfig.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(vector.set_vconfig.bits)
    vector.set_vstart.valid := false.B
    vector.set_vstart.bits := 0.U
    vector.set_vxsat := false.B
  }

  io.xs := csr.io.gstatus.xs
}

object EmitVsstatusXsHarness extends App {
  val targetDir = if (args.nonEmpty) args(0) else "generated"
  new ChiselStage().emitVerilog(
    new VsstatusXsHarness()(VsstatusXsHarnessParams.params),
    Array("--target-dir", targetDir)
  )
}
EOF

cat > "$CPP_FILE" <<'EOF'
#include "VVsstatusXsHarness.h"
#include "verilated.h"

static void tick(VVsstatusXsHarness& top) {
  top.clock = 0;
  top.eval();
  top.clock = 1;
  top.eval();
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  Verilated::commandArgs(argc, argv);
  VVsstatusXsHarness top;

  top.reset = 1;
  top.io_writeEnable = 0;
  top.io_writeData = 0;
  tick(top);
  tick(top);

  top.reset = 0;
  tick(top);

  top.io_writeEnable = 1;
  top.io_writeData = 0;
  tick(top);

  top.io_writeEnable = 0;
  tick(top);

  top.final();
  return top.io_xs == 3 ? 0 : 1;
}
EOF

run_test() {
  timeout 1100 bash -lc '
    set -euo pipefail
    cd /home/rocket-chip
    sbt -Dsbt.log.noformat=true "runMain hwebench.EmitVsstatusXsHarness '"$GEN_DIR"'" 
    '"$VERILATOR_BIN"' --cc --exe \
      --top-module VsstatusXsHarness \
      -Mdir '"$WORK_DIR"'/obj_dir \
      '"$GEN_DIR"'/VsstatusXsHarness.v \
      '"$CPP_FILE"'
    sed -i "s|^VERILATOR_ROOT = .*|VERILATOR_ROOT = '"$VERILATOR_WRAPPER"'|" '"$WORK_DIR"'/obj_dir/VVsstatusXsHarness.mk
    make -C '"$WORK_DIR"'/obj_dir -f VVsstatusXsHarness.mk -j"${NUM_JOBS:-4}"
    '"$WORK_DIR"'/obj_dir/VVsstatusXsHarness
  ' >"$RUN_LOG" 2>&1
}

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if run_test; then
  echo "TEST: vsstatus_xs_rocc_read_only ... PASS"
  status=0
else
  tail -n 80 "$RUN_LOG" || true
  echo "TEST: vsstatus_xs_rocc_read_only ... FAIL"
  status=1
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$status"
problem_statement: In Rocket Chip's VSSTATUS CSR write handling, software writes can incorrectly change the XS field. XS is the extra/custom-state status field, and in configurations that enable both the hypervisor extension and RoCC/custom coprocessor support it is expected to be read-only and hard-wired to dirty. Instead, writing VSSTATUS, including writing zero, can clear VSSTATUS.XS. Expected behavior: after any VSSTATUS write in a hypervisor-enabled Rocket configuration with RoCC support, XS must still report dirty (`11`) and must not be modified by software.

title: Hypervisor forward progress: prevent ITLB miss fault PTW thrashing DCache
body:
**Related issue**:
> This is a bug in the hypervisor implementation populating `htval2` starting from https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/pull/2841/commits/ebe27d681043f6df9393d9ff816db54cd406330a.
> 
> The core isn’t making forward progress because the ITLB is thrashing (it only has one copy of the GPA register, hence can’t support multiple speculative accesses that each need their own GPAs).  The resulting ITLB misses result in D$ conflict misses, which prevent an older load instruction from making progress.
> 
> The bug can only manifest when executing within a guest.  When not using the hypervisor extension, it can’t occur.
> 
> The RTL fix is to disable speculative ITLB refill unless recent forward progress has been made (perf impact should be imperceptible).
> 
> Andrew was able to demonstrate the bug can occur with both direct-mapped and 2-way associativity.  His test case couldn’t trip the bug on 4-way, which isn’t proof the bug can’t manifest on 4-way, but at minimum, it’s rarer, though.

**Type of change**: bug report

**Impact**: functional fix for forward progress, hopefully minimal-to-no performance degradation

**Development Phase**: implementation quoting both RTL and explanation from @aswaterman 

**Release Notes**
Speculative ITLB misses under Hypervisor thrash in D$, preventing an older load from making forward progress. Fix is to prevent speculative ITLB misses unless recent forward progress has been made.

resolved_issues.body:
This PR implements v0.6.2 of the RISC-V Hypervisor Extension.

The implementation was inspired by José Martins' and colleagues' work
described in [1].  Much of the microarchitecture and essentially all of
the code is new, but their implementation served as our baseline.
We thank them for trailblazing hypervisor support in rocket-chip.

Note that this PR only includes the mechanisms to virtualize the hart
itself.  Virtualized interrupt controllers, IOMMUs, etc. are future work.
Lots of future work.

Note also that some features are (legally) not implemented.  Currently,
misa.H is not writable, something we may or may not choose to fix.
The mtinst and htinst CSRs are hardwired to 0, placing
additional onus on hypervisor software to use the HLVX instruction.

[1] "A First Look at RISC-V Virtualization from an Embedded Systems Perspective", https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14951

problem_statement: Observed behavior: In Rocket's instruction frontend, when the RISC-V hypervisor extension is translating guest instruction fetches, speculative instruction-side TLB (ITLB) misses can keep launching new page-table walker (PTW) requests even after those fetches have started replaying and the core is no longer making forward progress. Expected behavior: Once speculative guest instruction fetches are replaying and there has been no recent forward progress, the frontend should quiesce and stop issuing additional speculative ITLB/PTW requests until progress resumes. Affected function: Rocket frontend handling of speculative instruction-address translation for guest execution, specifically the instruction-side ITLB/PTW path. Trigger condition: The bug appears only during guest execution with hypervisor support enabled, when speculative instruction fetches repeatedly miss in the ITLB and enter replay without intervening forward progress.

package freechips.rocketchip.repro

import Chisel._
import chisel3.testers.{BasicTester, TesterDriver}
import freechips.rocketchip.config.Parameters
import freechips.rocketchip.diplomacy.{AddressSet, LazyModule, LazyModuleImp, ValName}
import freechips.rocketchip.diplomaticobjectmodel.model.{OMDCache, OMICache}
import freechips.rocketchip.rocket._
import freechips.rocketchip.system.DefaultConfig
import freechips.rocketchip.tile.{RocketTileParams, TileKey}
import freechips.rocketchip.tile.{TileVisibilityNodeKey}
import freechips.rocketchip.tilelink.{ReadPattern, TLEdgeOut, TLEphemeralNode, TLRAM, TLPatternPusher}

class TLBBehaviorProbe(cfg: TLBConfig)(implicit p: Parameters) extends LazyModule {
  val pusher = LazyModule(new TLPatternPusher("tlb-behavior-probe", Seq(ReadPattern(0, 0))))
  val visibility = TLEphemeralNode()(ValName("tile_master"))
  val ram = LazyModule(new TLRAM(AddressSet(0x0, 0xffffL), beatBytes = 64))

  ram.node := visibility := pusher.node

  lazy val module = new LazyModuleImp(this) {
    val io = IO(new Bundle {
      val finished = Bool(OUTPUT)
    })
    pusher.module.io.run := Bool(false)
    val ramModule = ram.module

    implicit val edge: TLEdgeOut = visibility.edges.out.head
    implicit val localP: Parameters = p.alterMap(Map(
      TileKey -> RocketTileParams(),
      TileVisibilityNodeKey -> visibility))
    val tlb = Module(new TLB(false, 3, cfg))

    val phase = Reg(init = UInt(0, 4))
    val reqVAddr = Wire(UInt(width = tlb.io.req.bits.vaddr.getWidth))
    val refillVPN = Wire(UInt(width = tlb.io.ptw.resp.bits.pte.ppn.getWidth))
    val ptbr = Wire(new PTBR)
    val status = Wire(new MStatus)
    val resp = Wire(new PTWResp)

    reqVAddr := UInt(0)
    refillVPN := UInt(0)

    ptbr := UInt(0).asTypeOf(new PTBR)
    ptbr.mode := UInt(8)

    status := UInt(0).asTypeOf(new MStatus)
    status.prv := UInt(PRV.S)
    status.dprv := UInt(PRV.S)

    resp := UInt(0).asTypeOf(new PTWResp)
    resp.pte.v := Bool(true)
    resp.pte.r := Bool(true)
    resp.pte.w := Bool(true)
    resp.pte.d := Bool(true)
    resp.pte.a := Bool(true)
    resp.pte.g := Bool(true)
    resp.pte.ppn := refillVPN
    resp.level := UInt(localP(PgLevels) - 1)
    resp.homogeneous := Bool(true)

    tlb.io.req.valid := Bool(false)
    tlb.io.req.bits.vaddr := reqVAddr
    tlb.io.req.bits.passthrough := Bool(false)
    tlb.io.req.bits.size := UInt(0)
    tlb.io.req.bits.cmd := M_XRD
    tlb.io.sfence.valid := Bool(false)
    tlb.io.sfence.bits.rs1 := Bool(false)
    tlb.io.sfence.bits.rs2 := Bool(false)
    tlb.io.sfence.bits.addr := UInt(0)
    tlb.io.sfence.bits.asid := UInt(0)
    tlb.io.ptw.req.ready := Bool(true)
    tlb.io.ptw.resp.valid := Bool(false)
    tlb.io.ptw.resp.bits := resp
    tlb.io.ptw.ptbr := ptbr
    tlb.io.ptw.status := status
    tlb.io.ptw.pmp.foreach(_ := UInt(0).asTypeOf(new PMP))
    tlb.io.ptw.customCSRs.csrs.foreach(_ := UInt(0).asTypeOf(new freechips.rocketchip.tile.CustomCSRIO))
    tlb.io.kill := Bool(false)

    def issue(vpn: Int): Unit = {
      reqVAddr := UInt(BigInt(vpn) << 12)
      tlb.io.req.valid := Bool(true)
    }

    def refill(vpn: Int): Unit = {
      refillVPN := UInt(vpn)
      tlb.io.ptw.resp.valid := Bool(true)
    }

    switch (phase) {
      is (UInt(0)) { issue(0);  when (tlb.io.req.ready) { phase := UInt(1) } }
      is (UInt(1)) { when (tlb.io.ptw.req.fire()) { phase := UInt(2) } }
      is (UInt(2)) { refill(0); phase := UInt(3) }
      is (UInt(3)) { issue(8);  when (tlb.io.req.ready) { phase := UInt(4) } }
      is (UInt(4)) { when (tlb.io.ptw.req.fire()) { phase := UInt(5) } }
      is (UInt(5)) { refill(8); phase := UInt(6) }
      is (UInt(6)) { issue(16); when (tlb.io.req.ready) { phase := UInt(7) } }
      is (UInt(7)) { when (tlb.io.ptw.req.fire()) { phase := UInt(8) } }
      is (UInt(8)) { refill(16); phase := UInt(9) }
      is (UInt(9)) {
        issue(0)
        when (tlb.io.req.ready) {
          phase := Mux(tlb.io.resp.miss, UInt(11), UInt(10))
        }
      }
      is (UInt(10)) {
        issue(8)
        when (tlb.io.req.ready) {
          assert(tlb.io.resp.miss, "TLB retained too many same-set base-page translations")
          phase := UInt(11)
        }
      }
    }

    io.finished := phase === UInt(11)
  }
}

class TLBBehaviorTester(cfg: TLBConfig)(implicit p: Parameters) extends BasicTester {
  val dut = Module(LazyModule(new TLBBehaviorProbe(cfg)).module)
  when (dut.io.finished) {
    stop()
  }
}

object TLBCompatMain extends App {
  val cfg = TLBConfig(nSets = 2, nWays = 8, nSectors = 4, nSuperpageEntries = 2)
  val expectedEntries = cfg.nSets * cfg.nWays

  require(cfg.nWays == 8)

  val icache = OMICache(
    memoryRegions = Nil,
    interrupts = Nil,
    nSets = 64,
    nWays = 4,
    blockSizeBytes = 64,
    dataMemorySizeBytes = 64 * 4 * 64,
    dataECC = None,
    tagECC = None,
    nTLBEntries = expectedEntries,
    nTLBSets = cfg.nSets,
    nTLBWays = cfg.nWays,
    maxTimSize = 0,
    memories = Nil)

  val dcache = OMDCache(
    memoryRegions = Nil,
    interrupts = Nil,
    nSets = 64,
    nWays = 4,
    blockSizeBytes = 64,
    dataMemorySizeBytes = 64 * 4 * 64,
    dataECC = None,
    tagECC = None,
    nTLBEntries = expectedEntries,
    nTLBSets = cfg.nSets,
    nTLBWays = cfg.nWays,
    memories = Nil)

  require(icache.nTLBEntries == expectedEntries)
  require(dcache.nTLBEntries == expectedEntries)

  implicit val p: Parameters = (new DefaultConfig).toInstance
  require(TesterDriver.execute(() => new TLBBehaviorTester(cfg)), "TLB behavior tester failed")
}
EOF

log_file=/home/rocket-chip/tlb_compat_run.log
test_name=tlb-compat-api-and-shape
status=0

if sbt "runMain freechips.rocketchip.repro.TLBCompatMain" 2>&1 | tee "$log_file"; then
  result=PASS
else
  status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  result=FAIL
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
echo "TEST: ${test_name} ... ${result}"
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$status"

problem_statement: Observed behavior: after Rocket Chip added configurable sets and ways for the L1 instruction/data TLBs (translation lookaside buffers), the public Scala API became inconsistent for downstream users. Code that creates `TLBConfig` with a named `nWays` argument no longer compiles, and code that constructs or consumes the instruction/data cache metadata records (`OMICache` and `OMDCache`) with the legacy aggregate `nTLBEntries` field also fails because that field is no longer part of the public model. Expected behavior: configurable L1 TLB support should remain backward-compatible at the Scala API level. Downstream code should be able to configure `TLBConfig` in terms of sets and ways, and `OMICache`/`OMDCache` should continue to provide `nTLBEntries` as the total number of L1 TLB entries, equal to `nTLBSets * nTLBWays`. Affected function: the public Scala interfaces for L1 TLB configuration (`TLBConfig`) and the instruction/data cache metadata records (`OMICache` and `OMDCache`). Trigger condition: any downstream Scala integration that enables configurable L1 TLB sets/ways and then uses `TLBConfig(..., nWays = ...)` or expects `OMICache`/`OMDCache` to include `nTLBEntries`.

  val asyncReset = IO(Input(AsyncReset()))

This breaks the valid-signal synchronization used by `AsyncQueue`/`AsyncCrossing` when the synchronizer's reset type differs from the enclosing module's reset scheme. Expected behavior: `AsyncValidSync` should elaborate successfully in mixed-reset designs so it can be used in `AsyncQueue`/`AsyncCrossing` even when the enclosing scope uses a different reset type, including the verified case of a plain `Bool` parent reset with an `AsyncReset` applied to the synchronizer. Affected function: `AsyncValidSync`, the validity synchronizer used in the asynchronous queue crossing path. Trigger condition: instantiate `AsyncValidSync` under one reset type and drive it with another reset type, especially a plain `Bool` reset in the parent scope combined with an `AsyncReset` on the synchronizer.

problem_statement: In Rocket Chip's JTAG TAP controller, asserting `jtag_reset` does not immediately clear the TDO output state once TDO has already been latched active during a scan shift. After the TAP enters a shift state and starts driving TDO, an asynchronous reset can leave the pin continuing to drive the previously latched value until a later TCK transition. The expected behavior is that `jtag_reset` immediately forces TDO inactive and floating, with no stale output value or output-enable left asserted, without waiting for another JTAG clock edge. The affected logic is the JTAG TAP controller's handling of the TDO output and its output-enable during reset. The trigger condition is asserting asynchronous `jtag_reset` after TDO has become active in a shift operation.

problem_statement: In `TLToAHB`, which translates TileLink requests into AHB transactions, the AHB user field (`hauser`) can become unsynchronized from the rest of the outgoing transaction. When a TileLink A-channel request includes user bits and the AHB side delays acceptance of that request across multiple cycles, such as by inserting wait states, `hauser` can correspond to a different request than the output address (`haddr`) and the other transaction fields. The expected behavior is that every translated AHB transaction keeps its user bits aligned with the same address and control/data fields for the entire transfer, including while the transfer is being held. The affected function is request forwarding in `TLToAHB`, and the trigger condition is sending TileLink requests with A-channel user bits through this bridge while the AHB interface applies backpressure or otherwise stretches a transfer across cycles.

problem_statement: In Rocket Chip's CSR and privilege-state logic, the legality check for return-from-trap instructions can misidentify a normal `mret` (machine-mode trap return) as `dret` (debug-mode return). The observed behavior is that after entering a trap handler, executing `mret` may raise an illegal-instruction exception instead of returning to the saved `mepc`. The expected behavior is that outside debug mode only an actual `dret` should be illegal; `mret` must remain legal and resume execution from `mepc`. The bug is triggered when trap-handling code executes `mret` and the validity check reads stale CSR/address bits from the wrong pipeline stage, causing the instruction to be treated as `dret`.

During verification of the rocket chip against the RISC-V ISA, we found one opcode that the rocket chip accepts (at least in M mode), but that is not documented in the RISC-V ISA (user level or privileged) or the debug spec. Some digging in Scala and here suggests this was added in November 2018 as a "CEASE" instruction.
Should'n this be documented better?
As this is a non-standard opcode, should it not influence the misa register to reflect the presence of an instruction outside the RISC-V spec?

problem_statement: The RISC-V `misa` CSR is supposed to advertise which ISA extensions a hart supports. In Rocket Chip's standard/default configuration, the core implements the non-standard CEASE instruction (opcode `0x30500073`), but the CSR `misa` ISA-extension reporting logic still generates a `misa` value with the `X` bit clear. The affected function is `misa` extension reporting in the CSR logic, and the bug is triggered in the normal standard/default Rocket configuration. The expected behavior is that this configuration sets `misa.X` so the reported ISA matches the implemented instruction set and software can detect that a non-standard extension is present.

This addresses a simulation-pessimism problem.  The synthesis result will be the same either way.  Before, in simulation, the value held in these registers prior to the first write might not have had the appropriate bits zapped, because of random initialization.

resolved_issues.title: Issue with DIV result not being written back to register file
resolved_issues.body:
<!-- THIS REPOSITORY'S ISSUES ARE RESERVED FOR FEATURE REQUESTS AND BUG REPORTS. -->
<!-- For support questions related to Rocket Chip, please use [Stack Overflow [rocket-chip]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/rocket-chip). -->
<!-- For support questions related to Chisel, please use [Stack Overflow [chisel]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/chisel). -->
<!-- Please select the item best describing the issue in each category and delete the other items. -->

<!-- choose all that apply -->
**Type of issue**: bug report

**Other information**
On a Rocket core, I encountered the issue that the although the core accepts the result of the div (div.io_resp_valid & div.io_resp_ready), the data picked for the register file update (rf_wdata) is actually the dmem data. How did the core reach that situation? There is a memory instruction in the writeback state in that cycle that caught a npc_misaligned in the memory stage - so it turns to an exception in WB, allowing the div to write back its result by giving the div.io_resp_ready, but since the npc_misaligned case does not cause the activation of io_dmem_s1_kill, the dcache is free to actually give a response for this memory instruction, in particular, in case of a cache hit, the one that is causing the mux for rf_write to pick the dcache output instead of the div one.
I am attaching a waveform from a Scala-generated RTL. Please ignore the "ILLEGAL" text in the line otherwise showing the instruction - this is a debug signal from out verification environment that currently does not take the full instruction set into account.
Of course, this is on the Rocket level, not a full RocketTile. So can the Frontend deliver a misaligned PC like in this case? In general, it can - I have a configuration where misa is writeable, so take a write to clear the 'c' bit in misa followed by setting bit 1 in tvec followed by an instruction causing an exception. This requests the misaligned PC from tvec at the Frontend which it happily delivers, causing a situation where a non-CFI instruction causes a npc misaligned which is actually a "current PC misaligned".

![npc_misaligned](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45827187/49926841-d1aeca00-febc-11e8-9922-a0b1ffd194d1.png)

class CSRTVecPessimismTop(implicit val p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = new Bundle {

  zeroInterrupts.mtip := Bool(false)
  zeroInterrupts.msip := Bool(false)
  zeroInterrupts.meip := Bool(false)
  zeroInterrupts.lip.foreach(_ := Bool(false))

  }
  if (p(TileKey).beuAddr.isDefined) {
    zeroInterrupts.buserror.foreach(_ := Bool(false))
  }

  csr.io.ungated_clock := clock
  csr.io.interrupts := zeroInterrupts
  csr.io.hartid := UInt(0)
  csr.io.rw.addr := UInt(0)
  csr.io.rw.cmd := CSR.N
  csr.io.rw.wdata := UInt(0)
  csr.io.decode.foreach(_.csr := UInt(0))
  csr.io.exception := Bool(false)
  csr.io.retire := UInt(0)
  csr.io.cause := UInt(0)
  csr.io.pc := UInt(0)
  csr.io.tval := UInt(0)
  csr.io.fcsr_flags.valid := Bool(false)
  csr.io.fcsr_flags.bits := Bits(0, width = FPConstants.FLAGS_SZ)
  csr.io.rocc_interrupt := Bool(false)
  csr.io.inst.foreach(_ := UInt(0))

  val started = Reg(init = Bool(false))
  when (!started) {
    started := Bool(true)
  }
  when (started) {
    csr.io.exception := Bool(true)
    assert(csr.io.evec(1, 0) === UInt(0), "tvec must be aligned even before the first CSR write")
  }

  case MaxHartIdBits => 1
  case TileKey => RocketTileParams(

      blockBytes = site(CacheBlockBytes))),
    icache = Some(ICacheParams(
      rowBits = site(SystemBusKey).beatBits,
      blockBytes = site(CacheBlockBytes))))
})

class CSRTVecPessimismConfig extends Config(new WithCSRTVecPessimism ++ new BaseSubsystemConfig)

object CSRTVecPessimismEmitter {
  def main(args: Array[String]): Unit = {
    require(args.length == 1, "usage: CSRTVecPessimismEmitter <target-dir>")
    val base = (new CSRTVecPessimismConfig).toInstance
    implicit val p: Parameters = base.alterPartial {

        manager = TLManagerPortParameters(

#include "VCSRTVecPessimismTop.h"
#include "verilated.h"
#include <cstdlib>

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  Verilated::commandArgs(argc, argv);
  int seed = argc > 1 ? std::atoi(argv[1]) : 1;
  Verilated::randSeed(seed);
  Verilated::randReset(2);

  VCSRTVecPessimismTop top;
  top.reset = 1;
  top.clock = 0;

    top.eval();
    top.clock = 1;
    top.eval();

  return Verilated::gotFinish() ? 1 : 0;
}

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in Rocket's CSRFile trap-vector handling, the trap-vector CSR that provides the exception entry address can retain random low bits in simulation before software has written it for the first time. If an exception is taken in that state, the generated trap entry address (`evec`/`tvec`) can be misaligned. Expected behavior: trap-vector alignment must still be enforced when forming the trap entry address, even before the first CSR write, so an early exception always sees an aligned entry address. Affected function: the CSRFile logic that reads the trap-vector CSR and generates the trap entry address. Trigger condition: simulation with randomized or otherwise unspecified initial CSR state, followed by an exception before software initializes the trap-vector CSR.

title: A better HintHandler
body:
**Type of change**: enhancement
**Impact**: API modification
**Development Phase**: implementation

**Release Notes**
The old HintHandler was buggy because it reordered responses despite claiming that it would not. It was also grossly inefficient due to the use of Arbiters and Queues. This new HintHandler transforms Hints into empty PutPartials or Gets, avoiding the need to recombine the response stream. It can be placed between a device and it's Fragmenter as a very cheap stateless adapter, or higher up the tree like the old HintHandler, in which case it will use flops to hold the address steady.

This is a rebased version of #1654.

repo.name: rocket-chip
repo.description: Rocket Chip Generator

commits.message: tilelink: enhance trivial arbiters to reduce to nothing
HintHandler: rewrite for simpler hardware
HintHandler: add support for Get translation as well

TLToAHB: add direct support for Hints

As AHB does not support PutPartial and often connects to devices
which have side effects on Gets, the HintHandler cannot provide
Hint support for AHB slaves. Therefore, support Hints directly.
ToAHB: cut a_valid from d_valid for improved QoR

Revert "Revert "Merge pull request #1650 from freechipsproject/error-devices""

This reverts commit 9a30c4ba067c442cedcdac38b4399a21efa6ef2e.

resolved_issues.title: Refactor DevNullDevices and provide some within TLBusWrappers
resolved_issues.body:
DevNullDevices don't obey standard memory operation semantics. They may discard writes, refuse to respond to requests, issue error responses, or otherwise violate 'expected' memory behavior. The existing DevNullDevice subclasses were TLError and TLDeadlock, TLZero has now been refactored to extend it as well.

I also add the capability to add some such devices directly into the `PeripheryBus` and `MemoryBus` clock domain wrappers. Further wrappers may have similar devices added to them in future PRs.

resolved_issues.title: Better HintHandler
resolved_issues.body:
**Type of change**: enhancement
**Impact**: functional change
**Development Phase**:  implementation

**Release Notes**
The old HintHandler was buggy because it reordered responses despite claiming that it would not. It was also grossly inefficient due to the use of Arbiters and Queues. This new HintHandler transforms Hints into empty PutPartials, avoiding the need to recombine the response stream. It can be placed between a device and it's Fragmenter as a very cheap stateless adapter, or higher up the tree like the old HintHandler, in which case it will use flops to hold the address steady.

+// See LICENSE.SiFive for license details.
+
+package freechips.rocketchip.devices.tilelink
+
+import freechips.rocketchip.config.Parameters
+import freechips.rocketchip.diplomacy._
+import freechips.rocketchip.tilelink._
+
+case class DevNullParams(
+  address: Seq[AddressSet],
+  maxAtomic: Int,
+  maxTransfer: Int,
+  region: RegionType.T = RegionType.UNCACHEABLE,
+  executable: Boolean = true,
+  mayDenyGet: Boolean = true,
+  mayDenyPut: Boolean = true,
+) {
+  require (1 <= maxAtomic, s"Atomic transfer size must be > 1 (was $maxAtomic)")
+  require (maxAtomic <= maxTransfer, s"Atomic transfer size must be <= max transfer (but $maxAtomic > $maxTransfer)")
+  require (maxTransfer <= 4096, s"Max transfer size must be <= 4096 (was $maxTransfer)")
+  def acquire: Boolean = region == RegionType.TRACKED
+}
+
+/** DevNullDevices don't obey standard memory operation semantics.
+  * They may discard writes, refuse to respond to requests, issue error responses,
+  * or otherwise violate 'expected' memory behavior.
+  */
+abstract class DevNullDevice(params: DevNullParams, beatBytes: Int, device: SimpleDevice)
+                            (implicit p: Parameters)
+    extends LazyModule with HasClockDomainCrossing {
+  val xfer = TransferSizes(1, params.maxTransfer)
+  val atom = TransferSizes(1, params.maxAtomic)
+  val node = TLManagerNode(Seq(TLManagerPortParameters(
+    Seq(TLManagerParameters(
+      address            = params.address,
+      resources          = device.reg("mem"),
+      regionType         = params.region,
+      executable         = params.executable,
+      supportsAcquireT   = if (params.acquire) xfer else TransferSizes.none,
+      supportsAcquireB   = if (params.acquire) xfer else TransferSizes.none,
+      supportsGet        = xfer,
+      supportsPutPartial = xfer,
+      supportsPutFull    = xfer,
+      supportsArithmetic = atom,
+      supportsLogical    = atom,
+      supportsHint       = xfer,
+      fifoId             = Some(0), // requests are handled in order
+      mayDenyGet         = params.mayDenyGet,
+      mayDenyPut         = params.mayDenyPut,
+      alwaysGrantsT      = params.acquire)),
+    beatBytes  = beatBytes,
+    endSinkId  = if (params.acquire) 1 else 0,
+    minLatency = 1))) // no bypass needed for this device
+  val tl_xing = this.crossIn(node)
+}

problem_statement: Rocket Chip exposes several TileLink "dev-null" peripherals for endpoints that intentionally do not behave like normal memory, such as returning errors, never responding, or always returning zero data. At the base commit, their public Scala elaboration API is inconsistent enough to break downstream code at compile time: the package does not provide `DevNullParams`, the deadlock device is not exposed as `TLDeadlock`, and `TLZero` still requires explicit resource arguments instead of being constructible from just an address. The expected behavior is that elaboration code can treat these TileLink dev-null endpoints as one coherent public API: `TLError` and `TLDeadlock` should be instantiable from shared dev-null parameters, and `TLZero` should be instantiable as a simple zero-returning endpoint without extra resource plumbing. The affected API is the constructor and parameterization surface for TileLink dev-null devices during Scala compilation and elaboration. The bug is triggered when Scala code imports these dev-null peripherals and tries to elaborate error, deadlock, and zero-returning endpoints together.

problem_statement: Rocket Chip's generated Verilog `AsyncResetReg` module does not reliably hold its output low when reset is already asserted at startup. `AsyncResetReg` is the asynchronously reset register blackbox used in Rocket Chip RTL, and when `rst` starts high, especially with randomized register initialization enabled, its output `q` can come up as `X` or a randomized bit even though reset is still asserted. The expected behavior is specific: `q` must remain `0` for the entire time `rst` is high, and after `rst` is deasserted the module should resume normal operation and capture `d` on the next enabled rising clock edge. The bug is triggered by starting the design with `rst` asserted during initialization.

problem_statement: Observed behavior: when a Rocket Chip configuration places the periphery bus (pbus) in its own clock domain, a system-bus (sbus) access to the BootROM can stall indefinitely if the pbus clock is not advancing. In the verified case, the system is still running on sbus, but BootROM reads do not complete once pbus is asynchronously crossed and its clock is held low. Expected behavior: separating periphery I/O onto a differently clocked pbus must not make the BootROM unreachable from sbus; an sbus access to the BootROM should still complete even when the pbus clock is stopped. Affected function: subsystem bus attachment for the BootROM and the control-peripheral path when pbus uses a separate clock domain. Trigger condition: configure pbus with an asynchronous or otherwise independent clock crossing, then access the BootROM from sbus while the pbus clock is halted or not advancing.

import freechips.rocketchip.diplomacy.LazyModule

class TLMMIOExampleSystem(implicit p: Parameters) extends RocketCoreplex
    with HasAsyncExtInterrupts
    with HasMasterAXI4MemPort
    with HasMasterTLMMIOPort
    with HasSlaveAXI4Port
    with HasPeripheryBootROM
    with HasSystemErrorSlave {
  override lazy val module = new TLMMIOExampleSystemModule(this)
}

class TLMMIOExampleSystemModule[+L <: TLMMIOExampleSystem](_outer: L) extends RocketCoreplexModule(_outer)
    with HasRTCModuleImp
    with HasExtInterruptsModuleImp
    with HasMasterAXI4MemPortModuleImp
    with HasMasterTLMMIOPortModuleImp
    with HasSlaveAXI4PortModuleImp
    with HasPeripheryBootROMModuleImp
    with DontTouch

class TLMMIOTieoffHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = new Bundle {
    val success = Bool(OUTPUT)
  }

  val dut = Module(LazyModule(new TLMMIOExampleSystem).module)
  dut.reset := reset | dut.debug.ndreset

  dut.dontTouchPorts()
  dut.tieOffInterrupts()
  dut.connectSimAXIMem()
  dut.tieOffTLMMIO()
  dut.tieOffAXI4SlavePort()
  dut.connectDebug(clock, reset, io.success)
}

object EmitTLMMIOTieoffHarness extends App {
  require(args.size == 1, "usage: EmitTLMMIOTieoffHarness <target-dir>")
  implicit val p: Parameters = Parameters.root((new TinyConfig).toInstance)
  val targetDir = new File(args(0))
  if (!targetDir.exists()) targetDir.mkdirs()
  val circuit = chisel3.Driver.elaborate(() => new TLMMIOTieoffHarness)
  chisel3.Driver.dumpFirrtl(circuit, Some(new File(targetDir, "TLMMIOTieoffHarness.fir")))
}

rm -rf riscv-tools torture .git/modules/riscv-tools .git/modules/torture

SBT_FLAGS=(
  -Dsbt.log.noformat=true
  -Dsbt.override.build.repos=true
  -Dsbt.repository.config="${REPO_FILE}"
  -no-colors
)

ensure_firrtl_local() {
  if [[ -f "${LOCAL_FIRRTL_JAR}" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi

  (
    cd /home/rocket-chip/firrtl || exit 1
    timeout 1100 sbt "${SBT_FLAGS[@]}" publishLocal >"${FIRRTL_LOG}" 2>&1
  )
}

run_probe() {
  rm -rf "${RUN_DIR}"
  mkdir -p "${RUN_DIR}"
  ROCKETCHIP_ADDONS=".hwe-tlmmio/addon" \
    timeout 1100 sbt "${SBT_FLAGS[@]}" \
    "runMain hwebench.EmitTLMMIOTieoffHarness ${RUN_DIR}" >"${RUN_LOG}" 2>&1
}

extract_module_slice() {
  [[ -f "${FIR_FILE}" ]] || return 1
  awk '
    /^  module TLMMIOExampleSystem :/ { inmod = 1 }
    /^  (module|extmodule) / && inmod && $0 !~ /^  module TLMMIOExampleSystem :/ { exit }
    inmod { print }
  ' "${FIR_FILE}" >"${MODULE_FIR}"
}

port_is_internally_wired() {
  extract_module_slice || return 1
  grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]+mmio_tl\.0( <-|\.)' "${MODULE_FIR}"
}

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if ensure_firrtl_local && run_probe && port_is_internally_wired; then
  echo "TEST: tl_mmio_port_internal_wiring ... PASS"
  status=0
else
  tail -n 120 "${FIRRTL_LOG}" 2>/dev/null || true
  tail -n 120 "${RUN_LOG}" 2>/dev/null || true
  if [[ -f "${MODULE_FIR}" ]]; then
    grep -n "mmio_tl" "${MODULE_FIR}" | sed -n '1,40p' || true
  elif [[ -f "${FIR_FILE}" ]]; then
    grep -n "mmio_tl" "${FIR_FILE}" | sed -n '1,40p' || true
  fi
  echo "TEST: tl_mmio_port_internal_wiring ... FAIL"
  status=1
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "${status}"

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in Rocket system tops that expose a TileLink MMIO port with `HasMasterTLMMIOPort`, the generated top-level `mmio_tl` IO can elaborate without being wired to the actual internal MMIO bus. The exported TL MMIO port is therefore unusable, and tie-off logic operates on a disconnected port instead of the real MMIO connection. Expected behavior: when `HasMasterTLMMIOPort` is mixed into a RocketCoreplex-based top, the exported `mmio_tl` interface should be internally connected to the system MMIO bus so that tying off the port or attaching external MMIO-facing logic acts on the real bus connection. Affected function: the Rocket coreplex/system-top plumbing that exposes the external TL MMIO port, specifically `HasMasterTLMMIOPortModuleImp`. Trigger condition: elaborating any RocketCoreplex-based configuration that mixes in `HasMasterTLMMIOPort`, including minimal tops that only export the TL MMIO port and then apply TL MMIO tie-off logic.

title: generate local interrupts on bus/ecc errors

repo.name: rocket-chip
repo.description: Rocket Chip Generator

commits.message: Expose BusErrorUnit non-diplomatically for use as local interrupt

Make BusErrorUnit support 32-bit stores

Otherwise it isn't too useful for RV32!

Generate local interrupt #128 on bus errors

It doesn't have a correpsonding bit in mip/mie, so it isn't individually
maskable, nor is it delegable.
Provide separate masks for local & global BusErrorUnit interrupts
Invalidate TL error bit in D$ once progress is made

Don't permit vectoring of high interrupts

Send them to the base of the vector to obviate an adder

resolved_issues.title: Optionally support AHB buses at top level

problem_statement: The BusErrorUnit, which provides memory-mapped status for reporting bus or ECC faults, does not elaborate correctly when Rocket Chip is configured for RV32. In an XLen=32 configuration that instantiates a BusErrorUnit, elaboration fails while building the BusErrorUnit register map because the register fields placed at one register word exceed the 32-bit word limit, so the design cannot be generated. The affected functionality is the BusErrorUnit register interface. Expected behavior is that instantiating a BusErrorUnit should elaborate successfully on both RV64 and RV32, with its register map remaining valid for a 32-bit tile.

title: csr: allow for superscalar decode
body:
* CSR provides a decode port to check for an illegal instruction.
   * This commit now allows for multiple instructions in decode to get this
      illegal instruction information.
   * This commit leverages the existing decodeWidth parameter. This will
      potentially over-provision the number of decode ports needed for
      RVC-enabled cores.

Closes #1068

repo.name: rocket-chip
repo.description: Rocket Chip Generator

commits.message:
csr: allow for superscalar decode

   * CSR provides a decode port to check for an illegal instruction.
   * This commit now allows for multiple instructions in decode to get this
      illegal instruction information.
   * This commit leverages the existing decodeWidth parameter. This will
      potentially over-provision the number of decode ports needed for
      RVC-enabled cores.

resolved_issues.title: CSRFile does not support superscalar decode.
resolved_issues.body:
The CSRFile informs the pipeline of any illegal instructions by providing a `decode` interface (bits go in, illegal info goes out, can't explain that).

However, only a single decode port is provided, making it not possible to use the current rocket-chip CSRFile for superscalar processors.

https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/2786e42d994c504c1e54810187121ddad604882f/src/main/scala/rocket/CSR.scala#L174-L182

I'm not sure of the best way to tackle this. One easy solution is to make `decode` a Vec.

Is there a better way to provide a "function" that can be called against the CSRFile that provides a bit vector/tuple of illegal signals?

fix_patch:
diff --git a/src/main/scala/rocket/CSR.scala b/src/main/scala/rocket/CSR.scala
index ab136f9580b..86ede45be1c 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/rocket/CSR.scala

problem_statement: In Rocket's CSRFile, the control/status register block's `decode` interface is used to report whether a decoded instruction is illegal. When a core is configured for superscalar decode with `decodeWidth` greater than 1, `CSRFile.decode` still exposes only a single decode port. As a result, the decode stage cannot obtain separate illegal-instruction results for each instruction being decoded in parallel. The expected behavior is for `CSRFile.decode` to provide one decode port per decode slot, matching `decodeWidth`, so superscalar configurations can check each decoded instruction independently.

package hwebench

import Chisel._
import chisel3.testers.{BasicTester, TesterDriver}
import config._
import junctions._
import junctions.HastiConstants._

class HastiSingleSlaveReadyTester extends BasicTester {
  implicit val p: Parameters = Parameters.root(new Config((site, here, up) => {
    case HastiId => "repro"
    case HastiKey("repro") => HastiParameters(dataBits = 32, addrBits = 32)
  }))

  val dut = Module(new HastiXbar(2, Seq((_: UInt) => Bool(true))))

  private def driveMaster(m: HastiMasterIO, addr: Int): Unit = {
    m.htrans := HTRANS_NONSEQ
    m.hmastlock := Bool(false)
    m.haddr := UInt(addr, width = 32)
    m.hwrite := Bool(false)
    m.hburst := HBURST_SINGLE
    m.hsize := UInt(2, width = SZ_HSIZE)
    m.hprot := HPROT_DATA
    m.hwdata := Bits(0, width = 32)
  }

  driveMaster(dut.io.masters(1), 0x4)

  dut.io.slaves(0).hresp := HRESP_OKAY
  dut.io.slaves(0).hready := Bool(true)

    assert(!dut.io.masters(1).hready, "Ungranted master must stall behind the selected master")

  }

problem_statement: In `HastiXbar`, which arbitrates Hasti bus requests from multiple masters to slaves, the `hready` response can be propagated to a master that was not granted the single available slave. When two or more masters contend for one slave and that slave is ready, an ungranted master may also see `hready` asserted and advance as if its request had been accepted. The expected behavior is that in an N-masters-to-1-slave configuration, only the currently granted master should observe the slave's `hready` signal, and any other contending master must remain stalled until it is granted access.

resolved_issues.title: RoCCs not being built
resolved_issues.body:
Currently, RoCCs specified via the `coreplex/Configs.scala` are not actually built. This originates from a few missing changes in #550. Symptomatically, this results in the `msatus.xs` bits being unsettable, `misa` not including the 'X' bit, and (resultingly) all XCustom instructions tripping illegal instruction exceptions.

BaseTile's `usingRoCC` variable depends on `tileParams.rocc` existing, but `coreplex/Configs.scala` is only defining the old parameter `BuildRoCC`. See: 
  * https://github.com/ucb-bar/rocket-chip/blob/master/src/main/scala/coreplex/Configs.scala#L157
  * https://github.com/ucb-bar/rocket-chip/blob/master/src/main/scala/tile/BaseTile.scala#L31

The rough structure for the config should be the following:
```scala
class WithRoccExample extends Config((site, here, up) => {
  case RocketTilesKey => up(RocketTilesKey, site) map { r =>
    r.copy(rocc = Seq(
      RoCCParams(
        opcodes = OpcodeSet.custom0,
        generator = (p: Parameters) => Module(new AccumulatorExample()(p))),
      RoCCParams(
        opcodes = OpcodeSet.custom1,
        generator = (p: Parameters) => Module(new TranslatorExample()(p)),
        nPTWPorts = 1),
      RoCCParams(
        opcodes = OpcodeSet.custom2,
        generator = (p: Parameters) => Module(new CharacterCountExample()(p)))))
  }
  case RoccMaxTaggedMemXacts => 1
})
```

However, this results in an unbalanced TL input/output configuration due to the three RoCCs:
```
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: requirement failed: LegacyRoccComplex.TLOutputNode has 3 inputs and 1 outputs; they must match (LegacyRoCC.scala:29:25)
```

This does generate Verilog for a single RoCC (with `usingRoCC` defined and `misa` including the 'X' bit), but FIRRTL errors out:
```
firrtl.passes.CheckGenders$WrongGender:  @[LegacyRoCC.scala 69:22:rocketchip.RoccExampleConfig.fir@139016.4]: [module RocketTile]  Expression fpuOpt.io.cp_resp is used as a FEMALE but can only be used as a MALE.
firrtl.passes.CheckGenders$WrongGender:  @[LegacyRoCC.scala 69:22:rocketchip.RoccExampleConfig.fir@139016.4]: [module RocketTile]  Expression l1tol2_LegacyRoccComplex.io.fpu.cp_resp is used as a MALE but can only be used as a FEMALE.
```

This FIRRTL connection issue can be fixed with changing the connection polarity as seen in #559.

A spot check of running a single accumulator RoCC against [`rocket-rocc-examples`](../../../seldridge/rocket-rocc-examples) does pass the accumulator tests.
