problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's backend MemBlock, an atomic memory exception can stop being reported on the LSQ (load/store queue) exception-address output before the saved exception address is consumed. This means logic that reads the address several cycles later can miss the atomic exception address even though the exception is still pending. Expected behavior: once an atomic exception is raised, MemBlock should keep that exception address visible on the LSQ exception-address output across later cycles, so a consumer that samples it several cycles after the flush still sees the same address; the latched atomic exception should only be cleared when the later redirect/flush handling for that exception takes effect. Affected function: MemBlock logic that latches and forwards atomic exception addresses to the LSQ exception-address interface. Trigger condition: an atomic memory operation raises an exception, and the exception address is consumed several cycles later instead of immediately.

title: mem: reduce refill to use latency
body:
This commit updates lq entry flag carefully in load_s3 to avoid extra
refill delay. It removes the extra refill delay introduced by #1375
without harming memblock timing.

In #1375, we delayed load refill when dcache miss queue entry fails
to accept a miss. It exchanged performance for better timing.

repo.name: XiangShan
repo.description: Open-source high-performance RISC-V processor

commits.message:
mem: optimize missq reject to lq timing

DCache replay request is quite slow to generate, as it need to compare
load address with address in all valid miss queue entries.

Now we delay the usage of replay request from data cache.
Now replay request will not influence normal execuation flow until
load_s3 (1 cycle after load_s2, load result writeback to RS).

It is worth mentioning that "select refilling inst for load
writeback" will be disabled if dcacheRequireReplay in the
last cycle.
dcache: compare probe block addr instead of full addr

mem: do not replay from RS when ldld vio or fwd failed

ld-ld violation or forward failure will let an normal load inst replay
from fetch. If TLB hit and ld-ld violation / forward failure happens,
we write back that inst immediately. Meanwhile, such insts will not be
replayed from rs.

It should fix "mem: optimize missq reject to lq timing"
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master' into timing-memblock-211203
mem: fix replay from rs condition

}

  local path="$1"
  if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then

    git -C "$path" config --local --add url.https://github.com/.insteadOf git://github.com/ || true
    git -C "$path" config --local --add url.https://github.com/.insteadOf git@github.com: || true
    git -C "$path" submodule sync --recursive || true
    git -C "$path" submodule update --init --recursive || true
  fi
}

cd /home/xiangshan

git checkout d97210581eb11c608638db8c84b033f1cda64650

configure_git_urls

git submodule update --init --recursive || true

repair_torture_env rocket-chip/torture

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's load pipeline, a load that is rejected by the DCache miss queue/MSHR is marked for replay from the reservation station (RS). If a matching refill, meaning the returning cache-line data for that miss, arrives before the replay is reissued, the slow replay feedback still reports the load as needing replay, which adds an unnecessary extra refill-to-use delay. Expected behavior: when a refill for the same load address arrives in that window, the load should be treated as satisfied by the refill and the slow replay feedback should report it as a hit instead of forcing another replay. Affected function: LoadUnit slow replay feedback for miss-queue reject cases in the memory subsystem. Trigger condition: a load issues, the DCache cannot accept its miss request, and a refill for the same load address arrives before the replayed load is sent again.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan
source /etc/xiangshan_tools_path.sh 2>/dev/null || true
export JAVA_HOME="${JAVA_HOME:-/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64}"
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export MILL_VERSION="${MILL_VERSION:-0.9.8}"

mkdir -p src/test/scala/xiangshan
cat > src/test/scala/xiangshan/Wb2CtrlLoadDelaySpec.scala <<'EOF'
package xiangshan

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import chipsalliance.rocketchip.config.Parameters
import freechips.rocketchip.diplomacy.{LazyModule, LazyModuleImp}
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers
import top.BaseConfig
import xiangshan.backend.exu.Wb2Ctrl

class Wb2CtrlLoadDelayWrapper(implicit p: Parameters) extends LazyModule {
  val inner = LazyModule(new Wb2Ctrl(Seq(LdExeUnitCfg)))

  lazy val module = new LazyModuleImp(this) {
    val io = IO(new Bundle {
      val inValid = Input(Bool())
      val outValid = Output(Bool())
    })

    inner.module.io.redirect.valid := false.B
    inner.module.io.redirect.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new Redirect)
    inner.module.io.in(0).valid := io.inValid
    inner.module.io.in(0).ready := true.B
    inner.module.io.in(0).bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new ExuOutput)
    inner.module.io.elements.get("delayedLoadError").foreach { data =>
      data.asInstanceOf[Vec[Bool]].foreach(_ := false.B)
    }

    io.outValid := inner.module.io.out(0).valid
  }
}

class Wb2CtrlLoadDelaySpec extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "Wb2Ctrl load writeback timing"

  it should "delay load writeback by one cycle" in {
    implicit val p: Parameters = new BaseConfig(1).alterPartial {
      case XSCoreParamsKey => XSCoreParameters(HartId = 0)
    }
    test(LazyModule(new Wb2CtrlLoadDelayWrapper).module) { dut =>
      dut.io.inValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.clock.step()
      dut.io.outValid.expect(false.B)

      dut.io.inValid.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.outValid.expect(false.B)
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.outValid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.inValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.clock.step()
      dut.io.outValid.expect(false.B)
    }
  }
}
EOF

if timeout 1200s env MILL_VERSION="$MILL_VERSION" /usr/local/bin/mill --no-server \

else

fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$status"

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in the Nanhu load/store unit (LSU), after the data-cache ECC/error check was moved one cycle later for timing, a load could still be reported as written back in the original cycle. This means load completion can be signaled before the final result of the delayed error check is available. Expected behavior: any load on this repipelined data-cache path must write back to the reorder buffer (ROB) one cycle later, so completion is reported only after the delayed ECC/error stage, even when the load ultimately has no error. Affected function: the LSU/data-cache load writeback timing path to ROB writeback. Trigger condition: loads that use the data-cache path after ECC/error checking has been repipelined to occur one cycle after the data SRAM read.

title: rob: fix commitInstr performance counters
body:
This commit fixes the wrong update values of commitInstr in ROB.
Previously we add a RegNext to trueCommitCnt in #1644. However,
we don't add RegNext to the ifCommit condition. This makes the
commitInstr larger than the normal value and IPC looks better.

This commit fixes this bug and the IPC numbers should be correct now.

commits.message:
rob: fix commitInstr performance counters

This commit fixes the wrong update values of commitInstr in ROB.
Previously we add a RegNext to trueCommitCnt in #1644. However,
we don't add RegNext to the ifCommit condition. This makes the
commitInstr larger than the normal value and IPC looks better.

This commit fixes this bug and the IPC numbers should be correct now.

problem_statement: The backend reorder buffer (ROB) uses the `commitInstr` performance counter to report how many instructions retire. After the timing optimization introduced in #1644, this accounting can overcount retirements: during a single-instruction commit sequence, `commitInstr` may increment twice even though only one instruction actually commits, which makes IPC appear higher than it is. Expected behavior: each committed instruction must contribute exactly one to `commitInstr`, so a one-instruction commit sequence produces a `commitInstr` increment of one and IPC matches the true retirement rate. Affected function: ROB retirement performance accounting, specifically `commitInstr`. Trigger condition: this occurs when the ROB's commit accounting uses commit-count information and the commit-valid decision from different cycles after the #1644 timing change, causing the same retirement sequence to be charged again.

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's load unit, a load that should be reissued from the fetch side (`replay_from_fetch`) can lose that replay state when its load-queue entry is updated on a miss-path cycle. In the verified scenario, the load reaches the data-cache response stage, sees a data-cache miss together with an invalid forwarding match, and should stay marked as replay-from-fetch rather than taking a normal completion path. Expected behavior: once the load pipeline decides that a load must replay from fetch, the load-queue update for that instruction must preserve that replay state even on the miss path. After the miss-plus-invalid-forwarding case, the following stage must still report replay-from-fetch, and the load must not be emitted as a normal completed load. Affected function: replay-from-fetch handling in the load unit / load-queue update path. Trigger condition: a load reaches the data-cache response path and encounters the verified replay-from-fetch case of a data-cache miss combined with an invalid forwarding match.

repo.name: XiangShan
repo.description: Open-source high-performance RISC-V processor

commits.message:
ldu: optimize dcache hitvec wiring

In previous design, hitvec is generated in load s1, then send to dcache
and lsu (rs) side separately. As dcache and lsu (rs side) is far in real
chip, it caused severe wiring problem.

Now we generate 2 hitvec in parallel:

* hitvec 1 is generated near dcache.
To generate that signal, paddr from dtlb is sent to dcache in load_s1
to geerate hitvec. The hitvec is then sent to dcache to generate
data array read_way_en.

* hitvec 2 is generated near lsu and rs in load_s2, tag read result
from dcache, as well as coh_state, is sent to lsu in load_s1,
then it is used to calcuate hitvec in load_s2.  hitvec 2 is used
to generate hit/miss signal used by lsu.

It should fix the wiring problem caused by hitvec

ldu: opt loadViolationQuery.resp.ready timing

An extra release addr register is added near lsu to speed up the
generation of loadViolationQuery.resp.ready

l1tlb: replace NormalPage data module and add duplicate resp result

data module:
add BankedSyncDataMoudleWithDup data module:
divided the data array into banks and read as Async, bypass write data.
RegNext the data result * #banks. choose from the chosen data.

duplicate:
duplicate the chosen data and return to outside(tlb).
tlb return (ppn+perm) * #DUP to outside (for load unit only)

TODO: load unit use different tlb resp result to different module.
one for lsq, one for dcache.

l1tlb: Fix wrong vidx_bypass logic after using duplicate data module

We use BankedSyncDataMoudleWithDup instead of SyncDataModuleTemplate,
whose write ports are not Vec.

#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan

TEST_NAME="loadunit_fast_wakeup_on_miss"
SCALA_DIR="/home/xiangshan/src/test/scala/hwebench"
SCALA_FILE="${SCALA_DIR}/LoadUnitFastWakeupMain.scala"
CPP_FILE="/home/xiangshan/tmp_LoadUnitFastWakeup_main.cpp"

write_reproducer_sources() {
  mkdir -p "${SCALA_DIR}"

  cat > "${SCALA_FILE}" <<'EOF'
package hwebench

import chipsalliance.rocketchip.config.Parameters
import chisel3._
import chisel3.stage.ChiselStage
import top.MinimalConfig
import xiangshan._
import xiangshan.mem.LoadUnit

class LoadUnitFastWakeupHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val fastWakeupSeen = Output(Bool())
    val missSeen = Output(Bool())
  })

  val dut = Module(new LoadUnit)
  val cycle = RegInit(0.U(4.W))
  cycle := cycle + 1.U

  def zeroOf[T <: Data](target: T): T = 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(target))

  def setUIntLike(target: Data, value: UInt): Unit = target match {
    case field: UInt => field := value
    case vec: Vec[_] => vec.foreach(_.asInstanceOf[UInt] := value)
    case other => throw new IllegalArgumentException(s"unsupported UInt-like target: ${other.getClass}")
  }

  def setBoolLike(target: Data, value: Bool): Unit = target match {
    case field: Bool => field := value
    case vec: Vec[_] => vec.foreach(_.asInstanceOf[Bool] := value)
    case other => throw new IllegalArgumentException(s"unsupported Bool-like target: ${other.getClass}")
  }

  def recordField(target: Data, name: String): Option[Data] = target match {
    case record: Record => record.elements.get(name)
    case _ => None
  }

  val loadIn = WireInit(zeroOf(dut.io.ldin.bits))
  loadIn.src(0) := "h8000_0000".U
  loadIn.uop.ctrl.fuOpType := LSUOpType.ld
  loadIn.uop.ctrl.imm := 0.U
  loadIn.uop.cf.pc := "h1000".U

  dut.io.ldin.valid := cycle === 0.U
  dut.io.ldin.bits := loadIn
  dut.io.ldout.ready := true.B

  dut.io.redirect.valid := false.B
  dut.io.redirect.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.redirect.bits)
  dut.io.rsIdx := 0.U
  dut.io.isFirstIssue := true.B

  dut.io.fastpathIn := zeroOf(dut.io.fastpathIn)
  dut.io.loadFastMatch := false.B
  dut.io.loadFastImm := 0.U

  dut.io.tlb.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.tlb.resp.valid := cycle === 1.U
  dut.io.tlb.resp.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.tlb.resp.bits)
  recordField(dut.io.tlb.resp.bits, "paddr").foreach(setUIntLike(_, "h8000_0000".U))

  dut.io.pmp := zeroOf(dut.io.pmp)

  dut.io.dcache.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.dcache.resp.valid := cycle === 2.U
  dut.io.dcache.resp.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.dcache.resp.bits)
  dut.io.dcache.resp.bits.miss := true.B
  dut.io.dcache.resp.bits.replay := false.B
  dut.io.dcache.resp.bits.tag_error := false.B

  val dcacheIo = dut.io.dcache.asInstanceOf[Record]
  dcacheIo.elements.get("s1_hit_way").foreach(setUIntLike(_, 1.U))
  dcacheIo.elements.get("debug_s1_hit_way").foreach(setUIntLike(_, 1.U))
  dcacheIo.elements.get("s2_hit").foreach(setBoolLike(_, false.B))
  dcacheIo.elements.get("s1_disable_fast_wakeup").foreach(setBoolLike(_, false.B))
  dcacheIo.elements.get("s1_bank_conflict").foreach(setBoolLike(_, false.B))

  dut.io.sbuffer.forwardMaskFast.foreach(_ := false.B)
  dut.io.sbuffer.forwardMask.foreach(_ := false.B)
  dut.io.sbuffer.forwardData.foreach(_ := 0.U)
  dut.io.sbuffer.dataInvalid := false.B
  dut.io.sbuffer.matchInvalid := false.B

  dut.io.lsq.forward.forwardMaskFast.foreach(_ := false.B)
  dut.io.lsq.forward.forwardMask.foreach(_ := false.B)
  dut.io.lsq.forward.forwardData.foreach(_ := 0.U)
  dut.io.lsq.forward.dataInvalidFast := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.forward.dataInvalid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.forward.matchInvalid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.forward.dataInvalidSqIdx := 0.U

  dut.io.lsq.loadViolationQuery.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.lsq.loadViolationQuery.resp.valid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.loadViolationQuery.resp.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.loadViolationQuery.resp.bits)

  dut.io.lsq.ldout.valid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.ldout.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.ldout.bits)

  dut.io.lsq.trigger.lqLoadAddrTriggerHitVec.foreach(_ := false.B)

  dut.io.refill.valid := false.B
  dut.io.refill.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.refill.bits)

  dut.io.csrCtrl := zeroOf(dut.io.csrCtrl)

  dut.io.trigger.foreach { trigger =>
    trigger.tdata2 := 0.U
    trigger.matchType := 0.U
    trigger.tEnable := false.B
  }

  io.fastWakeupSeen := dut.io.fastUop.valid
  io.missSeen := dut.io.dcache.resp.valid && dut.io.dcache.resp.bits.miss

  when (cycle === 2.U && dut.io.dcache.resp.valid) {
    assert(!dut.io.fastUop.valid, "fast wakeup must stay low when the dcache response is a miss")
  }

  when (cycle === 5.U) {
    stop()
  }
}

object LoadUnitFastWakeupMain extends App {
  val targetDir = if (args.nonEmpty) args(0) else "build/hwe-loadunit-fastwakeup"
  val baseConfig = new MinimalConfig(1)
  val standaloneConfig = baseConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => baseConfig(XSTileKey).head
  }
  (new ChiselStage).emitVerilog(
    gen = new LoadUnitFastWakeupHarness()(standaloneConfig),
    args = Array("--target-dir", targetDir)
  )
}
EOF

  cat > "${CPP_FILE}" <<'EOF'

#include "verilated.h"

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  Verilated::commandArgs(argc, argv);
  VLoadUnitFastWakeupHarness top;

  for (int cycle = 0; cycle < 12 && !Verilated::gotFinish(); ++cycle) {
    top.reset = cycle < 2;
    top.clock = 0;
    top.eval();
    top.clock = 1;
    top.eval();
  }

  top.final();
  return Verilated::gotFinish() ? 0 : 1;
}
EOF
}

run_reproducer() {
  write_reproducer_sources

  rm -rf "${BUILD_DIR}" "${OBJ_DIR}"

  export JAVA_HOME="${JAVA_HOME:-/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64}"
  export PATH="${JAVA_HOME}/bin:/tools/bin:/tools/mill/bin:${PATH}"
  if [ -f /home/xiangshan/.mill-version ]; then
    export MILL_VERSION="$(tr -d ' \t\r\n' < /home/xiangshan/.mill-version)"
  else
    export MILL_VERSION="0.9.8"
  fi
  if [ -x /usr/local/bin/install-mill-version ]; then
    /usr/local/bin/install-mill-version "${MILL_VERSION}" >/dev/null
  fi

  /usr/local/bin/mill -i XiangShan.test.runMain hwebench.LoadUnitFastWakeupMain "${BUILD_DIR}" &&
    VERILATOR_ROOT="/tools/v4.210/share/verilator" \
    VERILATOR_BIN="../../bin/verilator_bin" \
    /tools/v4.210/bin/verilator --assert --cc "${BUILD_DIR}/${TOP_NAME}.v" \
      --exe "${CPP_FILE}" --build &&
    "${OBJ_DIR}/V${TOP_NAME}"
}

if run_reproducer; then
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit 0
else

  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit 1
fi
problem_statement: In XiangShan, the load/store unit (LSU) generates a fast wakeup signal to let dependent instructions proceed early when a load hits in the data cache (DCache). The bug is that this fast wakeup decision can follow an earlier cache hit indication instead of the LSU-visible DCache hit result for the same load. Under the trigger condition where a load sees an early hit-way or tag-match indication but the later DCache result is actually a miss, the LSU may still assert fast wakeup. The affected function is the LoadUnit fast-wakeup generation for DCache loads. The expected behavior is specific: fast wakeup must only be asserted for a confirmed DCache hit, and it must remain low whenever the DCache result is a miss.

package xiangshan.mem.mdp

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import chipsalliance.rocketchip.config.Parameters
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec

class LFSTHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(Flipped(new DispatchLFSTIO))

  dut.io.dispatch <> io

  dut.io.redirect.valid := false.B

class LFSTRegressionTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "LFST"

  private val baseConfig = new MinimalConfig()
  implicit val p: Parameters = baseConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => baseConfig(XSTileKey).head
  }
  private val renameWidth = p(XSCoreParamsKey).RenameWidth

  require(renameWidth >= 2, s"LFST regression test requires RenameWidth >= 2, got $renameWidth")

  private def clearReqs(dut: LFSTHarness): Unit = {
    for (slot <- 0 until renameWidth) {
      dut.io.req(slot).valid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.req(slot).bits.isstore.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.req(slot).bits.ssid.poke(0.U)
      dut.io.req(slot).bits.robIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.req(slot).bits.robIdx.value.poke(0.U)
    }
  }

  private def pokeReq(
    dut: LFSTHarness,
    slot: Int,
    isStore: Boolean,
    ssid: Int,
    robValue: Int,
    robFlag: Boolean = false
  ): Unit = {
    dut.io.req(slot).valid.poke(true.B)
    dut.io.req(slot).bits.isstore.poke(isStore.B)
    dut.io.req(slot).bits.ssid.poke(ssid.U)
    dut.io.req(slot).bits.robIdx.flag.poke(robFlag.B)
    dut.io.req(slot).bits.robIdx.value.poke(robValue.U)
  }

  private def expectRobIdx(dut: LFSTHarness, slot: Int, robValue: Int, robFlag: Boolean = false): Unit = {
    dut.io.resp(slot).bits.robIdx.flag.expect(robFlag.B)
    dut.io.resp(slot).bits.robIdx.value.expect(robValue.U)

      dut.io.resp(0).bits.shouldWait.expect(false.B)
      dut.io.resp(1).valid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.resp(1).bits.shouldWait.expect(true.B)

problem_statement: Observed behavior: In XiangShan's memory dependence predictor (MDP), the LFST/StoreSet logic uses a StoreSet ID (SSID) to remember the reorder-buffer (ROB) index of the older store that a load should wait for. When multiple instructions are dispatched together, this lookup can return the wrong ROB index. A load that follows an older store with the same SSID in the same dispatch bundle can be predicted as waiting on its own ROB entry, and if multiple stores are dispatched together, a later load can receive the ROB index from the wrong store. Expected behavior: for a load that matches an older store by SSID, the LFST response must indicate that the load should wait and must return the ROB index of that matching older store, never the load's own ROB index or the ROB index of an unrelated store. Affected function: the LFST/StoreSet logic in XiangShan's MDP. Trigger condition: dispatching multiple instructions in one group, especially a same-SSID store and load in the same bundle or multiple stores followed by a load that queries one of their SSIDs.

problem_statement: Observed behavior: In XiangShan's CtrlBlock, a frontend instruction can still enter decode during the brief window after a flush-after redirect has been raised but is still pending. If that wrong-path instruction is a `vset*` instruction, it incorrectly updates the vector configuration state used by later vector instructions, so the next correct-path vector instruction is dispatched with the wrong `vconfig`. Expected behavior: Once a flush-after redirect is pending, wrong-path frontend instructions must not reach decode. In particular, a wrong-path `vset*` must not update `vconfig`, and the following correct-path vector instruction must see the pre-redirect vector configuration. Affected function: CtrlBlock handling of frontend `cfVec` inputs while a redirect is pending. Trigger condition: A flush-after redirect, such as a memory-violation redirect, is raised; then a wrong-path `vset*` arrives before the redirect fully takes effect; then a correct-path vector instruction is decoded.

        zeroData(dut.io.fromBpu.resp.bits)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.valid.poke(false.B)
        zeroData(dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.valid.poke(false.B)
        zeroData(dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits.foreach { c =>
          c.valid.poke(false.B)
          zeroData(c.bits)
        }
        dut.io.toIfu.req.ready.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.toICache.req.ready.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.toPrefetch.req.ready.poke(false.B)
        zeroData(dut.io.mmioCommitRead.mmioFtqPtr)
      }

      def enqueueEntry(ftqIdx: Int, pc: UInt, taken: Boolean, target: UInt): Unit = {
        dut.io.fromBpu.resp.valid.poke(true.B)
        for (stage <- Seq(dut.io.fromBpu.resp.bits.s1, dut.io.fromBpu.resp.bits.s3)) {
          stage.valid.poke(true.B)
          stage.pc.poke(pc)
          stage.ftq_idx.flag.poke(false.B)
          stage.ftq_idx.value.poke(ftqIdx.U)
          stage.full_pred.hit.poke(taken.B)
          if (taken) {
            stage.full_pred.slot_valids.last.poke(true.B)
            stage.full_pred.offsets.last.poke(lastOffset)
            stage.full_pred.targets.last.poke(target)
            stage.full_pred.is_jal.poke(true.B)
          }
        }
      }

      def redirectEntry(ftqIdx: Int): Unit = {
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.ftqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.ftqIdx.value.poke(ftqIdx.U)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.ftqOffset.poke(lastOffset)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.level.poke(RedirectLevel.flushAfter)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.cfiUpdate.taken.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.cfiUpdate.target.poke("h3000".U)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.cfiUpdate.isMisPred.poke(true.B)
      }

      def writeBackTakenEntry1(): Unit = {
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.ftqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.ftqIdx.value.poke(1.U)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.pc(lastIndex).poke(entry1Pc)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.pd(lastIndex).valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.pd(lastIndex).isRVC.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.pd(lastIndex).brType.poke(BrType.jal)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.instrRange(lastIndex).poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.cfiOffset.valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.cfiOffset.bits.poke(lastOffset)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.target.poke(entry1Target)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.jalTarget.poke(entry1Target)
      }

      def commitTakenEntry1(): Unit = {
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).bits.ftqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).bits.ftqIdx.value.poke(1.U)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).bits.ftqOffset.poke(lastOffset)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).bits.commitType.poke(0.U)
      }

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      enqueueEntry(0, entry0Pc, taken = false, target = 0.U)
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      redirectEntry(0)
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      enqueueEntry(1, entry1Pc, taken = true, target = entry1Target)
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      writeBackTakenEntry1()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      commitTakenEntry1()
      dut.clock.step()

      var sawUpdate = false
      for (_ <- 0 until 6) {
        clearInputs()
        sawUpdate ||= dut.io.toBpu.update.valid.peek().litToBoolean
        dut.clock.step()
      }

      sawUpdate shouldBe true
    }
  }
}
EOF

problem_statement: The frontend FTQ (fetch target queue) tracks fetched instruction blocks and emits branch predictor (BPU) updates when a taken branch or jump entry commits. After redirect recovery, an older FTQ entry can end up with no surviving instructions, yet it still blocks the FTQ commit pointer. In that state, a younger FTQ entry behind it can write back and commit a taken branch or jump, but the expected branch predictor update is never emitted. The affected logic is the FTQ commit-state and commit-pointer handling during redirect recovery. The bug is triggered when a redirect empties an older FTQ entry and a later FTQ entry then commits a taken control-flow instruction. Expected behavior: an FTQ entry that becomes empty after redirect recovery must not block commit progress, so the following valid taken entry can commit normally and generate its branch predictor update.

+  val victim_vec = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(nSets)(0.U(width.W))))
+
+  // replace to search
+  def replace(set: UInt) = {
+    when(victim_vec(set) =/= Fill(width, 1.U)) {
+      victim_vec(set) := victim_vec(set) + 1.U
+    }
+  }

+}
+
+class WayConflictUpdIO (implicit p: Parameters) extends WayConflictPredictorBundle {
+  val en = Input(Bool())
+  val vaddr = Input(UInt(VAddrBits.W))
+  val dm_hit = Input(Bool())
+  val sa_hit = Input(Bool())
+}
+
+class WayConflictPredictor (nPorts: Int) (implicit p: Parameters) extends WayConflictPredictorModule{
+  val io = IO(new Bundle() {
+    val pred = Vec(nPorts, new WayConflictPredIO)
+    val update = Vec(nPorts, new WayConflictUpdIO)
+  })
+  val PredTable = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(WCPSize)(0.U(CounterSize.W))))
+
+  for (i <- 0 until nPorts){
+    io.pred(i).way_conflict := io.pred(i).en & PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.pred(i).vaddr))(CounterSize-1)
+    // saturation counter
+    when(io.update(i).en && io.update(i).sa_hit) {
+      when(PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) === Fill(CounterSize, 1.U)) {
+        PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr))
+      }.otherwise {
+        PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) + 1.U
+      }
+    }.elsewhen(io.update(i).en && io.update(i).dm_hit) {
+      when(PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) === Fill(CounterSize, 0.U)) {
+        PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr))
+      }.otherwise {
+        PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) - 1.U
+      }
+    }.otherwise {
+      PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr))
+    }
+  }
+
+}

+package xiangshan.cache.wpu
+
+import chipsalliance.rocketchip.config.{Field, Parameters}

+import chisel3.util._
+import utils.XSPerfAccumulate
+import xiangshan.cache.{HasL1CacheParameters, L1CacheParameters}
+import xiangshan.{XSBundle, XSModule}
+
+/*
+// TODO: need to learn the specific grammar
+abstract class WPUBaseModule[T <: Data](implicit P: Parameters) extends XSModule with HasWPUParameters{
+  def apply[T <: Data]
+  def pred(vaddr: UInt, en: Bool) : T
+  def update(vaddr: UInt, data: T ,en: Bool)
+}
+*/
+
+case object WPUParamsKey extends Field[WPUParameters]
+case class WPUParameters
+(
+  enWPU: Boolean = true,
+  algoName: String = "mru",
+  enCfPred: Boolean = false,
+  isICache: Boolean = false,
+  // how to impelement a extend inlcude hasL1Cache and L2 Cache
+)
+
+trait HasWPUParameters extends HasL1CacheParameters{
+  def AlgoWPUMap(wpuParam: WPUParameters, nPorts: Int): BaseWPU = {
+    wpuParam.algoName.toLowerCase match {
+      case "mru" => Module(new MruWPU(wpuParam, nPorts))
+      case "mmru" => Module(new MmruWPU(wpuParam, nPorts))
+      case "utag" => Module(new UtagWPU(wpuParam, nPorts))
+      case t => throw new IllegalArgumentException(s"unknown WPU Algorithm $t")
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+abstract class BaseWPUBundle(implicit P: Parameters) extends XSBundle
+abstract class WPUModule(implicit P: Parameters) extends XSModule with HasWPUParameters
+
+class BaseWpuUpdateBundle(nWays: Int)(implicit p: Parameters) extends BaseWPUBundle{
+  val en = Bool()
+  val vaddr = UInt(VAddrBits.W)
+  val way_en = UInt(nWays.W)
+}
+
+class LookupWpuUpdateBundle(nWays: Int)(implicit p: Parameters) extends BaseWpuUpdateBundle(nWays){
+  val pred_way_en = UInt(nWays.W)
+}
+
+class BaseWpuPredictIO(nWays: Int)(implicit p: Parameters) extends BaseWPUBundle{
+  val en = Input(Bool())
+  val vaddr = Input(UInt(VAddrBits.W))
+  val way_en = Output(UInt(nWays.W))
+}
+
+class WPUBaseIO(portNum: Int, nWays: Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends BaseWPUBundle {
+  val predVec = Vec(portNum, new BaseWpuPredictIO(nWays))
+  val updLookup = Input(Vec(portNum, new LookupWpuUpdateBundle(nWays)))
+  val updReplaycarry = Input(Vec(portNum, new BaseWpuUpdateBundle(nWays)))
+  val updTagwrite = Input(Vec(portNum, new BaseWpuUpdateBundle(nWays)))
+}
+
+abstract class BaseWPU(wpuParam: WPUParameters, nPorts: Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends WPUModule {
+  val cacheParams: L1CacheParameters = if (wpuParam.isICache) icacheParameters else dcacheParameters
+
+  val setSize = nSets
+  val nTagIdx = nWays
+  // auxiliary 1 bit is used to judge whether cache miss
+  val auxWayBits = wayBits + 1
+  val TagIdxBits = log2Up(nTagIdx)
+  val utagBits = 8
+
+  val io = IO(new WPUBaseIO(nPorts, nWays))
+
+  def get_wpu_idx(addr: UInt): UInt = {
+    addr(untagBits - 1, blockOffBits)
+  }
+}
+
+class MruWPU(wpuParam: WPUParameters, nPorts: Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends BaseWPU(wpuParam, nPorts){
+  println("  WpuType: MruWPU")
+  val predict_regs = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(setSize)(0.U(wayBits.W))))
+
+  def write(upd: BaseWpuUpdateBundle): Unit = {
+    when(upd.en) {
+      val upd_setIdx = get_wpu_idx(upd.vaddr)
+      predict_regs(upd_setIdx) := OHToUInt(upd.way_en)
+    }
+  }
+
+  def predict(pred: BaseWpuPredictIO): Unit = {
+    val predSetIdx = get_wpu_idx(pred.vaddr)
+    when(pred.en) {
+      pred.way_en := UIntToOH(predict_regs(predSetIdx))
+    }.otherwise {
+      pred.way_en := 0.U(nWays.W)
+    }
+  }
+
+  for(i <- 0 until nPorts){
+    predict(io.predVec(i))
+    write(io.updLookup(i))
+    write(io.updReplaycarry(i))
+    write(io.updTagwrite(i))
+  }
+
+}
+
+class MmruWPU(wpuParam: WPUParameters, nPorts: Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends BaseWPU(wpuParam, nPorts){
+  println("  WpuType: MmruWPU")
+  val predict_regs = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(setSize)(VecInit(Seq.fill(nTagIdx)(0.U(auxWayBits.W))))))
+
+  def write(upd: BaseWpuUpdateBundle): Unit = {
+    when(upd.en) {
+      val updSetIdx = get_wpu_idx(upd.vaddr)
+      val updTagIdx = get_vir_tag(upd.vaddr)
+      predict_regs(updSetIdx)(updTagIdx) := OHToUInt(upd.way_en)
+    }
+  }
+
+  def predict(pred: BaseWpuPredictIO): Unit = {
+    val predSetIdx = get_wpu_idx(pred.vaddr)
+    val predTagIdx = get_vir_tag(pred.vaddr)
+    when(pred.en) {
+      //UIntToOH(8.U(4.W))=100000000.U(16.W)=00000000.U(8.W)
+      //UIntToOH(8.U(4.W), 8)=00000001.U(8.W)
+      pred.way_en := UIntToOH(predict_regs(predSetIdx)(predTagIdx))
+    }.otherwise {
+      pred.way_en := 0.U(nWays.W)
+    }
+  }
+
+  for(i <- 0 until nPorts){
+    predict(io.predVec(i))
+    write(io.updLookup(i))
+    write(io.updReplaycarry(i))
+    write(io.updTagwrite(i))
+  }
+
+}
+
+class UtagWPU(wpuParam: WPUParameters, nPorts: Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends BaseWPU(wpuParam, nPorts){
+  println("  WpuType: UtagWPU")
+  val utag_regs = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(setSize)(VecInit(Seq.fill(nWays)(0.U(utagBits.W))))))
+  val valid_regs = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(setSize)(VecInit(Seq.fill(nWays)(false.B)))))
+
+  def get_hash_utag(addr: UInt): UInt = {
+    val utagQuotient = vtagBits / utagBits
+    val utagRemainder = vtagBits % utagBits
+    val vtag = get_vir_tag(addr)
+
+    /* old */
+    vtag(utagBits * 2 - 1, utagBits) ^ vtag(utagBits - 1, 0)
+    
+    /* new */
+    // val tmp = vtag(utagQuotient * utagBits - 1, 0).asTypeOf(Vec(utagQuotient, UInt(utagBits.W)))
+    // val res1 = tmp.reduce(_ ^ _)
+    // val res2 = Wire(UInt(utagRemainder.W))
+    // if(utagRemainder!=0){
+    //   res2 := res1(utagRemainder - 1, 0) ^ vtag(vtagBits - 1, utagBits * utagQuotient)
+    //   Cat(res1(utagBits - 1, utagRemainder), res2)
+    // }else{
+    //   res1
+    // }
+  }
+
+  def write_utag(upd: BaseWpuUpdateBundle): Unit = {
+    when(upd.en){
+      val upd_setIdx = get_wpu_idx(upd.vaddr)
+      val upd_utag = get_hash_utag(upd.vaddr)
+      val upd_way = OHToUInt(upd.way_en)
+      utag_regs(upd_setIdx)(upd_way) := upd_utag
+      valid_regs(upd_setIdx)(upd_way) := true.B
+    }
+  }
+
+  def unvalid_utag(upd: LookupWpuUpdateBundle): Unit = {
+    when(upd.en){
+      val upd_setIdx = get_wpu_idx(upd.vaddr)
+      val upd_way = OHToUInt(upd.pred_way_en)
+      valid_regs(upd_setIdx)(upd_way) := false.B
+    }
+  }
+
+  def predict(pred: BaseWpuPredictIO): Unit = {
+    val req_setIdx = get_wpu_idx(pred.vaddr)
+    val req_utag = get_hash_utag(pred.vaddr)
+    val pred_way_en = Wire(UInt(nWays.W))
+    when(pred.en) {
+      pred_way_en := VecInit((0 until nWays).map(i =>
+        req_utag === utag_regs(req_setIdx)(i) && valid_regs(req_setIdx)(i)
+      )).asUInt
+    }.otherwise {
+      pred_way_en := 0.U(nWays.W)
+    }
+    // avoid hash conflict
+    pred.way_en := UIntToOH(OHToUInt(pred_way_en))
+  }
+
+  val hash_conflict = Wire(Vec(nPorts, Bool()))
+  for(i <- 0 until nPorts){
+    predict(io.predVec(i))
+    val real_way_en = io.updLookup(i).way_en
+    val pred_way_en = io.updLookup(i).pred_way_en
+    val pred_miss = io.updLookup(i).en && !pred_way_en.orR
+    val real_miss = io.updLookup(i).en && !real_way_en.orR
+    val way_match = io.updLookup(i).en && pred_way_en === real_way_en
+
+    hash_conflict(i) := !pred_miss && !way_match
+      // look up: vtag miss but tag hit
+    when(pred_miss && !real_miss) {
+      write_utag(io.updLookup(i))
+    }
+    // look up: vtag hit but other tag hit ==> unvalid pred way; write real way
+    when(!pred_miss && !way_match) {
+      unvalid_utag(io.updLookup(i))
+    }
+    when(!pred_miss && !real_miss && !way_match) {
+      write_utag(io.updLookup(i))
+    }
+    // replay carry
+    write_utag(io.updReplaycarry(i))
+    // tag write
+    write_utag(io.updTagwrite(i))
+  }
+
+  XSPerfAccumulate("utag_hash_conflict", PopCount(hash_conflict))
+}

+package xiangshan.cache.wpu
+
+import chipsalliance.rocketchip.config.Parameters
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+import utils.XSPerfAccumulate
+import xiangshan._
+import xiangshan.cache.{DCacheModule, HasDCacheParameters}
+import xiangshan.frontend.icache.HasICacheParameters
+
+class ReplayCarry(nWays: Int)(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSBundle {
+  val real_way_en = UInt(nWays.W)
+  val valid = Bool()
+}
+
+object ReplayCarry{
+  def apply(nWays: Int, rwe: UInt = 0.U, v: Bool = false.B)(implicit p: Parameters): ReplayCarry = {
+    val rcry = Wire(new ReplayCarry(nWays))
+    rcry.real_way_en := rwe
+    rcry.valid := v
+    rcry
+  }
+
+  def init(nWays: Int)(implicit p: Parameters): ReplayCarry = {
+    val rcry = Wire(new ReplayCarry(nWays))
+    rcry.real_way_en := 0.U
+    rcry.valid := false.B
+    rcry
+  }
+}
+
+class WPUBaseReq(implicit p: Parameters) extends BaseWPUBundle{
+  val vaddr = UInt(VAddrBits.W)
+}
+
+class WPUReplayedReq(nWays: Int)(implicit p: Parameters) extends WPUBaseReq {
+  val replayCarry = new ReplayCarry(nWays)
+}
+
+class WPUResp(nWays:Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends BaseWPUBundle{
+  val s0_pred_way_en = UInt(nWays.W)
+}
+
+class WPUUpdate(nWays:Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends BaseWPUBundle{
+  val vaddr = UInt(VAddrBits.W)
+  val s1_real_way_en = UInt(nWays.W)
+}
+
+class WPUUpdateLookup(nWays:Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends WPUUpdate(nWays){
+  val s1_pred_way_en = UInt(nWays.W)
+}
+
+class ConflictPredictIO(nWays:Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends BaseWPUBundle{
+  // pred
+  val s0_vaddr = Input(UInt(VAddrBits.W))
+  // update
+  val s1_vaddr = Input(UInt(VAddrBits.W))
+  val s1_dm_hit = Input(Bool())
+}
+
+class IwpuBaseIO(nWays:Int, nPorts: Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends BaseWPUBundle{
+  val req = Vec(nPorts, Flipped(Decoupled(new WPUBaseReq)))
+  val resp = Vec(nPorts, ValidIO(new WPUResp(nWays)))
+  val lookup_upd = Vec(nPorts, Flipped(ValidIO(new WPUUpdateLookup(nWays))))
+}
+
+class IwpuIO(nWays:Int, nPorts: Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends IwpuBaseIO(nWays, nPorts){
+  val tagwrite_upd = Flipped(ValidIO(new WPUUpdate(nWays)))
+}
+
+class DwpuBaseIO(nWays:Int, nPorts: Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends BaseWPUBundle{
+  val req = Vec(nPorts, Flipped(Decoupled(new WPUReplayedReq(nWays))))
+  val resp = Vec(nPorts, ValidIO(new WPUResp(nWays)))
+  val lookup_upd = Vec(nPorts, Flipped(ValidIO(new WPUUpdateLookup(nWays))))
+  val cfpred = Vec(nPorts, new ConflictPredictIO(nWays))
+}
+
+class DwpuIO(nWays:Int, nPorts:Int)(implicit p:Parameters) extends DwpuBaseIO(nWays, nPorts){
+  val tagwrite_upd = Flipped(ValidIO(new WPUUpdate(nWays)))
+}
+
+class DCacheWpuWrapper (nPorts: Int = 1) (implicit p:Parameters) extends DCacheModule with HasWPUParameters  {
+  val wpu = AlgoWPUMap(dwpuParam, nPorts)
+  val wayConflictPredictor = Module(new WayConflictPredictor(nPorts))
+  val io = IO(new DwpuIO(nWays, nPorts))
+
+  /** pred */
+  val s0_dmSel = Wire(Vec(nPorts, Bool()))
+  val s0_pred_way_conflict = Wire(Vec(nPorts, Bool()))
+  val s0_pred_way_en = Wire(Vec(nPorts, UInt(nWays.W)))
+  val s1_lookup_valid = Wire(Vec(nPorts, Bool()))
+  val s1_dmSel = Wire(Vec(nPorts, Bool()))
+  val s1_pred_way_en = Wire(Vec(nPorts, UInt(nWays.W)))
+  val s1_pred_fail = Wire(Vec(nPorts, Bool()))
+  val s1_hit = Wire(Vec(nPorts, Bool()))
+
+  for(i <- 0 until nPorts){
+    wayConflictPredictor.io.pred(i).en := io.req(i).valid
+    wayConflictPredictor.io.pred(i).vaddr := io.cfpred(i).s0_vaddr
+    s0_pred_way_conflict(i) := wayConflictPredictor.io.pred(i).way_conflict
+
+    s0_dmSel(i) := false.B
+    wpu.io.predVec(i).en := io.req(i).valid
+    wpu.io.predVec(i).vaddr := io.req(i).bits.vaddr
+    when(io.req(i).bits.replayCarry.valid) {
+      // replay carry
+      s0_pred_way_en(i) := io.req(i).bits.replayCarry.real_way_en
+    }.otherwise {
+      // way prediction
+      s0_pred_way_en(i) := wpu.io.predVec(i).way_en
+
+      if (dwpuParam.enCfPred) {
+        // selective direct mapping
+        when(!s0_pred_way_conflict(i)) {
+          s0_pred_way_en(i) := UIntToOH(get_direct_map_way(io.req(i).bits.vaddr))
+          s0_dmSel(i) := true.B
+        }
+      }
+    }
+
+    /** check and update in s1 */
+    s1_lookup_valid(i) := io.lookup_upd(i).valid
+    s1_dmSel(i) := RegNext(s0_dmSel(i))
+    s1_pred_way_en(i) := io.lookup_upd(i).bits.s1_pred_way_en
+    s1_pred_fail(i) := io.lookup_upd(i).valid && s1_pred_way_en(i) =/= io.lookup_upd(i).bits.s1_real_way_en
+    s1_hit(i) := !s1_pred_fail(i) && s1_pred_way_en(i).orR
+
+    val s0_replay_upd = Wire(new BaseWpuUpdateBundle(nWays))
+    s0_replay_upd.en := io.req(i).valid && io.req(i).bits.replayCarry.valid
+    s0_replay_upd.vaddr := io.req(i).bits.vaddr
+    s0_replay_upd.way_en := io.req(i).bits.replayCarry.real_way_en
+    val s1_replay_upd = RegNext(s0_replay_upd)
+
+    wayConflictPredictor.io.update(i).en := io.lookup_upd(i).valid
+    wayConflictPredictor.io.update(i).vaddr := io.cfpred(i).s1_vaddr
+    wayConflictPredictor.io.update(i).dm_hit := s1_dmSel(i) && io.cfpred(i).s1_dm_hit
+    wayConflictPredictor.io.update(i).sa_hit := !s1_dmSel(i) && s1_hit(i)
+
+    // look up res
+    wpu.io.updLookup(i).en := io.lookup_upd(i).valid
+    wpu.io.updLookup(i).vaddr := io.lookup_upd(i).bits.vaddr
+    wpu.io.updLookup(i).way_en := io.lookup_upd(i).bits.s1_real_way_en
+    wpu.io.updLookup(i).pred_way_en := io.lookup_upd(i).bits.s1_pred_way_en
+
+    // which will update in look up pred fail
+    wpu.io.updReplaycarry(i) := s1_replay_upd
+
+    // replace / tag write
+    wpu.io.updTagwrite(i) := DontCare
+
+    /** predict and response in s0 */
+    io.req(i).ready := true.B
+    if (dwpuParam.enWPU) {
+      io.resp(i).valid := io.req(i).valid
+    } else {
+      io.resp(i).valid := false.B
+    }
+    io.resp(i).bits.s0_pred_way_en := s0_pred_way_en(i)
+    assert(PopCount(io.resp(i).bits.s0_pred_way_en) <= 1.U, "tag should not match with more than 1 way")
+  }
+  wpu.io.updTagwrite(0).en := io.tagwrite_upd.valid
+  wpu.io.updTagwrite(0).vaddr := io.tagwrite_upd.bits.vaddr
+  wpu.io.updTagwrite(0).way_en := io.tagwrite_upd.bits.s1_real_way_en
+
+  // PerfLog
+  // pred situation
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_total", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && s1_lookup_valid(i))))
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_succ", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && s1_lookup_valid(i) && !s1_pred_fail(i))))
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_fail", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && s1_lookup_valid(i) && s1_pred_fail(i))))
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_miss", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && s1_lookup_valid(i) && !s1_pred_way_en(i).orR)))
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_real_miss", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && s1_lookup_valid(i) && !io.lookup_upd(i).bits.s1_real_way_en.orR)))
+  // pred component
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_replayCarry", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => io.req(i).valid && io.req(i).bits.replayCarry.valid)))
+  if(!dwpuParam.enCfPred){
+    XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_wayPrediction", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => io.req(i).valid && !io.req(i).bits.replayCarry.valid)))
+  }else{
+    XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_wayPrediction", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => io.req(i).valid && !io.req(i).bits.replayCarry.valid && s0_pred_way_conflict(i))))
+    XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_directMap", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => io.req(i).valid && !io.req(i).bits.replayCarry.valid && !s0_pred_way_conflict(i))))
+    // dm situation
+    XSPerfAccumulate("direct_map_all", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => io.lookup_upd(i).valid)))
+    XSPerfAccumulate("direct_map_ok", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map(i => io.lookup_upd(i).valid && io.cfpred(i).s1_dm_hit)))
+  }
+}
+
+
+class ICacheWpuWrapper (nPorts: Int) (implicit p:Parameters) extends WPUModule with HasICacheParameters {
+  val wpu = AlgoWPUMap(iwpuParam, nPorts)
+  val io = IO(new IwpuIO(nWays, nPorts))
+
+  val s1_pred_fail = Wire(Vec(nPorts, Bool()))
+  val s0_pred_way_en = Wire(Vec(nPorts, UInt(nWays.W)))
+  val s1_pred_way_en = Wire(Vec(nPorts, UInt(nWays.W)))
+  val s1_real_way_en = Wire(Vec(nPorts, UInt(nWays.W)))
+  /** pred in s0*/
+  for (i <- 0 until nPorts){
+    wpu.io.predVec(i).en := io.req(i).valid
+    wpu.io.predVec(i).vaddr := io.req(i).bits.vaddr
+    s0_pred_way_en(i) := wpu.io.predVec(i).way_en
+    // io
+    io.req(i).ready := true.B
+    if (iwpuParam.enWPU) {
+      io.resp(i).valid := io.req(i).valid
+    } else {
+      io.resp(i).valid := false.B
+    }
+    io.resp(i).bits.s0_pred_way_en := s0_pred_way_en(i)
+    assert(PopCount(io.resp(i).bits.s0_pred_way_en) <= 1.U, "tag should not match with more than 1 way")
+
+    /** update in s1 */
+    s1_pred_way_en(i) := io.lookup_upd(i).bits.s1_pred_way_en
+    s1_real_way_en(i) := io.lookup_upd(i).bits.s1_real_way_en
+    s1_pred_fail(i) := io.lookup_upd(i).valid && s1_pred_way_en(i) =/= s1_real_way_en(i)
+    // look up res
+    wpu.io.updLookup(i).en := io.lookup_upd(i).valid
+    wpu.io.updLookup(i).vaddr := io.lookup_upd(i).bits.vaddr
+    wpu.io.updLookup(i).way_en := io.lookup_upd(i).bits.s1_real_way_en
+    wpu.io.updLookup(i).pred_way_en := io.lookup_upd(i).bits.s1_pred_way_en
+    // which will update in look up pred fail
+    wpu.io.updReplaycarry := DontCare
+    // replace / tag write
+    wpu.io.updTagwrite := DontCare
+  }
+  wpu.io.updTagwrite.head.en := io.tagwrite_upd.valid
+  wpu.io.updTagwrite.head.vaddr := io.tagwrite_upd.bits.vaddr
+  wpu.io.updTagwrite.head.way_en := io.tagwrite_upd.bits.s1_real_way_en
+
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_total", PopCount((0 until nPorts).map{i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && io.lookup_upd(i).valid}))
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_succ",  PopCount((0 until nPorts).map{i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && io.lookup_upd(i).valid && !s1_pred_fail(i)}))
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_fail",  PopCount((0 until nPorts).map{i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && io.lookup_upd(i).valid && s1_pred_fail(i)}))
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_pred_miss",  PopCount((0 until nPorts).map{i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && io.lookup_upd(i).valid && !RegNext(s0_pred_way_en(i)).orR}))
+  XSPerfAccumulate("wpu_real_miss",  PopCount((0 until nPorts).map{i => RegNext(io.req(i).valid) && io.lookup_upd(i).valid && !RegNext(s1_real_way_en(i)).orR}))
+}
+
+/** IdealWPU:
+  * req in s1 and resp in s1
+  */
+class IdealWPU(implicit p:Parameters) extends WPUModule with HasDCacheParameters {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle{
+    val req = Output(new Bundle {
+      val valid = Bool()
+      val s1_real_way_en = UInt(nWays.W)
+    })
+    val resp = Output(new Bundle{
+      val valid = Bool()
+      val s1_pred_way_en = UInt(nWays.W)
+    })
+  })
+
+  val s1_pred_way_en = io.req.s1_real_way_en
+
+  if(dwpuParam.enWPU){
+    io.resp.valid := io.req.valid
+  }else{
+    io.resp.valid := false.B
+  }
+  io.resp.s1_pred_way_en := s1_pred_way_en
+}

+package cache
+
+import chisel3._
+import chiseltest._
+import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
+import top.DefaultConfig
+import xiangshan.cache.wpu.DCacheWpuWrapper
+import xiangshan.{XSCoreParamsKey, XSTileKey}
+
+class WpuBasicTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester {
+  behavior of "DCacheWPU"
+  it should ("run") in {
+    val defaultConfig = (new DefaultConfig)
+    implicit val config = defaultConfig.alterPartial({
+      case XSCoreParamsKey => defaultConfig(XSTileKey).head.copy()
+    })
+    println("========== Test the correctness of syntactic and datapath ==========")
+    test(new DCacheWpuWrapper()) { c =>
+      println("========== in test ==========")
+      // s0
+      c.io.req(0).bits.vaddr.poke(0.U)
+      c.io.req(0).bits.replayCarry.valid.poke(false.B)
+      c.io.req(0).bits.replayCarry.real_way_en.poke(0.U)
+      c.io.req(0).valid.poke(true.B)
+      c.clock.step()
+      // s1
+      c.io.lookup_upd(0).valid.poke(true.B)
+      c.io.lookup_upd(0).bits.s1_real_way_en.poke("b00010000".U)
+      c.io.req(0).bits.vaddr.poke(0.U)
+      c.io.req(0).bits.replayCarry.valid.poke(false.B)
+      c.io.req(0).bits.replayCarry.real_way_en.poke(0.U)
+      c.io.req(0).valid.poke(true.B)
+      println("output value1 : " + c.io.resp(0).bits.s0_pred_way_en.peek().litValue)
+      c.clock.step()
+      println("output value2 : " + c.io.resp(0).bits.s0_pred_way_en.peek().litValue)
+    }
+    println("========== end test ==========")
+  }
+
+}
problem_statement: Observed behavior: when the DCache way predictor (WPU) is enabled, it can learn the real cache way for a load access but still fail to reuse that learned way on the next access to the same cache line. In the verified reproduced case, after a lookup updates the predictor with a hit in way 3, the following request for the same address returns no predicted way instead of predicting way 3. Expected behavior: after the DCache WPU is updated with the real hit way for an address, the next request to that same address should return that learned one-hot way as the prediction. Affected function: the DCache WPU's learned-way prediction for repeated accesses to the same cache line. Trigger condition: DCache WPU is enabled, a lookup/update records the real hit way for an address, and a subsequent request accesses the same cache line.

problem_statement: After the MemBlock IO optimization, XiangShan no longer compiles. In LoadQueueReplay, the memory-subsystem unit that decides which stalled load request should be replayed, the replay-selection logic contains invalid boolean expressions and references an undefined selection signal, so a normal XiangShan build fails during compilation. The expected behavior is that the MemBlock IO refactor leaves LoadQueueReplay's replay-selection logic well-typed and fully defined, and that a standard XiangShan configuration compiles successfully. The affected function is the load replay selection and arbitration logic in LoadQueueReplay. patch_gitlink_sha() {
  local path="$1"
  local patch_file

  for patch_file in /home/fix.patch; do
    if [[ -s "$patch_file" ]]; then
      awk -v path="$path" '
        $0 == "diff --git a/" path " b/" path { in_target = 1; next }
        /^diff --git / { in_target = 0 }
        in_target && /^\+Subproject commit [0-9a-f]+$/ { print $3; exit }

      return 0
    fi
  done

sync_submodules_to_gitlinks() {
  local path="coupledL2"
  local url
  local sha
  local patch_sha
  local current_sha

  : > "$SETUP_LOG"
  git submodule sync --recursive >>"$SETUP_LOG" 2>&1
  url="$(git config -f .gitmodules --get submodule.${path}.url)"
  sha="$(git ls-files -s "$path" | awk '{print $2}')"
  patch_sha="$(patch_gitlink_sha "$path")"

  if [[ -n "$patch_sha" ]] && ! git diff --quiet -- .; then
    sha="$patch_sha"
  fi

  if [[ -z "$url" || -z "$sha" ]]; then
    echo "Unable to resolve $path submodule metadata" >>"$SETUP_LOG"
    return 1
  fi

  current_sha=""
  if [[ -d "$path/.git" || -f "$path/.git" ]]; then
    current_sha="$(git -C "$path" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  if [[ "$current_sha" != "$sha" ]]; then
    if [[ -d "$path/.git" || -f "$path/.git" ]]; then
      git -C "$path" fetch origin >>"$SETUP_LOG" 2>&1 || true
      git -C "$path" checkout "$sha" >>"$SETUP_LOG" 2>&1
    else
      rm -rf "$path"
      git clone "$url" "$path" >>"$SETUP_LOG" 2>&1
      git -C "$path" checkout "$sha" >>"$SETUP_LOG" 2>&1
    fi
  fi

  git -C "$path" submodule update --init --recursive >>"$SETUP_LOG" 2>&1
}

run_probe() {
  local test_name="$1"
  local run_log="$2"
  local target_dir="$3"
  shift 3

  rm -rf "$target_dir"
  : > "$run_log"

  stdbuf -oL -eL "$@" >"$run_log" 2>&1 &
  local pid=$!
  local timed_out=0
  local bug_seen=0
  local pass_seen=0
  local deadline=$((SECONDS + TIMEOUT_SECS))

  while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
    if grep -Eq "$BUG_RE" "$run_log"; then
      bug_seen=1
      stop_pid "$pid"
      break
    fi

    if grep -q "$PASS_RE" "$run_log"; then
      pass_seen=1
      stop_pid "$pid"
      break
    fi

    if (( SECONDS >= deadline )); then
      timed_out=1
      stop_pid "$pid"
      break
    fi

    sleep 2
  done

  local run_rc
  if wait "$pid"; then
    run_rc=0
  else
    run_rc=$?
  fi

  cat "$run_log"

  if (( timed_out )); then
    echo "TEST: $test_name ... FAIL"
    return 124
  fi

  if (( bug_seen )) || grep -Eq "$BUG_RE" "$run_log"; then
    echo "TEST: $test_name ... FAIL"
    return 1
  fi

  if (( pass_seen )) || grep -q "$PASS_RE" "$run_log"; then
    echo "TEST: $test_name ... PASS"
    return 0
  fi

  if (( run_rc != 0 )); then
    echo "TEST: $test_name ... FAIL"
    return "$run_rc"
  fi

  echo "TEST: $test_name ... FAIL"
  return 1
}

problem_statement: Observed behavior: XiangShan's `XSTile` can instantiate a private `CoupledL2` cache. When a build enables `FPGAPlatform` and also includes that private L2, the private L2 still enables its L2 debug/performance instrumentation, and RTL elaboration emits instrumentation-related multiple-sink warnings instead of proceeding cleanly. Expected behavior: when `FPGAPlatform` is enabled, the private `CoupledL2` should inherit that FPGA setting and keep its L2 debug/performance instrumentation disabled, so elaboration completes without those warnings. Affected function: the `XSTile` path that constructs and configures the private `CoupledL2` instance. Trigger condition: any `FPGAPlatform` configuration that instantiates the private L2 cache, including minimal single-core configurations.

class SchedulerFastWakeupValidTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "Scheduler fast wakeup bypass"

  val defaultConfig = new top.DefaultConfig
  implicit val config = defaultConfig.alterPartial({
    case XSCoreParamsKey => defaultConfig(XSTileKey).head.copy(IssQueSize = 4)
  })

  it should "not bypass invalid writeback data over a ready source" in {
    test(new SchedulerFastWakeupHarness) { dut =>
      val goodData = BigInt("1122334455667788", 16)
      val badData = BigInt("deadbeefcafef00d", 16)

      dut.io.preloadValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.preloadData.poke(0.U)
      dut.io.dispatchValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.invalidWakeupValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.invalidWakeupData.poke(0.U)
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.preloadValid.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.preloadData.poke(goodData.U(64.W))
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.preloadValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.dispatchValid.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.invalidWakeupValid.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.invalidWakeupData.poke(badData.U(64.W))

      var seenIssue = false
      for (_ <- 0 until 8) {
        if (dut.io.issueValid.peek().litToBoolean) {
          seenIssue = true
          dut.io.issueSrc0.expect(goodData.U(64.W))
        }
        dut.clock.step()
        dut.io.dispatchValid.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.invalidWakeupValid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.invalidWakeupData.poke(badData.U(64.W))
      }

      seenIssue shouldBe true
    }
  }
}

    fi
  fi
fi

problem_statement: In XiangShan's backend scheduler, the reservation station uses a fast-wakeup bypass path to forward writeback data to source operands. The bug is that this bypass path can treat a fast-wakeup match as usable even when the corresponding writeback data is not valid. If a reservation-station entry already holds a ready source value for a physical register and a later fast-wakeup event for that same register arrives while the writeback port is invalid, the stored ready operand can be overwritten with invalid or stale data, and the issued instruction then sees the wrong source value. The expected behavior is that fast wakeup must only bypass data when the associated writeback is valid; otherwise the reservation station must leave the existing ready source value unchanged.

EOF
}

if write_project \
  && cd "$PROJ_DIR" \
  && timeout 1200 /tools/mill/bin/mill-0.11.1 --no-server app.test.testOnly '*HPerfCounterSelectionSpec'
then
  echo "TEST: $TEST_NAME ... PASS"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

  echo "TEST: $TEST_NAME ... FAIL"

problem_statement: In XiangShan's HPerfCounter logic, an `hpm_event` CSR can encode four source events and three combine operators to derive the value fed into a hardware performance counter. Observed behavior: when this four-source composition mode is used, the derived value can be wrong because the encoded composition order is not honored, so the module may combine the wrong source pairs and may apply the wrong final operator. Expected behavior: the selector must evaluate the first encoded pair with the first encoded operator, evaluate the second encoded pair with the second encoded operator, and then apply the separately encoded final operator to those two intermediate results, producing the value described by the `hpm_event` encoding. Affected function: the HPerfCounter event-selection path used by CSR-programmed HPM counters. Trigger condition: an HPM counter is configured to combine four selected events through two intermediate operations and a final operation, especially when source-pair order matters or the final operator differs from the second intermediate operator.

cat > src/test/scala/pr2513/FusionDecoderSameSrcSpec.scala <<'EOF'
package pr2513

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import chiseltest.simulator.TreadleBackendAnnotation
import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters
import xiangshan.XSTester
import xiangshan.backend.Bundles.DecodedInst
import xiangshan.backend.decode.FusionDecoder

class FusionDecoderHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val valid0 = Input(Bool())
    val inst0 = Input(UInt(32.W))
    val valid1 = Input(Bool())
    val inst1 = Input(UInt(32.W))
    val outValid = Output(Bool())
    val lsrc2Valid = Output(Bool())
    val lsrc2 = Output(UInt(6.W))
    val rs2FromRs1 = Output(Bool())
    val rs2FromRs2 = Output(Bool())
  })

  val timer = WireInit(0.U(64.W))
  val logEnable = WireInit(false.B)
  val clean = WireInit(false.B)
  val dump = WireInit(false.B)
  dontTouch(timer)
  dontTouch(logEnable)
  dontTouch(clean)
  dontTouch(dump)

  val dut = Module(new FusionDecoder)

  dut.io.in(0).valid := io.valid0
  dut.io.in(0).bits := io.inst0
  dut.io.in(1).valid := io.valid1
  dut.io.in(1).bits := io.inst1
  for (i <- 2 until dut.io.in.length) {
    dut.io.in(i).valid := false.B
    dut.io.in(i).bits := 0.U
  }

  dut.io.inReady.foreach(_ := true.B)
  dut.io.dec.foreach(_ := 0.U.asTypeOf(new DecodedInst))

  io.outValid := dut.io.out(0).valid
  io.lsrc2Valid := dut.io.out(0).bits.lsrc2.valid
  io.lsrc2 := dut.io.out(0).bits.lsrc2.bits
  io.rs2FromRs1 := dut.io.info(0).rs2FromRs1
  io.rs2FromRs2 := dut.io.info(0).rs2FromRs2
}

class FusionDecoderSameSrcSpec extends XSTester {
  private def encodeR(funct7: Int, rs2: Int, rs1: Int, funct3: Int, rd: Int, opcode: Int): BigInt = {
    BigInt(((funct7 & 0x7f) << 25) | ((rs2 & 0x1f) << 20) | ((rs1 & 0x1f) << 15) |
      ((funct3 & 0x7) << 12) | ((rd & 0x1f) << 7) | (opcode & 0x7f))
  }

  private def encodeI(imm: Int, rs1: Int, funct3: Int, rd: Int, opcode: Int): BigInt = {
    BigInt((((imm & 0xfff) << 20) | ((rs1 & 0x1f) << 15) | ((funct3 & 0x7) << 12) |
      ((rd & 0x1f) << 7) | (opcode & 0x7f)) & 0xffffffffL)
  }

  private def encodeShiftI(shamt: Int, rs1: Int, funct3: Int, rd: Int, opcode: Int): BigInt = {
    BigInt((((shamt & 0x3f) << 20) | ((rs1 & 0x1f) << 15) | ((funct3 & 0x7) << 12) |
      ((rd & 0x1f) << 7) | (opcode & 0x7f)) & 0xffffffffL)
  }

  behavior of "FusionDecoder"
  it should "reject fusion when inst2 reuses the same source register" in {
    test(new FusionDecoderHarness()(config)).withAnnotations(Seq(TreadleBackendAnnotation)) { dut =>
      def drive(inst0: BigInt, inst1: BigInt): Unit = {
        dut.io.valid0.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.inst0.poke(inst0.U)
        dut.io.valid1.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.inst1.poke(inst1.U)
        dut.clock.step()
      }

      def clearInputs(): Unit = {
        dut.io.valid0.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.inst0.poke(0.U)
        dut.io.valid1.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.inst1.poke(0.U)
        dut.clock.step()
      }

      val slli1 = encodeShiftI(shamt = 1, rs1 = 6, funct3 = 0x1, rd = 5, opcode = 0x13)
      val addDestRs1 = encodeR(funct7 = 0x00, rs2 = 7, rs1 = 5, funct3 = 0x0, rd = 5, opcode = 0x33)
      val addDestRs2 = encodeR(funct7 = 0x00, rs2 = 5, rs1 = 7, funct3 = 0x0, rd = 5, opcode = 0x33)
      val addSameSrc = encodeR(funct7 = 0x00, rs2 = 5, rs1 = 5, funct3 = 0x0, rd = 5, opcode = 0x33)

      drive(slli1, addDestRs1)
      dut.io.outValid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.lsrc2Valid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.lsrc2.expect(7.U)
      dut.io.rs2FromRs1.expect(false.B)
      dut.io.rs2FromRs2.expect(true.B)
      clearInputs()

      drive(slli1, addDestRs2)
      dut.io.outValid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.lsrc2Valid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.lsrc2.expect(7.U)
      dut.io.rs2FromRs1.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.rs2FromRs2.expect(false.B)
      clearInputs()

      drive(slli1, addSameSrc)
      dut.io.outValid.expect(false.B)
      clearInputs()

      val andi1 = encodeI(imm = 1, rs1 = 9, funct3 = 0x7, rd = 8, opcode = 0x13)
      val addwDestRs1 = encodeR(funct7 = 0x00, rs2 = 10, rs1 = 8, funct3 = 0x0, rd = 8, opcode = 0x3b)
      val addwSameSrc = encodeR(funct7 = 0x00, rs2 = 8, rs1 = 8, funct3 = 0x0, rd = 8, opcode = 0x3b)

      drive(andi1, addwDestRs1)
      dut.io.outValid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.lsrc2Valid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.lsrc2.expect(10.U)
      dut.io.rs2FromRs1.expect(false.B)
      dut.io.rs2FromRs2.expect(true.B)
      clearInputs()

      drive(andi1, addwSameSrc)
      dut.io.outValid.expect(false.B)
      clearInputs()
    }
  }
}
EOF

rm -rf test_run_dir/FusionDecoder_should_reject_fusion_when_inst2_reuses_the_same_source_register

status=0
if timeout 1200s mill -i "xiangshan[chisel3].test.testOnly" pr2513.FusionDecoderSameSrcSpec; then
  result=PASS
else
  status=$?
  result=FAIL
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
echo "TEST: fusiondecoder_same_src_guard ... $result"
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$status"
problem_statement: Observed behavior: XiangShan's backend FusionDecoder, which decides whether two adjacent decoded instructions can be combined into one fused operation, can incorrectly treat a fusion candidate as valid when instruction 2 reads the same architectural register through both rs1 and rs2. In that case the decoder may still emit a fused result even though instruction 2 does not contribute a distinct second source operand. Expected behavior: FusionDecoder should reject these pairs and produce no fused output when inst2.rs1 == inst2.rs2 for fusion patterns that depend on instruction 1 providing one operand and instruction 2 providing another. Fusion should still be allowed when instruction 2 reuses instruction 1's destination through only one source field and the other source register is different. Affected function: the backend FusionDecoder logic that validates two-instruction fusion candidates. Trigger condition: a fusible-looking pair reaches FusionDecoder with instruction 1's destination reused by instruction 2, but instruction 2 uses that same register as both source operands, for example in slli + add or andi + addw style sequences.

#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan

TEST_NAME="fma_rm_handoff"
WORK_DIR="/home/xiangshan/.tb_fma_rm"
TEST_SRC="src/test/scala/xiangshan/backend/fu/fpu/FmaRmSpec.scala"
FIXED_FMUL="${WORK_DIR}/FMUL.fixed.scala"
TRY1_LOG="${WORK_DIR}/try1.log"
TRY2_LOG="${WORK_DIR}/try2.log"

mkdir -p "${WORK_DIR}" "$(dirname "${TEST_SRC}")"

cat > "${TEST_SRC}" <<'EOF'
package xiangshan.backend.fu.fpu

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.should.Matchers
import top.DefaultConfig
import xiangshan.{MicroOp, Redirect, XSCoreParamsKey, XSTileKey}

class FmaRmHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val issue = Input(Bool())
    val rm = Input(UInt(3.W))
    val src = Input(Vec(3, UInt(64.W)))
    val outValid = Output(Bool())
    val outData = Output(UInt(64.W))
  })

  val dut = Module(new FMA)
  val uop = WireInit(0.U.asTypeOf(new MicroOp))
  uop.ctrl.fpu.typeTagIn := FPU.S
  uop.ctrl.fpu.typeTagOut := FPU.S
  uop.ctrl.fpu.isAddSub := false.B
  uop.ctrl.fpu.fmaCmd := 0.U
  uop.ctrl.fpu.ren3 := true.B
  uop.ctrl.fpu.wflags := true.B
  uop.ctrl.fpu.fpWen := true.B

  dut.io.in.valid := io.issue
  dut.io.in.bits.src := io.src
  dut.io.in.bits.uop := uop
  dut.rm := io.rm
  dut.io.out.ready := true.B

  dut.io.redirectIn.valid := false.B
  dut.io.redirectIn.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new Redirect)

  dut.midResult.in.valid := false.B
  dut.midResult.in.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new FMAMidResult)
  dut.midResult.waitForAdd := false.B

  io.outValid := dut.io.out.valid
  io.outData := dut.io.out.bits.data
}

class FmaRmSpec extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "FMA rounding mode retention"

  val defaultConfig = new DefaultConfig
  implicit val config: Parameters = defaultConfig.alterPartial({
    case XSCoreParamsKey => defaultConfig(XSTileKey).head.copy(IssQueSize = 12)
  })

  private def box32(bits: Int): BigInt = {
    (BigInt("ffffffff", 16) << 32) | BigInt(bits & 0xffffffffL)
  }

  it should "keep the issued rm after the mul-to-add handoff" in {
    val one = box32(java.lang.Float.floatToRawIntBits(1.0f))
    val addend = box32(java.lang.Float.floatToRawIntBits(java.lang.Math.scalb(1.5f, -24)))

    test(new FmaRmHarness) { dut =>
      // Issue a positive FMA under RDN, then change the external rm to RUP.
      // The buggy pipeline re-samples the newer rm when the mul result reaches add.
      dut.io.issue.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.rm.poke(2.U)
      dut.io.src.foreach(_.poke(0.U))
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.issue.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.rm.poke(2.U)
      dut.io.src(0).poke(one.U(64.W))
      dut.io.src(1).poke(one.U(64.W))
      dut.io.src(2).poke(addend.U(64.W))
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.issue.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.rm.poke(3.U)
      dut.io.src.foreach(_.poke(0.U))

      var waited = 0
      while (!dut.io.outValid.peek().litToBoolean && waited < 10) {
        dut.clock.step()
        waited += 1
      }
      dut.io.outValid.expect(true.B)

      // One more cycle exposes the post-add result at this interface boundary.
      dut.clock.step()
      dut.io.outData.expect(one.U(64.W))
    }
  }
}
EOF

run_case() {
  local log_file="$1"
  set +e
  mill -i xiangshan[chisel3].test.testOnly xiangshan.backend.fu.fpu.FmaRmSpec 2>&1 | tee "${log_file}"
  local status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  set -e
  return "${status}"
}

status=1
retry_with_fixed_fmul=0

if run_case "${TRY1_LOG}"; then
  status=0
else
  status=$?
  if rg -q 'value rm is not a member of fudian\.FMULToFADD|value rm is not a member of xiangshan\.backend\.fu\.fpu\.FMAMidResult' "${TRY1_LOG}"; then
    if [[ ! -f "${FIXED_FMUL}" ]]; then
      echo "[ERROR] Missing ${FIXED_FMUL}"
      status=1
    else
      cp "${FIXED_FMUL}" fudian/src/main/scala/fudian/FMUL.scala
      retry_with_fixed_fmul=1
      if run_case "${TRY2_LOG}"; then
        status=0
      else
        status=$?
      fi
    fi
  fi
fi

if [[ "${retry_with_fixed_fmul}" -eq 1 ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Retried with synced fudian/FMUL.scala"
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [[ "${status}" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "${status}"

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's backend floating-point fused multiply-add (FMA) path, an instruction can use the wrong rounding mode (`rm`) after its multiply stage completes. If the external `rm` input changes before the add stage consumes the intermediate result, the FMA may be rounded using the newer mode instead of the mode that was present when the instruction was issued, so the final value can be wrong. Expected behavior: an FMA must keep its original `rm` for the entire operation. When an instruction is issued under one rounding mode and the `rm` input changes before the add stage, the completed result must still match the rounding mode captured at issue time. Affected function: the backend FPU FMA unit, specifically the handoff from the multiply stage to the add stage. Trigger condition: a multi-stage FMA is in flight and the `rm` input changes between the mul and add stages, especially on operands where different rounding modes produce different final results.

resolved_issues.body: If not initialized, it will result in an X state and propagate forward.

diff --git a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/icache/IPrefetch.scala b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/icache/IPrefetch.scala

@@ -366,7 +366,7 @@ class IPrefetchPipe(implicit p: Parameters) extends  IPrefetchModule
     */
   val p1_valid  = generatePipeControl(lastFire = p0_fire, thisFire = p1_fire || p1_discard, thisFlush = false.B, lastFlush = false.B)
 
-  val p1_vaddr      = RegEnable(p0_vaddr, p0_fire)
+  val p1_vaddr      = RegEnable(p0_vaddr, 0.U(VAddrBits.W), p0_fire)
   val p1_req_cancel = Wire(Bool())
 
   /** 1. Receive resp from ITLB (no blocked) */
@@ -408,7 +408,7 @@ class IPrefetchPipe(implicit p: Parameters) extends  IPrefetchModule
   val p2_valid  = generatePipeControl(lastFire = p1_fire, thisFire = p2_fire || p2_discard, thisFlush = false.B, lastFlush = false.B)
   
   val p2_paddr      = RegEnable(p1_paddr, p1_fire)
-  val p2_vaddr      = RegEnable(p1_vaddr, p1_fire)
+  val p2_vaddr      = RegEnable(p1_vaddr, 0.U(VAddrBits.W), p1_fire)
   val p2_req_cancel = Wire(Bool())
   val p2_vidx       = get_idx(p2_vaddr)
problem_statement: The ICache prefetch pipeline (`IPrefetchPipe`) does not reset its stage-1 and stage-2 virtual-address registers to a defined value. After reset, those registers can hold X/unknown state, and that state can be consulted when the first prefetch request enters the pipeline. This can cause the first post-reset prefetch request to be cancelled spuriously, so the normal iTLB lookup and metadata-read request are not issued. The expected behavior is that reset leaves `IPrefetchPipe` in a defined idle state, and the first prefetch request after reset should proceed normally by issuing both the iTLB lookup and the metadata lookup instead of being dropped because of uninitialized address state.

#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan || exit 1

TEST_NAME="frontend_fallthrough_address_regression"
TEST_FILE="/home/xiangshan/src/test/scala/xiangshan/FallThroughAddressRegressionMain.scala"
GEN_DIR="/home/xiangshan/build/fallthrough-regression"
GEN_V="${GEN_DIR}/FallThroughAddressProbe.v"
LOG_FILE="/home/xiangshan/${TEST_NAME}.log"

mkdir -p "$(dirname "${TEST_FILE}")"

cat > "${TEST_FILE}" <<'EOF'
package xiangshan

import chisel3._
import chisel3.stage.ChiselGeneratorAnnotation
import chisel3.util.log2Ceil
import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters
import top.{ArgParser, DefaultConfig}
import types.ChiselStage
import xiangshan.backend.regfile.IntPregParams
import xiangshan.frontend.{FTBEntry, FetchRequestBundle, Ftq_RF_Components, FullBranchPrediction, HasBPUConst}
import xiangshan.frontend.icache.HasICacheParameters

class FallThroughAddressProbe(implicit val p: Parameters) extends RawModule with HasBPUConst with HasICacheParameters {
  private val splitBit = log2Ceil(PredictWidth) + instOffsetBits

  val nextStartAddr = IO(Output(UInt(VAddrBits.W)))
  val expectedNextStartAddr = IO(Output(UInt(VAddrBits.W)))
  val fallThruError = IO(Output(Bool()))
  val fallThroughAddr = IO(Output(UInt(VAddrBits.W)))
  val expectedFallThroughAddr = IO(Output(UInt(VAddrBits.W)))
  val pass = IO(Output(Bool()))

  val ftq = WireDefault(0.U.asTypeOf(new Ftq_RF_Components))
  ftq.startAddr := (BigInt(3) << splitBit).U(VAddrBits.W)
  ftq.nextLineAddr := (BigInt(5) << splitBit).U(VAddrBits.W)
  ftq.fallThruError := true.B

  val req = WireDefault(0.U.asTypeOf(new FetchRequestBundle))
  req.fromFtqPcBundle(ftq)
  nextStartAddr := req.nextStartAddr
  expectedNextStartAddr := (BigInt(4) << splitBit).U(VAddrBits.W)

  val entry = WireDefault(0.U.asTypeOf(new FTBEntry))
  entry.valid := true.B
  entry.carry := true.B
  entry.pftAddr := 1.U

  val pred = WireDefault(0.U.asTypeOf(new FullBranchPrediction))
  pred.fromFtbEntry(entry, 0.U(VAddrBits.W))
  pred.hit := true.B

  fallThruError := pred.fallThruError
  fallThroughAddr := pred.fallThroughAddr
  expectedFallThroughAddr := (FetchWidth * 4).U(VAddrBits.W)
  pass := nextStartAddr === expectedNextStartAddr && fallThruError && fallThroughAddr === expectedFallThroughAddr
}

object FallThroughAddressProbeMain extends App {
  ArgParser.parse(args)
  val defaultConfig = new DefaultConfig
  val testConfig = defaultConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => defaultConfig(XSTileKey).head.copy(
      intPreg = IntPregParams(
        numEntries = 64,
        numRead = Some(14),
        numWrite = Some(8),
      ),
    )
  }.alter((site, here, up) => {
    case DebugOptionsKey => up(DebugOptionsKey).copy(FPGAPlatform = true)
  })

  (new ChiselStage).execute(args, Seq(
    ChiselGeneratorAnnotation(() => new FallThroughAddressProbe()(testConfig))
  ))
}
EOF

export NOOP_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export XIANGSHAN_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64
export MILL_VERSION=0.11.8
export RISCV_HOME=/tools/riscv
export VERILATOR_ROOT=/tools/verilator
export VERILATOR_BIN=verilator_bin
export PATH="${JAVA_HOME}/bin:/tools/bin:/tools/mill/bin:${VERILATOR_ROOT}/bin:${RISCV_HOME}/bin:${PATH}"
MILL_BIN="/tools/mill/bin/mill-${MILL_VERSION}"

status=0
rm -rf "${GEN_DIR}"

timeout 1200s "${MILL_BIN}" -i xiangshan[chisel].test.runMain \
  xiangshan.FallThroughAddressProbeMain \
  -td "${GEN_DIR}" \
  --target verilog >"${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1 || status=$?

if [ "${status}" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ ! -f "${GEN_V}" ]; then
    echo "[ERROR] Generated Verilog not found: ${GEN_V}" >>"${LOG_FILE}"
    status=1
  else
    {
      echo
      echo "[INFO] Key assignments from ${GEN_V}"
      grep -nE "assign (nextStartAddr|expectedNextStartAddr|fallThruError|fallThroughAddr|expectedFallThroughAddr|pass)" "${GEN_V}" || true
    } >>"${LOG_FILE}"
    if ! grep -q "assign pass = 1'h1;" "${GEN_V}"; then
      echo "[ERROR] Elaborated probe did not match the expected fall-through behavior" >>"${LOG_FILE}"
      status=1
    fi
  fi
fi

cat "${LOG_FILE}"

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [ "${status}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "${status}"
problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's frontend, `FullBranchPrediction.fromFtbEntry` can accept an FTB (Fetch Target Buffer) entry whose encoded fall-through target goes past the current fetch window. Instead of marking that prediction as a fall-through error, it keeps the entry-derived `fallThroughAddr`. In the follow-on recovery path, `FetchRequestBundle.fromFtqPcBundle` can also compute the wrong `nextStartAddr` for a `fallThruError`, so the FTQ (Fetch Target Queue) restarts fetching from the wrong aligned block. Expected behavior: when an FTB entry's fall-through target extends beyond the current fetch window, `fallThruError` must be asserted and `fallThroughAddr` must fall back to the sequential next fetch block. When rebuilding the recovery request for that error case, `FetchRequestBundle.fromFtqPcBundle` must restart at the aligned block immediately after `startAddr`, even if `nextLineAddr` points to a later block. Affected function: `FullBranchPrediction.fromFtbEntry` and `FetchRequestBundle.fromFtqPcBundle` in the frontend branch-prediction/fetch path. Trigger condition: an FTB entry encodes a fall-through that crosses the current fetch-window boundary, and the frontend generates the recovery fetch request for that fall-through error.

class IFUMmioGpfTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  val defaultConfig = new DefaultConfig

  it should "forward the resend guest page fault and guest physical address" in {
    val startAddr = BigInt(0x0)
    val nextlineStart = BigInt(0x40)
    val nextStartAddr = BigInt(0x4)
    val icachePAddr = BigInt(0x6)
    val icacheGPAddr = BigInt(0x111)
    val tlbPAddr = BigInt(0x2006)
    val tlbGPAddr = BigInt(0x345)
    val uncacheInstr = BigInt("00000013", 16)

    Constantin.init(false)

    test(new IFUMmioGpfHarness()(config)).withAnnotations(
      Seq(
        VerilatorBackendAnnotation,
        VerilatorFlags(Seq("-DSIM_TOP_MODULE_NAME=IFUMmioGpfHarness"))

    ) { dut =>
      dut.io.ftqReqValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.startAddr.poke(startAddr.U)
      dut.io.nextlineStart.poke(nextlineStart.U)
      dut.io.nextStartAddr.poke(nextStartAddr.U)
      dut.io.icacheRespValid.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.icacheRespPAddr.poke(icachePAddr.U)
      dut.io.icacheRespGPAddr.poke(icacheGPAddr.U)
      dut.io.icacheRespData.poke(0.U)
      dut.io.uncacheRespValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.uncacheRespData.poke(uncacheInstr.U(32.W))
      dut.io.tlbRespGPF.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.tlbRespPAddr.poke(tlbPAddr.U)
      dut.io.tlbRespGPAddr.poke(tlbGPAddr.U)

      dut.clock.step(2)
      dut.io.ftqReqReady.expect(true.B)

      dut.io.ftqReqValid.poke(true.B)
      dut.clock.step()
      dut.io.ftqReqValid.poke(false.B)

      var sawUncacheReq = false
      var cycles = 0
      while (!sawUncacheReq && cycles < 20) {
        sawUncacheReq = dut.io.uncacheReqValid.peek().litToBoolean
        if (!sawUncacheReq) {
          dut.clock.step()
          cycles += 1
        }
      }
      assert(sawUncacheReq, "Timed out waiting for the MMIO uncache request")

      dut.io.uncacheRespValid.poke(true.B)
      dut.clock.step(2)
      dut.io.uncacheRespValid.poke(false.B)

      cycles = 0
      while (!dut.io.tlbReqValid.peek().litToBoolean && cycles < 20) {
        dut.clock.step()
        cycles += 1
      }
      assert(dut.io.tlbReqValid.peek().litToBoolean, "Timed out waiting for the MMIO TLB resend request")

      cycles = 0
      while (!dut.io.toIbufferValid.peek().litToBoolean && cycles < 20) {
        dut.clock.step()
        cycles += 1
      }
      assert(dut.io.toIbufferValid.peek().litToBoolean, "Timed out waiting for the MMIO ibuffer output")

      dut.io.exceptionType0.expect(ExceptionType.igpf)
      dut.io.gpaddrMemWen.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.gpaddrMemWaddr.expect(0.U)
      dut.io.gpaddrMemWdata.expect(tlbGPAddr.U(dut.io.gpaddrMemWdata.getWidth.W))
