problem_statement: Observed behavior: in `NewIFU`'s MMIO fetch resend path, when an uncache MMIO instruction needs a second fetch for the remaining half and the resend-side TLB lookup raises an instruction guest page fault, the IFU does not forward that fault to the instruction buffer (`ibuffer`) and does not write the resend guest physical address into the per-fetch guest-physical-address memory (`gpaddrMem`). Expected behavior: in that same situation, the IFU must report an instruction guest page fault (`igpf`) on the `ibuffer` output and store the guest physical address returned by the resend translation for the corresponding fetch entry. Affected function: frontend IFU MMIO resend handling in `NewIFU`, specifically the logic that turns resend translation results into `ibuffer` exceptions and guest-physical-address tracking. Trigger condition: a non-compressed MMIO instruction on the uncache path cannot be completed from the first response alone, so the IFU performs a resend/TLB lookup for the remaining half and that resend lookup reports a guest page fault.

title: FTQ: FTQ entry commit condition and move pointer condition
body:
An FTQ entry should be committed when last instruction is committed instead of all are committed, as backend may not commit every single instruction.

This PR also addresses the performance bugs noted in PR #3303, as it involves a complete rewrite. The description of PR #3303 is as follows.

PR #3086 fixes the bug where multiple load replays will fill the whole FTQ by committing the FTQ entries created by load replays. However, these committed entries will generate FTB entries that negatively impact the BP accuracy under certain conditions.

To mitigate this, FTQ entries containing only one single flushed instruction will no longer generate FTB entries. The commPtr and robcommPtr will sill advance in case of running FTQ entries.

repo.description: Open-source high-performance RISC-V processor

commits.message:
fix: FTQ entry commit condition and move pointer condition

An FTQ entry should be committed when last instruction is committed instead of all are committed, as backend may not commit every single instruction.

Now flushed FTQ entries will not create new FTB entries, which otherwise will significantly affect BP accuracy in some situations
fix: judgement of whether an entry is committed
fix: misuse of && and ||

resolved_issues.title: fix: multiple load replays lead to running out of FTQ entries
resolved_issues.body: Previously, FTQ did not handle flush-itself redirect level, which is used by load replays. This leads to running out of FTQ entries because commPtr remains the same while ifuPtr keeps increasing when a new replay redirect request arrives. Now, commPtr will also increase in this scenario.

resolved_issues.title: FTQ: now flushed FTQ entries will not create new FTB entries
resolved_issues.body:
PR #3086 fixes the bug where multiple load replays will fill the whole FTQ by committing the FTQ entries created by load replays. However, these committed entries will generate FTB entries that negatively impact the BP accuracy under certain conditions.

To mitigate this, FTQ entries containing only one single flushed instruction will no longer generate FTB entries. The `commPtr` and `robcommPtr` will sill advance in case of running FTQ entries.

diff --git a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/NewFtq.scala b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/NewFtq.scala
index fa0f3878620..905729154ae 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/NewFtq.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/NewFtq.scala
@@ -1261,13 +1261,21 @@ class Ftq(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSModule with HasCircularQueuePtrHelpe
   val may_have_stall_from_bpu = Wire(Bool())
   val bpu_ftb_update_stall = RegInit(0.U(2.W)) // 2-cycle stall, so we need 3 states
   may_have_stall_from_bpu := bpu_ftb_update_stall =/= 0.U
-  val noToCommit = commitStateQueueReg(commPtr.value).map(s => s =/= c_toCommit).reduce(_ && _)
-  val allEmpty = commitStateQueueReg(commPtr.value).map(s => s === c_empty).reduce(_ && _)
-  canCommit := commPtr =/= ifuWbPtr && !may_have_stall_from_bpu && (isAfter(robCommPtr, commPtr) || noToCommit && !allEmpty)
+
+  val validInstructions = commitStateQueueReg(commPtr.value).map(s => s === c_toCommit || s === c_committed)
+  val lastInstructionStatus = PriorityMux(validInstructions.reverse.zip(commitStateQueueReg(commPtr.value).reverse))
+  val firstInstructionFlushed = commitStateQueueReg(commPtr.value)(0) === c_flushed
+  canCommit := commPtr =/= ifuWbPtr && !may_have_stall_from_bpu &&
+    (isAfter(robCommPtr, commPtr) ||
+      validInstructions.reduce(_ || _) && lastInstructionStatus === c_committed)
+  val canMoveCommPtr = commPtr =/= ifuWbPtr && !may_have_stall_from_bpu &&
+    (isAfter(robCommPtr, commPtr) ||
+      validInstructions.reduce(_ || _) && lastInstructionStatus === c_committed ||
+      firstInstructionFlushed)
 
   when (io.fromBackend.rob_commits.map(_.valid).reduce(_ | _)) {
     robCommPtr_write := ParallelPriorityMux(io.fromBackend.rob_commits.map(_.valid).reverse, io.fromBackend.rob_commits.map(_.bits.ftqIdx).reverse)
-  } .elsewhen (commPtr =/= ifuWbPtr && !may_have_stall_from_bpu && noToCommit && !allEmpty) {

   } .otherwise {
     robCommPtr_write := robCommPtr
@@ -1279,8 +1287,8 @@ class Ftq(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSModule with HasCircularQueuePtrHelpe
     *************************************************************************************
     */
   val mmioReadPtr = io.mmioCommitRead.mmioFtqPtr
-  val mmioLastCommit = (isAfter(commPtr,mmioReadPtr) || (mmioReadPtr === commPtr)) &&
-                       Cat(commitStateQueueReg(mmioReadPtr.value).map(s => { s === c_empty || s === c_committed})).andR
+  val mmioLastCommit = isAfter(commPtr, mmioReadPtr) ||
+    commPtr === mmioReadPtr && validInstructions.reduce(_ || _) && lastInstructionStatus === c_committed
   io.mmioCommitRead.mmioLastCommit := RegNext(mmioLastCommit)

@@ -1303,7 +1311,7 @@ class Ftq(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSModule with HasCircularQueuePtrHelpe
   // need one cycle to read mem and srams

   val do_commit = RegNext(canCommit, init=false.B)
-  when (canCommit) {
+  when (canMoveCommPtr) {
     commPtr_write := commPtrPlus1

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in the frontend Fetch Target Queue (FTQ), the MMIO commit-read status can still report an entry as not committed when that entry contains multiple valid instructions and the backend reports commit for only the entry's last valid instruction. Expected behavior: once the last valid instruction in an FTQ entry has committed, the entry should be treated as committed even if the backend did not report commits for every instruction slot in that entry, and the MMIO commit-read status should report the entry as committed. Affected function: FTQ commit-status logic for frontend MMIO commit reads. Trigger condition: an FTQ entry has multiple valid instructions, and the backend commit report covers only the last valid instruction in that entry.

title: IFU: fix mmio fsm for itlb handshake
body:
Fixes state transfer condition of `m_sendTLB` and `m_tlbResp` in IFU mmio fsm.
https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/blob/091c28ff02749943c410f414784d991bc205e8cb/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/IFU.scala#L659-L663

## Story
2 years ago, TLB can be configured as `sameCycle` and therefore `io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.miss` is in the same cycle with `io.iTLBInter.req.fire`, see: https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/blob/c3b2d83a43a64198f94aced1db4b998ebf29a3bb/src/main/scala/xiangshan/cache/mmu/TLBStorage.scala#L59-L62

In that case, the current fsm will wait in state `m_sendTLB` until `io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.miss === false.B` (TLB hit or PTW work done), and enters state `m_tlbResp` in next cycle, getting the correct response (`paddr`, etc.).

However, currently `io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.miss` is returned 1 cycle after `io.iTLBInter.req.fire`, see:
https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/blob/091c28ff02749943c410f414784d991bc205e8cb/src/main/scala/xiangshan/cache/mmu/TLBStorage.scala#L125-L130

And the IFU mmio fsm is unchanged, it may use the `miss` from last TLB request, make real `miss` ignored and send invalid `paddr` to Uncache.

## Solution
1. Send `io.iTLBInter.req.valid` in state `m_sendTLB` as before, just wait `io.iTLBInter.req.fire` to enter state `m_tlbResp`.
2. Wait `io.iTLBInter.resp.valid` in state `m_tlbResp` (in blocked TLB, this also indicates `io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.miss === false.B`), get valid response and enter next state.

Also:
Close #2658

resolved_issues.title: TLB Timing interface not match with MMIO instruction fetch in IFU
resolved_issues.body:
**Issue Description:**

I have a question about the timing interface for accessing the TLB during MMIO instruction fetches. Although I may not have fully understood the code which is linked in below url. I'm unsure about the behavior of the IFU's (Instruction Fetch Unit) MMIO fetch state machine when checking the TLB's return result.
[https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/blob/8fae59bba57fd80fcd1d85aadbf87895b97d167a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/IFU.scala#L590C1-L590C1](url)

It seems that **whenever the condition `req.valid && !resp.bits.miss` is observed within the same cycle, the state will change**. However, the TLB requires at least one cycle to return the correct `resp.bits.miss`, even though the MMIO TLB is blocking. Suppose a TLB request for a specific MMIO is miss, due to the delayed response by one cycle, the MMIO state machine sees `miss == false.B`. However, the data in the TLB interface is incorrect. 

Personally, I wonder if using `resp.valid` would be better than `resp.bits.miss` in this case.

fix_patch:
diff --git a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/IFU.scala b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/IFU.scala
index 52af5874e76..16e6a68fddd 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/IFU.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/IFU.scala
@@ -231,9 +231,6 @@ class NewIFU(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSModule
   val frontendTrigger = Module(new FrontendTrigger)
   val (checkerIn, checkerOutStage1, checkerOutStage2)         = (predChecker.io.in, predChecker.io.out.stage1Out,predChecker.io.out.stage2Out)
 
-  io.iTLBInter.req_kill := false.B
-  io.iTLBInter.resp.ready := true.B
-
   /**
     ******************************************************************************
     * IFU Stage 0
@@ -657,48 +654,50 @@ class NewIFU(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSModule
     }
 
     is(m_sendTLB){
-      when( io.iTLBInter.req.valid && !io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.miss ){
-        mmio_state := m_tlbResp
-      }
+      mmio_state := Mux(io.iTLBInter.req.fire, m_tlbResp, m_sendTLB)
     }
 
     is(m_tlbResp){
-      val tlbExept = io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.excp(0).pf.instr ||
-                     io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.excp(0).af.instr ||
-                     io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.excp(0).gpf.instr
-      mmio_state         := Mux(tlbExept, m_waitCommit, m_sendPMP)
-      mmio_resend_addr   := io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.paddr(0)
-      mmio_resend_af     := mmio_resend_af || io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.excp(0).af.instr
-      mmio_resend_pf     := mmio_resend_pf || io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.excp(0).pf.instr
-      mmio_resend_gpf    := mmio_resend_gpf || io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.excp(0).gpf.instr
-      mmio_resend_gpaddr := io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.gpaddr(0)
+      when(io.iTLBInter.resp.fire) {
+        // we are using a blocked tlb, so resp.fire must have !resp.bits.miss
+        assert(!io.iTLBInter.resp.bits.miss, "blocked mode iTLB miss when resp.fire")

TEST_NAME="ifu_mmio_itlb_handshake"
TEST_CLASS="xiangshan.frontend.IFUMMIOITLBHandshakeTest"
TEST_FILE="src/test/scala/xiangshan/frontend/IFUMMIOITLBHandshakeTest.scala"

rm -rf out

package xiangshan.frontend

import chisel3._
import chisel3.util._
import chiseltest._
import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters
import utility.{LogUtilsOptions, LogUtilsOptionsKey, PerfCounterOptions, PerfCounterOptionsKey}
import xiangshan._
import xiangshan.frontend.icache.HasICacheParameters

class IFUMMIOITLBHandshakeHarness(implicit val p: Parameters)
  extends Module
    with HasXSParameter
    with HasICacheParameters {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val done = Output(Bool())
    val resendAddr = Output(UInt(PAddrBits.W))
    val expectedAddr = Output(UInt(PAddrBits.W))
  })

  private def zeroOf[T <: Data](target: T): T = 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(target))

  val ifu = Module(new NewIFU)

  val startVaddr = "h80000006".U(VAddrBits.W)
  val nextLineStart = Cat(startVaddr(VAddrBits - 1, blockOffBits) + 1.U, 0.U(blockOffBits.W))
  val firstPaddr = "h00001006".U(PAddrBits.W)
  val expectedResendAddr = "h00002008".U(PAddrBits.W)
  val mmioInsn = "h00000013".U(32.W)

  val ftqReqFired = RegInit(false.B)
  val icacheRespActive = RegInit(false.B)
  val uncacheReqCount = RegInit(0.U(2.W))
  val tlbReqSeen = RegInit(false.B)
  val done = RegInit(false.B)
  val observedResendAddr = RegInit(0.U(PAddrBits.W))

  val ftqReqBits = WireDefault(zeroOf(ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.req.bits))
  ftqReqBits.startAddr := startVaddr
  ftqReqBits.nextlineStart := nextLineStart
  ftqReqBits.nextStartAddr := startVaddr + 4.U
  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.req.valid := !ftqReqFired
  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.req.bits := ftqReqBits

  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.redirect.valid := false.B
  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.redirect.bits := zeroOf(ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.redirect.bits)
  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.topdown_redirect.valid := false.B
  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.topdown_redirect.bits := zeroOf(ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.topdown_redirect.bits)
  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.flushFromBpu.s2.valid := false.B
  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.flushFromBpu.s2.bits := zeroOf(ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.flushFromBpu.s2.bits)
  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.flushFromBpu.s3.valid := false.B
  ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.flushFromBpu.s3.bits := zeroOf(ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.flushFromBpu.s3.bits)

  ifu.io.icacheInter.icacheReady := true.B
  ifu.io.icacheInter.topdownIcacheMiss := false.B
  ifu.io.icacheInter.topdownItlbMiss := false.B
  ifu.io.icachePerfInfo := zeroOf(ifu.io.icachePerfInfo)

  val icacheRespBits = WireDefault(zeroOf(ifu.io.icacheInter.resp(0).bits))
  icacheRespBits.vaddr := startVaddr
  icacheRespBits.paddr := firstPaddr
  icacheRespBits.gpaddr := 0.U
  icacheRespBits.tlbExcp.mmio := true.B
  ifu.io.icacheInter.resp(0).valid := icacheRespActive
  ifu.io.icacheInter.resp(0).bits := icacheRespBits
  for (i <- 1 until ifu.io.icacheInter.resp.length) {
    ifu.io.icacheInter.resp(i).valid := false.B
    ifu.io.icacheInter.resp(i).bits := zeroOf(ifu.io.icacheInter.resp(i).bits)
  }

  ifu.io.toIbuffer.ready := true.B
  ifu.io.frontendTrigger := zeroOf(ifu.io.frontendTrigger)
  for (commit <- ifu.io.rob_commits) {
    commit.valid := false.B
    commit.bits := zeroOf(commit.bits)
  }

  ifu.io.mmioCommitRead.mmioLastCommit := true.B

  ifu.io.uncacheInter.toUncache.ready := true.B
  val firstUncacheReqFire = ifu.io.uncacheInter.toUncache.fire && uncacheReqCount === 0.U
  val secondUncacheReqFire = ifu.io.uncacheInter.toUncache.fire && uncacheReqCount === 1.U
  when(ifu.io.uncacheInter.toUncache.fire) {
    uncacheReqCount := uncacheReqCount + 1.U
  }

  val firstUncacheRespValid = RegNext(firstUncacheReqFire, init = false.B)
  val uncacheRespBits = WireDefault(zeroOf(ifu.io.uncacheInter.fromUncache.bits))
  uncacheRespBits.data := mmioInsn
  ifu.io.uncacheInter.fromUncache.valid := firstUncacheRespValid
  ifu.io.uncacheInter.fromUncache.bits := uncacheRespBits

  ifu.io.iTLBInter.req.ready := true.B
  val firstTlbReqFire = ifu.io.iTLBInter.req.fire && !tlbReqSeen
  when(firstTlbReqFire) {
    tlbReqSeen := true.B
  }
  val delayedTlbRespValid = RegNext(RegNext(firstTlbReqFire, init = false.B), init = false.B)
  val tlbRespBits = WireDefault(zeroOf(ifu.io.iTLBInter.resp.bits))
  tlbRespBits.miss := false.B
  when(delayedTlbRespValid) {
    tlbRespBits.paddr(0) := expectedResendAddr
  }
  ifu.io.iTLBInter.resp.valid := delayedTlbRespValid
  ifu.io.iTLBInter.resp.bits := tlbRespBits

  val pmpRespBits = WireDefault(zeroOf(ifu.io.pmp.resp))
  pmpRespBits.mmio := true.B
  ifu.io.pmp.resp := pmpRespBits

  when(ifu.io.ftqInter.fromFtq.req.fire) {
    ftqReqFired := true.B
    icacheRespActive := true.B
  }
  when(firstUncacheReqFire) {
    icacheRespActive := false.B
  }
  when(secondUncacheReqFire) {
    observedResendAddr := ifu.io.uncacheInter.toUncache.bits.addr
    done := true.B
  }

  io.done := done
  io.resendAddr := observedResendAddr
  io.expectedAddr := expectedResendAddr
}

class IFUMMIOITLBHandshakeTest extends XSTester {
  override implicit val config: Parameters = defaultConfig.alterPartial({
    case XSCoreParamsKey => defaultConfig(XSTileKey).head.copy()
    case LogUtilsOptionsKey => LogUtilsOptions(
      enableDebug = false,
      enablePerf = false,
      fpgaPlatform = false
    )
    case PerfCounterOptionsKey => PerfCounterOptions(
      enablePerfPrint = false,
      enablePerfDB = false,
      perfDBHartID = 0
    )
  })

  behavior of "IFU MMIO resend path"

  it should "wait for a valid itlb response before resending mmio fetch" in {
    test(new IFUMMIOITLBHandshakeHarness).withAnnotations(testAnnos) { c =>
      var cycles = 0
      while (cycles < 120 && !c.io.done.peek().litToBoolean) {
        c.clock.step()
        cycles += 1
      }

      c.io.done.expect(true.B)
      val expected = c.io.expectedAddr.peek().litValue
      val observed = c.io.resendAddr.peek().litValue
      observed should be(expected)
    }
  }
}
SCALA

fi

fi

exit 1
problem_statement: During memory-mapped I/O (MMIO) instruction fetches in the Instruction Fetch Unit (IFU), the MMIO state machine can leave its instruction TLB (iTLB) request step before the current iTLB response is valid. If the iTLB returns the translation one or more cycles after the request handshake, the IFU can treat stale response bits from an earlier request as the current result and resend the MMIO fetch on the uncache path with the wrong physical address. The affected logic is the IFU MMIO fetch/resend state machine around the iTLB handshake. The expected behavior is that, after issuing an iTLB request for an MMIO fetch, the IFU waits for the corresponding iTLB response to become valid before consuming the translation result or issuing the resend, so a delayed iTLB response still produces the correct resend address.

title: fix(StoreUnit): pass gpaddr from StoreUnit to MisalignBuffer
body: PR #3527 adds guest page fault logic of misalign buffer. However, that commit didn't pass store gpaddr to misalign buffer. This commit fixes it.

repo.name: XiangShan

commits.message:
fix(StoreUnit): pass gpaddr from StoreUnit to MisalignBuffer

PR #3527 adds guest page fault logic of misalign buffer. However, that commit didn't pass store gpaddr to misalign buffer. This commit fixes it.

resolved_issues.title: fix(LoadUnit): prefetch.i should not use HWPrefetch paddr
resolved_issues.body:
In previous design, prefetch.i would use HWPrefetch's paddr in load_s0 and send it to pmp in load_s1. However, when prefetch.i is valid, HWPrefetch's valid is 0 and paddr is X-stated, resulting in X-state propagation.

In fact, prefetch.i just sends vaddr to Frontend and does not use the result of the pmp check. In this commit, paddr that prefetch.i sends to pmp is written directly to 0, thus avoiding X-state propagation.

problem_statement: `CSRPermitModule` decides whether a CSR access is legal. In XiangShan, accesses to the supervisor timer compare CSRs (`stimecmp` and `vstimecmp`) from any privilege level below machine mode should raise `EX_II` (illegal instruction) when timer access is blocked by `mcounteren.TM = 0` or `menvcfg.STCE = 0`. The bug is that this permission check can be skipped, so a lower-privilege access is treated as legal when it should fault. The verified failing case is a non-M-mode read of `vstimecmp` with `mcounteren.TM` cleared: it must raise `EX_II`, while the same access from M-mode must remain legal.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan

export JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64"
export PATH="${JAVA_HOME}/bin:${PATH}"
export MILL_VERSION="$(cat .mill-version)"

TEST_NAME="interrupt_filter_aia_topi_priority_matrix"
TEST_LOG="/home/xiangshan/${TEST_NAME}.log"
TEST_DIR="src/test/scala/xiangshan/backend/fu/NewCSR"
TEST_FILE="${TEST_DIR}/InterruptFilterAiaTopiPriorityMatrixSpec.scala"
LEGACY_COMPAT_FILE="src/main/scala/difftest/DiffAIAXtopeiEventCompat.scala"

rm -rf out
mkdir -p "${TEST_DIR}"
rm -f "${LEGACY_COMPAT_FILE}"

git submodule update --init --recursive ready-to-run >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

if ! rg -q "class AIAXtopeiEvent" difftest/src/main/scala/Bundles.scala; then
  cat >> difftest/src/main/scala/Bundles.scala <<'EOF'

class AIAXtopeiEvent extends DifftestBaseBundle with HasValid {
  val mtopei = UInt(64.W)
  val stopei = UInt(64.W)
  val vstopei = UInt(64.W)
}
EOF
fi

if ! rg -q "class DiffAIAXtopeiEvent" difftest/src/main/scala/Difftest.scala; then
  cat >> difftest/src/main/scala/Difftest.scala <<'EOF'

class DiffAIAXtopeiEvent extends AIAXtopeiEvent with DifftestBundle {
  override val desiredCppName: String = "aia_xtopei"
}
EOF
fi

cat > "${TEST_FILE}" <<'EOF'
package xiangshan.backend.fu.NewCSR

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import xiangshan.backend.fu.NewCSR.CSRDefines.{PrivMode, VirtMode}

class InterruptFilterAiaTopiPriorityMatrixHarness extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val hsMode = Input(Bool())
    val pending = Input(UInt(64.W))
    val priorities = Input(UInt((64 * 8).W))
    val iid = Output(UInt(12.W))
    val iprio = Output(UInt(8.W))
  })

  private def initData(data: Data): Unit = data match {
    case b: Bool => b := false.B
    case e: CSREnumType => e := e.factory.all.head.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(e))
    case u: UInt => u := 0.U
    case s: SInt => s := 0.S
    case v: Vec[Data @unchecked] => v.foreach(initData)
    case r: Record => r.elements.values.foreach(initData)
  }

  val dut = Module(new InterruptFilter)
  val in = Wire(chiselTypeOf(dut.io.in))

  initData(in)
  in.privState.PRVM := PrivMode.M
  when (io.hsMode) {
    in.privState.PRVM := PrivMode.S
  }
  in.privState.V := VirtMode.Off
  in.mnstatusNMIE := true.B
  in.mstatusMIE := true.B
  in.sstatusSIE := true.B

  in.mip.MSIP := io.pending(InterruptNO.MSI)
  in.mip.MTIP := io.pending(InterruptNO.MTI)
  in.mip.MEIP := io.pending(InterruptNO.MEI)
  in.mie.MSIE := io.pending(InterruptNO.MSI)
  in.mie.MTIE := io.pending(InterruptNO.MTI)
  in.mie.MEIE := io.pending(InterruptNO.MEI)
  in.sip.SSIP := io.pending(InterruptNO.SSI)
  in.sip.STIP := io.pending(InterruptNO.STI)
  in.sip.SEIP := io.pending(InterruptNO.SEI)
  in.sie.SSIE := io.pending(InterruptNO.SSI)
  in.sie.STIE := io.pending(InterruptNO.STI)
  in.sie.SEIE := io.pending(InterruptNO.SEI)
  in.miprios := io.priorities
  in.hsiprios := io.priorities

  dut.io.in := in

  io.iid := Mux(io.hsMode, dut.io.out.stopi.IID.asUInt, dut.io.out.mtopi.IID.asUInt)
  io.iprio := Mux(io.hsMode, dut.io.out.stopi.IPRIO.asUInt, dut.io.out.mtopi.IPRIO.asUInt)
}

class InterruptFilterAiaTopiPriorityMatrixSpec extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester {
  behavior of "InterruptFilter AIA topi priority arbitration"

  private case class TopiCase(
    name: String,
    hsMode: Boolean,
    pending: Seq[Int],
    priorities: Map[Int, Int],
    expectedIid: Int,
    expectedIprio: Int
  )

  private def bit(irq: Int): BigInt = BigInt(1) << irq

  private def pendingBits(irqs: Seq[Int]): BigInt = irqs.foldLeft(BigInt(0))(_ | bit(_))

  private def priorityBits(priorities: Map[Int, Int]): BigInt =
    priorities.foldLeft(BigInt(0)) { case (acc, (irq, priority)) =>
      acc | (BigInt(priority) << (irq * 8))
    }

  private val cases = Seq(
    TopiCase(
      "programmed MEI beats zero MSI",
      hsMode = false,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.MSI, InterruptNO.MEI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.MEI -> 1),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.MEI,
      expectedIprio = 1
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "default MEI beats programmed MSI across the MEI reference",
      hsMode = false,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.MEI, InterruptNO.MSI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.MSI -> 2),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.MEI,
      expectedIprio = 0
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "default MEI beats programmed MTI across the MEI reference",
      hsMode = false,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.MEI, InterruptNO.MTI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.MTI -> 5),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.MEI,
      expectedIprio = 0
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "zero MSI loses to programmed MTI below the MEI reference",
      hsMode = false,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.MSI, InterruptNO.MTI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.MTI -> 4),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.MTI,
      expectedIprio = 4
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "equal non-zero machine priorities use default order",
      hsMode = false,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.MSI, InterruptNO.MTI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.MSI -> 7, InterruptNO.MTI -> 7),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.MSI,
      expectedIprio = 7
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "lower numeric machine priority wins",
      hsMode = false,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.MSI, InterruptNO.MTI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.MSI -> 8, InterruptNO.MTI -> 3),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.MTI,
      expectedIprio = 3
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "all-zero machine priorities use default order",
      hsMode = false,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.MEI, InterruptNO.MSI, InterruptNO.MTI),
      priorities = Map.empty,
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.MEI,
      expectedIprio = 1
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "default SEI beats programmed SSI across the SEI reference",
      hsMode = true,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.SEI, InterruptNO.SSI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.SSI -> 6),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.SEI,
      expectedIprio = 0
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "default SEI beats programmed STI across the SEI reference",
      hsMode = true,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.SEI, InterruptNO.STI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.STI -> 6),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.SEI,
      expectedIprio = 0
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "zero SSI loses to programmed STI below the SEI reference",
      hsMode = true,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.SSI, InterruptNO.STI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.STI -> 4),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.STI,
      expectedIprio = 4
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "equal non-zero HS priorities use default order",
      hsMode = true,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.SSI, InterruptNO.STI),
      priorities = Map(InterruptNO.SSI -> 7, InterruptNO.STI -> 7),
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.SSI,
      expectedIprio = 7
    ),
    TopiCase(
      "all-zero HS priorities use default order",
      hsMode = true,
      pending = Seq(InterruptNO.SEI, InterruptNO.SSI, InterruptNO.STI),
      priorities = Map.empty,
      expectedIid = InterruptNO.SEI,
      expectedIprio = 1
    )
  )

  it should "select the expected IID and IPRIO for mixed programmed and default priorities" in {
    test(new InterruptFilterAiaTopiPriorityMatrixHarness) { dut =>
      cases.foreach { c =>
        dut.io.hsMode.poke(c.hsMode.B)
        dut.io.pending.poke(pendingBits(c.pending).U(64.W))
        dut.io.priorities.poke(priorityBits(c.priorities).U((64 * 8).W))
        dut.clock.step(1)
        dut.io.iid.expect(c.expectedIid.U, s"${c.name}: IID")
        dut.io.iprio.expect(c.expectedIprio.U, s"${c.name}: IPRIO")
      }
    }
  }
}
EOF

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
set +e
timeout 1200s mill -i xiangshan.test.testOnly xiangshan.backend.fu.NewCSR.InterruptFilterAiaTopiPriorityMatrixSpec 2>&1 | tee "${TEST_LOG}"
status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e

if [ "${status}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

if [ "${status}" -ne 0 ]; then
  tail -n 200 "${TEST_LOG}" || true
fi

exit "${status}"
problem_statement: XiangShan's `InterruptFilter` implements AIA interrupt filtering and produces `mtopi`, the machine-level top-interrupt result. `mtopi.IID` identifies the selected pending interrupt and `mtopi.IPRIO` reports that interrupt's priority value. Observed behavior: when multiple machine-level interrupts are simultaneously pending in `mip` and enabled in `mie`, `mtopi` does not correctly follow the AIA specification's priority arbitration rules — it fails to properly combine the programmed per-interrupt priorities from `miprios` with the built-in default interrupt order, producing wrong IDs or priority values. Expected behavior: `mtopi` must report the interrupt selected per the AIA spec's priority rules, which jointly consider (a) per-interrupt programmed priority values in `miprios` where a lower numeric value means higher priority, (b) a zero priority field meaning "use the AIA default ordering" rather than numeric priority 0, and (c) the default interrupt order relative to the MEI reference position, which governs how zero and programmed priorities interact when both interrupts are enabled and pending. Across all combinations of programmed and zero priorities, `mtopi.IID` and `mtopi.IPRIO` must match what the AIA rules dictate. Affected function: the `InterruptFilter` priority-comparison step that reduces simultaneously pending machine-level interrupts to a single winning (ID, priority) pair. Trigger condition: two or more machine-level interrupts are simultaneously pending and enabled, with any mix of programmed (non-zero) and default (zero) priorities in `miprios`.

resolved_issues.title: When FS is 0 and a fld/fsd specific instruction causes an exception, there is a problem with the value of the mtval register
resolved_issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When the FS field in the mstatus register is 0, executing the `fld fa0, 288 (sp)` instruction causes an illegal instruction exception, and the values ​​of the xiangshan and nemu `mtval` registers are inconsistent.

Specifically, the value of the `xiangshan` mtval register is the machine code of the fld fa0, 288 (sp) instruction. 
The value of the mtval register in nemu is `0x00003512`

**To Reproduce**

```
.section .text
.globl _start
_start:
    li     t0, 0x8000000a00100a00     #FS: 00
    csrw    mstatus, t0 
    fld     fa0, 288(sp)
```


**Error log or Screenshots**

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef530af8-8bf7-4945-a792-7fe940b3a1bf)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41eb772e-9dd9-476c-b786-7849024df991)

When I use spike for debugging, the instruction corresponding to `0x00003512` is `c.fldsp fa0, 288 (sp)`. After testing, the `fsd `command also has this situation

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87563ceb-6e3b-429d-ae39-51ba54636cd1)


**Necessary information on versions**
- NEMU version: 34ba2259558ed89f5a042179ef0a9131e53ce037 (HEAD, origin/master, origin/HEAD)

problem_statement: Observed behavior: when `mstatus.fs = 0` disables floating-point state, XiangShan can still treat a compressed floating-point instruction as decodable in the frontend RVC predecode/expansion path. In the reported case, `fld fa0, 288(sp)` is encoded as the compressed instruction `c.fldsp fa0, 288(sp)`, but XiangShan expands it to the 32-bit floating-point form before the illegal-instruction exception is finalized. This can make exception reporting use the expanded instruction bits instead of the original 16-bit compressed encoding, leading to incorrect state such as `mtval`. Expected behavior: when `mstatus.fs = 0`, `c.fldsp` must be marked illegal during RVC predecode, and the original compressed instruction bits must be preserved for exception reporting. Affected function: the frontend RVC predecode and compressed-instruction expansion path. Trigger condition: software executes the compressed floating-point load encoded as `c.fldsp` while `mstatus.fs = 0`; the reproduced example is the stack-pointer load assembled from `fld fa0, 288(sp)`.

problem_statement: In XiangShan's backend Dispatch logic for single-step debug handling, a self-flushing instruction can break single-step detection when the next instruction is allocated into the same reorder buffer (ROB) entry. With single-step enabled, if one instruction redirects and flushes itself, the following instruction that reuses that ROB entry can be treated as if it were the same instruction, so Dispatch does not mark it with the required single-step state and exception. The expected behavior is specific: after such a self-flush redirect, an instruction that reuses the same ROB entry must still be recognized as a new machine instruction and be dispatched with single-step asserted and the corresponding exception set. The affected function is the backend Dispatch logic that assigns single-step/exception state to instructions entering the ROB. The trigger condition is single-step mode plus a redirect from an instruction that flushes itself, followed by the next instruction reusing the same ROB entry.

problem_statement: The `dret` handling logic in `DretEventModule` restores the privilege state incorrectly when leaving debug mode. If the saved return privilege in `dcsr.PRV` is Machine mode and the saved virtualization bit in `dcsr.V` is set, the module can restore a state equivalent to `PRV=M` with virtualization still enabled. The expected behavior is specific: a `dret` that returns to Machine mode must clear virtualization (`V=0`), while a `dret` that returns to a lower privilege mode should still restore the saved virtualization bit. The bug is triggered on a debug return to Machine mode with `dcsr.V=1`.

title: fix(dbltrp): fix sdt/dte interaction logic
body:
* menvcfg.DTE only control Smode dbltrp. Thus mstatus.sdt will not
    control by DTE.
  * as sstatus is alias of mstatus, when menvcfg.DTE close write
    sstatus.sdt cannot lead to shadow write of mstatus.sdt. As a result,
    we add wmask of sdt, when write source is from alias write.
    While vsstatus is not alias of any other CSR fields, so origin logic
    is correct.

  * align spike/nemu logic to xiangshan. see spike pr[60](https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/riscv-isa-sim/pull/60), NEMU pr[688](https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/NEMU/pull/688) for detail.

problem_statement: In XiangShan's CSR double-trap status handling for the `SDT` bit in the `mstatus`/`sstatus` path, `mstatus` is the machine status CSR and `sstatus` is its supervisor alias. The behavior is wrong when `menvcfg.DTE=0`: the logic applies `DTE` to the machine `mstatus.sdt` path as well, so software can no longer reliably write and read `mstatus.sdt` through the machine CSR, while a write through the aliased `sstatus.sdt` field can still change the underlying machine SDT state even though the supervisor view should be disabled. Expected behavior is specific and testable: `menvcfg.DTE` should only control the supervisor-mode view of double-trap state. When `DTE=0`, direct accesses to `mstatus.sdt` must still take effect and read back through `mstatus`, `sstatus.sdt` must read as 0, and writing `sstatus.sdt` must not modify the underlying `mstatus.sdt`. The bug is triggered when software accesses the SDT bit with `menvcfg.DTE` disabled, especially when mixing direct `mstatus` accesses with alias `sstatus` accesses.

    var nReleaseEntries = 0

problem_statement: Observed behavior: after cache-management operation (CMO) requests are merged into the DCache TileLink A channel through the CMOUnit in MissQueue, the DCache TileLink client/source-ID parameter calculation still sizes the source-ID space from only the miss-entry count and release-entry count. In a CMO-enabled DCache configuration, that generated capacity is one source slot too small for the traffic sources that can issue through the DCache client. Expected behavior: when the MissQueue CMOUnit path is present, DCache TileLink client parameter generation must include one additional source-ID slot for CMO traffic, so the DCache entry budget is at least nMissEntries + nReleaseEntries + 1 and the advertised TileLink client source range is large enough for that extra CMO slot. Affected function: DCache TileLink client parameter generation in HasDCacheParameters within the DCache wrapper. Trigger condition: elaborating a configuration that includes the CMO path added for merging CMO requests into the DCache TileLink A channel.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan

TEST_NAME="newcsr_vstopei_permission"
TEST_LOG="/home/xiangshan/${TEST_NAME}.log"
TEST_FILE="/home/xiangshan/src/test/scala/xiangshan/backend/fu/NewCSR/NewCSRVstopeiPermissionTest.scala"
SHIM_FILE="/home/xiangshan/difftest/src/main/scala/DiffSyncAIAEventCompat.scala"

write_compat_shim() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "${SHIM_FILE}")"
  cat > "${SHIM_FILE}" <<'EOF'
package difftest

import chisel3._

// This only restores a missing difftest event type in the pinned submodule.
class DiffSyncAIAEvent extends DiffAIAXtopeiEvent {
  val hgeip = UInt(64.W)
  override val desiredCppName: String = "sync_aia"
}
EOF
}

write_test_file() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "${TEST_FILE}")"
  cat > "${TEST_FILE}" <<'EOF'
package xiangshan.backend.fu.NewCSR

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import freechips.rocketchip.rocket.CSRs
import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.should.Matchers
import top.DefaultConfig
import xiangshan.{XSCoreParamsKey, XSTileKey}

class NewCSRVstopeiPermissionHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  private val dut = Module(new NewCSR)

  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val reqValid = Input(Bool())
    val reqWen = Input(Bool())
    val reqRen = Input(Bool())
    val reqAddr = Input(UInt(12.W))
    val reqWdata = Input(UInt(64.W))

    val reqReady = Output(Bool())
    val respValid = Output(Bool())
    val respEXII = Output(Bool())
    val respEXVI = Output(Bool())
    val respRData = Output(UInt(64.W))
  })

  dut.io.fromTop := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.fromTop)
  dut.io.in.valid := io.reqValid
  dut.io.in.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.in.bits)
  dut.io.in.bits.wen := io.reqWen
  dut.io.in.bits.ren := io.reqRen
  dut.io.in.bits.addr := io.reqAddr
  dut.io.in.bits.wdata := io.reqWdata
  dut.io.trapInst := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.trapInst)
  dut.io.fromMem := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.fromMem)
  dut.io.fromRob := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.fromRob)
  dut.io.fromVecExcpMod := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.fromVecExcpMod)
  dut.io.perf := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.perf)
  dut.platformIRP := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.platformIRP)
  dut.nonMaskableIRP := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.nonMaskableIRP)
  dut.io.out.ready := true.B
  dut.io.fetchMalTval := 0.U
  dut.fromAIA := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.fromAIA)

  io.reqReady := dut.io.in.ready
  io.respValid := dut.io.out.valid
  io.respEXII := dut.io.out.bits.EX_II
  io.respEXVI := dut.io.out.bits.EX_VI
  io.respRData := dut.io.out.bits.rData
}

class NewCSRVstopeiPermissionTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "NewCSR"

  private val defaultConfig = new DefaultConfig
  implicit private val config: Parameters = defaultConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => defaultConfig(XSTileKey).head.copy()
  }

  private case class Response(exII: Boolean, exVI: Boolean, rData: BigInt)

  private def issue(
    c: NewCSRVstopeiPermissionHarness,
    wen: Boolean,
    ren: Boolean,
    addr: Int,
    wdata: BigInt = 0,
  ): Response = {
    var spins = 0
    while (!c.io.reqReady.peek().litToBoolean && spins < 10) {
      c.clock.step()
      spins += 1
    }
    c.io.reqReady.expect(true.B)

    c.io.reqValid.poke(true.B)
    c.io.reqWen.poke(wen.B)
    c.io.reqRen.poke(ren.B)
    c.io.reqAddr.poke(addr.U(12.W))
    c.io.reqWdata.poke(wdata.U(64.W))
    c.clock.step()

    c.io.reqValid.poke(false.B)

    spins = 0
    while (!c.io.respValid.peek().litToBoolean && spins < 10) {
      c.clock.step()
      spins += 1
    }
    c.io.respValid.expect(true.B)

    val response = Response(
      exII = c.io.respEXII.peek().litToBoolean,
      exVI = c.io.respEXVI.peek().litToBoolean,
      rData = c.io.respRData.peek().litValue,
    )
    c.clock.step()

    c.io.reqWen.poke(false.B)
    c.io.reqRen.poke(false.B)
    c.io.reqAddr.poke(0.U)
    c.io.reqWdata.poke(0.U)

    response
  }

  it should "trap vstopei accesses when hstatus.VGEIN selects an unimplemented guest file" in {
    test(new NewCSRVstopeiPermissionHarness) { c =>
      c.io.reqValid.poke(false.B)
      c.io.reqWen.poke(false.B)
      c.io.reqRen.poke(false.B)
      c.io.reqAddr.poke(0.U)
      c.io.reqWdata.poke(0.U)

      c.reset.poke(true.B)
      c.clock.step(2)
      c.reset.poke(false.B)
      c.clock.step(1)

      val invalidVgein = 6
      val hstatusWrite = BigInt(invalidVgein) << 12

      val writeResp = issue(c, wen = true, ren = false, addr = CSRs.hstatus, wdata = hstatusWrite)
      writeResp.exII shouldBe false
      writeResp.exVI shouldBe false

      val hstatusResp = issue(c, wen = false, ren = true, addr = CSRs.hstatus)
      hstatusResp.exII shouldBe false
      hstatusResp.exVI shouldBe false
      ((hstatusResp.rData >> 12) & 0x3f) shouldBe invalidVgein

      val vstopeiResp = issue(c, wen = false, ren = true, addr = CSRs.vstopei)
      vstopeiResp.exII shouldBe true
      vstopeiResp.exVI shouldBe false
    }
  }
}
EOF
}

  export JAVA_HOME="${JAVA_HOME:-/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64}"

  timeout 1200s mill -i xiangshan.test.testOnly xiangshan.backend.fu.NewCSR.NewCSRVstopeiPermissionTest
}

write_compat_shim
write_test_file

status=0
run_test > "${TEST_LOG}" 2>&1 || status=$?

cat "${TEST_LOG}"
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [ "${status}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "${status}"
problem_statement: Observed behavior: In XiangShan's AIA CSR handling, `hstatus.VGEIN` selects the guest external interrupt file used by `vstopei`. If software writes `hstatus.VGEIN` to a value that does not correspond to an implemented guest external interrupt file, `NewCSR` can still treat a later `vstopei` access as a normal CSR access; in the verified case, an M-mode read of `vstopei` completes instead of raising an exception. Expected behavior: once `hstatus.VGEIN` names an unimplemented guest external interrupt file, an M-mode access to CSR `vstopei` must raise an illegal instruction exception rather than returning CSR data. Affected function: the AIA CSR permission and exception checks in `NewCSR` for `vstopei`. Trigger condition: software writes an out-of-range value to `hstatus.VGEIN` and then accesses `vstopei`.

title: fix(aia): external interrupt priority from PLIC or IMSIC
body:
* The current external interrupts come from two sources, `PLIC` and `IMSIC`.

* The external interrupt priority number of PLIC is `0`, and the external interrupt priority number of IMSIC is `1~2047`.

* The case where the priority number is greater than `255` is added to the interrupt priority comparison method.

* The priority number of each interrupt in the `iprios array` occupies `8` bits, and its read data is masked by the corresponding bit of the `xie` register, so when writing the `xie` register, the `read data` of the `iprios array` needs to be updated.

* Note: The external interrupt source comes from PLIC or IMSIC, the commit messages in NEMU and ready-to-run repositories are wrong.

package xiangshan

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import firrtl2.options.TargetDirAnnotation
import xiangshan.backend.fu.NewCSR._

class InterruptFilterPriorityCheck extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val caseIid = Output(UInt(12.W))
  })

  private def getField(target: AnyRef, name: String): Option[AnyRef] = {
    target.getClass.getMethods
      .find(m => m.getParameterCount == 0 && m.getName == name)
      .map(_.invoke(target).asInstanceOf[AnyRef])
  }

  private def lookupPath(root: AnyRef, path: Seq[String]): Option[AnyRef] = {
    path.foldLeft(Option(root)) { case (current, name) => current.flatMap(getField(_, name)) }
  }

  private def connectOptionalPath(root: AnyRef, path: Seq[String], value: BigInt): Unit = {
    lookupPath(root, path).foreach {
      case data: Data => data := value.U(data.getWidth.W).asTypeOf(data)
      case other => throw new IllegalArgumentException(s"Path ${path.mkString(".")} is not Data: ${other.getClass.getName}")
    }
  }

  private val filter = Module(new InterruptFilter)
  filter.io.in := DontCare
  filter.io.in.mip.MEIP := true.B
  filter.io.in.mip.MSIP := true.B
  filter.io.in.mie.MEIE := true.B
  filter.io.in.mie.MSIE := true.B
  filter.io.in.mideleg.MEI := false.B
  filter.io.in.mideleg.MSI := false.B
  filter.io.in.vsip.SEIP := false.B
  filter.io.in.vsie.SEIE := false.B
  filter.io.in.hvictl.VTI := false.B
  filter.io.in.hvictl.DPR := false.B
  filter.io.in.debugIntr := false.B
  filter.io.in.debugMode := false.B
  filter.io.in.nmi := false.B
  filter.io.in.mnstatusNMIE := false.B
  filter.io.in.hvictl.IID := 0.U.asTypeOf(filter.io.in.hvictl.IID)
  filter.io.in.hvictl.IPRIO := 0.U.asTypeOf(filter.io.in.hvictl.IPRIO)
  filter.io.in.hstatus.VGEIN := 0.U.asTypeOf(filter.io.in.hstatus.VGEIN)
  filter.io.in.miprios := ((BigInt(10) << (InterruptNO.MEI * 8)) | (BigInt(1) << (InterruptNO.MSI * 8))).U((64 * 8).W)
  connectOptionalPath(filter.io.in, Seq("platform", "meip"), 1)

  io.caseIid := filter.io.out.mtopi.IID.asUInt

  behavior of "InterruptFilter"
  it should "treat platform external interrupt as zero-priority MEI" in {
    test(new InterruptFilterPriorityCheck).withAnnotations(Seq(
      TargetDirAnnotation("build/interrupt-filter-priority-regression")

problem_statement: XiangShan's `InterruptFilter`, which chooses the highest-priority pending interrupt, does not correctly distinguish a machine external interrupt (MEI) coming from the platform interrupt source (`PLIC`/platform signal) from one coming from the IMSIC path. In the failing case, both MEI and machine software interrupt (MSI) are pending and enabled, and the programmed `miprios` value for MEI is numerically larger than MSI's. The filter still compares that platform-sourced MEI using the programmed `miprios` entry, so it can report MSI as the top machine interrupt. Expected behavior: when the pending MEI is from the platform source, `InterruptFilter` must treat it as architectural priority 0 during arbitration and therefore select MEI ahead of MSI and other machine-level interrupts even if the programmed `miprios` value would otherwise make MEI lose.

title: fix(DCache): fix wrong condition for blocking lr
body:
Following lr should be blocked when previous lr's resv_set is still valid, which means `lrsc_count > 0`.

In previous PR #3017 and #4117, `lrsc_count > 8` is used as block condition, and stop update `lrsc_count` when it reaches 8, fix it now.

import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters

import xiangshan.cache._
import xiangshan.{DebugOptionsKey, XSCoreParamsKey, XSTileKey}

class MainPipeLrscHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends DCacheModule {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val overrideValid = Input(Bool())
    val overrideLr = Input(Bool())
    val overrideSc = Input(Bool())
    val overrideCanDoAmo = Input(Bool())
    val overrideAddr = Input(UInt(PAddrBits.W))
    val blockLr = Output(Bool())
  })

  BoringUtils.addSource(io.overrideValid, "mainpipe_lrsc_override_valid")
  BoringUtils.addSource(io.overrideLr, "mainpipe_lrsc_override_lr")
  BoringUtils.addSource(io.overrideSc, "mainpipe_lrsc_override_sc")
  BoringUtils.addSource(io.overrideCanDoAmo, "mainpipe_lrsc_override_can_do_amo")
  BoringUtils.addSource(io.overrideAddr, "mainpipe_lrsc_override_addr")

  val dut = Module(new MainPipe)

  dut.io.probe_req.valid := false.B
  dut.io.probe_req.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.probe_req.bits)
  dut.io.refill_req.valid := false.B
  dut.io.refill_req.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.refill_req.bits)
  dut.io.store_req.valid := false.B
  dut.io.store_req.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.store_req.bits)
  dut.io.atomic_req.valid := false.B
  dut.io.atomic_req.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.atomic_req.bits)

  dut.io.miss_req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.miss_resp := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.miss_resp)
  dut.io.refill_info.valid := false.B
  dut.io.refill_info.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.refill_info.bits)
  dut.io.wbq_block_miss_req := false.B
  dut.io.wb.ready := true.B
  dut.io.wb_ready_dup.foreach(_ := true.B)

  dut.io.data_read := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.data_read)
  dut.io.data_readline.ready := true.B
  dut.io.data_resp := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.data_resp)
  dut.io.readline_error_delayed := false.B
  dut.io.data_write.ready := true.B
  dut.io.data_write_ready_dup.foreach(_ := true.B)

  dut.io.meta_read.ready := true.B
  dut.io.meta_resp := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.meta_resp)
  dut.io.meta_write.ready := true.B
  dut.io.extra_meta_resp := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.extra_meta_resp)
  dut.io.error_flag_write.ready := true.B
  dut.io.prefetch_flag_write.ready := true.B
  dut.io.access_flag_write.ready := true.B

  dut.io.tag_read.ready := true.B
  dut.io.tag_resp := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.tag_resp)
  dut.io.tag_write.ready := true.B
  dut.io.tag_write_ready_dup.foreach(_ := true.B)

  dut.io.replace_way.way := 0.U
  dut.io.replace_block := false.B
  dut.io.sms_agt_evict_req.ready := true.B

  dut.io.invalid_resv_set := false.B
  dut.io.pseudo_error.valid := false.B
  dut.io.pseudo_error.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.pseudo_error.bits)
  dut.io.force_write := false.B

  io.blockLr := dut.io.block_lr
}

class MainPipeLrscBlockTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  private val baseConfig = new DefaultConfig
  implicit val defaultConfig: Parameters = baseConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => baseConfig(XSTileKey).head.copy()
    case PerfCounterOptionsKey => PerfCounterOptions(
      enablePerfPrint = false,
      enablePerfDB = false,
      perfLevel = XSPerfLevel.CRITICAL,
      perfDBHartID = 0
    )
  }.alter((site, here, up) => {
    case LogUtilsOptionsKey => LogUtilsOptions(
      here(DebugOptionsKey).EnableDebug,
      here(DebugOptionsKey).EnablePerfDebug,
      here(DebugOptionsKey).FPGAPlatform
    )
  })

  behavior of "MainPipe LRSC block"

  it should "keep blocking LR while the reservation set is still alive" in {
    test(new MainPipeLrscHarness) { c =>
      c.io.overrideValid.poke(false.B)
      c.io.overrideLr.poke(false.B)
      c.io.overrideSc.poke(false.B)
      c.io.overrideCanDoAmo.poke(false.B)
      c.io.overrideAddr.poke("h1000".U)
      c.io.blockLr.expect(false.B)

      c.io.overrideValid.poke(true.B)
      c.io.overrideLr.poke(true.B)
      c.io.overrideCanDoAmo.poke(true.B)
      c.clock.step()

      c.io.overrideValid.poke(false.B)
      c.io.overrideLr.poke(false.B)
      c.io.overrideCanDoAmo.poke(false.B)
      c.clock.step(56)
      c.io.blockLr.expect(true.B)
      c.clock.step(8)
      c.io.blockLr.expect(false.B)
    }
  }
}
EOF

set +e
mill -i -Djvm-xmx=8G -Djvm-xss=64m xiangshan.test.testOnly cache.MainPipeLrscBlockTest 2>&1 | tee "$RUN_LOG"
status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e

if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
  emit_result "PASS"
else
  emit_result "FAIL"
fi

exit "$status"
problem_statement: Observed behavior: in the DCache MainPipe LR/SC handling, the logic that blocks a new load-reserved (LR) can be released before the reservation created by the previous LR has actually expired. As a result, the pipeline stops blocking a following LR even though the earlier reservation is still valid. Expected behavior: after an LR creates a reservation, every following LR must remain blocked until that reservation is invalidated or its full validity window expires. Affected function: DCache MainPipe logic that tracks LR/SC reservation validity and decides when a following LR should be blocked. Trigger condition: one LR succeeds, no invalidation occurs, and another LR arrives near the end of the first reservation's lifetime, while that reservation is still valid.

title: fix(LoadUnit): fix misalign exception and clearer uncache semantics
body:
I didn't REVIEW this pr(https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/pull/4326) carefully. :skull:
It resulted in a change in the semantics of the modification.

---

The loadAddrMisaligned exception is generated when misaligned accesses uncache space.

---

A misaligned load sets a loadAddrMisaligned exception at the s0 flag to ensure that it only enters the loadmisalignbuffer and has no other side effects.
So it will prevent s2_uncache from spawning properly.
Previously we used an additional `s2_un_misalign_exception` to flag this.
Now, after examining the semantics of s2_uncache, the semantics of s2_uncache can be appropriately represented by directly removing the excepiont related signals

repo.description: Open-source high-performance RISC-V processor

commits.message: fix(LoadUnit): fix misalign exception and clearer uncache semantics

resolved_issues.title: fix(LDU): nc is also not mis-aligned

fix_patch:
diff --git a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/LoadUnit.scala b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/LoadUnit.scala
index e8d66de7c28..e4cc2d0d204 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/LoadUnit.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/LoadUnit.scala
@@ -1177,8 +1177,6 @@ class LoadUnit(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSModule
   val s2_prf    = s2_in.isPrefetch
   val s2_hw_prf = s2_in.isHWPrefetch
   val s2_exception_vec = WireInit(s2_in.uop.exceptionVec)
-  val s2_un_misalign_exception =  s2_vecActive &&
-                                  (s2_trigger_debug_mode || ExceptionNO.selectByFuAndUnSelect(s2_exception_vec, LduCfg, Seq(loadAddrMisaligned)).asUInt.orR)
 
   // exception that may cause load addr to be invalid / illegal
   // if such exception happen, that inst and its exception info
@@ -1204,7 +1202,7 @@ class LoadUnit(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSModule
   }
   val s2_exception = s2_vecActive &&
                     (s2_trigger_debug_mode || ExceptionNO.selectByFu(s2_exception_vec, LduCfg).asUInt.orR)
-  val s2_uncache = !s2_prf && !s2_exception && !s2_un_misalign_exception && !s2_in.tlbMiss && s2_actually_uncache
+  val s2_uncache = !s2_prf && !s2_in.tlbMiss && s2_actually_uncache
   val s2_mis_align = s2_valid && GatedValidRegNext(io.csrCtrl.hd_misalign_ld_enable) &&
                      s2_out.isMisalign && !s2_in.misalignWith16Byte && !s2_exception_vec(breakPoint) && !s2_trigger_debug_mode && !s2_uncache
   val (s2_fwd_frm_d_chan, s2_fwd_data_frm_d_chan, s2_d_corrupt) = io.tl_d_channel.forward(s1_valid && s1_out.forward_tlDchannel, s1_out.mshrid, s1_out.paddr)

  dut.io.misalign_ldin.valid := false.B
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits := zeros(dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits)

  dut.io.tlb.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.tlb.resp.valid := true.B
  dut.io.tlb.resp.bits := zeros(dut.io.tlb.resp.bits)
  dut.io.tlb_hint := zeros(dut.io.tlb_hint)

  dut.io.tlb.resp.bits.miss := false.B

  dut.io.tlb.resp.bits.ptwBack := false.B
  dut.io.tlb.resp.bits.paddr.foreach { x =>

  dut.io.dcache.resp.valid := false.B

  dut.io.lsq.uncache.valid := false.B

  dut.io.lsq.ldin.ready := true.B
  dut.io.lsq.ld_raw_data := zeros(dut.io.lsq.ld_raw_data)

class LoadUnitFirstPassUncacheMisalignTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers with HasTestAnnos {

  implicit val config: Parameters = defaultConfig

        intPreg = IntPregParams(
          numEntries = 64,
          numRead = Some(14),
          numWrite = Some(8),
        ),
      )
    }
    .alter((site, here, up) => {
      case LogUtilsOptionsKey => LogUtilsOptions(
        here(DebugOptionsKey).EnableDebug,
        here(DebugOptionsKey).EnablePerfDebug,
        here(DebugOptionsKey).FPGAPlatform
      )
      case PerfCounterOptionsKey => PerfCounterOptions(
        here(DebugOptionsKey).EnablePerfDebug && !here(DebugOptionsKey).FPGAPlatform,
        here(DebugOptionsKey).EnableRollingDB && !here(DebugOptionsKey).FPGAPlatform,
        XSPerfLevel.withName(here(DebugOptionsKey).PerfLevel),
        0
      )
    })

  behavior of "LoadUnit first-pass uncache misalign routing"

  it should "keep a misaligned NC load on the uncache path instead of entering the misalign buffer" in {
    test(new LoadUnitFirstPassUncacheMisalignHarness).withAnnotations(testAnnos) { dut =>
      dut.io.start.poke(false.B)
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.start.poke(true.B)
      dut.clock.step()
      dut.io.start.poke(false.B)

      var sawLoadQueueEntry = false
      var sawUpdateAddrValid = false
      var sawNc = false
      var sawMisalignBuf = false

      for (_ <- 0 until 8) {
        if (dut.io.misalignBufValid.peek().litToBoolean) {
          sawMisalignBuf = true
        }
        if (dut.io.lsqLdinValid.peek().litToBoolean) {
          sawLoadQueueEntry = true
          if (dut.io.lsqLdinUpdateAddrValid.peek().litToBoolean) {
            sawUpdateAddrValid = true
          }
          if (dut.io.lsqLdinNc.peek().litToBoolean) {
            sawNc = true
          }
        }
        dut.clock.step()
      }

      println(s"summary: sawLoadQueueEntry=$sawLoadQueueEntry sawNc=$sawNc sawUpdateAddrValid=$sawUpdateAddrValid sawMisalignBuf=$sawMisalignBuf")
      assert(sawLoadQueueEntry, "LoadUnit never produced a load-queue entry for the misaligned NC load")
      assert(sawNc, "The load-queue entry was not marked as NC")
      assert(sawUpdateAddrValid, "The misaligned NC load never exposed updateAddrValid to the load queue")
      assert(!sawMisalignBuf, "The misaligned NC load entered the misalign buffer")
    }
  }
}

status=0

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if timeout 1200 "$MILL_CMD" -i xiangshan.test.testOnly xiangshan.LoadUnitFirstPassUncacheMisalignTest; then
  echo "TEST: loadunit_first_pass_uncache_misalign ... PASS"
else
  status=$?
  echo "TEST: loadunit_first_pass_uncache_misalign ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$status"
problem_statement: Observed behavior: In XiangShan's memory load pipeline, the LoadUnit routes a first-issue load to non-cacheable (NC/uncache) memory with a misaligned address into the misalign buffer as soon as the loadAddrMisaligned condition is set. This suppresses the uncache path, so the load queue does not receive the request as an NC load and does not receive the updated address information for that access. Expected behavior: a misaligned first-issue NC load should still preserve uncache semantics. It should produce a load-queue entry marked as NC, carry valid updated-address information, and not be consumed solely by the misalign buffer. Affected function: LoadUnit routing between uncache handling and misaligned-load handling in the load pipeline. Trigger condition: a first-issue load targets NC/uncache space, misaligned-load handling is enabled, and the access address is misaligned.

title: fix(LoadUnit): uncache should not be generated when page fault
body:
As the comment says, even if a `PF` is generated, an address is still generated for `PMP/PMA` checking, which can lead to some strange responses.
Since the previous(https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/pull/4426) modification removed `s2_exception`, this resulted in the incorrect generation of `s2_uncache`.

This is now represented using clearer semantics:
`s2_actually_uncache`: this real physical address is for uncache space.
The `s2_uncache` has been retained to distinguish if it's a request from prefetching, which may be handled in a subsequent change to **YQ senior sister**.

I synchronised the changes to StoreUnit in this pr(https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/pull/4441).

repo.name: XiangShan
repo.description: Open-source high-performance RISC-V processor

commits.message: fix(LoadUnit): uncache should not be generated when page fault

resolved_issues.title: fix(StoreUnit): no uncache store misalign of mmio
resolved_issues.body:
**Read this PR(https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/pull/4442) from LoadUnit first.**

---

In addition to the above, `nc` has been added to the misalign checks as well.
(https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/pull/4441/files#diff-cd162a95fcb65b10cf6ac087d3aac686ccb932ab4f5e270c0cfdb38437462b37L464-R471)

---

Currently, it is not to fully replace `s2_mmio` with `s2_actually_uncache` due to inconsistencies in the way `nc` and `mmio` are handled in the `StoreQueue`, so the original `s2_mmio` is still retained.
Other than that, there is no longer a need for an additional `s2_uncache`, as StoreUnit does not need to handle prefetching.

resolved_issues.title: fix(LoadUnit): fix misalign exception and clearer uncache semantics
resolved_issues.body:
I didn't REVIEW this pr(https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/pull/4326) carefully. :skull:
It resulted in a change in the semantics of the modification.

---

The loadAddrMisaligned exception is generated when misaligned accesses uncache space.

---

A misaligned load sets a loadAddrMisaligned exception at the s0 flag to ensure that it only enters the loadmisalignbuffer and has no other side effects.
So it will prevent s2_uncache from spawning properly.
Previously we used an additional `s2_un_misalign_exception` to flag this.

  dut.io.ldin.bits.uop.fuType := FuType.ldu.U
  dut.io.ldin.bits.uop.fuOpType := LSUOpType.ld

  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.vaddr := "h1000".U
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.fullva := "h1000".U
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.mask := "hff".U
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.uop.pc := "h80000000".U
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.uop.fuType := FuType.ldu.U
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.uop.fuOpType := LSUOpType.ld
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.uop.rfWen := true.B
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.uop.pdest := 1.U
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.uop.exceptionVec(ExceptionNO.loadPageFault) := true.B
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.isFrmMisAlignBuf := true.B
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.isFinalSplit := true.B
  dut.io.misalign_ldin.bits.misalignNeedWakeUp := false.B

  dut.io.tlb.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.tlb.resp.valid := true.B
  dut.io.tlb.resp.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.tlb.resp.bits)
  dut.io.tlb.resp.bits.paddr(0) := "h2000".U
  dut.io.tlb.resp.bits.paddr(1) := "h2000".U

  dut.io.dcache.debug_s2_dm_way_num := 0.U
  dut.io.dcache.debug_s2_real_way_num := 0.U

  tieForwardQuery(dut.io.sbuffer)
  tieForwardQuery(dut.io.ubuffer)
  tiePipeForwardQuery(dut.io.lsq.forward)

  dut.io.lsq.ldin.ready := true.B
  dut.io.lsq.uncache.valid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.uncache.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.uncache.bits)
  dut.io.lsq.ld_raw_data := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.ld_raw_data)
  dut.io.lsq.nc_ldin.valid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.nc_ldin.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.nc_ldin.bits)
  dut.io.lsq.stld_nuke_query.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.lsq.stld_nuke_query.resp.valid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.stld_nuke_query.resp.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.stld_nuke_query.resp.bits)
  dut.io.lsq.ldld_nuke_query.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.lsq.ldld_nuke_query.resp.valid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.ldld_nuke_query.resp.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.ldld_nuke_query.resp.bits)
  dut.io.lsq.lqDeqPtr := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.lqDeqPtr)

  dut.io.tl_d_channel := zeroOf(dut.io.tl_d_channel)
  dut.io.forward_mshr.forward_mshr := false.B
  dut.io.forward_mshr.forwardData.foreach(_ := 0.U)
  dut.io.forward_mshr.forward_result_valid := false.B

  val accessFaultSeen = RegInit(false.B)
  val lsqPageFaultSeen = RegInit(false.B)
  val lsqAccessFaultSeen = RegInit(false.B)
  val killSeen = RegInit(false.B)

  accessFaultSeen := accessFaultSeen || (dut.io.ldout.valid && dut.io.ldout.bits.uop.exceptionVec(ExceptionNO.loadAccessFault))
  lsqPageFaultSeen := lsqPageFaultSeen || (dut.io.lsq.ldin.fire && dut.io.lsq.ldin.bits.uop.exceptionVec(ExceptionNO.loadPageFault))
  lsqAccessFaultSeen := lsqAccessFaultSeen || (dut.io.lsq.ldin.fire && dut.io.lsq.ldin.bits.uop.exceptionVec(ExceptionNO.loadAccessFault))
  killSeen := killSeen || (observeKill && dut.io.dcache.s2_kill)

  io.pageFaultSeen := pageFaultSeen
  io.accessFaultSeen := accessFaultSeen
  io.lsqPageFaultSeen := lsqPageFaultSeen
  io.lsqAccessFaultSeen := lsqAccessFaultSeen
  io.killSeen := killSeen
}

class LoadUnitPageFaultUncacheTest extends XSTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "LoadUnit page fault uncache handling"

  private val testConfig = config.alter((site, here, up) => {
    case LogUtilsOptionsKey => LogUtilsOptions(
      here(DebugOptionsKey).EnableDebug,
      here(DebugOptionsKey).EnablePerfDebug,
      here(DebugOptionsKey).FPGAPlatform
    )
    case PerfCounterOptionsKey => PerfCounterOptions(
      here(DebugOptionsKey).EnablePerfDebug && !here(DebugOptionsKey).FPGAPlatform,
      here(DebugOptionsKey).EnableRollingDB && !here(DebugOptionsKey).FPGAPlatform,
      XSPerfLevel.withName(here(DebugOptionsKey).PerfLevel),
      0
    )
  })

  it should "avoid generating an uncache kill for a scalar load when translation already raised a page fault" in {
    test(new LoadUnitPageFaultWrapper(false)(testConfig)).withAnnotations(testAnnos) { dut =>
      dut.clock.step(8)
      dut.io.requestSeen.peek().litToBoolean shouldBe true
      dut.io.pageFaultSeen.peek().litToBoolean shouldBe true
      dut.io.killSeen.peek().litToBoolean shouldBe false
    }
  }

  it should "avoid adding a load access fault on the misalign-buffer path when translation already raised a page fault" in {
    test(new LoadUnitPageFaultWrapper(true)(testConfig)).withAnnotations(testAnnos) { dut =>
      dut.clock.step(8)
      dut.io.requestSeen.peek().litToBoolean shouldBe true
      dut.io.lsqPageFaultSeen.peek().litToBoolean shouldBe true
      dut.io.lsqAccessFaultSeen.peek().litToBoolean shouldBe false
      dut.io.killSeen.peek().litToBoolean shouldBe false
    }
  }
}
SCALAEOF

rm -rf out/xiangshan

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"

status=0
timeout 1200 mill -i xiangshan.test.testOnly xiangshan.LoadUnitPageFaultUncacheTest
status=$?

if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$status"
problem_statement: Observed behavior: in the LoadUnit, a load may still be treated as an uncache or MMIO access after address translation has already reported a load page fault, because the generated address is still used for PMP/PMA memory checks. That can trigger uncache-side control responses such as a cache kill even though the load is already faulting. Expected behavior: if translation reports a load page fault, the operation should be handled only as a page-faulting load; it must not also be classified as uncache/MMIO or produce cache-kill behavior based on the generated address. Affected function: the LoadUnit logic that decides uncache/MMIO handling from the translated address and PMP/PMA results. Trigger condition: a load gets a translation page fault while the generated address would otherwise fall into MMIO or other uncache space.

title: fix(vstopi): remove SEI from Candidate 4
body:
* if hvictl.VTI = 0:
* the highest-priority pending-and-enabled major interrupt indicated
* by vsip and vsie other than a supervisor external interrupt(code 9),
* using the priority numbers assigned by hviprio1 and hviprio2. 
* 
* A hypervisor can choose to employ registers hviprio1 and hviprio2
* when emulating the (virtual) supervisor-level iprio array accessed
* indirectly through siselect and sireg (really vsiselect and vsireg)
* for a virtual hart. For interrupts not in the subset supported by
* hviprio1 and hviprio2, the priority number bytes in the emulated
* iprio array can be read-only zeros.

problem_statement: Observed behavior: The `InterruptFilter` logic that produces `vstopi` (the virtual supervisor top interrupt selection) can choose a supervisor external interrupt (`SEI`, interrupt 9) on the `hvictl.VTI = 0` arbitration path. In the verified failing case, both `SEI` and supervisor software interrupt (`SSI`, interrupt 1) are pending and enabled in `vsip`/`vsie`, all `hviprio1`/`hviprio2` priority bytes are zero, and `vstopi` reports `SEI` instead of `SSI`. Expected behavior: When `hvictl.VTI = 0`, `vstopi` should select the highest-priority pending-and-enabled virtual supervisor major interrupt indicated by `vsip` and `vsie` other than `SEI`, using the priorities from `hviprio1` and `hviprio2`. In the verified zero-priority case with only `SEI` and `SSI` active, the selected interrupt must be `SSI`, not `SEI`. Affected function: the `InterruptFilter` arbitration that generates `vstopi` in XiangShan's CSR interrupt path. Trigger condition: `hvictl.VTI` is `0`, `SEI` is pending and enabled in `vsip`/`vsie`, and another virtual supervisor interrupt is also pending and enabled; the verified reproducer uses `SSI` with all `hviprio1`/`hviprio2` bytes equal to zero.

Bug descritpions:
* When there is a cacheline with `B` permission in DCache, and the `LoadPipe` execute `prefetch_w` requires BtoT, if there are 3 `BtoT`s in `MissQueue` at this time, this miss will still enter `MissQueue`.

How to fix:
* When a `BtoT` request appears in `LoadPipe`, it is necessary to confirm with `MissQueue` that the number of `BtoT` requests in the same set is less than `nWays - 1(3)`.

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in the DCache load path, a `prefetch_w` request that hits a cache line already present with `B` permission and therefore needs a `BtoT` permission upgrade can still be treated as a real `MissQueue` miss even when `MissQueue` already contains `nWays - 1` outstanding `BtoT` requests for that same cache set. In that case the request may proceed as a live miss instead of being replayed. Expected behavior: `MissQueue`, which tracks outstanding DCache misses and permission upgrades, must reject the request for the request's own cache set once same-set `BtoT` occupancy has reached `nWays - 1` (3 in the default 4-way configuration); the load should report a miss-queue nack/replay and retry later rather than creating a live miss entry. Affected function: `LoadPipe` handling of `prefetch_w` `BtoT` growth requests when handing them to `MissQueue`. Trigger condition: a `prefetch_w` on a DCache-resident line in `B` state while the relevant cache set already has `nWays - 1` outstanding `BtoT` upgrades.

title: fix(TrapEntry): hardwareError should be a memory exception
body:
Currently, the access memory generates hwe exception for bus error and the frontend generates iaf exception for bus error .
We plan to have the frontend also generate hwe exception in kmhV3.

---

HardwareError should belong to memory access exception, and use virtual addresses as the value of xtval when trapping.

Previously, no exception types were added for HardwareError to handle in trapEvent, which resulted in the inability to match and select valid xtval:
https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/blob/8769efd7b4782ab06aed08c14e330f602918c930/src/main/scala/xiangshan/backend/fu/NewCSR/CSREvents/TrapEntryMEvent.scala#L85-L90

---

**In addition**

Since fetch may also produce hardwareError exception in theory, and hardwareError exception produced by fetch should write pc to xtval.
Therefore, I have written a more accurate version(https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/pull/4765). 
Please consider which solution we should adopt.

Now, we are trying to distinguish between hardwareError exceptrion from fetch and memory access.

However, I noticed that the front end has not yet implemented hardwareError exception , and I am not sure what our plans are. 
https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/blob/8769efd7b4782ab06aed08c14e330f602918c930/src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/FrontendBundle.scala#L155-L170
Will the front end support hardwareError exception in the future? 

In any case, I have modified the other parts first.
I also have a simpler version that only affects memory access hardwareError exception(https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan/pull/4764).

**If do not plan to support hardwareError  exception for the front end, please ignore this PR.**

import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters
import xiangshan.backend.fu.NewCSR.CSRDefines.{HgatpMode, PrivMode, SatpMode, VirtMode}
import xiangshan.backend.fu.NewCSR.CSREvents.TrapEntryMEventModule

class TrapEntryHardwareErrorProbe(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val mtval = Output(UInt(64.W))
    val gva = Output(UInt(1.W))
    val interrupt = Output(UInt(1.W))
    val exceptionCode = Output(UInt(63.W))
  })

  val dut = Module(new TrapEntryMEventModule)

  dut.valid := true.B
  dut.in := DontCare

  dut.in.causeNO := Cat(0.U(1.W), ExceptionNO.hardwareError.U(63.W)).asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.causeNO))
  dut.in.trapPc := 0.U
  dut.in.trapPcGPA := 0.U
  dut.in.trapInst.valid := false.B
  dut.in.trapInst.bits := 0.U
  dut.in.fetchMalTval := 0.U
  dut.in.isCrossPageIPF := false.B
  dut.in.isHls := false.B
  dut.in.isFetchMalAddr := false.B
  dut.in.isFetchBkpt := false.B
  dut.in.trapIsForVSnonLeafPTE := false.B
  dut.in.hasDTExcp := false.B
  dut.in.iMode.PRVM := PrivMode.U.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.iMode.PRVM))
  dut.in.iMode.V := VirtMode.Off.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.iMode.V))
  dut.in.dMode.PRVM := PrivMode.S.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.dMode.PRVM))
  dut.in.dMode.V := VirtMode.On.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.dMode.V))
  dut.in.privState.PRVM := PrivMode.S.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.privState.PRVM))
  dut.in.privState.V := VirtMode.On.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.privState.V))
  dut.in.mstatus.MIE := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.mstatus.MIE))
  dut.in.satp.MODE := SatpMode.Bare.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.satp.MODE))
  dut.in.vsatp.MODE := SatpMode.Bare.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.vsatp.MODE))
  dut.in.hgatp.MODE := HgatpMode.Bare.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(dut.in.hgatp.MODE))
  dut.in.memExceptionVAddr := "h0000123456789abc".U
  dut.in.memExceptionGPAddr := 0.U
  dut.in.memExceptionIsForVSnonLeafPTE := false.B
  dut.in.pcFromXtvec := "h80000000".U

  io.mtval := dut.out.mtval.bits.ALL.asUInt
  io.gva := dut.out.mstatus.bits.GVA.asUInt
  io.interrupt := dut.out.mcause.bits.Interrupt.asUInt
  io.exceptionCode := dut.out.mcause.bits.ExceptionCode.asUInt
}

class TrapEntryHardwareErrorTest extends XSTester {
  behavior of "TrapEntryMEventModule"
  it should "treat hardwareError as a memory exception" in {
    test(new TrapEntryHardwareErrorProbe()(config)) { dut =>
      dut.clock.step()
      dut.io.mtval.expect("h0000123456789abc".U)
      dut.io.gva.expect(1.U)
      dut.io.interrupt.expect(0.U)
      dut.io.exceptionCode.expect(ExceptionNO.hardwareError.U)
    }
  }
}

export NOOP_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export XIANGSHAN_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export NEMU_HOME=/home/xiangshan/ready-to-run
export RISCV_HOME=/tools/riscv

status=0

timeout 1200s mill -i -Djvm-xmx=8G -Djvm-xss=256m \
  xiangshan.test.testOnly xiangshan.TrapEntryHardwareErrorTest >"$log_file" 2>&1 || status=$?

cat "$log_file"

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: trap_entry_hardware_error ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: trap_entry_hardware_error ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$status"
problem_statement: In XiangShan's machine-mode trap-entry logic (`TrapEntryMEvent`/`trapEvent`), a `hardwareError` raised by a load or store bus error is not treated as a data-memory exception. `hardwareError` is the trap cause used for this kind of bus error. As a result, trap entry can fail to write the faulting memory virtual address into the trap value register (`xtval`/`mtval`), and a virtualized data access can lose its guest virtual-address context. The expected behavior is that when a load or store triggers `hardwareError`, trap entry still reports the exception as `hardwareError`, records the faulting data virtual address in `xtval`/`mtval`, and preserves guest virtual-address state for virtualized accesses. This bug is triggered specifically when `hardwareError` comes from the load/store memory path.

title: fix(ICache,Ifu,InstrUncache): set tilelink user fields correctly
body:
- ICache,Ifu,InstrUncache: pick #4898
- ICache: declare MemBackTypeMMField()
- ICache: drop unused PrefetchField()

commits.message:
fix(ICache,Ifu): set memBackTypeMM and memPageTypeNC correctly (#4898)

`MemBackTypeMM`: requesting region backed by main memory (`!pmp.mmio`)
(don't care pbmt)
`MemPageTypeNC`: requesting `pbmt=nc` region (don't care backtype)

We need to tell L2 Cache about this via Tilelink to make it work.

This PR:
- ICache: Always work on main memory (`!pmp.mmio && pbmt=pmp`)
  - `MemBackTypeMM` is always true
  - `MemPageTypeNC` is always false (keep default value)
- Ifu/InstrUncache: Might be working on main memory, but pbmt=nc/io. Or
on real mmio region
  - `MemBackTypeMM = !f3_pmp_mmio`
  - `MemPageTypeNC = f3_itlb_pbmt === Pbmt.nc`

---------

Co-authored-by: Yanqin Li <maxpicca@qq.com>

fix(ICache): set tilelink user field properly

- follow-up #4898, declare MemBackTypeMMField()
- drop unused PrefetchField()
- set AliasField correctly

#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan

TEST_NAME="frontend_tl_user_fields_contract"
TEST_FILE="src/test/scala/xiangshan/frontend/FrontendTLUserFieldsContractTest.scala"
TEST_TARGET="xiangshan.frontend.FrontendTLUserFieldsContractTest"
MILL_VERSION="$(tr -d '\n' < .mill-version)"
MILL_BIN="/tools/mill/bin/mill-$MILL_VERSION"

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TEST_FILE")"
cat > "$TEST_FILE" <<'EOF'
package xiangshan.frontend

import coupledL2.{MemBackTypeMM, MemPageTypeNC}
import freechips.rocketchip.diplomacy.LazyModule
import freechips.rocketchip.util.BundleFieldBase
import huancun.{AliasKey, PrefetchKey}
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.should.Matchers
import top.DefaultConfig
import utility.ReqSourceKey
import xiangshan.{XSCoreParamsKey, XSTileKey}
import xiangshan.frontend.icache.ICache
import xiangshan.frontend.instruncache.{InstrUncache, InstrUncacheReq}

class FrontendTLUserFieldsContractTest extends AnyFlatSpec with Matchers {
  private val defaultConfig = new DefaultConfig
  private implicit val p: org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters = defaultConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => defaultConfig(XSTileKey).head
  }

  private def fieldNames(fields: Seq[BundleFieldBase]): Seq[String] = fields.map(_.key.name)

  private def fieldWidth(fields: Seq[BundleFieldBase], name: String): Int =
    fields.collectFirst { case field if field.key.name == name => field.data.getWidth }.getOrElse(-1)

  behavior of "Frontend TL user field contract"

  it should "declare the instruction uncache request metadata bundle" in {
    val req = new InstrUncacheReq
    req.elements.keySet should contain("memBackTypeMM")
    req.elements.keySet should contain("memPageTypeNC")
  }

  it should "advertise instruction uncache tilelink user fields" in {
    val instrUncache = LazyModule(new InstrUncache())
    val names = fieldNames(instrUncache.clientParameters.requestFields)

    names should contain(MemBackTypeMM.name)
    names should contain(MemPageTypeNC.name)
  }

  it should "advertise the icache tilelink user fields expected by L2" in {
    val icache = LazyModule(new ICache())
    val reqFields = icache.clientParameters.requestFields
    val names = fieldNames(reqFields)

    names should contain(ReqSourceKey.name)
    names should contain(MemBackTypeMM.name)
    names should contain(AliasKey.name)
    names should not contain PrefetchKey.name
    fieldWidth(reqFields, AliasKey.name) shouldBe 2
  }
}
EOF

rc=$?
