if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: $TEST_NAME ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: $TEST_NAME ... FAIL"
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
exit "$rc"
problem_statement: Observed behavior: the frontend TileLink user-field contract for instruction fetches is incomplete or incorrect. The IFU/InstrUncache path does not expose the MemBackTypeMM and MemPageTypeNC metadata that L2 needs to distinguish uncached fetches to main-memory-backed pbmt=nc/io regions from true MMIO fetches. The ICache refill client also advertises the wrong request-field contract: it is missing MemBackTypeMM, still advertises an unused prefetch field, and under the default configuration does not declare alias metadata with the expected 2-bit width. Expected behavior: frontend instruction-fetch requests must advertise the TileLink metadata needed by L2 to identify whether a fetch is backed by main memory (MemBackTypeMM) and whether the target page is non-cacheable (MemPageTypeNC). In the default ICache configuration, the declared request fields should include ReqSource, MemBackTypeMM, and a 2-bit alias field, and should not include a prefetch field. Affected function: frontend TileLink user-field declaration and request metadata interface for the ICache refill path and the IFU/InstrUncache uncached instruction-fetch path. Trigger condition: instruction fetch traffic that reaches L2 through the uncached IFU/InstrUncache path for pbmt=nc, pbmt=io, or MMIO regions, and default-configuration ICache refill traffic that depends on the declared frontend TileLink user-field contract.

title: feat(ICache): stall waylookup after exception until a flush
body:
Like #3139 and #3719, since we must receive a redirect after an exception (access fault, page fault, guest page fault) happens, we can store only the first exception encountered to save area. Also, we should be able to simply stop fetch/prefetch after exception (Bpu cannot predict exceptions so we're highly possible to be on the wrong fetch path), and restart after redirect, to save power.

We should be able to do this on IBuffer too, maybe in another PR

repo.name: XiangShan
repo.description: Open-source high-performance RISC-V processor

commits.message: feat(ICache): stall waylookup after exception until a flush
fix(ICache): remove unnecessary exception fsm in WayLookup

resolved_issues.title: Frontend: cut waylookup gpaddr
resolved_issues.body:
Currently, `gpaddr` is used only when guest page fault occurs, so it should be possible to not store every `gpaddr` in WayLookup (as well as in GPAMem).

Considering that every guest page fault should issue a redirect, and thus flush WayLookup/MainPipe/IPrefetch, we should be able to store only the first guest page fault and its `gpaddr` in WayLookup.

By doing this, we can save `2×nWayLookupSize - 1 = 63` registers that are used to store `gpaddr`.

This PR also includes some style changes for WayLookup to satisfy linter.

resolved_issues.title: fix(ICache): block waylookup if there is a pending gpf
resolved_issues.body:
In the existing design, ICache assumes that once a gpf occurs, it works on the wrong path until a flush (redirect) arrives, so it can discard redundant gpf/gpaddr data to reduce power/area.

As shown below, the 2nd(orange) and 3rd(blue) gpaddr write to wayLookup is discarded.
![241011-wave-old](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/878a0894-9d97-437d-aaa3-486d380da74f)

This assumption is mostly true, except:
1. Consider a 34B fetch block in which the first 32B have no exceptions and consist entirely of RVC instructions, and the last 2B cross a page boundary and a gpf occurs.
2. The IFU sends at most 16 instructions to the ibuffer, and therefore discards the last 2B. This way, none of the instructions received by the backend have exceptions and no flush (redirect) is generated.
3. The next fetch block again has a gpf, which ICache (wayLookup) considers redundant and discards the gpaddr data.
4. When the instruction with gpf is sent to the backend, the backend does not get the correct gpaddr and caused an error.

Fix: block writes when there is gpf/gpaddr data in wayLookup that is not read by mainPipe (i.e. is pending).

As shown below, the 1st(yellow) gpaddr write is bypassed to read port, the 2nd is stored in gpf entry, and the 3rd is stalled until the 2nd is read. So all 3 gpaddr data are sent to backend(gpaMem).

#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan || exit 1

export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"

TEST_NAME="waylookup_stalls_after_access_fault"
TEST_FILE="/home/xiangshan/src/test/scala/xiangshan/frontend/icache/ICacheWayLookupExceptionStallTest.scala"

cleanup() {
  rm -f "$TEST_FILE"
}

trap cleanup EXIT

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TEST_FILE")"
cat > "$TEST_FILE" <<'EOF'
package xiangshan.frontend.icache

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers
import top.DefaultConfig
import utility.{LogUtilsOptions, LogUtilsOptionsKey, PerfCounterOptions, PerfCounterOptionsKey, XSPerfLevel}
import xiangshan.{DebugOptionsKey, XSCoreParamsKey, XSTileKey}

class ICacheWayLookupExceptionStallTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  private val baseConfig = new DefaultConfig
  implicit val defaultConfig: Parameters = baseConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => baseConfig(XSTileKey).head
    case PerfCounterOptionsKey => PerfCounterOptions(
      enablePerfPrint = false,
      enablePerfDB = false,
      perfLevel = XSPerfLevel.CRITICAL,
      perfDBHartID = 0
    )
  }.alter((site, here, up) => {
    case LogUtilsOptionsKey => LogUtilsOptions(
      here(DebugOptionsKey).EnableDebug,
      here(DebugOptionsKey).EnablePerfDebug,
      here(DebugOptionsKey).FPGAPlatform,
      here(DebugOptionsKey).EnableXMR
    )
  })

  private def pokeFlushDefaults(dut: ICacheWayLookup): Unit = {
    dut.io.flush.poke(false.B)
    dut.io.flushFromBpu.s3.valid.poke(false.B)
    dut.io.flushFromBpu.s3.bits.flag.poke(false.B)
    dut.io.flushFromBpu.s3.bits.value.poke(0.U)
  }

  private def pokeUpdateDefaults(dut: ICacheWayLookup): Unit = {
    dut.io.update.valid.poke(false.B)
    dut.io.update.bits.blkPAddr.poke(0.U)
    dut.io.update.bits.vSetIdx.poke(0.U)
    dut.io.update.bits.waymask.poke(0.U)
    dut.io.update.bits.data.poke(0.U)
    dut.io.update.bits.maybeRvcMap.poke(0.U)
    dut.io.update.bits.corrupt.poke(false.B)
  }

  private def pokeWriteDefaults(dut: ICacheWayLookup): Unit = {
    dut.io.write.bits.vSetIdx.foreach(_.poke(0.U))
    dut.io.write.bits.waymask.foreach(_.poke(0.U))
    dut.io.write.bits.maybeRvcMap.foreach(_.poke(0.U))
    dut.io.write.bits.metaCodes.foreach(_.poke(0.U))
    dut.io.write.bits.pTag.poke(0.U)
    dut.io.write.bits.itlbException.value.poke(0.U)
    dut.io.write.bits.itlbPbmt.poke(0.U)
    dut.io.write.bits.gpAddr.addr.poke(0.U)
    dut.io.write.bits.isForVSnonLeafPTE.poke(false.B)
    dut.io.write.bits.ftqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
    dut.io.write.bits.ftqIdx.value.poke(0.U)
  }

  behavior of "ICacheWayLookup"
  it should "stall further writes after an access fault until flush" in {
    test(new ICacheWayLookup) { dut =>
      dut.io.read.ready.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.write.valid.poke(false.B)
      pokeFlushDefaults(dut)
      pokeUpdateDefaults(dut)
      pokeWriteDefaults(dut)
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.write.valid.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.write.bits.itlbException.value.poke(3.U)
      dut.io.write.ready.expect(true.B)
      dut.clock.step()

      pokeWriteDefaults(dut)
      dut.io.write.valid.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.write.ready.expect(false.B)

      dut.io.flush.poke(true.B)
      dut.clock.step()

      pokeFlushDefaults(dut)
      dut.io.write.ready.expect(true.B)
    }
  }
}
EOF

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if mill -i -Djvm-xmx=8G -Djvm-xss=64m xiangshan.test.testOnly xiangshan.frontend.icache.ICacheWayLookupExceptionStallTest; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
  status=0
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
  status=1
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$status"
problem_statement: `ICacheWayLookup` is the frontend ICache buffer that holds waylookup results until the main pipeline consumes them. The bug is that after this buffer accepts a waylookup write carrying an ITLB fetch exception, for example an access fault, it can still accept another write before the frontend is flushed. At that point the current fetch path should already be treated as invalid. The expected behavior is specific: once an exceptional waylookup entry has been accepted, `ICacheWayLookup` must block any further waylookup writes until a flush clears that exceptional state. The trigger condition is an exceptional waylookup write followed by another write attempt before that flush arrives.

title: fix(Bpu): wait Sram reset to avoid x-state
body:
Fix #4962 simv failure.

#4962 seems to have other problem, so instead merging this to it, I'd suggest merging this to kunminghu-v3 first and rebase #4962 later.

The root cause of that failure is we send read requests to mbtb/tage before their sram ready. #4946/kunminghu-v3 can pass CI because we don't have Bpu.io.train before #4962, chisel can opt-out train-related code, including the failure assertion.

From SRAMTemplate:
```scala
  private val singleHold = if(singlePort) io.w.req.valid else false.B
  private val resetHold = if(shouldReset) resetState else false.B
  io.r.req.ready := !resetHold && !singleHold && !conflictStallRead
```

We cannot connect `io.r.req.ready` directly to `s0_fire`, that forms a combinational loop in tage. So we use a resetDone register to block requests until Sram reset is done (`!resetHold`)

problem_statement: XiangShan's FDP data-prefetch logic uses CounterFilter to track incoming load requests. CounterFilter can fire its internal enqueue assertion during legal sustained traffic: when multiple load pipeline ports send back-to-back load requests for several cycles, the filter may report that no allocation slot is available and abort simulation even though those requests should still be accepted. The expected behavior is that CounterFilter must continue accepting valid consecutive load allocations from the load pipeline without raising an internal overflow or enqueue assertion.

title: fix(L1TLB): ignore addr when when mbmc.BME = 1 & CMODE = 0
body:
The current design of L2TLB always responds to a fixed 4k size page when Bitmap Check is enabled and CMODE=0, so L1TLB may store entries smaller than actual page size and fails to properly handle address matching, similar to the issue in #5114.
This patch just disables address matching during sfence.vma. And hfence.vvma is handled in #5114.

repo.name: XiangShan
repo.description: Open-source high-performance RISC-V processor

commits.message: fix(L1TLB): ignore addr when when mbmc.BME = 1 & CMODE = 0

resolved_issues.title: fix(L1TLB): ignore addr when hfence.vvma or sfence.vma when v=1
resolved_issues.body:
The current design of L1TLB fails to properly handle address matching when two-stage address translation is enabled. Both VS-stage and G-stage are merged into a single L1TLB entry, with address matching controlled by the smaller page size.

Consider the following scenario:
```
                VS-stage Page    G-stage Page
                 Large Page       Small Page
                  +--------+
                  |        |
                +=|========|=====+========+=+
 L1TLB Entry->  | |########|     |########| |
                +=|========|=====+========+=+
                  |        |
 sfence addr ---> |        |
 try to flush     |        |
                  +--------+
```

In this case, the VS-stage is a large page, while the G-stage is a small page. L1TLB stores them as a small page. When hfence.vvma (or sfence.vma when v=1) comes with an address in that VS large page but outside the small page, it should flush the VS page. However, since L1TLB always treats this entry as a small page, it cannot match this address, thus cannot flush this entry.

This patch disables address matching during hfence.vvma and sfence.vma when v=1. Now, hfence.vvma will ignore the address and flush all entries.

WARNING: This patch may cause performance degradation when two-stage address translation is enabled.

  behavior of "TLB bitmap sfence"

  it should "flush a matching-asid entry even when the sfence address misses the stored 4KB sector in bitmap mode" in {
    val refillVpn = 0x100
    val flushVpn = 0x101
    val refillPpn = 0x12345
    val asid = 0x2a

    implicit val perfConfig: Parameters = config.alterPartial({
      case PerfCounterOptionsKey => PerfCounterOptions(false, false, XSPerfLevel.CRITICAL, 0)
      case LogUtilsOptionsKey => LogUtilsOptions(false, false, false, false)
    })

      def clearInputs(): Unit = {

        c.io.refillVpn.poke(0.U)
        c.io.refillPpn.poke(0.U)
        c.io.lookupValid.poke(false.B)
        c.io.lookupVpn.poke(0.U)
        c.io.flushValid.poke(false.B)
        c.io.flushVpn.poke(0.U)

        c.io.lookupVpn.poke(vpn.U)

        c.io.lookupRespValid.expect(true.B)
        val hit = c.io.lookupHit.peek().litToBoolean

      c.io.asid.poke(asid.U)
      c.io.bitmapEnable.poke(true.B)
      c.clock.step()

      c.io.refillValid.poke(true.B)
      c.io.refillVpn.poke(refillVpn.U)
      c.io.refillPpn.poke(refillPpn.U)
      c.clock.step()
      c.io.refillValid.poke(false.B)
      c.io.refillVpn.poke(0.U)
      c.io.refillPpn.poke(0.U)

      lookup(refillVpn) shouldBe true

      c.io.flushValid.poke(true.B)
      c.io.flushVpn.poke(flushVpn.U)
      c.clock.step()
      c.io.flushValid.poke(false.B)
      c.io.flushVpn.poke(0.U)
      c.clock.step()

      withClue("sfence.vma should ignore address matching when bitmap check is enabled and CMODE=0") {

    }

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in the L1 translation lookaside buffer (L1TLB) sfence.vma invalidation path, when bitmap check is enabled (mbmc.BME=1) and CMODE=0, a cached entry can remain valid after sfence.vma if the flush address does not hit the 4 KB sector recorded in that entry. In this mode, the recorded sector can be narrower than the translation the entry should cover, so address matching can miss an entry that still ought to be invalidated. Expected behavior: sfence.vma should invalidate the matching-ASID L1TLB entry in this mode even when the supplied address misses the stored 4 KB sector, and the entry should no longer be returned by lookup afterward. Affected function: the L1TLB (TLBFA) sfence.vma flush and address-matching logic. Trigger condition: bitmap check enabled with mbmc.BME=1 and CMODE=0, a cached L1TLB entry for an ASID, and sfence.vma issued for the same ASID with an address outside the stored 4 KB sector.

title: fix(TLB): gpaddr should be same to vaddr when onlyS2
body:
When OnlyS2 gpaddr (64 bits) should be same to vaddr (50 bits), no need to do any extend (to 56 bits) or truncate (to 48 bits).

This commit re-fixes the bug that #4913 attempted to fix.

repo.description: Open-source high-performance RISC-V processor

commits.message:
fix(TLB): gpaddr should be same to vaddr when onlyS2

When OnlyS2 gpaddr (64 bits) should be same to vaddr (50 bits), no need

resolved_issues.title: fix(TLB): vaddr should be extended to PAddrBitsMax
resolved_issues.body:
In the previous design, vaddr was sign-extended to PAddrBits to prevent cases where the physical address width exceeds the virtual address width. However, in the SV48x4 mode, the actual width of vaddr is 50 bits, which ended up being truncated to 48 bits.

In the onlyStage2 case, the generated guest physical address (gpaddr) should match vaddr. But due to the truncation, gpaddr was also limited to 48 bits, and the upper 2 bits were lost (set to zero).

To fix this bug, and to better support future extensions—vaddr is now extended to the maximum physical address width (PAddrBitsMax) as defined by the RISC-V specification.

fix_patch:
diff --git a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/cache/mmu/TLB.scala b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/cache/mmu/TLB.scala
index 452e2d1a848..8eb8e92f478 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/cache/mmu/TLB.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/cache/mmu/TLB.scala
@@ -305,7 +305,7 @@ class TLB(Width: Int, nRespDups: Int = 1, Block: Seq[Boolean], q: TLBParameters)
     hit.suggestName(s"hit_read_${i}")
     miss.suggestName(s"miss_read_${i}")
 
-    val vaddr = SignExt(req_out(i).vaddr, PAddrBitsMax)
+    val vaddr = SignExt(req_out(i).vaddr, PAddrBits)
     resp(i).bits.miss := miss
     resp(i).bits.ptwBack := ptw.resp.fire
     resp(i).bits.memidx := RegEnable(req_in(i).bits.memidx, req_in(i).valid)
@@ -347,7 +347,7 @@ class TLB(Width: Int, nRespDups: Int = 1, Block: Seq[Boolean], q: TLBParameters)
       // Also, when onlyS2, if crosspage, gpaddr = vaddr(start address of a new page), else gpaddr = fullva(original vaddr)
       // By the way, frontend handles the cross page instruction fetch by itself, so TLB doesn't need to do anything extra.
       // Also, the fullva of iTLB is not used and always zero. crossPageVaddr should never use fullva in iTLB.
-      val crossPageVaddr = Mux(isitlb || req_out(i).fullva(12) =/= vaddr(12), vaddr, req_out(i).fullva)
+      val crossPageVaddr = Mux(isitlb || req_out(i).fullva(12) =/= vaddr(12), req_out(i).vaddr, req_out(i).fullva)
       val gpaddr_offset = Mux(isLeaf(d), get_off(crossPageVaddr), Cat(getVpnn(get_pn(crossPageVaddr), vpn_idx), 0.U(log2Up(XLEN/8).W)))
       val gpaddr = Cat(gvpn(d), gpaddr_offset)
       resp(i).bits.paddr(d) := Mux(enable, paddr, vaddr)

problem_statement: In XiangShan's TLB, the guest physical address (`gpaddr`) returned for an only-stage-2 translation request (`onlyS2`) is incorrect for 50-bit SV48x4 guest addresses. In this mode, `gpaddr` is expected to be exactly the same as the original request address (`vaddr`), but when the request has non-zero bits above bit 47, the returned `gpaddr` loses those upper bits and no longer matches the input address. The bug is in the TLB's only-stage-2 guest-address generation path and is triggered by an `onlyS2` translation of a 50-bit address, especially when bit 48 or bit 49 is set.

title: fix(uncache): revert the last fix and correct the fix logic
body:
When canMerge is confilct with rejectVec.orR, it should not be "keeping former" to guarantee the functional correction.

In this case, this request should not enter the buffer. So use `e0_canMerge && e0_fire` not `e0_canMerge && e0_req_valid` for the update logic.

problem_statement: In XiangShan's DCache uncache path, the buffer that tracks outstanding uncached requests can incorrectly accept a new uncached store even when it targets the same buffered word/address as an earlier uncached store and the two stores are not mergeable. When the first uncached store is still outstanding, a later store with a conflicting byte mask can still be reported as ready and accepted instead of being blocked. The expected behavior is specific: the later non-mergeable store must be backpressured, must not be reported as accepted, and must not enter the uncache buffer until the conflict is gone. The affected logic is the DCache Uncache request-buffer admission and ready/accept handling for uncached stores. The trigger condition is a second uncached store arriving for the same buffered word/address while the earlier store remains in the uncache buffer, with masks that make the new request non-mergeable with the existing entry.

title: fix(IFU): do fetch if only the second cacheline has exception
body: **For maintainer: This bug does not affect kunminghu-v3 as we've rewritten the whole uncache fetch logic. Do NOT cherry-pick.** We have `def crossCacheline = startAddr(blockOffBits - 1) === 1.U`, but uncache fetch only works on addr `[start:start+4)`. So, whether we should do uncache fetch should only depends on `f3_exception(0)`. For example in this case: ``` start page boundary assumed end (start+32) | uncache fetch region | | 0xfffc 0xffff 0x10018 | exception = None | exception = Access Fault ``` This is a crossline request (`start(5) === 1.U`), and it's also a crosspage request, different page can have different permissions / attributes, so we can have the first page normal while the second page af/pf/gpf. In this case, we should fetch and send the first 4B (assume it's an RVI instr) to ibuffer, and mark the first instr in next page as invalid/af/pf/gpf. However, in current implementation, we simply canceled the uncache fetch, sending 4B of 0 to backend, causing an Illegal Instruction Exception. This PR fixes this, we do uncache fetch if exception(0) is none, if there's an RVI instr crossing page, we'll check exception(1) before resend. Test: https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/nexus-am/pull/68 We can see mcause & mepc changes in this test: mcause: 0x2(illegal instr) -> 0x1(instr access fault) mepc: 0x82fffffa(first instr in test_func) -> 0x82fffffe(address of the cross page RVI)

problem_statement: In XiangShan's frontend instruction fetch unit (IFU), the uncached/MMIO fetch path is wrong for a request that starts in the last halfword of one cache line and the instruction then crosses into the next page. Uncached fetch only reads the first 4 bytes at the start address, so if that first 4-byte portion is accessible but the next page raises an instruction exception, the IFU should still issue the initial uncached fetch for the first 4 bytes. The observed bug is that the IFU cancels that initial uncached fetch because the later cache line/page has an exception. The expected behavior is specific and testable: for this cross-cacheline, cross-page uncached fetch case, the IFU must issue the first uncached 4-byte fetch, then report the second-page instruction fault for the crossing instruction, without attempting a resend for the second half once that second page already faults. The affected function is the IFU's uncached/MMIO instruction fetch handling for cross-cacheline requests. The trigger condition is a fetch whose start address is in the last halfword of a cache line, where the first 4-byte fetch region is valid but the next page raises an instruction access fault.

title: fix(LoadUnit): raise af for unalign access on MMIO region
body:
This pr fixes #5695 for v3. According to RISC-V spec: Non-idempotent regions might not support misaligned accesses. Misaligned accesses to such regions should raise access-fault exceptions, indicating that software should not emulate the misaligned access using multiple smaller accesses, which could cause unexpected side effects.

Therefore, unalign accesses to MMIO region should raise an af exception instead of a misalign exception. This commit fixes this issue. Unalign access to NC region still raises misalign exception for its idempotent memory attribute. Besides it should be noted that store has the same bug, which will be fixed in the subsequent StoreUnit refactoring.

resolved_issues.title: Misaligned accesses to non-idempotent regions raise AddrMisaligned instead of AccessFault
resolved_issues.body: ### Before start - [x] I have read the [RISC-V ISA Manual](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual) and this is not a RISC-V ISA question. 我已经阅读过 RISC-V 指令集手册，这不是一个指令集本身的问题。 - [x] I have read the [XiangShan Documents](https://xiangshan-doc.readthedocs.io/zh_CN/latest). 我已经阅读过香山文档。 - [x] I have searched the previous issues and did not find anything relevant. 我已经搜索过之前的 issue，并没有找到相关的。 - [x] I have reviewed the commit messages from the relevant commit history. 我已经浏览过相关的提交历史和提交信息。 - [] I have reproduced the incorrect behaviors using the latest commit on the master branch. 我已经使用 master 分支最新的 commit 复现了不正确的行为。 ### Branch master (kunminghu-v2) ### Describe the bug When a misaligned load or store targets a non-idempotent memory region (MMIO / uncacheable I/O), XiangShan raises `loadAddrMisaligned` / `storeAddrMisaligned` exceptions. The RISC-V Privileged Specification (§3.6.1 "Idempotency PMAs") recommends that such accesses should raise `*AccessFault` exceptions. ### Spec Reference From the RISC-V Privileged Specification, §3.6.1 *Idempotency PMAs* (NOTE block): > Non-idempotent regions might not support misaligned accesses. Misaligned accesses to such regions **should** raise access-fault exceptions rather than address-misaligned exceptions, indicating that software should not emulate the misaligned access using multiple smaller accesses, which could cause unexpected side effects. ### Code Evidence **1. Load pipeline** (`src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/LoadUnit.scala`): ```scala // Line 1312-1314 // We will generate misaligned exceptions at mmio. val s2_real_exceptionVec = WireInit(s2_exception_vec) s2_real_exceptionVec(loadAddrMisaligned) := (s2_out.isMisalign || s2_out.isFrmMisAlignBuf) && s2_uncache ``` **2. Store pipeline** (`src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/StoreUnit.scala`): ```scala // Line 388 s1_out.uop.exceptionVec(storeAddrMisaligned) := s1_out.mmio && s1_in.isMisalign ``` And in S2: ```scala s2_out.uop.exceptionVec(storeAddrMisaligned) := s2_actually_uncache && (s2_in.isMisalign || s2_in.isFrmMisAlignBuf) && !s2_un_misalign_exception ``` **3. LoadMisalignBuffer** (`src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/lsqueue/LoadMisalignBuffer.scala`): ```scala exceptionVec(loadAddrMisaligned) := true.B ``` ### Expected behavior Per the spec recommendation, when a misaligned load or store targets a non-idempotent (MMIO / uncacheable I/O) region: - A misaligned **load** should raise `loadAccessFault` (exception code 5) instead of `loadAddrMisaligned` (exception code 4). - A misaligned **store** should raise `storeAccessFault` (exception code 7) instead of `storeAddrMisaligned` (exception code 6). ### Environment XiangShan branch:master XiangShan config:DefaultConfig ### To Reproduce N/A —sorry for no minimal reproducer yet. The issue was found via code inspection. ### Additional context _No response_

fix_patch:
diff --git a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/NewLoadUnit.scala b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/NewLoadUnit.scala
index 29b7334743c..8bf2bcc2ea6 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/NewLoadUnit.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/pipeline/NewLoadUnit.scala
@@ -286,7 +286,10 @@ class LoadUnitS0(param: ExeUnitParams)(
     */
   val needAlignCheckSources = Seq(replayHiPrio, fastReplay, replayLoPrio, vectorIssue, scalarIssue)
   val needAlignCheckValids = needAlignCheckSources.map(_.valid)
-  val noAlignCheckSources = sources.filterNot(needAlignCheckSources.contains) // unalign tail, hardware prefetch
+  val alwaysUnalignSources = Seq(unalignTail)
+  val alwaysUnalign = Cat(alwaysUnalignSources.map(_.fire)).orR
+  val alwaysAlignSources = Seq(prefetchHiConf, prefetchLoConf)
+  val noAlignCheckSources = alwaysUnalignSources ++ alwaysAlignSources // unalign tail, hardware prefetch
   val noAlignCheck = Cat(noAlignCheckSources.map(_.fire)).orR || isPrefetch // unalign tail, hardware & software prefetch
   val needAlignCheck = !noAlignCheck
 
@@ -294,7 +297,7 @@ class LoadUnitS0(param: ExeUnitParams)(
   val _align = ParallelPriorityMux(needAlignCheckValids, alignCheckResults._1)
   val _crossWordInsideBank = ParallelPriorityMux(needAlignCheckValids, alignCheckResults._2)
   val _crossBank = ParallelPriorityMux(needAlignCheckValids, alignCheckResults._3)
-  val align = noAlignCheck || _align
+  val align = !alwaysUnalign && (noAlignCheck || _align)
   val crossWordInsideBank = needAlignCheck && _crossWordInsideBank
   val crossBank = needAlignCheck && _crossBank
   val readWholeBank = unalignTail.valid || crossWordInsideBank
@@ -914,12 +917,13 @@ class LoadUnitS2(param: ExeUnitParams)(
   // load access fault
   val afUnaccessable = uop.exceptionVec(loadAccessFault) || pmpUnaccessable
   val afVectorUncache = accessType.isVector() && isUncache
+  val afUnalignMMIO = !in.align.get && isMMIO
   val afTagError = io.dcacheResp.bits.tag_error && tlbHit && io.csrCtrl.cache_error_enable
   val afForwardDenied = Wire(Bool())
   val afBypassDenied = Wire(Bool())
-  val af = afUnaccessable || afVectorUncache || afTagError || afForwardDenied || afBypassDenied
+  val af = afUnaccessable || afVectorUncache || afUnalignMMIO || afTagError || afForwardDenied || afBypassDenied
   // load address misaligned
-  val am = !in.align.get && accessType.isScalar() && isUncache && !pmpUnaccessable
+  val am = !in.align.get && accessType.isScalar() && isNC && !pmpUnaccessable
   // hardware error
   val hweForwardCorrupt = Wire(Bool())
   val hweBypassCorrupt = Wire(Bool())

#!/bin/bash
set -u -o pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan || exit 1

export NOOP_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export XIANGSHAN_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export JAVA_HOME="${JAVA_HOME:-/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64}"
VERILATOR_REAL_ROOT="${VERILATOR_ROOT:-/tools/verilator}"
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$VERILATOR_REAL_ROOT/bin:/tools/riscv/bin:$PATH"

GEN_SCALA="/home/xiangshan/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem/LoadUnitPr5700Gen.scala"
S1S0_CPP="/home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s1s0_main.cpp"
S2_CPP="/home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s2_main.cpp"
WRAP_ROOT="/home/xiangshan/verilator-toolroot"

write_sources() {
  mkdir -p /home/xiangshan/src/main/scala/xiangshan/mem
  mkdir -p /home/xiangshan/build

  cat > "$GEN_SCALA" <<'SCALA_EOF'
package xiangshan.mem

import chisel3._
import org.chipsalliance.cde.config.Parameters
import utility.{PerfCounterOptions, PerfCounterOptionsKey, XSPerfLevel}
import xiangshan._
import xiangshan.ExceptionNO._
import xiangshan.cache.mmu.Pbmt
import xiangshan.mem.LoadStage._

object Pr5700HarnessConfig {
  private val rootConfig = new top.TLConfig
  private val coreParams = rootConfig(XSTileKey).head
  private val backendParams = coreParams.backendParams

  backendParams.allExuParams.zipWithIndex.foreach { case (exuCfg, i) =>
    exuCfg.bindBackendParam(backendParams)
    exuCfg.updateIQWakeUpConfigs(backendParams.iqWakeUpParams)
    exuCfg.updateExuIdx(i)
  }
  backendParams.allSchdParams.foreach(_.bindBackendParam(backendParams))
  backendParams.allIssueParams.foreach { iqCfg =>
    iqCfg.bindBackendParam(backendParams)
    iqCfg.exuBlockParams.foreach(_.bindIssueBlockParam(iqCfg))
  }

  implicit val defaultConfig: Parameters = rootConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => coreParams
  }.alter((site, here, up) => {
    case PerfCounterOptionsKey => PerfCounterOptions(false, false, XSPerfLevel.VERBOSE, 0)
  })
}

class Pr5700LoadUnitS1S0Harness(implicit override val p: Parameters) extends Module with HasMemBlockParameters {
  private val param = ldaParams.head
  param.bindBackendParam(backendParams)

  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val inValid = Input(Bool())
    val outValid = Output(Bool())
    val outAlign = Output(Bool())
  })

  val s1 = Module(new LoadUnitS1(param))
  val s0 = Module(new LoadUnitS0(param))
  s0.io.unalignTail <> s1.io.unalignTail

  val inBits = WireDefault(0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s1.io_pipeIn.get.bits)))
  inBits.entrance := LoadEntrance.scalarIssue.U
  inBits.accessType.instrType := InstrType.scalar.U
  inBits.uop.fuOpType := LSUOpType.lw
  inBits.size := MemorySize.W.U
  inBits.mask := "hf".U
  inBits.vaddr := 15.U
  inBits.fullva := 15.U
  inBits.paddr.get := 15.U
  inBits.noQuery.get := true.B
  inBits.align.get := false.B
  inBits.unalignHead.get := true.B
  inBits.readWholeBank.get := false.B
  inBits.hasROBEntry := true.B
  s1.io_pipeIn.get.valid := io.inValid
  s1.io_pipeIn.get.bits := inBits
  s1.io_pipeOut.get.ready := true.B

  s1.io.redirect.valid := false.B
  s1.io.redirect.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s1.io.redirect.bits))
  s1.io.kill := false.B
  s1.io.tlbResp.valid := false.B
  s1.io.tlbResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s1.io.tlbResp.bits))
  s1.io.sqForwardResp.valid := false.B
  s1.io.sqForwardResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s1.io.sqForwardResp.bits))
  s1.io.uncacheBypassResp.valid := false.B
  s1.io.uncacheBypassResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s1.io.uncacheBypassResp.bits))
  s1.io.staNukeQueryReq.foreach { req =>
    req.valid := false.B
    req.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(req.bits))
  }
  s1.io.csrTrigger := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s1.io.csrTrigger))

  s0.io.replay.valid := false.B
  s0.io.replay.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s0.io.replay.bits))
  s0.io.fastReplay.valid := false.B
  s0.io.fastReplay.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s0.io.fastReplay.bits))
  s0.io.prefetchReq.valid := false.B
  s0.io.prefetchReq.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s0.io.prefetchReq.bits))
  s0.io.vecldin.valid := false.B
  s0.io.vecldin.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s0.io.vecldin.bits))
  s0.io.ldin.valid := false.B
  s0.io.ldin.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(s0.io.ldin.bits))

  s0.io.tlbReq.ready := true.B
  s0.io.dcacheReq.ready := true.B
  s0.io_pipeOut.get.ready := true.B

  io.outValid := s0.io_pipeOut.get.valid
  io.outAlign := s0.io_pipeOut.get.bits.align.get
}

class Pr5700LoadUnitS2Harness(implicit override val p: Parameters) extends Module with HasMemBlockParameters {
  private val param = ldaParams.head
  param.bindBackendParam(backendParams)

  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val inValid = Input(Bool())
    val align = Input(Bool())
    val pbmt = Input(UInt(Pbmt.width.W))
    val outValid = Output(Bool())
    val loadAddrMisaligned = Output(Bool())
    val loadAccessFault = Output(Bool())
  })

  val stage = Module(new LoadUnitS2(param))

  val inBits = WireDefault(0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io_pipeIn.get.bits)))
  inBits.entrance := LoadEntrance.scalarIssue.U
  inBits.accessType.instrType := InstrType.scalar.U
  inBits.align.get := io.align
  inBits.unalignHead.get := false.B
  inBits.readWholeBank.get := false.B
  inBits.tlbAccessResult.get := TlbAccessResult.hit.U
  inBits.pbmt.get := io.pbmt
  inBits.mask := "hf".U
  inBits.vaddr := 1.U
  inBits.fullva := 1.U
  inBits.paddr.get := 1.U
  inBits.hasROBEntry := true.B
  inBits.shouldFastReplay.get := false.B
  stage.io_pipeIn.get.valid := io.inValid
  stage.io_pipeIn.get.bits := inBits
  stage.io_pipeOut.get.ready := true.B

  stage.io.redirect.valid := false.B
  stage.io.redirect.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.redirect.bits))
  stage.io.kill := false.B
  stage.io.pmp := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.pmp))
  stage.io.tlbHint := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.tlbHint))
  stage.io.dcacheBankConflict := false.B
  stage.io.dcacheMSHRNack := false.B
  stage.io.dcacheResp.valid := false.B
  stage.io.dcacheResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.dcacheResp.bits))
  stage.io.sqForwardResp.valid := false.B
  stage.io.sqForwardResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.sqForwardResp.bits))
  stage.io.sbufferForwardResp.valid := false.B
  stage.io.sbufferForwardResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.sbufferForwardResp.bits))
  stage.io.uncacheForwardResp.valid := false.B
  stage.io.uncacheForwardResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.uncacheForwardResp.bits))
  stage.io.mshrForwardResp.valid := false.B
  stage.io.mshrForwardResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.mshrForwardResp.bits))
  stage.io.tldForwardResp.valid := false.B
  stage.io.tldForwardResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.tldForwardResp.bits))
  stage.io.uncacheBypassResp.valid := false.B
  stage.io.uncacheBypassResp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.uncacheBypassResp.bits))
  stage.io.staNukeQueryReq.foreach { req =>
    req.valid := false.B
    req.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(req.bits))
  }
  stage.io.rarNukeQueryReq.ready := true.B
  stage.io.rawNukeQueryReq.ready := true.B
  stage.io.csrCtrl := 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(stage.io.csrCtrl))

  io.outValid := stage.io_pipeOut.get.valid
  io.loadAddrMisaligned := stage.io_pipeOut.get.bits.uop.exceptionVec(loadAddrMisaligned)
  io.loadAccessFault := stage.io_pipeOut.get.bits.uop.exceptionVec(loadAccessFault)
}

object Pr5700LoadUnitS1S0Main extends App {
  import Pr5700HarnessConfig.defaultConfig
  circt.stage.ChiselStage.emitSystemVerilogFile(
    new Pr5700LoadUnitS1S0Harness()(defaultConfig),
    Array("--target-dir", "build/pr5700-s1s0"),
    Array("--split-verilog")
  )
}

object Pr5700LoadUnitS2Main extends App {
  import Pr5700HarnessConfig.defaultConfig
  circt.stage.ChiselStage.emitSystemVerilogFile(
    new Pr5700LoadUnitS2Harness()(defaultConfig),
    Array("--target-dir", "build/pr5700-s2"),
    Array("--split-verilog")
  )
}
SCALA_EOF

  cat > "$S1S0_CPP" <<'CPP_EOF'
#include <iostream>
#include <verilated.h>
#include "VPr5700LoadUnitS1S0Harness.h"

static void tick(VPr5700LoadUnitS1S0Harness* top) {
  top->clock = 0;
  top->eval();
  top->clock = 1;
  top->eval();
  top->clock = 0;
  top->eval();
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  Verilated::commandArgs(argc, argv);
  auto* top = new VPr5700LoadUnitS1S0Harness;
  top->reset = 1;
  top->io_inValid = 0;
  tick(top);

  top->reset = 0;
  top->io_inValid = 1;
  tick(top);

  const bool pass = top->io_outValid && !top->io_outAlign;
  std::cout << "s1->s0 outValid=" << int(top->io_outValid)
            << " outAlign=" << int(top->io_outAlign) << std::endl;
  delete top;
  return pass ? 0 : 1;
}
CPP_EOF

  cat > "$S2_CPP" <<'CPP_EOF'
#include <iostream>
#include <verilated.h>
#include "VPr5700LoadUnitS2Harness.h"

static void tick(VPr5700LoadUnitS2Harness* top) {
  top->clock = 0;
  top->eval();
  top->clock = 1;
  top->eval();
  top->clock = 0;
  top->eval();
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  Verilated::commandArgs(argc, argv);
  auto* top = new VPr5700LoadUnitS2Harness;
  top->reset = 1;
  top->io_inValid = 0;
  top->io_align = 0;
  top->io_pbmt = 0;
  tick(top);

  top->reset = 0;
  top->io_inValid = 1;
  top->io_align = 0;

  top->io_pbmt = 2;
  tick(top);
  const bool mmio_pass = top->io_outValid && top->io_loadAccessFault && !top->io_loadAddrMisaligned;
  std::cout << "s2 mmio outValid=" << int(top->io_outValid)
            << " AF=" << int(top->io_loadAccessFault)
            << " AM=" << int(top->io_loadAddrMisaligned) << std::endl;

  top->io_pbmt = 1;
  tick(top);
  const bool nc_pass = top->io_outValid && !top->io_loadAccessFault && top->io_loadAddrMisaligned;
  std::cout << "s2 nc outValid=" << int(top->io_outValid)
            << " AF=" << int(top->io_loadAccessFault)
            << " AM=" << int(top->io_loadAddrMisaligned) << std::endl;

  delete top;
  return (mmio_pass && nc_pass) ? 0 : 1;
}
CPP_EOF
}

prepare_verilator_root() {
  local verilator_root="$VERILATOR_REAL_ROOT"
  mkdir -p "$WRAP_ROOT/bin"
  ln -sfn "$verilator_root/share/verilator/include" "$WRAP_ROOT/include"
  ln -sfn "$verilator_root/share/verilator/bin/verilator_includer" "$WRAP_ROOT/bin/verilator_includer"
  ln -sfn "$verilator_root/share/verilator/bin/verilator_ccache_report" "$WRAP_ROOT/bin/verilator_ccache_report"

  cat > "$WRAP_ROOT/bin/verilator_bin" <<'SH_EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
args=()
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
  if [ "$1" = "-j" ] && [ "$#" -ge 2 ] && [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    args+=("-j" "1")
    shift 2
  else
    args+=("$1")
    shift
  fi
done
exec "${VERILATOR_REAL_ROOT:-/tools/verilator}/bin/verilator_bin" "${args[@]}"
SH_EOF
  chmod +x "$WRAP_ROOT/bin/verilator_bin"
}

collect_sv_files() {
  local dir="$1"
  find "$dir" -type f -name '*.sv' | sort
}

emit_wrappers() {
  rm -rf /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s1s0 /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s2
  mkdir -p /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s1s0 /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s2

  mill --no-server -Djvm-xmx=8G -Djvm-xss=256m \
    xiangshan.runMain xiangshan.mem.Pr5700LoadUnitS1S0Main \
    > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_emit_s1s0.log 2>&1 || return 1

  mill --no-server -Djvm-xmx=8G -Djvm-xss=256m \
    xiangshan.runMain xiangshan.mem.Pr5700LoadUnitS2Main \
    > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_emit_s2.log 2>&1 || return 1

  return 0
}

run_s1s0() {
  local src_dir="/home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s1s0"
  local -a sv_files=()
  local -a inc_flags=("-I$src_dir")
  [ -d "$src_dir/verification" ] && inc_flags+=("-I$src_dir/verification")
  mapfile -t sv_files < <(collect_sv_files "$src_dir")

  if [ "${#sv_files[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "[ERROR] No generated SystemVerilog found under $src_dir" > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_vlt_gen_s1s0.log
    return 1
  fi

  rm -rf /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s1s0_obj
  verilator -Wno-LATCH -Wno-UNOPTFLAT --cc --exe -j 1 \
    -CFLAGS -std=c++17 \
    --top-module Pr5700LoadUnitS1S0Harness \
    "${inc_flags[@]}" \
    "${sv_files[@]}" \
    "$S1S0_CPP" \
    -Mdir /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s1s0_obj \
    > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_vlt_gen_s1s0.log 2>&1 || return 1

  make -C /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s1s0_obj \
    -f VPr5700LoadUnitS1S0Harness.mk \
    VERILATOR_ROOT="$WRAP_ROOT" \
    -j 1 \
    > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_vlt_make_s1s0.log 2>&1 || return 1

  /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s1s0_obj/VPr5700LoadUnitS1S0Harness \
    > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_run_s1s0.log 2>&1
}

run_s2() {
  local src_dir="/home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s2"
  local -a sv_files=()
  local -a inc_flags=("-I$src_dir")
  [ -d "$src_dir/verification" ] && inc_flags+=("-I$src_dir/verification")
  mapfile -t sv_files < <(collect_sv_files "$src_dir")

  if [ "${#sv_files[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "[ERROR] No generated SystemVerilog found under $src_dir" > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_vlt_gen_s2.log
    return 1
  fi

  rm -rf /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s2_obj
  verilator -Wno-LATCH -Wno-UNOPTFLAT --cc --exe -j 1 \
    -CFLAGS -std=c++17 \
    --top-module Pr5700LoadUnitS2Harness \
    "${inc_flags[@]}" \
    "${sv_files[@]}" \
    "$S2_CPP" \
    -Mdir /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s2_obj \
    > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_vlt_gen_s2.log 2>&1 || return 1

  make -C /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s2_obj \
    -f VPr5700LoadUnitS2Harness.mk \
    VERILATOR_ROOT="$WRAP_ROOT" \
    -j 1 \
    > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_vlt_make_s2.log 2>&1 || return 1

  /home/xiangshan/build/pr5700-s2_obj/VPr5700LoadUnitS2Harness \
    > /home/xiangshan/pr5700_run_s2.log 2>&1
}

show_log_tail() {
  local file="$1"
  if [ -f "$file" ]; then
    echo "----- $(basename "$file") -----"
    tail -n 40 "$file"
  fi
}

write_sources
prepare_verilator_root

s1s0_rc=1
s2_rc=1

if emit_wrappers; then
  run_s1s0
  s1s0_rc=$?
  run_s2
  s2_rc=$?
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [ "$s1s0_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: loadunit_s0_unalign_tail ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: loadunit_s0_unalign_tail ... FAIL"
fi
if [ "$s2_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: loadunit_s2_mmio_exception ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: loadunit_s2_mmio_exception ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

if [ "$s1s0_rc" -eq 0 ] && [ "$s2_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's LoadUnit load path, a scalar load that is already misaligned can lose that unaligned status when it continues through the split or unaligned-tail path, and a misaligned scalar load to an MMIO region is then reported as loadAddrMisaligned instead of loadAccessFault. Expected behavior: the LoadUnit must preserve the unaligned status of split or unaligned-tail load requests so exception classification remains correct; for a misaligned scalar load to MMIO, which is a non-idempotent uncacheable region, the reported exception must be loadAccessFault, while a misaligned scalar load to NC, which is idempotent normal uncacheable memory, must still report loadAddrMisaligned. Affected function: LoadUnit alignment tracking and exception classification for scalar uncacheable loads. Trigger condition: a naturally misaligned scalar load, especially one that enters the split or unaligned-tail path, targets MMIO or NC memory.

title: [prim/rtl] Synthesizable `countones` function
body:
Two commits:

1. Remove `countones` logic from DAI. The count value is released unconditionally.
2. Use `prim_sum_tree` for the calculation of `countones`.

Addresses #28017.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[otp_ctrl/rtl] Unconditionally release countones after zeroization

In the absence of an error, the `ZEROIZE` command should always
release the `countones` value of the zeroized word to software.

Signed-off-by: Andrea Caforio <andrea.caforio@lowrisc.org>

[otp_ctrl/rtl] Use prim_sum_tree as $countones primitive

The SystemVerilog function `$countones` is not supported by all
tools. Emulate it using the `prim_sum_tree` primitive.

Signed-off-by: Andrea Caforio <andrea.caforio@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [otp_ctrl] Move `countones` function from `otp_ctrl_top_specific_pkg.sv.tpl` to `prim_util_pkg`

prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 073b849f6d62f7c2f04839dff3cac419d843217f
git submodule update --init --recursive

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
fi

python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
python -m pip install -r python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location

toolchain_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi
if [[ -n "${toolchain_version}" ]]; then
  python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "${toolchain_version}"
else
  python util/get-toolchain.py --update
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
ns = {}
exec(Path('hw/tool_requirements.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8'), ns)
reqs = ns.get('__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__', {})
entry = reqs.get('verible', '')
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get('min_version', ''))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "${verible_version}" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi
if [[ -n "${verible_version}" ]]; then
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's OTP (One-Time Programmable) Controller exposes a Direct Access Interface (DAI) `ZEROIZE` command that lets firmware erase words in zeroizable partitions. When the target word belongs to a secret partition, firmware cannot inspect the returned raw word directly because secret-partition contents are scrambled, so the controller is supposed to return the number of set bits observed in the zeroized word through the DAI read-data path. Firmware uses that count to decide whether the word was zeroized successfully enough or whether the operation must be retried.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the OTP controller's DAI `ZEROIZE` path for zeroizable secret partitions, specifically the logic that publishes the post-zeroization set-bit count back to software.

## Expected Behavior
If a `ZEROIZE` command on a zeroizable secret-partition word completes with no OTP macro error, the controller must always return the observed set-bit count for that word to software through the DAI read-data path. This must remain true even when the count is below the macro-specific threshold used to decide whether a partition should be considered sufficiently zeroized. That threshold is only for judging the zeroization result, not for deciding whether software can see the count.

## Actual Behavior
The DAI can suppress the returned set-bit count for a secret-partition `ZEROIZE` operation even when the OTP macro reports success. When the observed count is below the zeroization-valid threshold, software does not receive the count value that it needs to evaluate a partial zeroization result and decide whether to retry or escalate.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when firmware issues `ZEROIZE` through the OTP controller DAI to a zeroizable secret partition, the OTP macro completes the command with `NoError`, and the returned zeroization word contains fewer set bits than the zeroization-valid threshold, for example one count below that bound.

title: [usbdev] Support conditional updates of the `rxenable_out` register
body:
This PR implements conditional changes to the enabled/disabled state of OUT transaction reception (`rxenable_out`) as described in #27434 in order to avoids a software/hardware race when the `set_nak_out` functionality is in use.

The register is implemented as `hwext` so that write enables may be supplied in the upper half-word, corresponding to new enable states (for those to be changed) in the lower half-word (USB supports a maximum of 16 OUT endpoints).

A follow-up PR implements a block-level DV sequence. The DV changes in this PR are necessary to keep the existing tests building and passing.

Fixes #27434

repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[usbdev] Conditional update of rxenable_out register

Avoid a sw-hw race in which the USB device may disable OUT packet
reception on an endpoint - because of the set_nak_out functionality -
and software then re-enables OUT packet on that endpoint when it
was simply trying to re-enable OUT packet reception on another
active endpoint.

This is achieved by including 'preserve' bits in the upper half of
word writes to the rxenable_out register; software may then update
only the endpoint(s) it wants to affect.

The use of 'preserve' bits, along with the priority of software writes
over hardware clears achieves backwards compatibility whilst allowing
firmware to be simplified on future versions of the USB device.

Signed-off-by: Adrian Lees <a.lees@lowrisc.org>

[dif/usbdev] Update DIF to modify selected rxenable_out bit(s)

Implement conditional update of the rxenable_out.out bit(s) to
avoid race with any other endpoints that are active and are
configured to accept only a single OUT packet before NAKing.

Signed-off-by: Adrian Lees <a.lees@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [USB] Interface for rxenable_out with set_nak_out is non-atomic
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

After much debugging, I am pretty sure I have tracked down a rare race condition that is currently impossible to avoid with the current register interface for `rxenable_out` when `set_nak_out` is enabled. The race condition occurs because both software and hardware are writing to `rxenable_out` at the same time, but the register is `rw` instead of an atomic safe interface.

This is the situation:
  * `set_nak_out` is enabled for all endpoints (i.e. `0xfff`)
  * An OUT packet comes in on endpoint 3
      *  Hardware immediately clears `(1 << 3)` in `rxenable_out`. Value of `rxenable_out` is `0xf7`.
   * Software processes endpoint 3 packet and can now receive another on that endpoint
   * Software must read-modify-write `rxenable_out`, however this can happen:
      * Software reads `rxenable_out` value as `0xf7`
      * USB HW peripheral receives a packet on endpoint 2 and clears bit `(1 << 2)` in `rxenable_out`. Value of `rxenable_out` is now `0xf3`.
      * Software sets bit `(1 << 3)` high again and write back `0xff` to `rxenable_out`
      * Now we have re-enabled endpoint 2 unintentionally even though software isn't ready for another packet on endpoint 2

I cannot figure out a way to prevent this race condition from occurring. It seems that the register interface for `rxenable_out` should be converted to two `rw1s` registers that either enable or disable `rxenable_out` so software has a option atomically enable/disable just a single endpoint.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's USB device (`usbdev`) IP uses the `rxenable_out` control/status register (CSR) to decide which OUT endpoints are allowed to accept USB OUT transactions. When `set_nak_out` is enabled for an endpoint, hardware automatically clears that endpoint's `rxenable_out` bit after one OUT packet so later packets on that endpoint are answered with a negative acknowledgement (NAK) until firmware explicitly re-enables it.

The current `rxenable_out` behavior is not safe when software needs to change one endpoint while hardware may clear another endpoint at the same time. Because software must use a read-modify-write sequence, a concurrent hardware clear can be lost and an endpoint can be re-enabled unintentionally.

## Expected Behavior
The `rxenable_out` CSR must support conditional per-endpoint updates in a single write to the same register. Software must be able to change only the targeted OUT endpoint enables while leaving all untargeted endpoints at their current values, and a write that targets all endpoints must still replace the full OUT-enable bitmap as requested. Reads of `rxenable_out` must continue to report the current OUT-enable state.

## Actual Behavior
Any write to `rxenable_out` overwrites the entire OUT-enable bitmap. If firmware reads the register, changes one endpoint, and writes the result back while hardware clears a different endpoint in the meantime, the write can accidentally re-enable that other endpoint. More generally, a write that is intended to preserve one subset of endpoint states while updating another subset instead replaces every endpoint's enable state.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered in the USBDEV OUT reception path when multiple OUT endpoints are enabled, `set_nak_out` is in use, and firmware re-enables or disables one endpoint while another endpoint may be cleared by hardware. It is also exposed by software writes that are intended to preserve one subset of OUT endpoint enables while updating a different subset in a single `rxenable_out` access.

problem_statement:
The Access Control Range Check (`ac_range_check`) IP filters TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) requests against configured address ranges and permissions. If a request matches multiple enabled ranges, the lowest-index matching range has priority and is supposed to determine whether that specific access type is allowed.

The current RTL can violate that priority rule when overlapping enabled ranges disagree on permissions by access type. In particular, a higher-priority range that denies reads but allows writes can be overridden by a lower-priority overlapping range that allows reads but denies writes, causing a read request that hits both ranges to be forwarded even though the higher-priority range should block it.

Expected behavior is that `ac_range_check` resolves permissions per requested access type using the highest-priority matching range. In the overlapping-range scenario above, the read must be denied: the filtered TL-UL request must not be forwarded, the module must generate its deny response, and, when deny logging is enabled, `LOG_STATUS.deny_range_index` must report the index of the range that actually caused the deny. The same overlap must still allow the write request, because the highest-priority matching range permits writes.

Trigger condition: at least two enabled `ac_range_check` ranges overlap on the same address, the lower-index range has higher priority, and the overlapping ranges grant different access types for that address. The bug is visible when a request uses an access type that the highest-priority matching range denies but a lower-priority matching range allows.

resolved_issues.title: [keymgr_dpe] Seed material going into creator root key
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

keymgr_dpe seems not to inlclude all the seed material into the creator root key it is meant to (see 
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/keymgr_dpe/rtl/keymgr_dpe.sv#L460-L469). More precisely, we have
```sv
    adv_matrix[Creator] = AdvDataWidth'({sw_binding,     // 256b
                                        revision_seed,   // 256b
                                        otp_device_id_i, // 256b
                                        lc_keymgr_div_i, // 128b
                                        rom_digests,     // 512b
                                        creator_seed});  // 256b
```
This adds up to a total of 1664 bits whereas `AdvDataWidth` is just 1152 bits.

This means the `revision_seed` as well as the `sw_binding` are not actually included in the creator root key. All remaining values either come from OTP or ROM and as a result there is currently no way to modify the creator root key. I don't think this is intentional but an oversight and we need to decide how to fix this.

The most obvious option is to define a keymgre_dpe custom `AdvDataWidth` parameter that is set to 1664. (keymgr should remain untouched)
Any ideas anyone? @ballifatih , @sameo , @Razer6 

For comparison, the regular keymgr in Earlgrey constructs the adv_matrix as follows:
```sv
  assign adv_matrix[Creator] = AdvDataWidth'({sw_binding,        // 256b
                                              otp_device_id_i,   // 256b
                                              lc_keymgr_div_i,   // 128b
                                              rom_digest_i.data, // 256b - Note there is just one ROM digest for Earlgrey instead of 2.
                                              revision_seed});   // 256b
```
We changed this before the Earlgrey production tapeout (see #22878 for details).

problem_statement:
## Description
In OpenTitan's Key Manager DPE (`keymgr_dpe`) IP, an advance operation that derives the creator root key from a source slot at the Creator boot stage (`boot_stage = 0`) does not pass all intended seed material to the Keccak Message Authentication Code (KMAC) input. The Creator-stage advance message is supposed to concatenate the software binding value (`sw_binding`, 256 bits), the hardware revision seed (`revision_seed`, 256 bits), the One-Time Programmable (OTP) device identifier (256 bits), the life cycle key-manager diversification value (128 bits), two Read-Only Memory (ROM) digests (512 bits total), and the creator seed (256 bits), for 1664 bits in total. Instead, only 1152 bits are forwarded, so the leading 512 bits are truncated.

## Expected Behavior
When `keymgr_dpe` performs an advance operation from a source slot at the Creator boot stage, the KMAC message for creator root key derivation must include all 1664 bits of Creator-stage seed material in the defined order: software binding, hardware revision seed, OTP device identifier, life cycle diversification value, both ROM digests, and creator seed. The software binding and hardware revision seed must participate in the derivation and must not be dropped before the KMAC request is issued.

## Actual Behavior
The Creator-stage advance message is truncated to 1152 bits before it reaches KMAC. As a result, the software binding and hardware revision seed do not contribute to the creator root key derivation, and the KMAC request only includes the remaining OTP- and ROM-backed inputs plus the creator seed.

## Affected Function
This affects the `keymgr_dpe` Creator boot-stage advance path, specifically the logic that assembles and forwards the advance-operation message to the KMAC interface for creator root key derivation.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when `keymgr_dpe` executes an advance operation whose source slot is at the Creator boot stage (`boot_stage = 0`), which is the path that constructs the creator root key input from software binding, hardware revision seed, OTP device ID, life cycle diversification data, ROM digests, and creator seed.

title: [pwrmgr] Take external SoC reset into account in FSM
body:
1. Internally generated reset request passed to SoC.
2. Create a sticky assertion internally to log request. Sticky flag cleared only upon external reset deassertion.
3. SoC transfers this request to platform to assert external reset.
4. External SoC reset deasserts after some time.
5. Pwrmgr stays in FastPwrStateRstWait state until the external SoC reset deasserts.
6. Boot / reset sequence continues.
7. Also fixes the external reset signal glitch filter to use the por reset. This is required to make sure that the external reset state does not self-reset once asserted and faithfully forwards that state to pwrmgr.
8. Added some debug visibility signals for pwrmgr.
9. Added temporary reset loop back path in pwrmgr TB to translate internal reset req from OT --> ext reset from SoC to OT.  Needs a proper fix in testbench (issue #22710).

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) controls reset sequencing and decides when the system can resume boot. When `pwrmgr` forwards an internally generated non-power-on reset request to an external SoC (system-on-chip) or platform reset controller, OpenTitan is expected to stay in reset until that external reset has been asserted and then deasserted.

## Expected Behavior
After an internal non-power-on reset request is handed off to the SoC/platform, the `pwrmgr` fast power finite-state machine (FSM) must remain in its reset-wait phase until the corresponding external reset cycle is fully complete. During that interval, `pwrmgr` must keep the system reset request asserted and keep processor instruction fetch disabled both before the external reset is asserted and while the external reset remains asserted. Normal boot may resume only after the external reset is deasserted.

## Actual Behavior
`pwrmgr` can treat the handoff as complete as soon as the original internal reset request clears. If the external reset is asserted later or remains asserted for longer, the FSM can leave the reset-wait phase too early, release the system reset request, and resume boot / processor fetch before the external reset cycle has finished.

## Affected Function
The bug is in the Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) fast power FSM logic that handles non-power-on reset handoff from an internally generated OpenTitan reset request to an externally driven SoC/platform reset.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs for an internally generated non-power-on reset, such as a software reset request, when the request is exported to the SoC/platform and the original internal request clears before the externally driven reset has completed its full assert/deassert cycle.

resolved_issues.title: [hmac] `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT` and `HMAC_CMD_HASH_PROCESS` commands causing hang conditions

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) IP can hang while finalizing a SHA-256 hash when software writes the last message word into the HMAC message FIFO, waits briefly, and only then issues `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT`, the command that tells the hardware that no more message data is coming. The affected functionality is the SHA-2 finalization path inside the HMAC IP.

## Expected Behavior
After the last message word has been accepted, issuing `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT` after a short delay must still finalize the pending message block, report that the hash operation is complete, and return the HMAC IP to idle. In software-visible terms, the idle bit in `HMAC.STATUS` (`hmac_idle`) must become set again instead of remaining cleared. This must also hold when the message length is exactly one full 512-bit SHA-256 block.

## Actual Behavior
With a short delay between the final FIFO write and `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT`, the hash operation can remain stuck in a non-idle state. Completion is never reported, `HMAC.STATUS.hmac_idle` stays cleared, and software waiting for the HMAC hardware to become idle can block indefinitely.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when a block-aligned SHA-256 message is written to the HMAC message FIFO, the final 32-bit word completes the last 512-bit block, no further message words are written, and `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT` is issued only after a small delay such as interrupt latency.

title: [top_earlgrey,pinmux] Enable pull-down for TAP strap 0 at reset
body:
TAP strap 0 is sampled after reset (and only once for life cycle states
that are not TEST_UNLOCKED* or RMA).  To ensure it gets sampled as 0
unless driven to 1 from an external source (and specifically that it
gets sampled as 0 when left floating / not connected), this enables the
pull-down of the pad at reset.

This resolves issue #24576 on `master`.

resolved_issues.body:
Earlgrey's IOC8 pad is used as TAP strap 0. [TAP strap 0 gets sampled at least once at boot in every LC state.](https://opentitan.org/book/hw/ip/pinmux/doc/theory_of_operation.html#strap-sampling-and-tap-isolation) Thus if the pad is not properly pulled down on a PCB and gets sampled as 1 at boot, the pads used for JTAG are not available as MIOs until the next reset (even if the LC state does not allow JTAG debug). To prevent this, we need to activate the pad-internal pull down of IOC8 at reset.

~~As the pad attributes of IOC8 are part of a multireg, we currently cannot set their reset value separately. We probably have to extend our multireg syntax and features to allow this.~~

This change needs to be applied on the `earlgrey_1.0.0` release branch (an ECO confirmed by a local RTL modification has already happened) as well as on `master`.

problem_statement:
## Description
In the top_earlgrey integration, IOC8 is the muxed I/O (MIO) pad used as TAP (Test Access Port) strap 0. TAP strap 0 is sampled during boot, and the sampled value determines whether the JTAG (Joint Test Action Group) pads remain reserved for TAP handling or stay available as general MIOs. The affected functionality is the pinmux IP reset state for the pad attributes of the MIO pad assigned to TAP strap 0.

## Expected Behavior
During reset and immediately after reset release, before software reprograms pad attributes, the pinmux pad-attribute state for the TAP strap 0 MIO pad must have its internal pull-down enabled. With that reset default, a floating or unconnected IOC8 pad is biased low and TAP strap 0 is sampled as 0 unless external hardware intentionally drives it high.

## Actual Behavior
The pinmux reset state leaves the TAP strap 0 MIO pad without its internal pull-down enabled. If IOC8 is floating or otherwise not driven low when the strap is sampled, it can be observed as 1 instead of 0. In that case, the JTAG-designated pads are not available as MIOs until the next reset, even in life cycle states that do not allow JTAG debug.

## Trigger Conditions
This occurs on Earlgrey systems when IOC8 serves as TAP strap 0, the device reaches the boot-time strap-sampling window after reset, and the pad is left floating, unconnected, or not actively driven low before software updates pad attributes.

title: [entropy_src/rtl] Delay the main_sm_done signal
body:
Due to the relocation of the 1-4-bit packer FIFO, the main SM done signal arrived one cycle too early in the single lane mode. This caused the SHA3 process_i signal to go high one cycle too early. This in turn caused the issue that the last word from the precon FIFO is not absorbed properly by SHA3.
This commit fixes this by delaying the main_sm_done signal by 1 cycle in the single lane mode. The ht_error signal has to be delayed by 1 cycle as well to guarantee that the error signal arrives at the same time as the main_sm_done signal.

Resolves #23773

resolved_issues.title: [entropy_src] Delay ht_done_pulse_i for the main SM by 1 cycle
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

Moving the 1-4-bit packer back in the pipeline #21626 introduced an issue where the `ht_done_pulse_i` can go high 1 cycle too early. This in combination with some other recent changes caused some unwanted words to be absorbed by SHA3.

When `ht_done_pulse_i` goes high this causes `process_i` for SHA3 to go high, which in turn leads to SHA3 not accepting any new inputs. If these signals go high 1 cycle too early SHA3 doesn't absorb the last word. The result were some test sequences that were failing due to a mismatch in the produced seeds.

I only observed it happening for the single lane mode, where one of the 4 random bit lanes is selected. This might be because the `post_ht` FIFO still receives the entropy without delay in normal operation.

Unfortunately I can't post a failing seed here for the `entropy_src_rng` test, since I had to change a lot in the DV environment to discover this bug.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan ENTROPY_SRC (Entropy Source) IP's hardware-conditioned FIPS seed generation path, specifically the handoff from the health-test completion logic to the SHA3 conditioner when `RNG_BIT_ENABLE` selects a single RNG lane. In this mode, the completion of a health-test window can be signaled before the final word from that window has been accepted from the pre-conditioner FIFO.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the ENTROPY_SRC main state machine and SHA3 conditioning interface that convert health-tested raw entropy into a conditioned seed output in single-lane FIPS operation.

## Expected Behavior
When ENTROPY_SRC is generating hardware-conditioned FIPS seeds from a single RNG lane, SHA3 must not start processing until every word belonging to the completed health-test window has been accepted from the pre-conditioner FIFO. The resulting conditioned seed must therefore be derived from the entire completed window, including its final word.

## Actual Behavior
In single-lane mode, the health-test completion pulse can arrive one cycle too early. This causes SHA3 `process_i` to assert before the last word from the pre-conditioner FIFO has been absorbed. Once `process_i` is asserted, SHA3 stops accepting new input words, so the final word of the completed window is omitted and the resulting conditioned seed no longer matches the expected seed for that window.

## Trigger Condition
The failure occurs when ENTROPY_SRC is configured for FIPS hardware conditioning with `RNG_BIT_ENABLE` selecting one of the four RNG lanes, and a health-test window completes while the final pre-conditioner FIFO word for that window is still being handed to SHA3. Under that boundary condition, the conditioned seed output is generated from incomplete input data and can mismatch.

resolved_issues.title: [edn] valid/ready protocol violations in case of ack errors and disablement
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

I noticed a couple of issues between EDN / CSRNG related to the CSRNG CMD interface:
- In case of disablement and in case of ACK errors triggered inside CSRNG, EDN can de-asserted the valid without waiting for the ready. Similarly, it can send less additional data than announced in the first command word (CSRNG cannot handle that).
- In case of ACK errors, CSRNG pops the erroneous word from the command FIFO. But the command FIFO may already contain additional data belonging to that command which may be left in the FIFO. Instead of just popping the FIFO, the FIFO should probably be cleared.

Both things are non-ideal but not catastrophic as we can always get out of these situations by disabling / re-enabling both EDNs and CSRNG which is anyway recommended in the programmer's guide right now. However, it would be better if those protocol violations wouldn't happen and if we wouldn't have to shutdown all CSRNG contexts because of an issue triggered by a single EDN.

problem_statement:
## Description
The Entropy Distribution Network (EDN) hardware-controlled command path to the Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator (CSRNG) can violate the CSRNG command valid/ready protocol when CSRNG reports an acknowledge/status error while an EDN hardware command is already pending. The affected logic is the EDN path that issues hardware-controlled CSRNG commands, including the boot request mode sequence.

## Expected Behavior
After EDN asserts the CSRNG command-valid signal for a hardware command, it must keep that request asserted until CSRNG raises the corresponding ready signal and the valid/ready handshake completes. If CSRNG reports an acknowledge/status error before that handshake completes, EDN must still finish the outstanding handshake first. Only after the handshake is complete should EDN record the CSRNG acknowledge error, raise its recovery status, and move into its reject/error state.

## Actual Behavior
If CSRNG signals an acknowledge/status error while the request is stalled and CSRNG is still not ready, EDN can drop the command-valid signal immediately. This cancels the in-flight hardware command before the handshake completes and violates the EDN-to-CSRNG valid/ready protocol.

## Trigger Conditions
This happens when EDN is issuing a hardware-controlled CSRNG command, CSRNG is backpressuring the interface so the request is waiting with valid high and ready low, and a CSRNG acknowledge/status error is reported during that stall. A representative case is boot request mode, where EDN has started a boot-time instantiate or generate command and CSRNG is not yet ready to accept it.

title: [csrng] Flush command FIFO after signaling ACK errors
body:
The decision whether a command is invalid is taken based on the command header but EDN might continue and send the additional data as well (it might already be in the FIFO). Previously, CSRNG would just pop the invalid command header from the FIFO and leave any additional data in the FIFO which can then erroneously be interpreted as the next command header.

Instead, we have to absorb the full invalid command before we can continue. This commit modifies the design to keep emptying the FIFO until the command interface is idle.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#23526.

problem_statement:
## Description
In OpenTitan's entropy complex, the Entropy Distribution Network (EDN) sends command packets to the Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator (CSRNG) over a hardware application command interface. Each packet begins with a 32-bit header word and may include additional 32-bit data words, as indicated by the header's `clen` field. The bug is in CSRNG's command-stage handling when the header of such a packet is rejected immediately as an invalid application command.

## Expected Behavior
When CSRNG rejects a command from its header and returns an acknowledgment (ACK) error for that packet, it must consume the entire packet before treating any later FIFO entry as the start of a new command. All additional data words that belong to the rejected packet, as indicated by `clen`, must be discarded as part of that same rejected packet. The rejected packet must produce only its single expected ACK/error response, and a following valid command must still be accepted at the next true packet boundary.

## Actual Behavior
If EDN sends an invalid command header with `clen > 0`, CSRNG removes only the rejected header word from the command FIFO. Any remaining data words from that rejected packet stay queued and can then be decoded as if they were a new command header. This can create an unexpected extra ACK response and can shift the command stream so that a later valid command is no longer interpreted at the correct packet boundary.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the CSRNG command-stage and command FIFO handling for the EDN-to-CSRNG hardware application command interface, specifically the handling of header-rejected command packets that still have additional data words buffered or arriving immediately afterward.

## Trigger Condition
This is triggered when EDN issues a command that CSRNG rejects immediately based on the first 32-bit header word, while the same packet contains at least one additional data word (`clen > 0`) that is already buffered or arrives back-to-back after the header.

title: [csrng] Locally escalate upon FSM errors
body:
Previously, these errors would trigger a fatal alert but not cause a local escalation (i.e. lock up the main SM). Since these FSM errors are structural errors that can't occur e.g. due to how the module currently operates but instead due to FI attacks only, these errors should also cause a local escalation.

This change better aligns CSRNG with EDN and ENTROPY_SRC.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#19789.

resolved_issues.title: [edn] FIFO error does not cause local escalation
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

Currently FIFO errors do not cause local escalation as can be seen in this snippet from the edn_core.sv:

https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/e13ff43f1b951c00ea2e24cafa60f7ac11d04e01/hw/ip/edn/rtl/edn_core.sv?plain=1#L295-L307

Other errors like counter or state machine errors cause the SM to enter an error state, while after a FIFO error the SM continues its operation. 

According to secure hardware design guideline [5.2](https://opentitan.org/book/doc/security/implementation_guidelines/hardware/index.html#recommendation-5-alerts) we should "prefer to take a local action (clearing/randomizing state, cease processing) in addition to generating the alert".

There could very well be a reason for not escalating locally but I couldn't find any reason in the documentation or in the lines of code above.

Should this be changed in the design (local escalation on FIFO error) or documented why *no* local escalation is preferable in this case?

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/csrng/rtl/csrng_core.sv b/hw/ip/csrng/rtl/csrng_core.sv
index 9a78fdcf0efc9..a390f7131ae89 100644
--- a/hw/ip/csrng/rtl/csrng_core.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/csrng/rtl/csrng_core.sv
@@ -490,6 +490,17 @@ module csrng_core import csrng_pkg::*; #(
     .intr_o                 (intr_cs_fatal_err_o)
   );
 
+  // Counter and FSM errors are structural errors and are always active regardless of the
+  // functional state. main_sm_err_sum is not included here to prevent some tools from
+  // inferring combo loops.
+  logic fatal_loc_events;
+  assign fatal_loc_events = cmd_gen_cnt_err_sum ||
+                            cmd_stage_sm_err_sum ||
+                            drbg_gen_sm_err_sum ||
+                            drbg_updbe_sm_err_sum ||
+                            drbg_updob_sm_err_sum ||
+                            aes_cipher_sm_err_sum;
+
   // set the interrupt sources
   assign event_cs_fatal_err = (cs_enable_fo[1]  && (
          (|cmd_stage_sfifo_cmd_err_sum) ||
@@ -512,13 +523,8 @@ module csrng_core import csrng_pkg::*; #(
          fifo_read_err_sum ||
          fifo_status_err_sum)) ||
          // errs not gated by cs_enable
-         cmd_stage_sm_err_sum ||
          main_sm_err_sum ||
-         drbg_gen_sm_err_sum ||
-         drbg_updbe_sm_err_sum ||
-         drbg_updob_sm_err_sum ||
-         aes_cipher_sm_err_sum ||
-         cmd_gen_cnt_err_sum;
+         fatal_loc_events;
 
   // set fifo errors that are single instances of source
   assign ctr_drbg_cmd_sfifo_cmdreq_err_sum = (|ctr_drbg_cmd_sfifo_cmdreq_err) ||
@@ -1160,7 +1166,7 @@ module csrng_core import csrng_pkg::*; #(
     .uninstant_req_o        (uninstant_req),
     .clr_adata_packer_o     (clr_adata_packer),
     .cmd_complete_i         (state_db_wr_req),
-    .local_escalate_i       (cmd_gen_cnt_err_sum),
+    .local_escalate_i       (fatal_loc_events),
     .main_sm_state_o        (cs_main_sm_state),
     .main_sm_err_o          (cs_main_sm_err)
   );
