#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout the PR baseline in a clean workspace.
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 6c32a3aa08440e994de820681cfc1e2ca6f0fbb0
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies for this baseline.
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at the baseline commit"
fi

# Stage 3: install Python dependencies needed by dvsim / FuseSoC.
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at the baseline commit"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install the RISC-V toolchain and persist its PATH.
# Verible download is intentionally skipped because the release URL used by the
# default harness prepare flow is no longer valid for this baseline.
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at the baseline commit; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) has a clock-domain crossing (CDC) bug in its escalation-reset handling path. The affected function is the logic that takes an escalation-reset request on `esc_rst_tx_i`, transfers it into the slow clock domain, and turns it into the escalation-triggered reset request path that drives the life-cycle reset request output (`rst_lc_req`).

## Expected Behavior
If `pwrmgr` observes an escalation-reset request on `esc_rst_tx_i`, it must capture that request even when the input is only a brief, non-permanent pulse that begins and ends between consecutive slow-clock sampling edges. After the request has been captured, the slow-domain escalation reset request must assert, `rst_lc_req` must assert, and the captured escalation request must remain asserted until reset clears it.

## Actual Behavior
When `esc_rst_tx_i` is only asserted briefly, `pwrmgr` can lose the request while synchronizing it into the slow clock domain. The escalation receiver can observe the pulse, but the slow-domain escalation reset request never asserts, `rst_lc_req` does not assert, and the escalation reset is effectively dropped.

## Affected Function
This affects `pwrmgr`'s escalation-reset CDC and request-latching logic between the escalation input and the slow-domain reset-request path.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when `esc_rst_tx_i` is a transient pulse asserted for fewer than two slow-clock cycles, so the pulse can occur entirely between slow-clock sampling edges instead of remaining continuously asserted.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Reset Manager (rstmgr) includes a leaf-reset consistency mechanism that watches generated leaf resets for unexpected child reset assertions or releases. The Always-On (AON) leaf reset `por_io_div4` is special: instead of only driving downstream logic, it is routed back into rstmgr as the block's own reset input. A shadowed copy of this leaf output exists as well.

## Expected Behavior
Because `por_io_div4` and its shadowed copy are part of rstmgr's own incoming reset path, they must not be treated as ordinary independently checkable leaf resets. When leaf-reset consistency checking is exercised, those two outputs should be excluded from consistency-fault checking instead of being expected to raise a leaf-reset consistency fault.

## Actual Behavior
The current rstmgr implementation includes `por_io_div4` and its shadowed copy in the normal leaf-reset consistency flow. If unexpected child reset activity is applied on either path, the same event can reset or shut down the checker before it finishes, so the consistency check for that leaf cannot complete.

## Affected Function
Reset Manager (rstmgr) leaf-reset consistency checking for the AON `por_io_div4` leaf reset, which loops back into rstmgr, and for the shadowed copy of that leaf output.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when the leaf-reset consistency mechanism iterates across reset leaves and includes `por_io_div4` or its shadowed copy, then applies unexpected child reset activity to that path.

title: fix(spi_device): Re-timing sck_cmdfifo_set clear time
body:
Related issue https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/11871

In previous design, the `sck_cmdfifo_set` signal is set by the ACK of
CMDFIFO write port and cleared by the FIFO DEPTH == 0.

THe clearing of FIFO depth depends on the SW processing time. This
commit revises it to CSb assertion pulse signal.

It is still bounded by the clock ratio between the SYS_CLK and the SCK.
SYS_CLK should not be 3 times slower than the SCK to correctly generate
the pulse signal within the opcode timeline.

repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
fix(spi_device): Missed Command Upload

This commit fixes one of the issue #11871

Problem:

    SW read incorrect opcode for Page Program.

Analysis
--------

The Page Program (0x02) opcode is adjacent to other commands that
SPI_DEVICE processes. So, the Datapath is fixed when the exact last beat
of the command opcode arrives. It is the second half of the 7th SCK.

The command parser activates Upload module at that time. However, the
top module switches the SRAM mux to the Upload module when the datapath
is latched by inverted SCK, which is right after the 8th posedge of SCK.

The Upload module, however, pushes the CMDFIFO entry (0x02 Page Program)
prior to 8th posedge of SCK to safely update the FIFO content as SCK
may not have 9th posedge if the SPI command is opcode only commands.
Examples are CHIP ERASE (0xC7), SECTOR ERASE, etc.

Resolution
----------

This commit revises the Mux design. Rather than using
`cmd_dp_sel_outclk`, it uses `cmd_dp_sel` (SCK clock) directly for the
SRAM mux. Other signals must be in inverted SCK clock domain to match
the output data phase.

Signed-off-by: Eunchan Kim <eunchan@opentitan.org>

fix(spi_device): Re-timing sck_cmdfifo_set clear time

Related issue #11871

In previous design, the `sck_cmdfifo_set` signal is set by the ACK of
CMDFIFO write port and cleared by the FIFO DEPTH == 0.

THe clearing of FIFO depth depends on the SW processing time. This
commit revises it to CSb assertion pulse signal.

It is still bounded by the clock ratio between the SYS_CLK and the SCK.
SYS_CLK should not be 3 times slower than the SCK to correctly generate
the pulse signal within the opcode timeline.

Signed-off-by: Eunchan Kim <eunchan@opentitan.org>

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] When and how should SW read cmdfifo, addrfifo, and payload buffer for correct data?
resolved_issues.body:
* spi_device should have a bit that indicates the completion of a SPI transaction and the FIFOs & the payload buffer are ready to be read from.
  * It looks like `cmdfifo_notempty` and `addrfifo_notempty` are updated independently during a SPI transaction.
  * According to the spec, `upload_payload_not_empty` in `INTR_STATE` register is updated after the transaction ends but it's not useful for commands without payloads.
  * `csb` in the `STATUS` register can possibly be used to check if a SPI transaction is complete but it is not clear whether sw can read from the FIFOs and the payload buffer right away.


* spi_device should ensure that values read from cmdfifo, addrfifo and payload are consistent with each other, e.g. they should always reflect the last transaction.
  * The address read from the address FIFO could belong to any command in the command FIFO (some commands don't have address fields), and similarly for the payload.
  * Please see [this thread](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/11884#discussion_r842004669).

cc @cfrantz @a-will

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan

TEST_NAME="spid_passthrough_upload_dynamic"
TB_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_spid_passthrough_upload_dynamic"
SCRATCH_ROOT="${TB_ROOT}/scratch"
BUILD_LOG="${TB_ROOT}/build.log"
RUN_LOG="${TB_ROOT}/run.log"
SIM_DIR="${SCRATCH_ROOT}/HEAD/spid_passthrough-sim-vcs/default"

rm -rf "${TB_ROOT}"
mkdir -p "${TB_ROOT}"

if [[ -f /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh ]]; then
  # Keep tool binaries on PATH when the harness replays the script.
  source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh
fi

python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

host_path = Path("hw/ip/spi_device/pre_dv/program/prog_passthrough_host.sv")
host_text = host_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
host_old = """  static task test_upload(output bit pass);
    SpiTransProgram trans;
    // Sequence
"""
host_new = """  static task test_upload(output bit pass);
    SpiTransProgram trans;
    pass = 1'b 1;

    // Sequence
"""
if host_old in host_text:
    host_text = host_text.replace(host_old, host_new, 1)
elif host_new not in host_text:
    raise SystemExit("host upload task patch point not found")
host_path.write_text(host_text, encoding="utf-8")

sw_path = Path("hw/ip/spi_device/pre_dv/program/prog_passthrough_sw.sv")
sw_text = sw_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
sw_new = """  static task test_upload();
    automatic logic [31:0] tl_rdata;
    automatic logic [ 7:0] opcode;

    wait(intr.upload_cmdfifo_not_empty);

    tlul_read(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_UPLOAD_CMDFIFO_OFFSET),
      tl_rdata
    );

    opcode = tl_rdata[7:0];
    $display("SW: Received Command: %2Xh", opcode);
    if (opcode != spi_device_pkg::CmdChipErase) begin
      $fatal(1, "SW: Unexpected Command: %2Xh / EXP(%2Xh)",
        opcode, spi_device_pkg::CmdChipErase);
    end

    tlul_write(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_INTR_STATE_OFFSET),
      1 << BitCmdfifoNotEmpty,
      4'b 1111
    );

    tlul_read(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_UPLOAD_STATUS_OFFSET),
      tl_rdata
    );
    if (tl_rdata[4:0] != 0) begin
      $display("SW: CMDFIFO not empty after fetching: %2d", tl_rdata[4:0]);
    end

    #3us;
    @(negedge clk);

    tlul_rmw(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_FLASH_STATUS_OFFSET),
      32'h 0,
      32'h 1
    );

    wait(intr.upload_cmdfifo_not_empty);

    tlul_read(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_UPLOAD_CMDFIFO_OFFSET),
      tl_rdata
    );

    opcode = tl_rdata[7:0];
    $display("SW: Received Command: %2Xh", opcode);
    if (opcode != spi_device_pkg::CmdPageProgram) begin
      $fatal(1, "SW: Unexpected Command: %2Xh / EXP(%2Xh)",
        opcode, spi_device_pkg::CmdPageProgram);
    end

  endtask : test_upload
"""
sw_pattern = re.compile(
    r"  static task test_upload\(\);\n.*?  endtask : test_upload\n",
    re.DOTALL,
)
if sw_pattern.search(sw_text):
    sw_text = sw_pattern.sub(sw_new, sw_text, count=1)
elif sw_new not in sw_text:
    raise SystemExit("sw upload task patch point not found")
sw_path.write_text(sw_text, encoding="utf-8")
PY

set +e
timeout 1800 bash -lc "
  set -euo pipefail
  ./util/dvsim/dvsim.py \
    hw/ip/spi_device/pre_dv/spid_passthrough_sim_cfg.hjson \
    -i spid_passthrough_upload \
    -t vcs \
    --build-only \
    --fixed-seed 1 \
    --build-seed 1 \
    --scratch-root '${SCRATCH_ROOT}' \
    >'${BUILD_LOG}' 2>&1

  cd '${SIM_DIR}'
  ./simv +ntb_random_seed=1 +TESTNAME=upload -l '${RUN_LOG}' >/dev/null 2>&1
"
flow_rc=$?
set -e

result="FAIL"
exit_code=1

if [[ ${flow_rc} -eq 0 ]] && [[ -f "${RUN_LOG}" ]] && \
   grep -q "TEST PASSED CHECKS" "${RUN_LOG}" && ! grep -q "Fatal:" "${RUN_LOG}"; then
  result="PASS"
  exit_code=0
fi

if [[ -f "${BUILD_LOG}" ]]; then
  cat "${BUILD_LOG}"
fi

if [[ -f "${RUN_LOG}" ]]; then
  cat "${RUN_LOG}"
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... ${result}"
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "${exit_code}"

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan SPI Device IP's flash Passthrough mode, where selected SPI flash commands are forwarded to flash but also uploaded to software, the command upload path does not always preserve transaction boundaries. After software consumes one uploaded command, later bus activity can leave the upload notification associated with the old transaction instead of the next completed uploaded transaction.

## Expected Behavior
Each uploaded SPI flash transaction must be reported exactly once after chip-select (CSb) is deasserted for that transaction. Once software reads an opcode from `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` and clears the corresponding `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` interrupt, later non-uploaded transactions such as `READ_STATUS` must not re-assert that interrupt or expose a stale command entry. When the next uploaded transaction completes, software must receive a new `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` event, and reading `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` must return the opcode for that new transaction.

## Actual Behavior
If software first consumes an uploaded opcode-only command such as `CHIP_ERASE`, intervening hardware-handled `READ_STATUS` transactions can leave the upload indication tied to the earlier command. The next wait for `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` may therefore wake on a stale event, and reading `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` can return `0x00` or the previous opcode instead of the opcode for the next uploaded command. In a later uploaded `PAGE_PROGRAM` transaction, software can therefore miss the new upload or read the stale erase opcode rather than `PAGE_PROGRAM`.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the SPI Device IP flash command upload path in Passthrough mode, specifically the software-visible command reporting mechanism through `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` and `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty`.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when an uploaded command that ends after the opcode phase, such as `CHIP_ERASE`, is followed by one or more non-uploaded `READ_STATUS` polling transactions, and then another uploaded command such as `PAGE_PROGRAM`. The failure depends on software having already read the earlier uploaded command and cleared its interrupt before the later uploaded command arrives.

  * `csb` in the `STATUS` register can possibly be used to check if a SPI transaction is complete but it is not clear whether sw can read from the FIFOs and the payload buffer right away.


* spi_device should ensure that values read from cmdfifo, addrfifo and payload are consistent with each other, e.g. they should always reflect the last transaction.
  * The address read from the address FIFO could belong to any command in the command FIFO (some commands don't have address fields), and similarly for the payload.
  * Please see [this thread](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/11884#discussion_r842004669).

cc @cfrantz @a-will

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the SPI Device IP's command-upload path in flash/passthrough mode. Software uses the uploaded command FIFO to identify flash transactions that are forwarded through the SPI device, so the uploaded opcode must correspond to the transaction that software is about to process.

## Expected Behavior
In flash/passthrough mode, when software observes that the upload command FIFO is non-empty and reads `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO`, the opcode returned by that register must match the newly completed uploaded flash transaction. In particular, after software has already consumed an uploaded opcode-only erase command such as Chip Erase, a later uploaded Page Program transaction must be reported as Page Program (`0x02`), not as an empty or stale previous opcode.

## Actual Behavior
After an uploaded opcode-only erase command has been handled, a subsequent uploaded Page Program transaction can be reported through `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` with an incorrect opcode instead of `0x02`. The value seen by software may be stale from earlier traffic, causing software to misidentify the Page Program transaction.

## Trigger Condition
The failure occurs in the SPI Device IP flash/passthrough upload path when command upload is enabled, software handles an uploaded opcode-only erase command, the flash is then polled with Read Status until the BUSY bit clears, and a Page Program command is issued afterward.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan SPI Host (Serial Peripheral Interface host) IP executes a transfer as a sequence of segments. When clock phase 1 (`CPHA=1`) is used, the end of the final segment can be mishandled: the last bit of that segment is not sampled correctly.

## Expected Behavior
For a `CPHA=1` transfer, the active segment must remain in progress until its final data bit has been sampled on the correct serial clock (`SCK`) edge. The data captured for the final segment must match the bits present on the SPI data lines, including the last bit.

## Actual Behavior
With `CPHA=1`, the final sampling point at the end of a segment can be mis-timed, so the last bit of the final segment is captured incorrectly.

## Affected Function
This affects the SPI Host IP's `CPHA=1` segment-completion timing and sampling logic.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the SPI Host runs a transfer with `CPHA=1` and reaches the boundary where the final bit of the final segment should be sampled.

problem_statement:
## Description
The affected module is the Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) Device IP's passthrough clock-forwarding path, which drives `passthrough_req_t.sck` toward the downstream SPI flash while the SPI Device is operating in passthrough mode. In this mode, the passthrough command filter can block configured command bytes instead of forwarding them. The forwarded downstream clock is expected to honor the passthrough clock-gating condition (`passthrough_req_t.sck_gate_en` in the current design), but it does not.

## Expected Behavior
When passthrough mode is enabled and the command filter identifies the command byte as blocked, the downstream transaction should be cut off immediately. The downstream active-low chip select (`CSb`) should deassert, and the forwarded downstream serial clock (`SCK`) should remain low even if the upstream SPI host continues toggling `SCK` until it releases `CSb`.

## Actual Behavior
After a filtered passthrough command, the downstream `CSb` can deassert, but the forwarded `SCK` still mirrors the upstream SPI host's `SCK`. As a result, the downstream SPI flash continues to observe clock edges for a command that the SPI Device has already filtered out.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs in the SPI Device passthrough command-filter path when passthrough mode is enabled, the upstream SPI host sends a command whose opcode is configured to be filtered, and the upstream SPI host continues clocking after the command byte has been rejected.

title: [flash_ctrl] Select appropriate ready's based on request source
body:
- fixes https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/12381
- the previous design used the read stage's ready for arbitration.
  Due to the way the design is currently done, the read stage ready
  is actually dependent on the the downstream flash macro actually
  ack-ing the transaction.  To fix this, we would need to de-couple
  the req/ack interface on the side facing the phy and the side facing
  the macro.  While this is doable, it would also require us to latch
  incoming bus attributes.  However, there is not a lot to gain by doing
  so, because as long as the flash has not responded, the next read
  cannot proceed anyways.
- This dependency can cause program/erase operations to lock-up if the
  the downstream macro does not always keep ack asserted when idle (in
  effect behaving more like ready).
- Even though the above fix would be cleaner long term, the quick fix is
  simply to pick the appropriate ready for host and controller operations
  separately.

  is actually dependent on the the downstream flash macro actually
  ack-ing the transaction.  To fix this, we would need to de-couple
  the req/ack interface on the side facing the phy and the side facing
  the macro.  While this is doable, it would also require us to latch
  incoming bus attributes.  However, there is not a lot to gain by doing
  so, because as long as the flash has not responded, the next read
  cannot proceed anyways.
- This dependency can cause program/erase operations to lock-up if the
  the downstream macro does not always keep ack asserted when idle (in
  effect behaving more like ready).
- Even though the above fix would be cleaner long term, the quick fix is
  simply to pick the appropriate ready for host and controller operations
  separately.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

[flash_ctrl] Allow fixed priority arbiter

- allow prim_arbiter_tree_dup to instantiate either rr or fixed priority
  arbiters
- switch phy arbitration to fixed priority since host most of the time
  has priority over controller

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

resolved_issues.title: Smoke test failing in the closed-source due to changes in the OS design
resolved_issues.body:
Hi,

Before everything, is it possible you'll add me as CC to the flash_ctrl's design PRs? It will help me to expect issues or things I need to update in the closed-source DV.

First of all, it seems the flash_ctrl prog_fifo depth has been changed in the flash_ctrl_env_pkg from 16 to 4, even though in the flash_ctrl spec is stated to still be 16. Is that intentional?
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/tb/tb.sv#L94-L98
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/env/flash_ctrl_env_pkg.sv#L34-L35
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78012616/165791068-5483a74b-f86e-49e4-a17b-49e96751deea.png)


Secondly and more important, it seems that some changes that were done in the flash_ctrl files are causing some issues.
Before the full description, in order to reproduce the issue run flash_ctrl_smoke test in the closed-source env (and in the OS as well, to understand the difference). Notice that this issue happens in program transactions, so there is a some small chance the random smoke test will not create a program scenario, so it's better to run a few to make sure.

**Description:**
All program transactions are failing in the closed-source environment due to that program requests are initiated in the flash_ctrl but are blocked from being sent to the inner closed-source hierarchy.
It seems that in order to send prog_i to the inner hierarchies, the signal state_d in file flash_phy_core should be set to StCtrlProg:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv#L298-L306
For state_d to change from idle to prog:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv#L283-L284
Now, while prog_i is 1 as expected, ctrl_gnt stays 0.
This comes from:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv#L98-L99
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree.sv#L124-L126
While the 2 first signals are 1 as needed, the ready signal isn't and comes from:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_rd.sv#L333-L335
All of those signals are as needed, except the ack. Notice that in order for the ready to be 1 the ack signal coming from the inner hierarchy should be 1, which isn't seems reasonable. Since no request was sent to the inner hierarchy by now, why would it send an acknowledge?
What comes from this is a loop - the request waits for an acknowledge which waits for a request.

In addition, it seems that the smoke test is passing in the OS env. The reason it's passing is because for some reason the acknowledge seems to always come before the request:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78012616/165788041-8ba36cc3-b7f0-4f12-b579-9b03dae0cc73.png)

Thanks!

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv
index 05ecbe32e14ba..f1982d6e50d0d 100644
--- a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv
@@ -101,7 +101,7 @@ module flash_phy_core
   state_e state_q, state_d;
 
   // request signals to flash macro
-  logic [PhyOps-1:0] reqs;
+  logic [PhyLastOp-1:0] reqs;
 
   // host select for address

@@ -236,7 +236,7 @@ module flash_phy_core
   // controller request can only win after the entire read pipeline
   // clears
   logic ctrl_req;
-  assign ctrl_req = req_i & rd_stage_idle & ~host_req &
+  assign ctrl_req = req_i & rd_stage_idle &
                     mubi4_test_false_strict(flash_disable[CtrlDisableIdx]);
 
   logic [1:0] data_tie_off [2];
@@ -244,24 +244,30 @@ module flash_phy_core
 
   // SEC_CM: PHY_ARBITER.CTRL.REDUN

+  logic phy_rdy;

   prim_arbiter_tree_dup #(

diff --git a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_pkg.sv b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_pkg.sv

--- a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_pkg.sv

@@ -84,14 +84,12 @@ package flash_phy_pkg;

-    PhyRead      = 2'h0,
-    PhyProg      = 2'h1,
-    PhyPgErase   = 2'h2,
-    PhyBkErase   = 2'h3
+    PhyProg,
+    PhyPgErase,
+    PhyBkErase,
+    PhyLastOp
   } flash_phy_op_e;
 
-  localparam int PhyOps = 4;
-
   // Flash Operations Selected
   typedef enum logic [1:0] {
     None         = 2'h0,
diff --git a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv
index 58d7abb5b42d9..8ed2a7c20dc09 100644
--- a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv
@@ -20,6 +20,9 @@ module prim_arbiter_tree_dup #(
   // EnDataPort: {0, 1}, if 0, input data will be ignored
   parameter bit EnDataPort = 1,
 
+  // if arbiter has fixed priority
+  parameter bit FixedArb = 0,
+
   // Derived parameters
   localparam int IdxW = $clog2(N)
 ) (
@@ -77,22 +80,43 @@ module prim_arbiter_tree_dup #(
       );
     end
 
-    prim_arbiter_tree #(
-      .N(N),
-      .DW(DW),
-      .EnDataPort(EnDataPort)
-    ) u_arb (
-      .clk_i,
-      .rst_ni,
-      .req_chk_i,
-      .req_i(req_buf),
-      .data_i(data_buf),
-      .gnt_o(arb_output_buf[i].gnt),
-      .idx_o(arb_output_buf[i].idx),
-      .valid_o(arb_output_buf[i].valid),
-      .data_o(arb_output_buf[i].data),
-      .ready_i
-    );
+    if (FixedArb) begin : gen_fixed_arbiter
+      prim_arbiter_fixed  #(
+        .N(N),
+        .DW(DW),
+        .EnDataPort(EnDataPort)
+      ) u_arb (
+        .clk_i,
+        .rst_ni,
+        .req_i(req_buf),
+        .data_i(data_buf),
+        .gnt_o(arb_output_buf[i].gnt),
+        .idx_o(arb_output_buf[i].idx),
+        .valid_o(arb_output_buf[i].valid),
+        .data_o(arb_output_buf[i].data),
+        .ready_i
+      );
+      logic unused_req_chk;
+      assign unused_req_chk = req_chk_i;
+
+    end else begin : gen_rr_arbiter
+      prim_arbiter_tree #(
+        .N(N),

+        .clk_i,
+        .rst_ni,

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout b2fed682d4b0617078c16527c69f72fca7f895f8
git submodule update --init --recursive

PREP_DIR=/home/opentitan/.prepare
rm -rf "$PREP_DIR"
mkdir -p "$PREP_DIR"

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt "$PREP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt"
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' "$PREP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt"
  if [[ -s "$PREP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt" ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < "$PREP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt"
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt "$PREP_DIR/python-requirements.txt"
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/home/opentitan/.prepare/python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r "$PREP_DIR/python-requirements.txt" --no-warn-script-location
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o "$PREP_DIR/verible.tar.gz" \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-18.04-bionic-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf "$PREP_DIR/verible.tar.gz" --strip-components=1
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in OpenTitan's flash controller (`flash_ctrl`), specifically in `flash_phy_core`, the block that arbitrates between an external host-side flash access and an internal controller-initiated flash operation before forwarding a request to the downstream flash macro.

## Expected Behavior
When the controller side issues an erase request while the `flash_phy_core` read stage is idle and there is no competing host-side request, `flash_phy_core` must grant that controller request and forward the corresponding erase request to the flash macro. The flash macro's acknowledge (`ack`) signal may legally remain low while idle and only assert after a request is presented, so controller-side progress must not depend on `ack` already being asserted before the request is sent.

## Actual Behavior
A controller-originated erase request can deadlock inside `flash_phy_core`. The controller request waits for a grant/readiness condition that is itself derived from the downstream flash macro's `ack`, while the flash macro waits to see the erase request before asserting `ack`. As a result, the erase request never reaches the flash macro and the controller operation never completes.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the `flash_ctrl` `flash_phy_core` arbitration and request handoff for controller-side erase operations to the downstream flash macro.

## Trigger Conditions
The failure occurs when a controller-side erase operation, including page erase, is issued while the `flash_phy_core` read stage is idle, no host-side request is competing for arbitration, and the downstream flash macro uses a request/acknowledge handshake where `ack` is asserted only after a request is presented rather than being held high while idle.

title: [spi_device] spi_p2s to run only when `data_valid`
body:
This commit addresses the issue #12342.

As dummy cycle may not be byte granularity, the output logic `spi_p2s`
now runs only when `data_valid_i` is high.

Now, `data_sent_o` is asserted when `data_valid_i` is high. The
data_sent_o is high based on the io_mode to compare `cnt` with the
correct value. The logic increases `cnt` only when `data_valid_i` is
high.

As `last_beat` is not asserted anymore, the `io_mode` does not latch
`io_mode_i` at `last_beat`. The logic uses `io_mode_i` directly. It is
OK as spi_device top latches comb logic io_mode at @ iSCK.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[spi_device] spi_p2s to run only when `data_valid`

This commit addresses the issue #12342.

As dummy cycle may not be byte granularity, the output logic `spi_p2s`
now runs only when `data_valid_i` is high.

Now, `data_sent_o` is asserted when `data_valid_i` is high. The
data_sent_o is high based on the io_mode to compare `cnt` with the
correct value. The logic increases `cnt` only when `data_valid_i` is
high.

As `last_beat` is not asserted anymore, the `io_mode` does not latch
`io_mode_i` at `last_beat`. The logic uses `io_mode_i` directly. It is
OK as spi_device top latches comb logic io_mode at @iSCK.

Signed-off-by: Eunchan Kim <eunchan@opentitan.org>

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] Dummy Cycle should be io_mode independent
resolved_issues.body:
dummy size should be independent of IoMode (Single, Dual, Quad).

In current design, the readcmd FSM assigns default IoSingle mode while in the dummy state. It results the parallel-to-serial logic to assert the `p2s_sent` signal in 8th cycle. If host system issues *Fast Read Dual* command, the dummy cycle is usually multiple of 4 cycles. As CMD_INFO slot for *Fast Read Dual* command is configured as to have 4 dummy cycles, the HW could not send correct values to the host system.

CC: @weicaiyang @kosta-kojdic

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_p2s.sv b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_p2s.sv
index 514993e84caad..0a1841cfbe20c 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_p2s.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_p2s.sv
@@ -170,22 +170,13 @@ module spi_p2s
 
   // io_mode
   // io_mode reset value is SingleIO (as described in assumption)
-  // Then, every byte sent, the logic updates its value to `io_mode_i`
-  // This makes the logic safer than direct use of `io_mode_i`.
-  // If `io_mode_i` value is changed within a byte, it affects to `last_beat`
-  // then, the incorrect `last_beat` affects `cnt`, which could break
-  // the data operation.
+  // Previously, logic updated io_mode at every byte. It was to make io_mode
+  // safer. However, as `io_mode_i` is updated at @iSCK (from spi_device top),
+  // and also spi_p2s logic runs only when `data_valid_i` is high, the need of
+  // latching logic disapears.
   //
-  // Following logic has high chance to break the rule. As there's no
-  // indication of the end of a byte. `data_sent_o` is not a valid indicator
-  // as the signal asserted one cycle earlier than the last beat.
-  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
-    if (!rst_ni) begin
-      io_mode <= SingleIO;
-    end else if (last_beat) begin
-      io_mode <= io_mode_i;
-    end
-  end
+  // Now, the logic uses `io_mode_i` directly.
+  assign io_mode = io_mode_i;
 
   // cnt
   always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
@@ -193,7 +184,7 @@ module spi_p2s
       cnt <= BitWidth'(0);
     end else if (last_beat) begin
       cnt <= BitWidth'(0);
-    end else if (tx_state != TxIdle || cpha_i == 1'b 0) begin
+    end else if (data_valid_i && (tx_state != TxIdle || cpha_i == 1'b 0)) begin
       cnt <= cnt + 1'b 1;
     end
   end

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) Device IP, specifically the `spi_p2s` transmit logic used by the read-command data path after dummy clocks. The dummy-clock phase is currently not treated independently from the selected SPI I/O width, even though Single I/O, Dual I/O, and Quad I/O read commands can use different numbers of data lines while still defining dummy time in SPI clock cycles.

## Expected Behavior
Dummy clocks must be consumed as command-defined idle SPI clock cycles, not counted as payload-transfer progress. During the dummy phase of a read command, the SPI Device must not treat the transfer as having advanced by part of a byte, must not indicate that a payload byte has been sent, and must not drive payload output enables. When the data phase starts, transmission must resume in the configured I/O mode. For example, if a Fast Read Dual command is configured with 4 dummy clocks before data, the SPI Device should consume exactly those 4 clocks as dummy time, then start the payload phase in Dual I/O, and only indicate that a byte has been sent after two valid Dual-I/O beats.

## Actual Behavior
In the current design, entering the dummy state can make byte-progress tracking behave as if Single I/O rules still applied. As a result, dummy clocks can be counted toward byte completion, causing the byte-sent indication to assert too early and the payload phase to start on the wrong boundary.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs for SPI Device read commands that use Dual I/O or Quad I/O and include a dummy phase whose length is not an 8-clock Single-I/O byte. A concrete failing case is a Fast Read Dual transaction configured with 4 dummy clocks before the payload data phase.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Power Manager (pwrmgr) uses a slow finite state machine (FSM) in the slow clock domain and a fast FSM in the main clock domain. When the slow FSM enters an invalid sparse-encoded state and raises `slow_fsm_invalid`, that condition is supposed to be treated as a terminal security fault. The invalid indication must still cross from the slow clock domain into the fast clock domain so that the fast FSM can leave normal operation and enter its invalid fault-handling state.

## Expected Behavior
If the slow pwrmgr FSM enters an invalid sparse-encoded state, the `slow_fsm_invalid` indication must continue to propagate through the slow-to-fast clock-domain crossing (CDC) path even when pwrmgr is in, or entering, a low-power or clock-gating transition. After observing that indication, the fast FSM must not remain in its normal active flow; it must enter its invalid terminal state and assert the reset requests required by pwrmgr's terminal fault response.

## Actual Behavior
When `slow_fsm_invalid` is asserted while the slow FSM would otherwise allow clocks to be turned off, the clock feeding the slow-to-fast CDC path can stop before the invalid indication is sampled in the fast clock domain. As a result, the fast FSM can remain in its normal active state instead of entering invalid fault handling, so the terminal response to the slow-FSM sparse fault is not completed correctly.

## Affected Function
This bug affects the pwrmgr slow FSM clock-enable logic during invalid-state handling, specifically the clocks that keep the slow-to-fast invalid-signal CDC path alive, and therefore the fast FSM's response to a slow-FSM sparse-encoding fault.

## Trigger Condition
The failure is triggered when the slow pwrmgr FSM is forced into an invalid sparse-encoded state at a time when its normal sequencing would otherwise gate clocks off or allow them to turn off.

title: [flash_ctrl] Separate invalid and disabled states.
body:
- fixes https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/11825

Part of the D2S design fixes was to unify the disabled behavior across
more of the flash controller state machines. However this created a
problem for RMA entry.

When RMA entry is done, the RMA fsm also requests flash operationst to be
disabled. Previosuly, this caused the RMA fsm itself to transition into
an invalid state.  This caused 2 problems:

1. At the end of RMA, a fatal alert is generated. While this is
   not bad behavior in any meaningful way, it is very inconsistent with alert
   defintion because no fatal event has occurred. This leads to unnecessary
   DV work.

2. Since the RMA fsm transitions out of its ack state, it means the ack
   indication sent to life cycle controller will be held for only 1 cycle.
   This is most definitely not enough for CDC and means RMA cannot be completed.

This commit separates the idea of "disabled" and "invalid" for most of the fsms.
Disabled simply means functionally disabled from future operations, while
invalid is both disabled AND alert generation.

At the end of RMA transition, the device is simply "disabled" and not "invalid".
Invalid then can only be caused by an explicit error, or the FSMs going
completely to an undefined state.

This makes the overall definition more consistent.

repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[flash_ctrl] Separate invalid and disabled states.

- fixes #11825

Part of the D2S design fixes was to unify the disabled behavior across
more of the flash controller state machines. However this created a
problem for RMA entry.

When RMA entry is done, the RMA fsm also requests flash operationst to be
disabled. Previosuly, this caused the RMA fsm itself to transition into
an invalid state.  This caused 2 problems:

1. At the end of RMA, a fatal alert is generated. While this is
   not bad behavior in any meaningful way, it is very inconsistent with alert
   defintion because no fatal event has occurred. This leads to unnecessary
   DV work.

2. Since the RMA fsm transitions out of its ack state, it means the ack
   indication sent to life cycle controller will be held for only 1 cycle.
   This is most definitely not enough for CDC and means RMA cannot be completed.

This commit separates the idea of "disabled" and "invalid" for most of the fsms.
Disabled simply means functionally disabled from future operations, while
invalid is both disabled AND alert generation.

At the end of RMA transition, the device is simply "disabled" and not "invalid".
Invalid then can only be caused by an explicit error, or the FSMs going
completely to an undefined state.

This makes the overall definition more consistent.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

#!/bin/bash
set -u -o pipefail

cd /home/opentitan

if [[ -f /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh ]]; then
  source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh
fi

TEST_NAME="flash_ctrl_rma_ack_hold"
VSEQ_FILE="hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/env/seq_lib/${TEST_NAME}_vseq.sv"
VSEQ_LIST="hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/env/seq_lib/flash_ctrl_vseq_list.sv"
ENV_CORE="hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/env/flash_ctrl_env.core"

report_result_and_exit() {
  local status="$1"
  local rc="$2"

  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... ${status}"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit "${rc}"
}

ST_RMA_RSP_VALUE="$(sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*StRmaRsp[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*\\([^,]*\\),/\\1/p" \
  hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_ctrl_lcmgr.sv | head -n1)"

if [[ -z "${ST_RMA_RSP_VALUE}" ]]; then
  report_result_and_exit "FAIL" 1
fi

cat > "${VSEQ_FILE}" <<EOF
// Copyright lowRISC contributors.
// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, see LICENSE for details.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

class ${TEST_NAME}_vseq extends flash_ctrl_base_vseq;
  \`uvm_object_utils(${TEST_NAME}_vseq)
  \`uvm_object_new

  localparam logic [10:0] StRmaRspValue = ${ST_RMA_RSP_VALUE};

  virtual task body();
    string lcmgr_state_path = "tb.dut.u_flash_hw_if.state_q";
    string lcmgr_state_raw_path = "tb.dut.u_flash_hw_if.u_state_regs.state_o";
    int ack_high_cycles = 0;
    bit ack_seen = 0;

    \`uvm_info(\`gfn, "FLASH_CTRL_RMA_ACK_HOLD", UVM_LOW)

    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(10);
    cfg.flash_ctrl_vif.rma_seed = 32'h1badc0de;
    cfg.flash_ctrl_vif.rma_req = lc_ctrl_pkg::On;

    if (!uvm_hdl_deposit(lcmgr_state_path, StRmaRspValue)) begin
      \`uvm_fatal(\`gfn, \$sformatf("Failed to deposit %s", lcmgr_state_path))
    end
    if (!uvm_hdl_deposit(lcmgr_state_raw_path, StRmaRspValue)) begin
      \`uvm_fatal(\`gfn, \$sformatf("Failed to deposit %s", lcmgr_state_raw_path))
    end

    repeat (20) begin
      cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(1);
      if (cfg.flash_ctrl_vif.rma_ack == lc_ctrl_pkg::On) begin
        ack_seen = 1;
        break;
      end
    end

    if (!ack_seen) begin
      \`uvm_fatal(\`gfn, "RMA ACK did not rise after depositing StRmaRsp")
    end

    repeat (10) begin
      if (cfg.flash_ctrl_vif.rma_ack == lc_ctrl_pkg::On) begin
        ack_high_cycles++;
      end
      cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(1);
    end

    \`uvm_info(\`gfn, \$sformatf("Observed RMA ACK high for %0d / 10 cycles", ack_high_cycles),
               UVM_LOW)
    if (ack_high_cycles < 10) begin
      \`uvm_error(\`gfn, \$sformatf("RMA ACK was not held high long enough: %0d / 10 cycles",
                                   ack_high_cycles))
    end
  endtask
endclass
EOF

if ! grep -q "${TEST_NAME}_vseq" "${VSEQ_LIST}"; then
  printf '%s\n' "\`include \"${TEST_NAME}_vseq.sv\"" >> "${VSEQ_LIST}"
fi

python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/env/flash_ctrl_env.core")
text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
needle = "      - seq_lib/flash_ctrl_vseq_list.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n"
insert = needle + "      - seq_lib/flash_ctrl_rma_ack_hold_vseq.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n"
if "seq_lib/flash_ctrl_rma_ack_hold_vseq.sv" not in text:
    text = text.replace(needle, insert)
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
PY

rm -rf scratch/HEAD/flash_ctrl_wrapper-sim-vcs

timeout 1800 ./util/dvsim/dvsim.py \
  hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/flash_ctrl_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i flash_ctrl_smoke \
  -t vcs \
  --fixed-seed 1 \
  --build-seed 1 \
  --run-opts +UVM_TEST_SEQ=${TEST_NAME}_vseq
rc=$?

if [[ ${rc} -eq 0 ]]; then
  report_result_and_exit "PASS" 0
else
  report_result_and_exit "FAIL" "${rc}"
fi

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan flash controller, the life cycle manager logic that finishes an RMA (Return Material Authorization) entry mis-handles the final response phase. When the wipe flow completes and the controller simultaneously marks flash access as disabled for all future operations, the RMA completion path treats that normal post-RMA disabled condition as an invalid/error condition. The controller then leaves the final RMA response state immediately, so the RMA acknowledgement signal `rma_ack` is asserted for only one cycle instead of being held long enough for the life cycle controller to sample it.

## Expected Behavior
After a successful RMA entry, the flash controller should enter a disabled post-RMA state that blocks future flash operations without being treated as an invalid state. While RMA completion is being reported, `rma_ack` must remain asserted until the life cycle controller can observe the acknowledgement across the clock-domain crossing (CDC) handshake.

## Affected Functionality
This affects the flash controller's life cycle manager submodule responsible for RMA completion and the acknowledgement path from the flash controller back to the life cycle controller, especially the boundary between the final RMA response state and the post-RMA disabled state.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered at the end of a successful RMA wipe sequence, when the controller enters the final RMA response phase and the same transition also disables subsequent flash access.

resolved_issues.body:
- d2s item

Unexpeted acks are checked in two places, the controller access
path and the host access path.

For the controller access path, the accesses are fsm controlled,
so whenever the fsm is idle it should not see an ack.

For the host access path, a small amount of logic is added to track
the number of outstanding host transactions. When there are no
outstanding transactions, a response is not expected and would constitute a
spurious ack.

if [[ -z "${verible_version}" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "${verible_version}" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  static_url="https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  bionic_url="https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-18.04-bionic-x86_64.tar.gz"
  if ! curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz "${static_url}"; then
    curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz "${bionic_url}"
  fi
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The Flash Controller (`flash_ctrl`) exposes flash memory through a host direct-access TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) interface, separate from its control and status register interface. On that host direct-access path, command-integrity errors from the embedded-flash SRAM adapter are not connected to the controller's fatal fault reporting.

## Expected Behavior
If a TL-UL request on the flash host direct-access interface arrives with invalid command integrity bits, `flash_ctrl` must treat it as the same standard fatal integrity fault used for other Flash Controller TL-UL command-integrity failures. The error must be reported through the controller's normal standard fault and alert path rather than being ignored.

## Actual Behavior
When invalid command integrity is detected on the host direct-access path, the error is dropped before it reaches the Flash Controller's fatal fault handling. As a result, the integrity violation on that path is not reported as a fatal standard fault.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the Flash Controller host direct-access memory interface, specifically the command-integrity reporting path from the embedded-flash TL-UL/SRAM adapter into `flash_ctrl`'s standard fatal fault reporting.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a bus master accesses the flash memory window through the host direct-access TL-UL interface, rather than through the control and status register interface, and the TL-UL command carries invalid integrity bits.

1 | LC_CTRL | cSHAKE128 | “LC_CTRL”
2 | ROM_CTRL | cSHAKE256 | “ROM_CTRL”

cc: @cindychip @timothytrippel

prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout d8b2ed5accf591796a58e0a428ae9670e74d5646
git submodule update --init --recursive

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
fi

if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {"types-dataclasses", "types-pkg_resources"}:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
fi

toolchain_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "${toolchain_version}" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "${toolchain_version}"
  else
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "${verible_version}" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-18.04-bionic-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) IP has prefix control/status registers (CSRs) that hold the cSHAKE/KMAC function-name and customization prefix. The key manager (KeyMgr) also depends on this prefix when it uses KMAC internally. The bug is that software can still rewrite a KMAC prefix CSR after a KMAC operation has started and the engine is no longer idle.

## Expected Behavior
Once a KMAC operation has started, the prefix CSRs must remain unchanged until that operation finishes and the KMAC engine returns to the idle state. A write attempted while the engine is busy must not change the stored prefix value.

## Actual Behavior
A write to a prefix CSR during an active KMAC operation can change the stored prefix value before the engine returns to idle. As a result, the prefix setting is not guaranteed to stay stable for the full duration of the request, which is also unsafe for KeyMgr operations that rely on the same KMAC prefix setting.

## Trigger Condition
Program the KMAC prefix CSRs, start a KMAC operation, wait until the KMAC engine has left the idle state, and then write a new value to a prefix CSR before the operation completes.

resolved_issues.title: [adc_ctrl/rtl] Fix Interrupt clock domain crossing
resolved_issues.body:
Currently the interrupt clock domain crossing uses a primitive with the unfortunate property that multiple triggers on the always on clock side while the gated clock is off can cause difficult to predict results.
The first trigger sets the interrupt, a second occurring during a gated period clears the interrupt again, a third sets it again and so on.
This leads to unexpected results.

Perhaps a scheme where all the interrupt logic is performed on the always on side, then copied via a request/acknowledge type CDC to the gated side, would be preferable.

I've re-enabled interrupts for test adc_ctrl_clock_gating in this PR https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/11760

problem_statement:
## Description
The ADC Controller has an interrupt clock-domain crossing bug in the path that carries filter-match events from the always-on clock domain into the gated main clock domain.

## Expected Behavior
If an enabled filter-match event occurs while the main ADC interrupt/register clock is gated off, that event must remain pending until the main clock resumes. Repeated pulses from the same filter-match source during the gated interval must not cancel or clear the pending interrupt. Once the main clock is running again, the corresponding ADC interrupt-status bit and the top-level interrupt pending state must both be asserted.

## Actual Behavior
When the same filter-match source pulses multiple times while the main clock is gated, the current synchronization logic can toggle the pending state on each pulse. After an even number of pulses during one gated interval, the ADC Controller can resume with no pending interrupt, even though an enabled filter-match event occurred.

## Affected Function
ADC Controller interrupt handling for filter-match events that are generated in the always-on clock domain but must update interrupt status and interrupt pending state in the gated main clock domain.

## Trigger Condition
This is triggered when the ADC Controller enters a state where the main clock domain is gated but the always-on ADC logic continues running, and the same enabled filter-match interrupt source fires multiple times before the main clock domain is ungated.

title: [spi_device] Change `addr_latched` to a pulse signal
body:
Problem:

    `addr_latched_i` in `spid_readsram` module is expected to be a pulse
    signal. The `spi_readcmd` module generates the signal as a level by
    comparing `addr_cnt_d` with all zero value.

    As a result, the `strb` register in `spid_readsram` follows the
    current address, which is increased by when a byte is sent to the
    host system. However, the `spid_readsram` logic pushes the data into
    the FIFO already. As the FIFO depth is 2, one more entry has been
    added to the FIFO, which results the host system sees the a byte has
    been shifted.

Resolution:

    Revised the `addr_latched` logic to be a pulse. Either `addr_cnt_d`
    or `addr_latched` can be revised. I chose the latter. Latching the
    latched signal and generated a pulse.

This PR contains #11829  Please review the last commit only. I will rebase once the PR is merged

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug affects the SPI_DEVICE IP's internally handled Read SFDP (Serial Flash Discoverable Parameters, opcode `0x5A`) path, specifically the flash-read datapath between `spi_readcmd` and `spid_readsram` that serves bytes from the SFDP region of the internal dual-port SRAM (DPSRAM).

## Observed Behavior
When an external SPI master performs a multi-byte SFDP read, the byte stream returned by SPI_DEVICE can be shifted relative to the contents stored in the SFDP SRAM region. The memory contents are correct, but the bytes driven on the SPI interface do not match the requested address sequence.

## Expected Behavior
After the 24-bit SFDP address has been accepted, SPI_DEVICE should return the bytes stored at that address and each following address in order, with no skipped, duplicated, or shifted bytes. For example, an 8-byte read starting at address `0x000080` should return the eight bytes stored at `0x000080` through `0x000087` in that same order.

## Trigger Condition
The failure appears when the Read SFDP command transitions from address capture into continuous multi-byte data output. It is observable on sequential SFDP reads, including an aligned 8-byte transfer starting at `0x000080`.

resolved_issues.body:
This was brought up during the RV_DM testplan review. 

Currently, if the debugger-initiated access into the full chip over the SBA interface results in an error response, the error is silently dropped and the debugger has no way of knowing that that has happened. What the engineer intended to do using the debugger would actually not happen, and they wouldn't know about it. 

The SBCS register specification in the [RISCV debug spec 0.13.2](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-debug-spec/raw/4e0bb0fc2d843473db2356623792c6b7603b94d4/riscv-debug-release.pdf) (page 34) defines a 3-bit `sberror` field, with value of '7' representing "other" error. It does not explain well what constitutes as "other" error, but we could very well use that to indicate the returned error response. The `dm_sba.sv` module just needs to gain an input signal which will be wired up to the error response from the external device, and when asserted, it could be used to set `sberror = 7`. This seems like a fairly simple enhancement, which will improve the debug experience a bit.

If there is consensus on whether this is feasible and the right thing to do, we can open up a PR in the PULP repo and have it fixed.

problem_statement:
OpenTitan's RISC-V debug module (`rv_dm`) does not correctly report a System Bus Access (SBA) write failure when the downstream TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) target returns an error response. SBA is the path that lets an external debugger access memory-mapped addresses through JTAG and the Debug Module Interface (DMI). In the failing case, the debugger issues a normal SBA write, the request is accepted, and the target later responds with a TL-UL error. That response is currently dropped, so the debugger can observe the transaction without any corresponding SBA error being recorded.

This affects the `rv_dm` SBA path, specifically the logic that turns TL-UL response errors into status in the System Bus Control and Status (`SBCS`) register.

Expected behavior: when an SBA write receives a TL-UL error response from the addressed target, `rv_dm` must update `SBCS.sberror` to the SBA bad-address / bus-access error classification so the debugger can tell that the access failed. The failure must not be reported as a busy error (`sbbusyerror`), and it must not be indistinguishable from a timeout or a successful completion.

Trigger condition: a debugger-initiated SBA write reaches the TL-UL system bus and the downstream target returns an error response for that write on the response path.

problem_statement:
## Description
In OpenTitan's life cycle controller (`lc_ctrl`), the controller finite state machine (FSM) keeps the current life cycle state and the life cycle transition count in the internal sparse-encoded registers `u_state_regs` and `u_cnt_regs`. These values are derived from the chip's One-Time Programmable (OTP) life cycle data.

## Expected Behavior
`u_state_regs` and `u_cnt_regs` should be protected in the same way as the main `lc_ctrl` FSM state register. If either register is corrupted to an invalid sparse encoding after reset, OpenTitan's predefined security-countermeasure fault-injection checks for sparse FSM state should be able to target that register, and `lc_ctrl` should treat the corruption as a life cycle state error: it must raise `fatal_state_error` instead of continuing to report a normal life cycle state.

## Actual Behavior
`u_state_regs` and `u_cnt_regs` are not handled as protected sparse FSM state elements in the same way as the main FSM state register. Because of that, the predefined security-countermeasure checks do not cover these two registers correctly, and fault injection or other corruption in either register can miss the expected fatal life cycle state error response.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a runtime fault, tamper event, or security-countermeasure fault injection corrupts `u_state_regs` or `u_cnt_regs` after reset so that the stored life cycle state or life cycle count is no longer a valid sparse encoding.

    value is continuously checked with the original configuration.
  - check that when the main fsm changes state into one of the key states,

## Description
The OpenTitan Key Manager (`keymgr`) issues one decoded command to its Keccak Message Authentication Code (`KMAC`) interface for each operation. For identity-generation and output-generation requests, that command is represented by a one-hot internal selection. Once a KMAC transaction has started, the in-flight command must remain identical to the command implied by the original software-programmed operation.

## Expected Behavior
After `keymgr` launches a KMAC transaction, the one-hot command delivered to the KMAC interface must stay unchanged until that transaction completes. In particular, if software starts an identity-generation operation (`OpGenId`), the in-flight request must remain an identity-generation request for the full transaction. If the command changes to a different legal one-hot value before completion, `keymgr` must treat this as a fatal command-consistency fault: the operation must end with `OP_STATUS` reporting failure, `FAULT_STATUS.CMD` set, and the key manager entering the terminal `Invalid` working state rather than accepting the altered command.

## Actual Behavior
In the buggy implementation, `keymgr` checks that the command is one-hot, but does not continuously verify that the active KMAC command still matches the command that started the transaction. A request can therefore begin as one legal command and later appear as a different legal one-hot command without triggering the fatal command-consistency fault. In that case, the operation is not forced onto the `OP_STATUS` failure, `FAULT_STATUS.CMD`, and `Invalid`-state path described above.

## Affected Function
This affects the `keymgr` KMAC command interface, specifically the in-flight command-consistency check for identity-generation and output-generation operations.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a valid generation request has already launched a KMAC transaction and, before KMAC signals completion, the internal one-hot command changes to a different legal command. A concrete failing case is an identity-generation request (`OpGenId`) whose in-flight KMAC command changes to a non-identity generate command while the transaction is still active.

title: [spi_device] Block the passthrough with BUSY status
body:
This commit addresses the issue #10785.

The BUSY @ SYS_CLK is set when SPI_DEVICE receives commands that satisfy:

- busy field in the CMD_INFO of the opcode is set
- CSb is de-asserted (SPI transaction completion)

When BUSY is set, SW may process the received command (assuming upload
field is set). After the command is processed by SW, SW may clear the
BUSY @SYS_CLK, which then will be propagated into SPI CLK (SCK) domain
at the next SPI transaction.

This commit is to turn off the passthrough interface if BUSY is set. So,
that the SW does not have to manually turn off the passthrough.

Keep in mind that this change cannot fully cover the corner cases:

- CSb is about to asserted (Beginning of the SPI transaction) at the
  same time BUSY is cleared by SW.

It is due to the CDC path of CSb to be used in SYS_CLK domain. It needs
to pass through 2FF synchronizer to be used in SYS_CLK safely. The delay
is 2 SYS_CLK. If BUSY falls in that window, the BUSY clearing may
unblock passthrough while SPI is active. The behavior of the IP is
undetermined.
