problem_statement:
## Description
The KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) IP's `kmac_entropy` submodule does not keep the selected entropy source stable after software finishes configuration. Once software asserts `entropy_ready` and the block has already completed an initial entropy-seeding cycle, a later write to the `CFG.entropy_mode` register can still affect the live entropy path even though the IP has not been reset.

## Expected Behavior
After `entropy_ready` is asserted, the entropy mode for the current KMAC session must remain fixed until the KMAC IP is reset and configured again. A software write to `CFG.entropy_mode` after that point must not change how a later entropy refresh is handled. For example, if the session was configured to use EDN (Entropy Distribution Network) entropy, a subsequent refresh in the same session should still request and consume EDN-provided seed data, even if software writes `EntropyModeNone` before the refresh.

## Actual Behavior
After a previous operation has completed and the entropy block is back in its ready state, `kmac_entropy` still observes the live `CFG.entropy_mode` value. If software changes the mode from `EntropyModeEdn` to `EntropyModeNone` without resetting the IP, the next refresh can behave as though the mode changed mid-session instead of preserving the original EDN-backed configuration.

## Affected Function
This affects the KMAC `kmac_entropy` entropy refresh and reseed path that supplies entropy to the SHA3/KMAC datapath.

## Trigger Condition
Configure `kmac_entropy` to use EDN entropy, assert `entropy_ready`, let it complete an initial seed or hash-related entropy cycle, and then, without resetting the KMAC IP, rewrite `CFG.entropy_mode` to `EntropyModeNone` before requesting another entropy refresh.

title: [lc_ctrl] Do not assert escalate_en in post transition state
body:
Although the post-transition state is a virtual scrap state, we should not assert `escalate_en` in order to avoid accidental triggering of alerts and escalation sequences. Such escalation sequences typically lead to lead to autonomous system resets, and that could cause issues with the life cycle transition status readout via the life cycle TAP.

Addresses https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/7251

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

resolved_issues.title: [chip/lc_ctrl] should we assert escalation_en during PostTrans State?
resolved_issues.body:
This tracks an offline discussion between Michael and I.

Issue:
When lc transition handshake finished without error, LC_CTRL goes to PostTrans state. 
In lc_ctrl_signal_decode.sv, this will turn on `escalation_en` signal:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/rtl/lc_ctrl_signal_decode.sv#L179

Michael and I found this `escalation_en` will trigger alert, and can potentially trigger `reset` (depends on how alert_handler is configured). We believe this behavior is not ideal because this automatically triggered `reset` might block user from using TAP to access LC_CTRL registers.
We plan to not turn on `escalation_en` when reaches PostTrans state.

Screenshot as below:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11466553/124972887-b908e100-dfdf-11eb-8367-9099d34c0bda.png)

@msfschaffner, please correct me if I misunderstand any part.

Thanks,
Cindy

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan life cycle controller (`lc_ctrl`) enters an internal post-transition FSM state (`PostTransSt`) after a life cycle transition handshake completes successfully. In that state, software or debug logic may need to read the transition result through the life cycle Test Access Port (TAP). The bug is in the `lc_ctrl` output decode path that drives life cycle enable signals while the controller is in `PostTransSt`.

## Expected Behavior
While `lc_ctrl` is in `PostTransSt`, it must remain in a post-transition holding state rather than behaving like an escalation-related state. `lc_escalate_en_o` must stay deasserted, and normal life cycle permission outputs, including `lc_cpu_en_o`, must remain deasserted. A real escalation or scrap-handling state, such as `EscalateSt`, may still assert `lc_escalate_en_o`.

## Actual Behavior
When a transition completes without error and the FSM enters `PostTransSt`, `lc_ctrl` asserts `lc_escalate_en_o`. That assertion can trigger the Alert Handler and, depending on configuration, start an escalation sequence that resets the system. As a result, a successful transition can interfere with reading the transition status through the TAP.

## Affected Function
This affects the `lc_ctrl` IP's post-transition signal decode logic, specifically how `PostTransSt` drives `lc_escalate_en_o` and other life cycle permission outputs.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a life cycle transition handshake finishes successfully and the `lc_ctrl` FSM moves into `PostTransSt`. In that condition, the design raises the escalation output even though the controller is only holding the successful transition result for readout.

resolved_issues.body:
Hi Michael,

Here is an issue with LC state transition to Scrap state:
1). LC current state: RMA, cnt: 7.
2). Request transition to Scrap state.
3). LC send otp_program_o to update count to 16 (because it is Scrap state)   --> successed
4). LC send otp_program_o to update state to Scrap state ---> Failed because the request count is 8 instead of 16.

Issue:
When we request lc_cnt update, `lc_fsm_state` is in `CntIncrSt`, and `next_lc_cnt` is updated to `16`.
When we request state update, `lc_fsm_state` is in `TransProgSt` and the `next_lc_cnt` is equal to `lc_cnt_i`, which is 8.
LC_cnt updates to `16` only at `CntIncrSt` or `CntProgSt`.

Related code: https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/rtl/lc_ctrl_state_transition.sv#L42

Screenshot:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11466553/124509050-0ee24c80-dd86-11eb-9088-3a3088a66e6f.png)

thanks,
Cindy

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan life cycle controller (`lc_ctrl`), a transition to the terminal Scrap state can use the wrong life cycle counter during the second OTP (One-Time Programmable) programming pass. In the reported Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) to Scrap transition, the controller first issues a counter-programming request for counter value 16, which is the value required for Scrap. During the later state-programming pass, however, the transition logic falls back to the current counter input and requests 8 instead of keeping 16, causing the update to the Scrap state to fail.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the `lc_ctrl_state_transition` block in the life cycle controller IP, which computes the next life cycle state and next life cycle counter for life cycle transitions.

## Expected Behavior
For a valid RMA-to-Scrap transition, once the earlier counter-programming pass has requested counter value 16 for the Scrap transition, the later state-programming pass must continue to request the Scrap state together with counter value 16. The transition must remain valid in that second pass and must not be rejected because the requested counter falls back to 8.

## Actual Behavior
When the finite state machine (FSM) reaches `TransProgSt` for the state-programming pass, the logic recomputes the next counter from the current counter input and requests 8 instead of 16, so the Scrap state programming step fails even though the transition itself is valid.

## Trigger Condition
This bug occurs in the second OTP programming pass of an RMA-to-Scrap transition, specifically when the FSM is in `TransProgSt` and the current counter input seen by the transition logic is 8 after the earlier counter-programming request.

resolved_issues.title: [otp / flash_ctrl] Isolated partition access during DEV state
resolved_issues.body:
There is some concern that having the isolated partition readable during DEV state could impact the security of secrets injected during the very early stages of production. 

We should consider making `ISO_SW_RD_EN` only possible during production states (PROD and PROD_END), but this will come at the cost of some early sample debuggability.  

This is something we should quickly settle on.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Life Cycle Controller (`lc_ctrl`) IP derives software access permissions for the isolated flash partition from the device life cycle state. In the current behavior, when the device is in the development state (`DEV`), software can still read that partition. This is a problem because the isolated flash partition is used to hold manufacturing data that may be written before the device enters production, and those contents are supposed to remain secret until the device reaches a production life cycle state.

## Expected Behavior
When the device is in the `DEV` life cycle state, the isolated flash partition must remain writable for provisioning but must not be software-readable. This restriction should apply only to software read access for that partition: normal development-state debug and provisioning behavior should otherwise remain available. Software read access to the isolated flash partition should only be enabled once the device enters a production life cycle state such as `PROD` or `PROD_END`.

## Actual Behavior
In the current `lc_ctrl` behavior, the `DEV` life cycle state allows software read access to the isolated flash partition, so data placed there before production can be read back too early.

## Affected Module
The bug is in the `lc_ctrl` IP's life-cycle-based access-permission logic for the isolated flash partition.

## Trigger Condition
The issue is triggered whenever `lc_ctrl` evaluates software access permissions while the device is in the `DEV` life cycle state and software accesses the isolated flash partition. Under that condition, reads are incorrectly allowed even though they should remain blocked until a production state.

problem_statement:
## Description
The affected functionality is the TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) host-side A-channel write integrity generation path. Some OpenTitan hosts, including the debug module and the then-current Ibex integration, do not generate their own write-data integrity field (`a_user.data_intg`), so this shared TL-UL host path must generate it for outgoing write requests.

## Expected Behavior
For every TL-UL write request, the host-side path must output a valid write-data integrity value in `a_user.data_intg` that matches the data sent on the bus. This applies to both full writes (`PutFullData`) and partial writes (`PutPartialData`). For a partial write, the byte-enable mask `a_mask` defines which byte lanes are actually written; lanes with `a_mask = 0` must be driven as zero on the outgoing `a_data`, and `a_user.data_intg` must be computed from that masked data word. The command integrity field `a_user.cmd_intg` must still remain correct.

## Actual Behavior
The current host-side generation path does not reliably provide correct write-data integrity for host-originated writes. In particular, on partial writes it can forward unmasked byte lanes on `a_data`, which causes `a_user.data_intg` to no longer match the effective write payload defined by `a_mask`. As a result, TL-UL write requests produced by hosts that rely on this path can carry incorrect A-channel data integrity.

## Trigger Conditions
The bug is triggered when a TL-UL host that relies on the shared host-side integrity generator issues a write request. It is especially visible on `PutPartialData` transactions with one or more cleared bits in `a_mask`, and full-word writes from those hosts still require `a_user.data_intg` to be generated correctly.

problem_statement:
## Description
The affected logic is the Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) fast clock-domain finite state machine that handles software-requested entry into low power and drives the `low_power_o` status signal to always-on logic.

## Trigger Conditions
A low-power entry attempt starts when software sets `CONTROL.LOW_POWER_HINT` and the CPU sleep indication from wait-for-interrupt (WFI) is sampled. The failure occurs when that entry sequence reaches `FastPwrStateNvmIdleChk` while the Flash Controller is still busy, so the transition is aborted instead of completing low-power entry.

## Expected Behavior
If the low-power entry attempt is aborted in `FastPwrStateNvmIdleChk`, the system must resume normal active execution with `low_power_o` deasserted. `low_power_o` must only remain asserted for a low-power transition that actually completes.

## Actual Behavior
`low_power_o` is asserted during the attempted entry, but when the Flash Controller busy condition aborts the transition, the system resumes execution without clearing `low_power_o`. The signal therefore remains high even though the device never entered low power.

prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 08bb642d96ece87b922d79ef49e1522343d16e92
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at 08bb642d96ece87b922d79ef49e1522343d16e92; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at 08bb642d96ece87b922d79ef49e1522343d16e92"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at 08bb642d96ece87b922d79ef49e1522343d16e92; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  if [ -d "$d" ]; then
    export PATH="$d:$PATH"
  fi
done
true
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan ENTROPY_SRC (entropy source) IP does not correctly sequence its health-test phases. The design is expected to distinguish three phases of operation: a boot-time bypass phase, a separate startup health-test phase, and the steady-state continuous health-test phase. In the buggy RTL, the startup phase is skipped, so the block can move from the boot-time path directly into the normal path.

## Expected Behavior
After the boot-time bypass phase, when firmware enables ENTROPY_SRC for normal, non-bypass operation, the main sequencer must enter a distinct startup health-test phase before it enters the continuous phase. That startup phase must be selectable separately from the boot and continuous phases and must honor startup-specific health-test window and threshold settings instead of collapsing directly into the continuous path. If the boot-phase window and the later health-test window are configured differently, the design must still transition through the startup phase before steady-state operation.

## Actual Behavior
The buggy RTL does not expose the startup health-test phase as a separate part of the sequencer flow. After boot-time bypass handling, the main state machine can transition directly toward the normal path, so the startup-specific phase and its configuration are not applied.

## Affected Function
This bug affects the ENTROPY_SRC IP health-test phase sequencer, specifically the main state machine that chooses between boot, startup, and continuous testing.

## Trigger Condition
The issue is triggered when firmware switches ENTROPY_SRC from the initial boot-time bypass behavior into normal non-bypass operation, especially if the boot-phase health-test window and the later health-test window are configured to different sizes.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan

TEST_NAME="alert_handler_fsm_glitch"
TB_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_alert_handler_fsm_glitch"
mkdir -p "${TB_ROOT}"

finish_test() {
  local status="$1"
  local rc="$2"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... ${status}"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit "${rc}"
}

if [[ -f /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh ]]; then
  # Default prepare persists tool paths here.
  source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh || true
fi

cat > hw/ip/alert_handler/dv/env/seq_lib/alert_handler_fsm_glitch_vseq.sv <<'EOF'
// Copyright lowRISC contributors.
// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, see LICENSE for details.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

class alert_handler_fsm_glitch_vseq extends alert_handler_base_vseq;
  `uvm_object_utils(alert_handler_fsm_glitch_vseq)

  `uvm_object_new

  localparam bit [TL_DW-1:0] ExpectedFsmError = 'h2;

  virtual task body();
    string glitch_path;
    uvm_hdl_data_t glitch_val;
    bit [TL_DW-1:0] csr_val;
    bit [NUM_ESCS-1:0] esc_seen;

    glitch_val = '0;
    esc_seen   = '0;

    alert_handler_init(.intr_en('0),
                       .alert_en('0),
                       .alert_class('0),
                       .loc_alert_en('1),
                       .loc_alert_class('0));
    csr_wr(.ptr(ral.classa_ctrl), .value('h3d));

    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(5);

    if (uvm_hdl_check_path("tb.dut.gen_classes[0].u_esc_timer.state_raw_q")) begin
      glitch_path = "tb.dut.gen_classes[0].u_esc_timer.state_raw_q";
      glitch_val[9:0] = 10'h000;
    end else if (uvm_hdl_check_path("tb.dut.gen_classes[0].u_esc_timer.state_q")) begin
      glitch_path = "tb.dut.gen_classes[0].u_esc_timer.state_q";
      glitch_val[2:0] = 3'b010;
    end else if (uvm_hdl_check_path("tb.dut.gen_classes[0].i_esc_timer.state_q")) begin
      glitch_path = "tb.dut.gen_classes[0].i_esc_timer.state_q";
      glitch_val[2:0] = 3'b010;
    end else begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "Unable to locate alert_handler esc_timer state register")
    end

    `uvm_info(`gfn, $sformatf("Injecting illegal esc_timer state via %0s", glitch_path), UVM_LOW)
    `DV_CHECK_FATAL(uvm_hdl_force(glitch_path, glitch_val))
    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(2);
    `DV_CHECK_FATAL(uvm_hdl_release(glitch_path))

    for (int cycle = 0; cycle < 10; cycle++) begin
      foreach (cfg.esc_device_cfg[i]) begin
        if (cfg.esc_device_cfg[i].vif.esc_tx.esc_p === 1'b1 &&
            cfg.esc_device_cfg[i].vif.esc_tx.esc_n === 1'b0) begin
          esc_seen[i] = 1'b1;
        end
      end
      if (&esc_seen) break;
      cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(1);
    end

    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(esc_seen, '1,
                       $sformatf("Expected all esc outputs high after glitch, saw %0b", esc_seen))

    csr_rd(.ptr(ral.classa_state), .value(csr_val));
    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(csr_val, ExpectedFsmError,
                       $sformatf("Expected classa_state=%0h after glitch, got %0h",
                                 ExpectedFsmError, csr_val))
  endtask
endclass
EOF

python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

core = Path("hw/ip/alert_handler/dv/env/alert_handler_env.core")
core_text = core.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
core_line = "      - seq_lib/alert_handler_fsm_glitch_vseq.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n"
if core_line not in core_text:
    anchor = "      - seq_lib/alert_handler_stress_all_vseq.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n"
    core_text = core_text.replace(anchor, anchor + core_line)
    core.write_text(core_text, encoding="utf-8")

vseq = Path("hw/ip/alert_handler/dv/env/seq_lib/alert_handler_vseq_list.sv")
vseq_text = vseq.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
vseq_line = '`include "alert_handler_fsm_glitch_vseq.sv"\n'
if vseq_line not in vseq_text:
    vseq.write_text(vseq_text + vseq_line, encoding="utf-8")

cfg = Path("hw/ip/alert_handler/dv/alert_handler_generic_sim_cfg.hjson")
cfg_text = cfg.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
if "name: alert_handler_fsm_glitch" not in cfg_text:
    block = """
    {
      name: alert_handler_fsm_glitch
      uvm_test_seq: alert_handler_fsm_glitch_vseq
      run_opts: ["+en_scb=0"]
    }
"""
    anchor = """
    {
      name: alert_handler_stress_all
      run_opts: ["+test_timeout_ns=15_000_000_000"]
    }
"""
    cfg_text = cfg_text.replace(anchor, block + anchor)
    cfg.write_text(cfg_text, encoding="utf-8")

tb = Path("hw/ip/alert_handler/dv/tb/tb.sv")
tb_lines = []
for line in tb.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    if "force dut.i_ping_timer.wait_cyc_mask_i" in line or "force dut.u_ping_timer.wait_cyc_mask_i" in line:
        tb_lines.append('    if (reduce_ping_timer_wait_cycles) `uvm_info("tb", "reduce_ping_timer_wait_cycles ignored", UVM_LOW)')
    else:
        tb_lines.append(line)
tb.write_text("\n".join(tb_lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

utils = Path("util/dvsim/utils.py")
utils_text = utils.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
needle = "                          cssutils_logging_level=log.ERROR)"
replacement = "                          cssutils_logging_level=log.ERROR,\n                          allow_loading_external_files=True)"
if "allow_loading_external_files=True" not in utils_text:
    utils_text = utils_text.replace(needle, replacement)
    utils.write_text(utils_text, encoding="utf-8")
PY

set +e
timeout 1500s python util/dvsim/dvsim.py \
  hw/ip/alert_handler/dv/alert_handler_generic_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i "${TEST_NAME}" \
  -t vcs \
  --purge \

  2>&1 | tee "${TB_ROOT}/dvsim.log"
rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

  finish_test "PASS" 0
fi

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Alert Handler is the hardware block that collects alerts and, for each alert class, uses an escalation timer finite-state machine (FSM) to decide when escalation outputs must be asserted. The escalation timer for a configured alert class is not hardened against illegal FSM state corruption. If a glitch or fault-injection event drives that FSM into an encoding outside its valid states, the class can remain in a non-fail-safe state instead of immediately treating the corruption as an internal fault.

## Expected Behavior
For any enabled alert class, corruption of the escalation timer FSM into an illegal state must be handled as a terminal fault of that class, even if no normal accumulation threshold or interrupt-timeout event has occurred yet. The affected class must report the visible `FsmError` class state, and all escalation actions for that class must be triggered rather than leaving the class in `Idle` or normal timeout/phase sequencing.

## Actual Behavior
If the escalation timer FSM for an enabled class is forced into an invalid encoding, the Alert Handler does not reliably enter a terminal error response for that class. The class state can fail to indicate `FsmError`, and not all escalation actions for the class are triggered.

## Affected Function
This affects the Alert Handler alert-class escalation timer FSM and the visible class-state reporting associated with escalation handling.

## Trigger Condition
The issue appears when an alert class has been configured and enabled, and the corresponding escalation timer FSM is corrupted into an illegal state encoding, including corruption that happens before any normal accumulation-triggered or timeout-triggered escalation occurs.

resolved_issues.title: [kmac] configuration errors
resolved_issues.body:
Currently, the `sha3pad::ModeStrengthCombinations_M` assertion checks that the selected mode and strength are confined within correct values.

Should the KMAC output this as an error state instead of an assertion?

resolved_issues.title: [kmac] entropy_timer questions
resolved_issues.body:
Hi Eunchan,

I had a couple of questions about the `entropy_timer` that came up as I was implementing a related testcase.

In the scenario, we're running a Shake hash with fast entropy enabled.

It seems that the `entropy_timer` does not stop counting down even when keccak rounds are running, like so:

![Screenshot from 2021-05-19 22-34-06](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/118924745-5e61db80-b8f2-11eb-93bd-9749ef7ed587.png)

Is this expected?

Followup question - if this is expected behavior, does this mean that `entropy_timer` will only stop counting during keccak rounds when fast entropy is disabled? Similarly, what about processing the keyblocks?

resolved_issues.title: [kmac] Write incorrect cmd from Idle state
resolved_issues.body:
Hi Eunchan,

I'm seeing some odd behavior when I test an error case where I push an incorrect command from the Idle state (anything but CmdStart):

![Screenshot from 2021-05-20 01-42-48](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/118947949-b3125000-b90c-11eb-9551-c3fb447e9d95.png)

Here, I write CmdManualRun from the Idle state, and then `kmac_app` reports an `ErrSwPushedWrongCmd` and raises the error interrupt.

However, since in this test case I am not using the app interface, I'd expect that the `ErrSha3SwControl` error should be asserted from `sha3` module instead (which checks for the exact same thing, but only applies to SW controlled hashing).

It looks like the error from `kmac_app` is incorrectly being thrown here due to [this condition](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/kmac/rtl/kmac_app.sv#L490), which only checks that we are not using `SelSw` mux mode in `kmac_app` module.

As you can see in the waves, `mux_sel` is actually still remaining as `SelNone` here since we are sending an incorrect SW command - I think this condition needs to change to become:
`if (mux_sel != SelSw && mux_sel != SelNone) begin...` or equivalent.
WDYT?

diff --git a/hw/ip/kmac/doc/_index.md b/hw/ip/kmac/doc/_index.md
index b5f45420f7d57..cbbfe8eef85b7 100644
--- a/hw/ip/kmac/doc/_index.md
+++ b/hw/ip/kmac/doc/_index.md
@@ -256,7 +256,97 @@ The refresh does not block the internal entropy expansion operation.
 
 ### Error Report
 
-_TBD_
+This section explains the errors KMAC HWIP raises during the hasing operations, their meanings, and the error handling process.
+
+KMAC HWIP has the error checkers in its internal datapath.
+If the checkers detect errors, whether they are triggered by the SW mis-configure, or HW malfunctions, they report the error to {{< regref "ERR_CODE" >}} and raise an `kmac_error` interrupt.
+Each error code gives debugging information at the lower 24 bits of {{< regref "ERR_CODE" >}}.
+
+Value | Error Code | Description
+------|------------|-------------
+0x01  | KeyNotValid | In KMAC mode with the sideloaded key, the IP raises an error if the sideloaded secret key is not ready.
+0x02  | SwPushedMsgFifo | MsgFifo is updated while not being in the Message Feed state.
+0x03  | SwIssuedCmdInAppActive | SW issued a command while the application interface is being used
+0x04  | WaitTimerExpired | EDN has not responded within the wait timer limit.
+0x05  | IncorrectEntropyMode | When SW sets `entropy_ready`, the `entropy_mode` is neither SW nor EDN.
+0x06  | UnexpectedModeStrength | SHA3 mode and Keccak Strength combination is not expected.
+0x07  | IncorrectFunctionName | In KMAC mode, the PREFIX has the value other than `encoded_string("KMAC")`
+0x08  | SwCmdSequence | SW does not follow the guided sequence, `start` -> `process` -> {`run` ->} `done`
+0x80  | Sha3Control | SW may receive Sha3Control error along with `SwCmdSequence` error. Can be ignored.
+
+#### KeyNotValid (0x01)
+
+The `KeyNotValid` error is raised in the application interface module.
+When a KMAC application requests a hashing operation, the module checks if the sideloaded key is ready.
+If the key is not ready, the module reports `KeyNotValid` error and moves to dead-end state and waits the IP reset.
+
+This error does not provide any additional information.
+
+#### SwPushedMsgFifo (0x02)
+
+The `SwPushedMsgFifo` error happens when the Message FIFO receives TL-UL transactions while the application interface is busy.
+The Message FIFO drops the request.
+
+The IP reports the error with an info field.
+
+Bits    | Name        | Description
+--------|-------------|-------------
+[23:16] | reserved    | all zero
+[15:8]  | kmac_app_st | KMAC_APP FSM state.
+[7:0]   | mux_sel     | Current APP Mux selection. 0: None, 1: SW, 2: App
+
+#### SwIssuedCmdInAppActive (0x03)
+
+If the SW issues any commands while the application interface is being used, the module reports `SwIssuedCmdInAppActive` error.
+The received command does not affect the Application process.
+The request is dropped by the KMAC_APP module.
+
+The lower 3 bits of {{< regref "ERR_CODE" >}} contains the received command from the SW.
+#### WaitTimerExpired (0x04)
+
+The SW may set the EDN wait timer to exit from EDN request state if the response from EDN takes long.
+If the timer expires, the module cancels the transaction and report the `WaitTimerExpired` error.
+
+When this error happens, the state machine in KMAC_ENTROPY module moves to Wait state.
+In that state, it keeps using the pre-generated entropy and asserting the entropy valid signal.
+It asserts the entropy valid signal to complete the current hashing operation.
+If the module does not complete, or flush the pending operation, it creates the back pressure to the message FIFO.
+Then, the SW may not be able to access the KMAC IP at all, as the crossbar is stuck.
+
+The SW may move the state machine to the reset state by issuing {{<regref "CFG.err_processed" >}}.
+
+#### IncorrectEntropyMode (0x05)
+
+If SW misconfigures the entropy mode and let the entropy module prepare the random data, the module reports `IncorrectEntropyMode` error.
+The state machine moves to Wait state after reporting the error.
+
+The SW may move the state machine to the reset state by issuing {{<regref "CFG.err_processed" >}}.
+
+#### UnexpectedModeStrength (0x06)
+
+When the SW issues `Start` command, the KMAC_ERRCHK module checks the {{< regref "CFG.mode" >}} and {{< regref "CFG.kstrength" >}}.
+The KMAC HWIP assumes the combinations of two to be **SHA3-224**, **SHA3-256**, **SHA3-384**, **SHA3-512**, **SHAKE-128**, **SHAKE-256**, **cSHAKE-128**, and **cSHAKE-256**.
+If the combination of the `mode` and `kstrength` does not fall into above, the module reports the `UnexpectedModeStrength` error.
+
+However, the KMAC HWIP proceeds the hashing operation as other combinations does not cause any malfunctions inside the IP.
+The SW may get the incorrect digest value.
+
+#### IncorrectFunctionName (0x07)
+
+If {{< regref "CFG.kmac_en" >}} is set and the SW issues the `Start` command, the KMAC_ERRCHK checks if the {{< regref "PREFIX" >}} has correct function name, `encode_string("KMAC")`.
+If the value does not match to the byte form of `encode_string("KMAC")` (`0x4341_4D4B_2001`), it reports the `IncorrectFunctionName` error.
+
+As same as `UnexpectedModeStrength` error, this error does not block the hashing operation.
+The SW may get the incorrect signature value.
+
+#### SwCmdSequence (0x08)
+
+The KMAC_ERRCHK module checks the SW issued commands if it follows the guideline.
+If the SW issues the command that is not relavant to the current context, the module reports the `SwCmdSequence` error.
+The lower 3bits of the {{< regref "ERR_CODE" >}} contains the received command.
+
+This error, however, does not stop the KMAC HWIP.
+The incorrect command is dropped at the following datapath, SHA3 core.
 
 # Programmers Guide

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+//
+// KMAC Error Checking logic
+//
+// `kmac_err` module checks the SW introduced errors.
+//  1. SW command sequencing error.
+//  2. SW configuration error.
+//
+// ## SW Command Sequencing Error
+//
+// KMAC assumes the application interface and the SW register interface to
+// follow the specific sequence. It expects the requester to send the `Start`
+// command then push the message body. The `Process` command follows the message
+// body. The SW may issue `Run` command if it needs the digest result more than
+// a block rate. Then SW completes the hash operation with `Done` command.
+//
+// This `kmac_err` module checks if the SW issues the correct command. If not,
+// it reports the error via ERR_CODE register.
+//
+// However, the logic does not prevent the error-ed command to be propagated.
+// The unexpected commands are filtered by each individual submodule.
+//
+// st := { Idle, MsgFeed, Processing, Absorbed, Squeeze}
+//
+// allowed := {
+//   Idle :      { Start     },
+//   MsgFeed:    { Process   },
+//   Processing: { None      },
+//   Absorbed:   { Run, Done },
+//   Squeeze:    { None      }
+// }
+//
+// ## SW Configuration Error
+//
+// `kmac_errchk` module checks if SW configured correct combinations of the
+// configuration registers when the hashing operation begins.
+//
+// 1. Mode & Strength combinations
+// 2. Kmac Prefix
+// * sideload & key_valid -> Checker in kmac_core
+
+module kmac_errchk
+  import kmac_pkg::*;
+  import sha3_pkg::sha3_mode_e;
+  import sha3_pkg::keccak_strength_e;
+(
+  input clk_i,
+  input rst_ni,
+
+  // Configurations
+  input sha3_mode_e       cfg_mode_i,
+  input keccak_strength_e cfg_strength_i,
+
+  input        kmac_en_i,
+  input [47:0] cfg_prefix_6B_i, // first 6B of PREFIX
+
+  // SW commands
+  input kmac_cmd_e sw_cmd_i,
+
+  // Status from KMAC_APP
+  input app_active_i,
+
+  // Status from SHA3 core
+  input sha3_absorbed_i,
+  input keccak_done_i,
+
+  output err_t error_o
+);
+
+  // sha3_pkg::sha3_mode_e
+  import sha3_pkg::L128;
+  import sha3_pkg::L224;
+  import sha3_pkg::L256;
+  import sha3_pkg::L384;
+  import sha3_pkg::L512;
+
+  // sha3_pkg::keccak_strength_e
+  import sha3_pkg::Sha3;
+  import sha3_pkg::Shake;
+  import sha3_pkg::CShake;
+
+  /////////////////
+  // Definitions //
+  /////////////////
+  typedef enum logic [2:0] {
+    StIdle,
+    StMsgFeed,
+    StProcessing,
+    StAbsorbed,
+    StSqueezing
+  } st_e;
+  st_e st, st_d;
+
+  /////////////
+  // Signals //
+  /////////////
+
+  // `err_swsequence` occurs when SW issues wrong command
+  logic err_swsequence;
+
+  // `err_modestrength` occcurs when Mode & Strength combinations are not
+  // allowed. This error does not block the hashing operation.
+  logic err_modestrength;
+
+  // `err_prefix` occurs when the first 6B of !!PREFIX is not
+  // `encode_string("KMAC")` and kmac is enabled. This error does not block the
+  // KMAC operation.
+  logic err_prefix;
+
+  ///////////////////
+  // Error Checker //
+  ///////////////////
+
+  // SW sequence Error
+  // info field: Current state, Received command
+  always_comb begin
+    err_swsequence = 1'b 0;
+
+    unique case (st)
+      StIdle: begin
+        // Allow Start command only
+        if (!(sw_cmd_i inside {CmdNone, CmdStart})) begin
+          err_swsequence = 1'b 1;
+        end
+      end
+
+      StMsgFeed: begin
+        // Allow Process only
+        if (!(sw_cmd_i inside {CmdNone, CmdProcess})) begin
+          err_swsequence = 1'b 1;
+        end
+      end
+
+      StProcessing: begin
+        if (sw_cmd_i != CmdNone) begin
+          err_swsequence = 1'b 1;
+        end
+      end
+
+      StAbsorbed: begin
+        // Allow ManualRun and Done
+        if (!(sw_cmd_i inside {CmdNone, CmdManualRun, CmdDone})) begin
+          err_swsequence = 1'b 1;
+        end
+      end
+
+      StSqueezing: begin
+        if (sw_cmd_i != CmdNone) begin
+          err_swsequence = 1'b 1;
+        end
+      end
+
+      default: begin
+        err_swsequence = 1'b 0;
+      end
+    endcase
+  end
+
+  // Mode & Strength
+  always_comb begin : check_modestrength
+    err_modestrength = 1'b 0;
+
+    if (st == StIdle && st_d == StMsgFeed) begin
+      // When moving to the next stage, checks the config
+      if (!((cfg_mode_i == Sha3 &&
+             cfg_strength_i inside {L224, L256, L384, L512}) ||
+            ((cfg_mode_i == Shake || cfg_mode_i == CShake) &&
+             (cfg_strength_i inside {L128, L256})))) begin
+        err_modestrength = 1'b 1;
+      end
+    end
+  end : check_modestrength
+
+
+  // Check prefix 6B is `encode_string("KMAC")`
+  always_comb begin : check_prefix
+    err_prefix = 1'b 0;
+
+    if (st == StIdle && st_d == StMsgFeed && kmac_en_i) begin
+      if (cfg_prefix_6B_i != EncodedStringKMAC) begin
+        err_prefix = 1'b 1;
+      end
+    end
+  end : check_prefix
+
+
+  // Return error code
+  err_t err;
+  always_comb begin : err_return
+    err = '{valid: 1'b0, code: ErrNone, info: '0};
+
+    priority case (1'b 1)
+      err_swsequence: begin
+        err = '{ valid: 1'b 1,
+                 code: ErrSwCmdSequence,
+                 info: {5'h0,
+                        {err_swsequence, err_modestrength, err_prefix},
+                        8'h0,
+                        {1'b0, st, sw_cmd_i}
+                       }
+               };
+      end
+
+      err_modestrength: begin
+        err = '{ valid: 1'b 1,
+                 code:  ErrUnexpectedModeStrength,
+                 info:  { 5'h 0,
+                          {err_swsequence, err_modestrength, err_prefix},
+                          8'h 0,
+                          {2'b 00, cfg_mode_i},
+                          {1'b 0,  cfg_strength_i}
+                        }
+               };
+      end
+
+      err_prefix: begin
+        err = '{ valid: 1'b 1,
+                 code:  ErrIncorrectFunctionName,
+                 info:  { 5'h 0,
+                          {err_swsequence, err_modestrength, err_prefix},
+                          16'h 0000
+                        }
+               };
+      end
+
+      default: begin
+        err = '{valid: 1'b0, code: ErrNone, info: '0};
+      end
+    endcase
+  end : err_return
+
+  assign error_o = err;
+
+  // If below failed, revise err_swsequence error response info field.
+  `ASSERT_INIT(ExpectedStSwCmdBits_A, $bits(st) == 3 && $bits(sw_cmd_i) == 4)
+
+  // If failed, revise err_modestrength error info field.
+  `ASSERT_INIT(ExpectedModeStrengthBits_A,
+               $bits(cfg_mode_i) == 2 && $bits(cfg_strength_i) == 3)
+
+
+  ///////////////////
+  // State Machine //
+  ///////////////////
+  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
+    if (!rst_ni) begin
+      st <= StIdle;
+    end else begin
+      st <= st_d;
+    end
+  end
+
+  always_comb begin : next_state
+    st_d = st;
+
+    unique case (st)
+      StIdle: begin
+        if (!app_active_i && sw_cmd_i == CmdStart) begin
+          // Proceed to the next state only when the SW issues the Start command
+          // in a valid period.
+          st_d = StMsgFeed;
+        end
+      end
+
+      StMsgFeed: begin
+        if (sw_cmd_i == CmdProcess) begin
+          st_d = StProcessing;
+        end
+      end
+
+      StProcessing: begin
+        if (sha3_absorbed_i) begin
+          st_d = StAbsorbed;
+        end
+      end
+
+      StAbsorbed: begin
+        if (sw_cmd_i == CmdManualRun) begin
+          st_d = StSqueezing;
+        end else if (sw_cmd_i == CmdDone) begin
+          st_d = StIdle;
+        end
+      end
+
+      StSqueezing: begin
+        if (keccak_done_i) begin
+          st_d = StAbsorbed;
+        end
+      end
+
+      default: begin
+        st_d = StIdle;
+      end
+    endcase
+  end : next_state
+  `ASSERT_KNOWN(StKnown_A, st)
+
+endmodule : kmac_errchk
diff --git a/hw/ip/kmac/rtl/kmac_pkg.sv b/hw/ip/kmac/rtl/kmac_pkg.sv
index 645cd862afb71..4d022515f2fb1 100644

+++ b/hw/ip/kmac/rtl/kmac_pkg.sv

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 7cbebc2e6901384b1fa5be73fd345ceb956278b5
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at 7cbebc2e6901384b1fa5be73fd345ceb956278b5; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  python -m pip install --no-warn-script-location \
    hjson \
    "git+https://github.com/lowRISC/fusesoc.git@ot#egg=fusesoc" \
    "git+https://github.com/lowRISC/edalize.git@ot#egg=edalize"
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at 7cbebc2e6901384b1fa5be73fd345ceb956278b5"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at 7cbebc2e6901384b1fa5be73fd345ceb956278b5; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  if [ -d "$d" ]; then
    export PATH="$d:$PATH"
  fi
done
true
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) IP can be controlled either through its software-visible command/register interface or through an internal application interface used by other hardware blocks. In the software-controlled hashing flow, an illegal software command issued while the block is still in the Idle state can be classified as an application-interface error even when no application-interface request is active. This misclassifies the failure reported through the `ERR_CODE` error-status register.

## Expected Behavior
When KMAC is idle and the internal application interface is inactive, software may begin a software-controlled hash operation only with `CmdStart`. If software writes any other command in that state, including `CmdManualRun`, the KMAC IP must latch an `ERR_CODE` value that classifies the event as an invalid software command sequence for the software-controlled hashing flow. The error information must also preserve the offending command value.

## Actual Behavior
If software writes `CmdManualRun` from the Idle state before any `CmdStart`, KMAC can instead classify the event as the application-interface error intended for commands issued while the application interface is active, even though the application interface is not in use.

## Affected Function
This bug affects the KMAC IP's software command validation and error classification logic for commands issued from the Idle state.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when software uses the command register interface while KMAC is idle, no application-interface transaction is active, and software writes a non-`CmdStart` command such as `CmdManualRun`.

title: [hmac] Idle logic
body:
This commit implements the idle signal. Idle signal is used in the
clkmgr to ensure the safe clock off by checking the logic's idle status.

HMAC implements the idle logic by checking four submodules' idle status:

- packer: packer does not have empty status signal sending out. So,
  currently, the logic relies on the fifo valid out signal. However, the
  case that packer has partial data and not sending out the write signal
  is covered by HMAC_CORE or SHA_CORE idle signals.
- msg_fifo: fifo_wvalid output signal is used as an idle signal.
- HMAC_CORE: the core raises an idle signal when the core sits in the
  Idle state or HMAC mode is not set.
- SHA_CORE: If the FIFO FSM sits in Idle state, SHA core is in idle. SHA
  state machine is dependent on the Fifo FSM.

This is related to #6650

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) IP exposes a top-level idle status that is consumed by the clock manager (`clkmgr`) and by software. That idle status is not properly connected to activity on the HMAC message-input path, so the HMAC block can report idle even when message work is already pending.

## Expected Behavior
Immediately after reset, the HMAC block may report idle while no message work is pending. Once the HMAC message packer has a pending write for the message first-in, first-out (FIFO) queue, the exported HMAC idle status must deassert to indicate that the block is no longer idle.

## Actual Behavior
The exported HMAC idle status can remain asserted after reset even when the message packer already has a valid word waiting to be written into the message FIFO. This makes the HMAC IP appear quiescent too early to logic that depends on the idle indication.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered after reset when the HMAC message packer presents a pending write toward the message FIFO.

Hey Michael,

For the assertion below:
```
  `ASSERT(SyncReqAckAckNeedsReq, dst_ack_i |-> dst_req_o, clk_dst_i, !rst_dst_ni)
```
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_sync_reqack.sv#L176

I have a corner case that EDN request happened right when otp_ctrl goes to FsmErrorSt.
Then the edn request will be high for exactly one clock cycle and then goes low.
Current push-pull-agent from the DV side sees `req` goes high for a clock cycle, and will issue an `ack`. But this fires the assertion above.

I would like to double check:
1). Will the EDN response side behave the same as DV's push-pull agent?
2). If so, can I change the assertion to this one:
```
  `ASSERT(SyncReqAckAckNeedsReq, dst_ack_i |-> $past(dst_req_o), clk_dst_i, !rst_dst_ni)
```

Thanks
Cindy

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan OTP (One-Time Programmable) Controller includes a Key Derivation Interface (KDI) that requests random data from the EDN (Entropy Distribution Network) during scrambling-key derivation. This EDN sideband uses a request/acknowledge handshake: once the KDI asserts an EDN request, that request must remain asserted until the matching EDN acknowledge arrives.

## Expected Behavior
If the OTP controller enters its terminal error state after the KDI has already issued an EDN request but before the EDN returns the acknowledge, the outstanding handshake must still complete correctly. The EDN acknowledge must only be observed while the request is still asserted, and entering the error state must not cause the request to be withdrawn early.

## Actual Behavior
In the buggy design, an EDN request can be asserted for one cycle and then dropped when the OTP controller transitions into its error state. If the EDN returns the acknowledge on the following cycle, the acknowledge is observed after the request has already deasserted, creating an ACK-without-REQ handshake violation.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the OTP controller KDI path that drives EDN requests for scrambling-key derivation.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a scrambling-key derivation operation has already issued an EDN request and, before the EDN responds, an escalation or other fault pushes the OTP controller into its terminal error state. A delayed EDN acknowledge after that state transition exposes the protocol violation.

resolved_issues.body:
This commit re-designs the passthrough logic. The logic used 256 command
info structure, which is the compile-time predefined parameter.

Now, it defines SW configurable command info slots. By default the
register has 16 command info slots. First 10 slots are also used in the
flash mode. Following 6 slots are used in the passthrough logic only.

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)

if isinstance(entry, dict):

problem_statement:
OpenTitan's SPI Device IP has a bug in its flash-emulation mode command parser (`FlashMode`). In this IP, some software-configurable `cmd_info` control/status register (CSR) entries are reserved for internal flash-mode commands, including read commands. The parser is expected to decide which internal datapath to activate from the opcode stored in the relevant `cmd_info` entry, but for the flash read-command path it still behaves as if only the legacy fixed opcode values are valid.

Expected behavior: when the SPI Device IP is in `FlashMode` and software programs a non-default opcode into a flash-mode read-command `cmd_info` entry, the first received command byte matching that programmed opcode must select the internal read-command datapath. Matching only the old built-in opcode is not sufficient.

Observed behavior: after software changes a flash-mode read-command opcode in `cmd_info`, the parser does not recognize that new opcode on the first command byte and does not route the transaction to the internal read-command handling path unless the byte still matches the legacy hardcoded opcode.

Trigger condition: the SPI Device IP is operating in `FlashMode`, software has changed the opcode in a flash-mode read-command `cmd_info` CSR entry from its default value, and a transaction begins with that newly programmed opcode.

title: [rom_ctrl] Only raise ROM req line when not in reset
body:
*This PR is in draft because it depends on #6473 (no logical connection, but they touch the same lines and rebasing would be a mess). The first commit is from there; the second commit is the "real" PR.*

The previous code assumed that the checker always requested ROM
accesses. This is logically correct, but meant that we were raising
the ROM's req line when in reset. Since the ROM doesn't itself have a
reset signal, this would mean spurious activations of the ROM
macrocell.

This patch explicitly registers the req signal in the checker's
address counter and passes it through the rest of the design.

repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

accesses. This is logically correct, but meant that we were raising
the ROM's req line when in reset. Since the ROM doesn't itself have a
reset signal, this would mean spurious activations of the ROM
macrocell.

This patch explicitly registers the req signal in the checker's
address counter and passes it through the rest of the design.

Signed-off-by: Rupert Swarbrick <rswarbrick@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [rom_ctrl] Fix KMAC back pressure handling
resolved_issues.body:
Here, `rom_addr_o` is the address that `rom_ctrl_counter` passes to the
ROM (to tell it what to read next). We need to increment it
"immediately" when the ready signal from KMAC goes high, otherwise
there's a extra cycle with data from the first address.

(This is the same fix as in Tim's #6379)

problem_statement:
## Description
`rom_ctrl` arbitrates ROM access between the boot-time ROM integrity checker and the normal ROM bus path. While the checker owns this ROM mux, the ROM request output must only be asserted when the checker is actually issuing a ROM read.

## Expected Behavior
When the checker-selected path is active, the muxed ROM request output must remain low during reset and must stay low after reset until the checker asserts a real read request. Once the checker does assert a read request, the ROM request output must assert as well. After control switches to the normal ROM bus path, the ROM request output must continue to reflect bus requests. This matters because the ROM macrocell has no reset input and must not be spuriously activated.

## Actual Behavior
The checker-selected ROM path can drive the ROM request output high even when the checker has not yet issued a read request. This can produce unintended ROM activations during reset and in the first cycle(s) after reset deassertion, before the checker starts reading.

## Affected Function
The bug is in the `rom_ctrl` ROM-access arbitration path, specifically the `rom_ctrl_mux` behavior and the checker request signal that feeds it during the boot-time ROM integrity check.

## Trigger Condition
The problem occurs when `rom_ctrl` is still selecting the checker-owned ROM path and the checker has not yet asserted a read request, including while reset is active and immediately after reset release.

old = """  parameter bit [TL_DW-1:0] [3:0] ZERO_SEED_GENBITS = {32'h0,
                                                       32'h0,
                                                       32'h0,
                                                       32'h7};
"""

                                                       32'h0,
                                                       32'h0,
                                                       32'h4};
"""
if new in text:

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's CSRNG (Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator) RTL mishandles the software-application `GEN` command. In the CSRNG zero-seed NIST SP 800-90A known-answer-test flow, the `GENBITS` register value produced by RTL does not match the value expected by DV.

## Expected Behavior
If the software application first instantiates CSRNG in deterministic mode with no additional seed data (`INS` with `clen = 0`, which uses the all-zero seed) and then issues `GEN` with no additional data (`clen = 0`) requesting one 128-bit block (`glen = 1`), the four 32-bit reads from the software-visible `GENBITS` register should match the NIST known-answer-test output for that zero-seed generate operation.

## Actual Behavior
For that command sequence, the RTL returns `GENBITS` data that disagree with the DV model / NIST expected result.

## Affected Function
This affects the CSRNG IP's RTL generate-command path that drives the software-visible `GENBITS` output.

## Trigger Condition
The mismatch is reproducible when CSRNG is instantiated with the all-zero deterministic seed and the next software-application `GEN` request asks for a single 128-bit block with no additional data.

When injecting a bit flip to cause a fatal alert in the AES engine - reading the status register will give information on the status of the core. Idle, data_in_ready, stall etc.

could this be a security risk?
I imagine that running the AES module in manual mode and injecting errors at different times then reading the status could potentially give away information.

The aes_alert_reset test currently do not fail on this - but maybe we want to force an all 0's or a random value on the status register in case of a fatal?

I have tried to read the other registers but I don't see any feasible way of trying to correlate this to internal round keys etc.

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) hardware module, entering a fatal alert can still leave non-fatal operational state visible through the STATUS and TRIGGER registers. These registers expose the progress of the AES engine and software-issued requests such as START, KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR, DATA_OUT_CLEAR, and PRNG_RESEED, which requests reseeding of the module's pseudo-random number generators.

## Expected Behavior
When a fatal alert is active, the AES module must blank non-fatal operational state instead of exposing it. Specifically, STATUS.IDLE, STATUS.STALL, STATUS.OUTPUT_LOST, STATUS.OUTPUT_VALID, and STATUS.INPUT_READY must be forced to 0, and any pending TRIGGER requests START, KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR, DATA_OUT_CLEAR, and PRNG_RESEED must be cleared so they are no longer observable after the fatal alert.

## Actual Behavior
After a fatal alert, STATUS bits such as IDLE, INPUT_READY, STALL, OUTPUT_VALID, and OUTPUT_LOST can still reflect the interrupted state of the AES engine, and TRIGGER state can remain observable as well. This leaks information about what the AES module was doing when the fatal fault occurred.

## Affected Function
This affects the AES control logic that drives the STATUS and TRIGGER register outputs for the AES hardware module.

## Trigger Conditions
The issue appears when fault injection or another fatal condition raises a fatal alert while the AES module is in a non-default operational state or while a trigger request is pending. For example, if the module is idle, stalled, ready for input, holding valid output, reporting lost output, or carrying a START, KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR, DATA_OUT_CLEAR, or PRNG_RESEED request at the moment of the fatal alert, the post-alert register view still exposes that residual state.

title: [rom_ctrl] Fix KMAC back pressure handling
body:
Here, `rom_addr_o` is the address that `rom_ctrl_counter` passes to the
ROM (to tell it what to read next). We need to increment it
"immediately" when the ready signal from KMAC goes high, otherwise
there's a extra cycle with data from the first address.

(This is the same fix as in Tim's #6379)

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan ROM Controller (`rom_ctrl`) performs a boot-time integrity check by reading ROM words in order and presenting them to KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code). The affected functionality is the `rom_ctrl_counter` / ROM-address generation path that drives `rom_addr_o` for this ROM-to-KMAC stream.

## Expected Behavior
When a ROM word is already valid and KMAC accepts it by asserting ready, `rom_addr_o` must advance to the next sequential ROM word in that same cycle so the next ROM fetch starts immediately. In particular, if the first pending word is at address 0 and KMAC changes from not ready to ready, `rom_addr_o` must become 1 immediately rather than remaining at 0 for an extra cycle.

## Actual Behavior
After KMAC applies back-pressure and then becomes ready again, the ROM Controller keeps `rom_addr_o` on the previous address for one extra cycle. In the reset-start case, address 0 is presented for an extra cycle when KMAC first accepts data, so the first ROM word is fetched twice instead of the read stream advancing immediately to the next word.

## Trigger Condition
This bug is triggered while `rom_ctrl` is streaming ROM contents to KMAC and KMAC temporarily deasserts ready while a valid ROM word is pending, then reasserts ready. A concrete edge case is immediately after reset release: the first ROM word is pending at address 0, KMAC is initially not ready, and then KMAC asserts ready.

Additionally, the sha3 block will sit idle in this state.
This fixes #6084.

resolved_issues.title: [entropy_src/rtl] optional new drop points when entropy overflows FIFOs
resolved_issues.body:
Requirements have changed such that the drop point where new entropy cannot be consumed by entropy_src should be changed. A proposal would be to make this selectable (config bits). The choices would be the current input to the FIFO chain, the tail of the final FIFO (keep prior entropy seeds), and the head of the final FIFO (always push old entropy seeds out).

The attached diagram shows where these points are in the entropy flow.
[drop_point_diag.pdf](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/files/6305109/drop_point_diag.pdf)

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/entropy_src/doc/_index.md b/hw/ip/entropy_src/doc/_index.md
index cec43a89348e9..2252e5e13e343 100644
--- a/hw/ip/entropy_src/doc/_index.md
+++ b/hw/ip/entropy_src/doc/_index.md
@@ -169,7 +169,9 @@ The control bit `ES_TYPE` sets whether the entropy will come from the conditioni
 A status bit will be set that can either be polled or generate an interrupt when the entropy bits are available to be read from the {{< regref "ENTROPY_DATA" >}} register.
 The firmware needs to read the {{< regref "ENTROPY_DATA" >}} register twelve times in order to cleanly evacuate the 384-bit seed from the hardware path (12*32bits=384bits total).
 The firmware will directly read out of the main entropy FIFO, and when the control bit `ES_ROUTE` is set, no entropy is being passed to the block hardware interface.
-If the main entropy FIFO fills up, additional entropy that has been health checked and conditioned will be dropped at that point.
+
+If the `esfinal` FIFO fills up, additional entropy that has been health checked will be dropped before entering the conditioner.
+This drop point will save on conditioner power, and still preserve `esfinal` FIFO entropy that has already been collected.
 
 The above process will be repeated for as long as entropy bits are to be collected and processed.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Entropy Source (`entropy_src`) IP does not correctly handle its conditioned-entropy path when its final output FIFO (`esfinal`) is full. On this path, health-tested entropy passes through a 64-bit packer FIFO and then into the SHA3 conditioning block before reaching `esfinal`. In normal conditioning mode (not bypass mode), if `esfinal` is already full, the design can still advance a new word from the 64-bit packer FIFO into the SHA3 conditioner and start a new SHA3 operation.

## Expected Behavior
While `esfinal` is full, the conditioned path must stop at the 64-bit packer FIFO. New health-tested entropy must be dropped at that boundary instead of entering the SHA3 conditioner, and the SHA3 block must remain idle. Concretely, the path must not push a new word from the 64-bit packer FIFO into the conditioner and must not start SHA3 processing while `esfinal` remains full.

## Actual Behavior
When `esfinal` is full, the design can still forward a word from the 64-bit packer FIFO into the conditioner path and assert the start of SHA3 processing even though the final output FIFO has no space.

## Affected Function
This affects the Entropy Source (`entropy_src`) conditioned-entropy pipeline, specifically the boundary between the 64-bit packer FIFO, the SHA3 conditioner, and the final output FIFO (`esfinal`).

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered in normal conditioning mode when `esfinal` is full and the conditioned path otherwise has a word ready to move from the 64-bit packer FIFO into the SHA3 conditioner.

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/opentitan || exit 1
set -u
set -o pipefail

TEST_NAME="edn_disable_repro"
TB_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_${TEST_NAME}"
SCRATCH_ROOT="${TB_ROOT}/scratch"
DVSIM_LOG="${TB_ROOT}/dvsim.log"

emit_result() {
  local status="$1"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... ${status}"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
}

pass() {
  emit_result "PASS"
  exit 0
}

fail() {
  emit_result "FAIL"
  exit 1
}

show_failure_context() {
  local run_log="$1"
  local build_log="$2"

  if [[ -n "${run_log}" && -f "${run_log}" ]]; then
    tail -n 80 "${run_log}"
    return
  fi

  if [[ -n "${build_log}" && -f "${build_log}" ]]; then
    tail -n 80 "${build_log}"
    return
  fi

  if [[ -f "${DVSIM_LOG}" ]]; then
    tail -n 80 "${DVSIM_LOG}"
  fi
}

inject_repro_vseq() {
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("/home/opentitan/hw/ip/edn/dv/env/seq_lib/edn_vseq_list.sv")
text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
marker = "class edn_disable_repro_vseq extends edn_base_vseq;"

if marker not in text:
    text = text.replace('`include "edn_common_vseq.sv"\n', '''`include "edn_common_vseq.sv"

class edn_disable_repro_vseq extends edn_base_vseq;
  `uvm_object_utils(edn_disable_repro_vseq)
  `uvm_object_new

  localparam string BootReqPath = "tb.dut.u_edn_core.boot_req_q";

  virtual task body();
    uvm_hdl_data_t boot_req_q;

    super.body();

    `uvm_info(`gfn, "Enable EDN in boot request mode.", UVM_LOW)
    csr_wr(.ptr(ral.ctrl), .value(32'h9));

    `DV_SPINWAIT(
      forever begin
        cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(1);
        `DV_CHECK_FATAL(uvm_hdl_read(BootReqPath, boot_req_q))
        if (boot_req_q[3:1] != 3'b000) break;
      end
    )

    `uvm_info(`gfn, $sformatf("Observed boot_req_q=0x%0h, disabling EDN.", boot_req_q[3:0]),
              UVM_LOW)
    csr_wr(.ptr(ral.ctrl), .value(32'h0), .backdoor(1));
    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(1);

    `DV_CHECK_FATAL(uvm_hdl_read(BootReqPath, boot_req_q))
    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(boot_req_q[3:0], 4'h0,
                       $sformatf("boot_req_q should clear when EDN is disabled, got 0x%0h",
                                 boot_req_q[3:0]))

    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(2);
  endtask
endclass : edn_disable_repro_vseq
''')

text = text.replace('`include "edn_disable_repro_vseq.sv"\n', "")
path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
PY
}

export PATH="/tools/riscv/bin:/tools/verible/bin:${PATH}"
mkdir -p "${TB_ROOT}"
rm -rf "${SCRATCH_ROOT}"

inject_repro_vseq || fail

timeout 1800 python util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/edn/dv/edn_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i edn_smoke \
  -t vcs \
  --fixed-seed 1 \
  --scratch-root "${SCRATCH_ROOT}" \
  -ro +UVM_TEST_SEQ=edn_disable_repro_vseq +test_timeout_ns=100000 \
  >"${DVSIM_LOG}" 2>&1
dvsim_rc=$?

run_log="$(find "${SCRATCH_ROOT}" -path '*/run.log' | sort | head -n1)"
build_log="$(find "${SCRATCH_ROOT}" -path '*/build.log' | sort | head -n1)"

if [[ ${dvsim_rc} -eq 124 ]]; then
  echo "[ERROR] Simulation timed out after 1800 seconds."
  show_failure_context "${run_log}" "${build_log}"
  fail
fi

if [[ -n "${run_log}" && -f "${run_log}" ]]; then
  # Prefer the simulator's per-test verdict over dvsim's aggregate exit status.
  if grep -q "TEST PASSED CHECKS" "${run_log}"; then
    pass
  fi

  if grep -q "TEST FAILED CHECKS" "${run_log}"; then
    show_failure_context "${run_log}" "${build_log}"
    fail
  fi
fi

if [[ ${dvsim_rc} -eq 0 ]]; then
  pass
fi

show_failure_context "${run_log}" "${build_log}"
fail

problem_statement:
Observed behavior: The Entropy Distribution Network (EDN) does not fully stop when firmware clears the `EDN_ENABLE` control while EDN is already partway through boot-time request mode, the mode where EDN hardware automatically issues a fixed instantiate-then-generate sequence to the Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator (CSRNG). Some progress from the earlier boot-time sequence remains latched after disable, which breaks the required start/stop/start workflow for switching EDN from boot-time operation to a later reconfigured mode.

Expected behavior: Clearing `EDN_ENABLE` must discard all in-progress boot-time request sequencing state and return the EDN boot-request control path to its idle reset condition. After firmware re-enables and reconfigures EDN, the next boot-time start must begin from the first step of the fixed boot sequence, not from a partially completed earlier run.

Affected functionality: EDN boot-time request sequencing in the entropy complex, specifically the hardware-controlled path that drives the fixed boot instantiate/generate flow toward CSRNG.

Trigger condition: EDN is enabled in boot-time request mode, the hardware-controlled boot sequence has already started, and firmware clears `EDN_ENABLE` before that sequence has completed or returned to idle.

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/opentitan || exit 1
set +e
set -o pipefail

TB_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_pr5830"
RESULTS=()
failures=0
overall_rc=0

rm -rf "$TB_ROOT"
mkdir -p "$TB_ROOT"

ensure_test_patch() {
  if grep -q 'cs_aes_halt_i' hw/ip/csrng/dv/tb.sv \
    && grep -q 'cs_aes_halt_i' hw/ip/entropy_src/dv/tb/tb.sv; then
    return 0
  fi

  # The standardized verify flow is expected to run after applying test.patch.
  patch --forward --silent -p1 < /home/test.patch
}

build_passed() {
  local run_log="$1"

  # dvsim returns non-zero after a successful build on this baseline because
  # premailer rejects loading the local style.css while writing the HTML summary.
  grep -Eq '\[ *build *\]: \[Q: 0, D: 0, P: 1, F: 0, K: 0, T: 1\] 100%' "$run_log"
}

run_build() {
  local test_name="$1"
  local cfg="$2"
  local branch="$3"
  local run_dir="$TB_ROOT/$test_name"
  local run_log="$run_dir/dvsim.log"
  local scratch_root="$run_dir/scratch"

  mkdir -p "$run_dir"

  timeout 1800 ./util/dvsim/dvsim.py "$cfg" \
    -i smoke \
    -t vcs \
    --local \
    --max-parallel 1 \
    --build-only \
    --purge \
    --branch "$branch" \
    --scratch-root "$scratch_root" \
    2>&1 | tee "$run_log"
  local dvsim_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

  if build_passed "$run_log"; then
    RESULTS+=("TEST: ${test_name} ... PASS")
    return 0
  fi

  RESULTS+=("TEST: ${test_name} ... FAIL")
  failures=$((failures + 1))
  overall_rc=$dvsim_rc
  return "$dvsim_rc"
}

  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: csrng_standalone_build ... FAIL"

problem_statement:
## Description
The Entropy Source (ENTROPY_SRC) IP and the Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator (CSRNG) IP can both use power-hungry cryptographic datapaths in the background. In the affected path, ENTROPY_SRC uses its SHA3 conditioning path while CSRNG uses its AES cipher datapath. The affected functionality is the inter-module coordination between these two IPs that is needed to avoid a worst-case chip power spike when both datapaths would otherwise be active at the same time.

## Expected Behavior
The `entropy_src` and `csrng` IPs should expose an explicit coordination mechanism at their module boundary so an integration can prevent the SHA3 conditioning work in ENTROPY_SRC and the AES work in CSRNG from running simultaneously. This requirement belongs to the public interface between the two IPs, not only to one specific top-level integration.

## Actual Behavior
The current `entropy_src`/`csrng` IP boundary does not provide that coordination path. As a result, the design cannot express the power-spike-prevention contract between these two IPs at their integration boundary.

## Trigger Conditions
The issue is relevant when both IPs are present in a design, ENTROPY_SRC is configured to use its conditioning path instead of bypassing it, and CSRNG may still have AES activity in progress when ENTROPY_SRC needs to start conditioning.

## Implementation Constraint
The coordination mechanism between `entropy_src` and `csrng` should expose boundary signals using the exact tokens `cs_aes_halt_i` and `cs_aes_halt_o`, so integration can explicitly stall the SHA3/AES power-hungry datapaths when needed.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan OTP (One-Time Programmable) controller can leave a TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) read outstanding after a life cycle escalation event. If `lc_escalate_en` drives an unbuffered OTP software partition into the terminal `ErrorSt` state, a read through that partition's TL-UL software window, the memory-mapped read path exposed to software, may be accepted but never produce a valid response. From the bus master's point of view, the transaction hangs instead of completing.

## Expected Behavior
After life cycle escalation has moved an unbuffered OTP software partition into `ErrorSt`, a TL-UL read to that partition's software window must still complete with an error response. The read response must assert the TL-UL error indication (`d_error`), return `d_data` as 0, and present a valid completion so the request does not remain outstanding on the bus.

## Actual Behavior
After `lc_escalate_en` is asserted, the partition enters `ErrorSt`, but a subsequent TL-UL read to the software window does not return the expected error completion. The request is visible on the request side, yet no valid response is returned, so neither `d_error` nor zero data is observed.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the OTP controller's TL-UL software-window read path for unbuffered software partitions once the partition finite-state machine has entered its terminal error state because of life cycle escalation.

## Trigger Condition
Let an unbuffered OTP software partition finish initialization so its TL-UL software window is available, assert `lc_escalate_en` to force that partition into `ErrorSt`, and then issue a TL-UL read to the partition's software window.

resolved_issues.title: [prim] prim_ram_*p and wmask handling
resolved_issues.body:
Currently, if the data width of a memory is not fully divisible by the `DataBitsPerMask` parameter, this could lead to some bits of the memory not being writeable. 

This has come up as a problem in scramble capable memories. 
The scramble capable memories contain an sbox based diffusion layer to slightly scramble the XOR'd values on a multiple of 4 boundary.  As a result, the `DataBitsPerMask` needs to be set accordingly as well. 

This becomes a problem because if we set `DataBitsPerMask` to 8 on non-divisible widths (such as 39), some of the bits won't ever be written.  We should remove this requirement from prim_ram_*p to and allow a bit of write mask to cover any range that is less than `DataBitsPerMask`.

+ *   A module can neither generate an integrity response nor pass through any pre-existing
