#!/bin/bash
set -e

cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 39abe941ebe45d6673ebc522875b1274470e2b8f
git submodule update --init --recursive

if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at baseline commit"
  exit 1
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
`tlul_adapter_sram` is the TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) to SRAM bridge used by OpenTitan blocks such as OpenTitan Big Number Accelerator (OTBN) memories. Some of these memories store each 32-bit TL-UL data word together with per-word integrity bits in a wider physical SRAM word, for example a 39-bit word that contains 32 data bits plus 7 integrity bits. The adapter does not currently provide a usable word-level data-integrity passthrough mode for this kind of memory.

## Expected Behavior
For word-level accesses, `tlul_adapter_sram` should support a dedicated passthrough configuration for pre-existing SRAM data integrity. When that mode is enabled, the SRAM-side write-data, write-mask, and read-data interfaces must match the full physical SRAM word width, including the integrity bits, so a memory that stores a 32-bit TL-UL payload as a 39-bit physical word can be connected directly through the adapter.

## Actual Behavior
In the current implementation, the adapter's SRAM-side interface is effectively limited to the 32-bit payload width. As a result, a design that tries to place `tlul_adapter_sram` in front of an SRAM with stored word-level integrity cannot be instantiated or connected cleanly as a direct 39-bit SRAM-side interface.

## Trigger Condition
The problem appears when `tlul_adapter_sram` is used for word-level accesses and is connected to an SRAM whose physical word contains both the TL-UL payload and stored integrity bits, such as OTBN memories organized as 39-bit words.

[rstmgr] Fix several controllable reset issues

See #5601 and #5602

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

resolved_issues.title: DFT - In rstmgr_ctl block rst_pd_nq[0] and rst_aon_nq resets should be controlled in scan-mode
resolved_issues.body:
rst_pd_nq[0] and rst_aon_nq affecting ~26 FFs. In scan mode it is not controlled, hence these FFs are removed from scan.

SpyGlass-DFT messages: 

'top_earlgrey_asic.top_earlgrey.u_rstmgr_aon.u_sys_src.rst_pd_nq[0]' is not disabled for 20 flip-flop(s).

'top_earlgrey_asic.top_earlgrey.u_rstmgr_aon.u_sys_src.rst_aon_nq' is not disabled for 6 flip-flop(s).
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/79256454/111061787-af49f380-84ad-11eb-8884-9b378c20091b.png)

Suggested fix in rstmgr_ctl.sv file - add a scan reset mux for rst_pd_nq and rst_aon_nq resets

prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 263165193173262dd701517a99da0f271f830222
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  if [ -d "$d" ]; then
    export PATH="$d:$PATH"
  fi
done
true
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The Reset Manager (`rstmgr`) has a Design-for-Test (DFT) scan-reset controllability bug. The linked DFT reports identify uncontrollable reset roots in both `rstmgr_ctrl` (`rst_pd_nq[0]` and `rst_aon_nq`) and the power-on-reset block `rstmgr_por` (`rst_nq` and `rst_root_n`). For the observable failure used in this benchmark, the relevant consequence is in `rstmgr_por`: in scan mode, the active-low reset output `rst_no` is not fully overridden by the dedicated active-low scan reset input `scan_rst_ni`, so scan-resettable logic behind that output can remain uncontrollable.

## Expected Behavior
When `scanmode_i` is asserted, the active-low scan reset input `scan_rst_ni` must directly determine the active-low `rstmgr_por` output `rst_no`. If `scan_rst_ni` changes from `0` to `1` while scan mode is active, `rst_no` must also change from `0` to `1` immediately, even if the normal power-on-reset release sequence has not finished yet.

## Actual Behavior
If scan mode is enabled before the normal `rstmgr_por` power-on-reset release sequence completes, changing `scan_rst_ni` from `0` to `1` does not immediately change `rst_no` from `0` to `1`. `rst_no` can remain low because the normal `rstmgr_por` reset path is still gating the release. The linked DFT reports also describe related scan-reset controllability problems on `rstmgr_ctrl` reset roots such as `rst_pd_nq[0]` and `rst_aon_nq`.

## Affected Function
Reset Manager DFT scan-reset control, with the benchmarked failure in the `rstmgr_por` power-on-reset output path.

## Trigger Condition
Release `rst_ni`, assert `scanmode_i` before the normal `rstmgr_por` power-on-reset release sequence finishes, and then change `scan_rst_ni` from `0` to `1`. Under those conditions, `rst_no` should rise immediately but does not.

body: This addresses #5497

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[otp_ctrl] Make sure timeout error is asserted permanently

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

[otp_ctrl] Properly end cnsty/integ checks that found an error

This changes the behavior of the buffered partition checker logic such
that failing checks signal back to the LFSR timer that they have
finished performing the check.

That way, the LFSR timer can still continue running and triggering
checks in other partitions, despite the faulty partition being in the
terminal error state.

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

resolved_issues.title: [otp_ctrl] otp_check failures and error status
resolved_issues.body:
Hey Michael, 
I have three questions/issues related to OTP_CHECK failure.

1. If otp check has timeout error, it reports incorrect status error:
   Expected status: "timeout_error" should stay high;
   Actual status: "timeout_error" is high for ONE CLOCK CYCLE, then "lsfr_fsm_error" stays high.
   
   Reason: [`chk_timeout_d`](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/otp_ctrl/rtl/otp_ctrl_lfsr_timer.sv#L211) is cleared when state machine changes from `IntegWaitSt` to `ErrorSt`.
Please refer to the screenshot below:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11466553/110259794-64385980-7f5e-11eb-9ca8-9167eb036803.png)

2. Regarding `check_pending` status, I found the `check_pending` status will stay high even if any check failure are found.
   
   For example if we have a ECC uncorrectable error.  A fatal alert will trigger, but LFSR state machine will be stuck at ["CnstyWaitSt"](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/otp_ctrl/rtl/otp_ctrl_lfsr_timer.sv#L265) state, and status `check_pending` field will be `1` until reset or timeout.
This is because in `otp_ctrl_part_buf.sv` we only return [`integ_chk_ack_o = 1'b1`](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/otp_ctrl/rtl/otp_ctrl_part_buf.sv#L332) if a check is passed. 
I want to double check if the behavior is expected? Would it be more clear if design exits `CnstyWaitSt` state and clear `check_pending` bit after ECC uncorrectable error is found.

3. In [otp_ctrl spec](https://docs.opentitan.org/hw/ip/otp_ctrl/doc/index.html#partition-checks) I found a statement saying: "If a failure is encountered, the OTP controller will send out a fatal_check_error alert and reset all of its hardware outputs to their defaults."
  Are the "defaults value" referring to the values before OTP_INIT or after OTP_INIT?

Thanks for your time and inputs :)
Cindy

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's OTP (One-Time Programmable) controller performs background integrity and consistency checks on buffered OTP partitions. During one of these checks, the `otp_ctrl_lfsr_timer` finite state machine waits for the targeted partition or partitions to acknowledge completion.

## Expected Behavior
If the configured timeout expires while the timer is waiting in `IntegWaitSt` or `CnstyWaitSt`, the OTP controller must latch the timeout failure and keep the `timeout_error` status asserted after the timer enters `ErrorSt`. The reported failure must remain a timeout-caused check failure until reset, rather than changing on the next cycle to a generic Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) / finite state machine (FSM) error.

## Actual Behavior
When a background integrity or consistency check times out in `IntegWaitSt` or `CnstyWaitSt`, `timeout_error` is asserted for only one clock cycle. After the timer transitions to `ErrorSt`, the timeout indication is cleared and the controller instead reports a generic LFSR/FSM error.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the OTP controller's background partition-check timer, specifically timeout reporting in `otp_ctrl_lfsr_timer`.

## Trigger Conditions
The bug is triggered when the OTP controller starts a background integrity or consistency check, at least one partition acknowledgement does not arrive before the configured timeout expires, and the timer transitions from the corresponding wait state into `ErrorSt`.

title: [lc_ctrl] Several life cycle updates
body: This addresses #5226

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[lc_ctrl] Assert lc_escalate_en in (virtual) SCRAP and INVALID states

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

[lc_ctrl] Do not latch new LC state in register

Previously, the new LC state has been latched inside the lc_ctrl before
programming it, with the intent to reuse some of the error checking
logic on that LC state.

However, this path can potentially be dangerous since it requires
additional logic to make sure the life cycle signals are not decoded
anymore once the new state has been latched.

This change therefore removes this feedback path into the life cycle
state register, and directly feeds out the combinationally computed next
state. This logic is running on a very slow clock <=25 MHz, hence this
should not create timing issues.

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

[lc_ctrl] Update the docs to reflect escalation updates

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

[lc_ctrl] Buffer incoming life cycle ACK signals

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

[lc_ctrl] Max out the transition counter when going into SCRAP

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

resolved_issues.title: [lc_ctrl] Output escalate_en when in virtual scrap
resolved_issues.body:
Always escalate when life cycle state transitions to virtual scrap.
This is because alert_handler may be configured to skip escalation and go straight to scrap.

See [comment](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/4883#discussion_r567849094) for details

prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 466585e351fbe8687445131a20317c465ca43c36
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at 466585e351fbe8687445131a20317c465ca43c36; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at 466585e351fbe8687445131a20317c465ca43c36"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at 466585e351fbe8687445131a20317c465ca43c36; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  if [[ -d "$d" ]]; then
    export PATH="$d:$PATH"
  fi
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
In the `lc_ctrl` IP, which is OpenTitan's life cycle controller, the `ESCALATE_EN` output (`lc_escalate_en_o`) is not handled correctly for SCRAP-class life cycle conditions. OpenTitan can represent a scrapped device either as the permanent `SCRAP` life cycle state stored in One-Time Programmable (OTP) memory, or as a temporary virtual SCRAP condition entered at runtime without reprogramming OTP.

## Expected Behavior
Whenever `lc_ctrl` decodes a SCRAP-class condition, `lc_escalate_en_o` must be asserted. In particular, if the OTP life cycle state is already `SCRAP` when the controller initializes, then `lc_escalate_en_o` must be asserted once initialization completes. The same output must also be asserted when the controller enters the temporary virtual SCRAP condition.

## Actual Behavior
`lc_ctrl` can leave `lc_escalate_en_o` deasserted even though the decoded life cycle condition is SCRAP. As a result, downstream logic can observe a scrapped device without seeing the escalation indication that should accompany that state.

## Affected Function
The bug is in the `lc_ctrl` life cycle signal decode logic that generates external function-enable outputs, specifically the rule that drives `ESCALATE_EN` for SCRAP-class states.

## Trigger Conditions
The problem appears when `lc_ctrl` decodes a SCRAP-class condition, especially when the device starts up with OTP already programmed to `SCRAP`, and also when a runtime path moves the controller into the temporary virtual SCRAP condition.

git checkout cfe964410159b16c904f7329d490168be27846c5
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at cfe964410159b16c904f7329d490168be27846c5; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at cfe964410159b16c904f7329d490168be27846c5"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at cfe964410159b16c904f7329d490168be27846c5; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \

problem_statement:
## Description
Among the OpenTitan peripherals that are supposed to be connected to the EDN (Entropy Distribution Network), the Alert Handler IP is still modeled as if it receives entropy from a dedicated local input. This leaves the block's external interface inconsistent with an EDN-connected peripheral.

## Expected Behavior
The Alert Handler IP must expose the standard EDN consumer interface used by OpenTitan peripherals: entropy must be obtained through an EDN request/response connection, together with the EDN-related clock and reset inputs required by that interface. A standalone build or integration that instantiates Alert Handler as an EDN consumer must compile without requiring a separate local entropy input.

## Actual Behavior
The Alert Handler IP still exposes a separate local entropy input instead of the EDN consumer interface. As a result, environments that instantiate the block as an EDN-connected peripheral cannot connect the expected interface cleanly and fail to build.

## Affected Component
The affected component is the Alert Handler IP, specifically its entropy-consumer interface to the EDN.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the Alert Handler is instantiated in a standalone build or integration environment that expects it to consume entropy from the EDN rather than from a dedicated local entropy signal.

title: [otp_ctrl] Do not descramble digest values when read through the DAI
body:
Fix #4799

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[otp_ctrl] Do not descramble digest values when read through the DAI

Fix #4799

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@opentitan.org>

resolved_issues.title: [otp] read digest with DAI interface
resolved_issues.body:
Hi Michael,

Could you take a look at this question reading secret digest reading from DAI interface.

Firstly I would like to confirm: reading a digest from DAI interface (using `direct_access_cmd` -> rd command and `direct_access_address` -> the digest address) is legal. I believe it is legal because I did not see any status error when I read digests from DAI.

If the sequence is confirmed to be legal, then when reading secret partitions' digests, the CSR (for example: `secret0_digest_0`) register readout is different from the DAI readout result. From the waveform, we are trying to read address ('h7c3), normalized to decimal `1984` which is `Secret2DigestOffset`. Looks like the DAI readout added a descrambling step. (in the screenshot, where the second inserted bookmark, DAI interface returns data `0x59731f0b`, but partition_digest is all 0, and digest CSR readout is all 0s).

I think it would be good to unify both returns to avoid confusion. Do you think that is something the OTP_init script fix is enough, say by initializing the digest to descrambling as all 0s? Or severe enough to be a corner case that needs to be aligned and fixed in RTL?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11466553/104258022-941e2180-5433-11eb-8e33-5312fa143773.png)

Thanks,
Cindy

from pathlib import Path

seq_path = Path("/home/opentitan/hw/ip/otp_ctrl/dv/env/seq_lib/otp_ctrl_dai_digest_read_vseq.sv")
seq_path.write_text(
    """// Copyright lowRISC contributors.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

class otp_ctrl_dai_digest_read_vseq extends otp_ctrl_base_vseq;
  `uvm_object_utils(otp_ctrl_dai_digest_read_vseq)

  `uvm_object_new

  virtual task dai_rd_exact(bit [TL_AW-1:0] addr,
                            output bit [TL_DW-1:0] rdata0,
                            output bit [TL_DW-1:0] rdata1,
                            output bit [TL_DW-1:0] status);
    csr_wr(ral.direct_access_address, addr);
    csr_wr(ral.direct_access_cmd, int'(otp_ctrl_pkg::DaiRead));
    csr_spinwait(ral.intr_state.otp_operation_done, 1);
    csr_rd(ral.status, status);
    csr_rd(ral.direct_access_rdata_0, rdata0);
    if (is_secret(addr)) begin
      csr_rd(ral.direct_access_rdata_1, rdata1);
    end
    csr_wr(ral.intr_state, 1'b1 << OtpOperationDone);
  endtask

  task body();
    bit [TL_DW-1:0] status;
    bit [TL_DW-1:0] rdata0;
    bit [TL_DW-1:0] rdata1;
    bit [TL_DW-1:0] digest0;
    bit [TL_DW-1:0] digest1;

    do_otp_ctrl_init = 1'b1;
    dut_init();
    do_otp_ctrl_init = 1'b0;
    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(2);
    csr_rd_check(.ptr(ral.status), .compare_value(OtpDaiIdle));

    `uvm_info(`gfn, "Read secret digest through DAI before programming digest", UVM_MEDIUM)
    dai_rd_exact(Secret2DigestOffset, rdata0, rdata1, status);
    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(status, OtpDaiIdle)
    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(rdata0, '0)
    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(rdata1, '0)

    `uvm_info(`gfn, "Program secret digest and verify DAI read still works after lock", UVM_MEDIUM)
    cal_digest(Secret2Idx);
    dut_init();
    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(2);

    csr_rd(.ptr(ral.secret2_digest_0), .value(digest0));
    csr_rd(.ptr(ral.secret2_digest_1), .value(digest1));
    dai_rd_exact(Secret2DigestOffset, rdata0, rdata1, status);
    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(status, OtpDaiIdle)
    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(rdata0, digest0)
    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(rdata1, digest1)
  endtask
endclass
""",
    encoding="utf-8",
)

vseq_list = Path("/home/opentitan/hw/ip/otp_ctrl/dv/env/seq_lib/otp_ctrl_vseq_list.sv")

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan OTP (One-Time Programmable) Controller, software can legally use the DAI (Direct Access Interface) to read the hardware digest location of a secret partition by writing a read command to `direct_access_cmd` and the digest address to `direct_access_address` (for example, `Secret2DigestOffset`). For secret partitions, the value returned through the DAI does not always match the digest value exposed through the corresponding Control and Status Registers (CSRs), even though that digest is also software-visible through those CSRs.

## Expected Behavior
Reading a secret partition's hardware digest through the DAI should return the same digest value that software observes through the partition's digest CSRs once the controller has re-sensed the OTP contents. In the initialization case where the digest contents are zero, both interfaces should return zero. After a hardware digest has been computed or programmed and the partition becomes read-locked, the digest must still remain readable through the DAI and must still match the CSR value.

## Actual Behavior
When the DAI reads a secret partition digest address, the returned value can differ from the digest CSRs. In the zero-digest initialization case, the digest CSRs read as zero while the DAI can return a non-zero value. There is also a locked-partition corner case where reading the hardware digest through the DAI reports an access error instead of returning the stored digest.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the OTP Controller DAI read handling for hardware digest locations of secret partitions.

## Trigger Condition
The issue is triggered by issuing a DAI read to the digest address of a secret OTP partition, such as `Secret2DigestOffset`, both before a digest has been computed or programmed and after a hardware digest has been computed or programmed and the partition is read-locked.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan key manager (`keymgr`) can incorrectly report success for a KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code)-backed software output generation request that violates the creator-stage key version policy. After `keymgr` advances into `CreatorRootKey`, which is the first operational state where software output generation is allowed, software can program `key_version` to a value greater than `max_creator_key_ver` and then start `OpGenSwOut`. In this boundary case, the request should be rejected, but the invalid-input condition is not preserved through final completion, so the operation can finish with a success status instead of a failure.

## Expected Behavior
In the `CreatorRootKey` state, an `OpGenSwOut` request with `key_version > max_creator_key_ver` must complete as a failed operation. When the request finishes, the final operation status must report failure (`OpDoneFail`), not success, for this out-of-range key version.

## Actual Behavior
When software starts `OpGenSwOut` from the `CreatorRootKey` state with `key_version` above `max_creator_key_ver`, the key manager can still finish with a success status (`OpDoneSuccess`). As a result, the key version policy violation is not visible in the final operation result.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the OpenTitan key manager (`keymgr`) control path for KMAC-backed software output generation in the `CreatorRootKey` stage, specifically the logic that carries invalid-input errors into the final operation status.

## Trigger Conditions
The bug is triggered when the key manager has advanced into `CreatorRootKey`, software programs `key_version` above `max_creator_key_ver`, and software then starts an `OpGenSwOut` request.

problem_statement:
## Description
In the buffered `prim_fifo_sync` synchronous FIFO primitive (`Depth > 0`, not the pass-through configuration), the external write-side handshake is inconsistent while the active-low reset input `rst_ni` is asserted. When the FIFO is empty and held in reset, `wready_o` can remain high, so upstream logic can interpret the FIFO as ready to accept a write even though the FIFO is still under reset. Because `prim_fifo_sync` is a reusable OpenTitan primitive, any IP block that samples this interface during reset can observe the incorrect handshake behavior.

## Expected Behavior
For an empty buffered `prim_fifo_sync` while `rst_ni == 0`, the FIFO should present an inactive empty interface: `wready_o` must be `0`, `rvalid_o` must be `0`, and the reported occupancy `depth_o` must remain `0`. After reset is released, the same empty FIFO should return to normal empty-FIFO behavior by becoming write-ready again while still reporting no readable entry and zero occupancy.

## Actual Behavior
During reset, the FIFO can assert `wready_o` even though it is empty and being reset. This makes the reset-time interface inconsistent with an inactive empty FIFO and can cause surrounding logic to treat the FIFO as ready for a write during the reset window. The observable failure is the incorrect `wready_o` value during reset.

## Affected Module
The bug affects the buffered implementation of the `prim_fifo_sync` FIFO primitive, specifically its externally visible write-side ready signal and reset-time empty-interface behavior.

## Trigger Condition
The problem occurs when a buffered `prim_fifo_sync` instance is empty and `rst_ni` is asserted while surrounding logic observes the FIFO interface. The key failing case is sampling `wready_o` during reset and seeing it high instead of low.

resolved_issues.title: [top / edn] inter-module broadcast bus
resolved_issues.body:
The inter-module function supports the broadcast function where a single port on a particular instance is connected to ports of multiple instances (see `csrng`).  However, it doesn't seem to support the case if only a partial number of the connections are populated.

As an example, `edn` is able to support 4 connections. However, when hooking up only one, the other 3 seem to just be left dangling.  This might be a problem because the total number of connection points on `edn` is fixed, so if we don't have EXACTLY the same number of points (and we might not) something might be left dangling. 

I think we can do some pretty simple fixes such as declaring default values for those connections and just overriding the rest in an always block.  Of course there may be other fixes as well.

problem_statement:
## Description
The Alert Handler's escalation output is not fully connected into the Power Manager (pwrmgr) reset path. In OpenTitan, an escalation event should create a dedicated escalation-driven reset request inside pwrmgr instead of being treated like an ordinary peripheral reset request.

## Expected Behavior
When the Alert Handler asserts an escalation reset, pwrmgr must detect that escalation, propagate the resulting reset request through the clock-domain crossing into the slow reset logic, and expose that event through its escalation-reset status indication. This reset path must remain effective even if ordinary peripheral reset requests are disabled by the software-controlled reset-enable mask.

## Actual Behavior
The current design can detect incoming escalation activity, but the corresponding escalation-driven reset request is not carried through the internal pwrmgr reset path correctly. As a result, the slow-domain masked reset-request path does not reflect the escalation reset, and the escalation-reset status indication does not assert.

## Affected Function
Power Manager (pwrmgr) handling of Alert Handler escalation resets, specifically the dedicated escalation-reset input path, the propagation of that request into the slow reset domain, and the status reporting for an observed escalation reset.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the Alert Handler asserts an escalation reset into pwrmgr.

resolved_issues.title: [lc / flash] Access rights
resolved_issues.body:
The flash isolated partitions have the following access rules

Accessible = read / write
Readable = read only
Writeable = write only

Software Access Table 
| Asset                  |   Raw / Test Locked   |  Test unlocked         | Production states  | RMA |
|------------------      | ----------------------------  | -------------------         | ------------------------ |  ----- | 
| creator seed       |  no access                  |  no access               | accessible if ID blank | accessible |
| owner seed        |   no access                 |  no access               | accessible  | accessible |
| isolated partition |  no access                   |  writeable               | accessible |  accessible  |

Hardware Access Table 
| Asset                  |   Raw / Test Locked   |  Test unlocked         | Production states / RMA |
|------------------      | ----------------------------  | -------------------         | ------------------------ | 
| creator seed       |  no access                  |  no access               | readable if ID not blank | 
| owner seed        |   no access                 |  no access               | readable if ID not blank |
| isolated partition |  no access                  |  no access               | no access                       |

To support this function, the life cycle controller will implement the following signals instead of the existing `provision_wr_en` and `provision_rd_en` which are not enough to cover its needs. 

```
creator_seed_sw_rw_en
owner_seed_sw_rw_en
iso_part_sw_rd_en
iso_part_sw_wr_en
seed_hw_rd_en
```


Additionally, the `lc_nvm_debug_en` signal also needs an earlier cut-off (before production states) to ensure the isolated partition above cannot be backdoor'd during specific TEST states.  Whether this should be tied directly to life cycle or another OTP needs to be quickly discussed.

problem_statement:
## Description
The flash access-control interface between the Life Cycle Controller (lc_ctrl) and the Flash Controller (flash_ctrl) is too coarse to express the required policy for the creator seed, owner seed, isolated flash information partition, and hardware reads of the seed pages. Software access to the creator seed, software access to the owner seed, software read access to the isolated partition, software write access to the isolated partition, and hardware read access to the seeds are not independently controllable, so some required life-cycle access combinations cannot be represented correctly.

## Expected Behavior
For this issue, "accessible" means read/write, "readable" means read only, and "writeable" means write only.

In RAW and TEST_LOCKED states, neither software nor hardware should have access to the creator seed, owner seed, or isolated partition.

In TEST_UNLOCKED states, software should have write-only access to the isolated partition. Software should still have no access to the creator seed or owner seed, and hardware should still have no access to the seed pages or isolated partition.

In production states before the device has been personalized (`ID blank`), software should be able to access the creator seed, owner seed, and isolated partition, while hardware should not yet be able to read the creator or owner seed.

In production states after the device has been personalized (`ID not blank`), software should lose access to the creator seed but keep access to the owner seed and isolated partition. Hardware should gain read access to the creator and owner seeds, and should still have no access to the isolated partition.

In RMA, software should be able to access the creator seed, owner seed, and isolated partition.

## Actual Behavior
The current life-cycle-to-flash interface ties these permissions together through coarse enable signals. As a result, the Flash Controller cannot distinguish all required cases independently, and valid combinations of creator-seed software access, owner-seed software access, isolated-partition software read access, isolated-partition software write access, and hardware seed-read access are mis-gated.

## Affected Function
This affects the Flash Controller's info-partition privilege gating and hardware seed-read control, together with the Life Cycle Controller's decode and broadcast of flash access-rights signals.

## Trigger Condition
A concrete failing case is a production-state configuration after personalization (`ID not blank`) where creator-seed software access must be Off while owner-seed software access, isolated-partition software read access, isolated-partition software write access, and hardware seed-read access must all be On at the same time.

## Implementation Constraint
The flash/lc integration should expose separate life-cycle qualifiers whose identifiers include the exact tokens `creator_seed_sw_rw_en`, `owner_seed_sw_rw_en`, `iso_part_sw_rd_en`, `iso_part_sw_wr_en`, and `seed_hw_rd_en`. These qualifiers must be independently controllable rather than collapsed into coarse provision or iso-flash enables.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Key Manager (`keymgr`) IP has a bug in the logic that controls `CFGEN`, the hardware-maintained bit that keeps key manager configuration control/status registers (CSRs) writable before an operation begins. After `keymgr` has completed its one-time initialization and is already idle in the initialized state, software can still write `CONTROL.INIT`. That write is supposed to be ignored once initialization is complete, but the current design clears `CFGEN` again.

## Expected Behavior
Once `keymgr` has completed initialization and no key manager operation is in progress, writing `CONTROL.INIT` again must not change the configuration-write-enable state. `CFGEN` must remain asserted, and configuration CSRs gated by `CFGEN`, including `KEY_VERSION`, must stay writable until software starts a real operation with `CONTROL.START`.

## Actual Behavior
A redundant write to `CONTROL.INIT` after initialization clears `CFGEN` even though no operation has started. As a result, `keymgr` still appears initialized, but its configuration CSRs become locked prematurely. One observable symptom is that a subsequent write to `KEY_VERSION` is ignored.

## Trigger Condition
Bring `keymgr` through its normal initialization so that it reaches the initialized idle state with `CFGEN` asserted and `KEY_VERSION` writable. Then write `CONTROL.INIT` again before issuing `CONTROL.START`.

title: [kmac] Revise to release MsgFIFO access when Idle
body:
Problem:

    When Idle or KeyMgr is in operation (KDF), Sw access to MsgFIFO
    hangs the interconnect.

`kmac_keymgr` drops the `sw_ready_o` if `mux_sel` is not `SelSw`. The
mux is switched to the software when KeyMgr is not operating and the
software issues `CmdStart`.

In this case when the mux is not switched to the software, if the
software writes data into the Msg FIFO, the keymgr interface module
never asserts the ready. So, there's no way for software to release this
condition, as the software cannot issue CmdStart.

This commit is to fix the behavior by asserting the ready always. Then
it also creates an error code for this scenario so that the software
knows what it did wrong.

This is related to issue #4409

  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"

  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at 4fc0b2196c60ba6b19a29039fe6a54861079bb18; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then

  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt

    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

  python -m pip install "premailer==3.8.0" --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at 4fc0b2196c60ba6b19a29039fe6a54861079bb18"

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH

  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at 4fc0b2196c60ba6b19a29039fe6a54861079bb18; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do

  fi

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then

for pkg in edalize fusesoc hjson; do

problem_statement:
## Description
The affected logic is the KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) message-input ownership and arbitration around the `MSG_FIFO` window. `MSG_FIFO` is the memory window software uses to stream message data into KMAC. That path is shared with the Key Manager (KeyMgr) application interface, and software does not own the software message path until it has issued the KMAC start command (`CmdStart`).

## Expected Behavior
If software writes to `MSG_FIFO` before issuing `CmdStart`, the TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) write must complete instead of leaving the bus transaction outstanding. KMAC must reject the access as invalid software use of `MSG_FIFO` and record a software-visible error code for that condition.

## Actual Behavior
On the affected implementation, a software write to `MSG_FIFO` while KMAC is idle and the software path has not been selected can wait indefinitely for the ready/response handshake. This wedges the TL-UL interconnect and prevents software from recovering by issuing `CmdStart` afterward, because the original write never completes.

## Trigger Conditions
KMAC is idle, no software `CmdStart` has been issued for the operation, and software performs a write to the `MSG_FIFO` window.

resolved_issues.title: [csrng/rtl] Mechanism to disable the AES cipher block bypass function
resolved_issues.body:
There is a concern that the disabling of the AES cipher block in csrng may be forced by some security attack. There exists two mechanisms to prevent this: one is the lock register will prevents registers to be written after boot time. Another is use an efuse to prevent this from happening. 
A third alternative is to remove the bypass logic altogether, via the use of a parameter and a condition statement. 
Looking for a consistent system level way to handle this case.

Referencing https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/3842#issue-505088218.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's CSRNG (Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator) contains a block encryption path that can either run an AES encryption round or return the input block unchanged through a bypass path. That bypass is intended to be available only when the lifecycle Design-for-Test (DFT) enable allows it. In the current behavior, asserting the bypass request can disable AES even when the lifecycle DFT enable is Off.

## Expected Behavior
For a CSRNG block encryption request, if the lifecycle DFT enable is Off, the bypass request must be ignored and the AES cipher must still run. The request should still complete normally, preserve the associated command and instance ID, and return the AES-transformed output block rather than the original input block. The bypass path may only take effect when the lifecycle DFT enable explicitly allows DFT operation.

## Actual Behavior
When bypass is requested while the lifecycle DFT enable is Off, the CSRNG block encryption path can still bypass the AES cipher. The request completes, but the returned data block is the same as the input block instead of an AES output.

## Affected Function
CSRNG `block_encrypt`, specifically the lifecycle gating of the AES cipher bypass in the CSRNG block encryption path.

## Trigger Conditions
This occurs when a CSRNG block encryption request asserts the bypass path while the lifecycle DFT enable input is Off.

resolved_issues.title: [otp] secret encrypt and decrypt data mismatch
resolved_issues.body:
Hi Michael,

When reading out secret data, I found they are not the same data as I wrote. Seems like the issue this related to presence instantiation:

1. We instantiate prim_presence `NumRounds` as `1` here: 
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/otp_ctrl/rtl/otp_ctrl_scrmbl.sv#L370

2. But in calculating `otp_dec_key_lut`, we are using `present_round_lut` instead of `1`:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/otp_ctrl/rtl/otp_ctrl_scrmbl.sv#L108

I think we have to align them to get the correct dec_key.

I also think either way we do not need the variable `otp_dec_key_lut`:
If we are using `round_index` as NumPresentRounds, we can do:
```
otp_dec_key_lut[k] = prim_cipher_pkg::present_update_key128(otp_dec_key_lut[k], 5'(j+1)); 
```

Hope that is clear.
Thanks,
Cindy

problem_statement:
## Description
The OTP (One-Time Programmable) controller's secret-data scrambling path can corrupt an encrypt/decrypt round trip. In `otp_ctrl_scrmbl`, data encrypted with a secret partition scrambling key and then decrypted with the same key can come back as a different 64-bit value instead of the original plaintext.

## Expected Behavior
For the OTP controller's secret partition scrambling path, an `Encrypt` operation followed by a `Decrypt` operation with the same secret key selection must be lossless: decrypting the produced ciphertext must return exactly the original 64-bit plaintext, and the scrambler must complete the operation without entering an FSM error state.

## Actual Behavior
In the current implementation, the decrypt path is not consistent with the way the iterative one-round PRESENT block-cipher primitive advances its key-schedule index. As a result, `otp_ctrl_scrmbl` can produce ciphertext that its own decrypt path does not recover to the original plaintext, so secret data read back from OTP does not match what was previously written.

## Affected Function
This affects the OTP controller secret partition scrambling datapath in `otp_ctrl_scrmbl`, specifically the encrypt/decrypt path that uses the PRESENT block-cipher primitive (`prim_present`) and the derived decryption key for secret-partition data.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when `otp_ctrl_scrmbl` performs an `Encrypt` operation on secret-partition data and then performs the matching `Decrypt` operation on that ciphertext with the same secret key selection in the iterative one-round PRESENT configuration used by the OTP scrambler.

#!/bin/bash
set -e

cd /home/opentitan

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
fi

if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at b13857eb2413b0a8056f153698cce41d60fd75d9"
  exit 1
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan primitive interrupt generator `prim_intr_hw` currently drives its outgoing interrupt output `intr_o` directly from the interrupt state and interrupt enable inputs. The affected functionality is the `prim_intr_hw` output stage that turns a peripheral's interrupt state bit and enable bit into the exported hardware interrupt line.

## Expected Behavior
`intr_o` should be a registered output of `prim_intr_hw`, updated only on the rising edge of the primitive clock after reset is released. If an interrupt becomes pending while its enable is already set between two clock edges, `intr_o` must remain low until the next rising edge and assert there. If the pending interrupt state is cleared between two clock edges, `intr_o` must remain high until the next rising edge and deassert there.

## Actual Behavior
`intr_o` behaves as a combinational AND of the interrupt state and interrupt enable signals. As a result, when the pending interrupt state changes between clock edges while the interrupt is enabled, `intr_o` asserts or deasserts immediately in the same cycle instead of waiting for the next clock edge.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs in `prim_intr_hw` after reset when the interrupt state changes between clock edges while the corresponding interrupt enable is already asserted.

title: [aes] Clear all reg status trackers on writes to control reg
body:
With the commit contained in this PR, any write to the control register will clear the status tracking for the initial key, IV, data input and data output registers. As a result, software has to provide a fresh key, IV, input data whenever the control register is updated and the unit is operated in automatic mode. Without this commit and unless software initiated a clear of these registers with random data, it is possible to:
- re-use the key of a previous message,
- re-use the last content of the IV registers (can be the CTR value) of the previous message.
Note that the actual registers are not cleared upon a write to the control register. This clearing with random data should be initiated by software.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#2913.

resolved_issues.title: [aes:rtl] AES produces wrong result when data is interleaved with key
resolved_issues.body:
Hi Pirmin

I am seeing error when I interleave the data_in and key (also if I throw in IV but I am trying to go as simple as possible for debugging purposes)

I am seeing the issue on both xcelium and VCS.
to reproduce
checkout my aes_alert_dv branch
and run the aes_sanity_test with seed 1322140672

for the puposes of this problem it only produces one message of 16 bytes 
the following is fixed
data_in
key
key_len ( 256)
Mode (ecb)

the reference model produce the expected output 
the current input is
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53917183/88074444-b5364180-cb77-11ea-9090-e7a4fdde0a28.png)


My best guess is that the DUT starts prematurely when data is received before all key is received.

diff --git a/hw/ip/aes/data/aes.hjson b/hw/ip/aes/data/aes.hjson
index 01d5dddd2a139..cbc735fbb7662 100644
--- a/hw/ip/aes/data/aes.hjson
+++ b/hw/ip/aes/data/aes.hjson
@@ -151,6 +151,9 @@
       AES unit is non-idle, writes to this register are ignored.
       This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content.
       If the two write operations try to set a different value, a ctrl_err alert is triggered.
+      Any write operation to this register will clear the status tracking required for automatic mode (See MANUAL_OPERATION field).
+      A write to the Control Register is considered the start of a new message.
+      Hence, software needs to provide new key, IV and input data afterwards.
     '''
     swaccess: "rw",
     hwaccess: "hrw",
@@ -236,6 +239,7 @@
           Controls whether the AES unit is operated in normal/automatic mode (0) or fully manual mode (1).
           In automatic mode (0), the AES unit automatically i) starts to encrypt/decrypt when it receives new input data, and ii) stalls during the last encryption/decryption cycle if the previous output data has not yet been read.
           This is the most efficient mode to operate in.
+          Note that the corresponding status tracking is automatically cleared upon a write to the Control Register.
           In manual mode (1), the AES unit i) only starts to encrypt/decrypt after receiving a start trigger (see Trigger Register), and ii) overwrites previous output data irrespective of whether it has been read out or not.
           This mode is useful if software needs full control over the AES unit.
         '''

@@ -138,7 +138,9 @@ The following description explains how the AES unit operates, i.e., how the oper

 For a general introduction into these cipher modes, refer to [Recommendation for Block Cipher Modes of Operation](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nistspecialpublication800-38a.pdf).
 
-1. The initial key and configuration is provided to the AES unit via a set of control and status registers (CSRs) accessible by the processor via TL-UL bus interface.
+1. The configuration and initial key is provided to the AES unit via a set of control and status registers (CSRs) accessible by the processor via TL-UL bus interface.
+   The processor must first provide the configuration to the {{< regref "CTRL_SHADOWED" >}} register.
+   Then follows the initial key.
    Each key register must be written at least once.
    The order in which the registers are written does not matter.
 1. _The processor provides the initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value to the four IV registers via TL-UL bus interface in CBC or CTR mode, respectively.

@@ -135,6 +137,8 @@ module aes_control (

   logic       doing_cbc_enc, doing_cbc_dec;
   logic       doing_ctr;
+  logic       ctrl_we_q;
+  logic       clear_in_out_status;
 
   // Software updates IV in chunks of 32 bits, the counter updates 16 bits at a time.
   // Convert word write enable to internal half-word write enable.
@@ -193,8 +197,11 @@ module aes_control (
     key_init_we_o  = 8'h00;
 
     // IV registers
-    iv_sel_o    = IV_INPUT;
-    iv_we_o     = 8'h00;
+    iv_sel_o = IV_INPUT;
+    iv_we_o  = 8'h00;

+    // Control register

     // Pseudo-random number generator control

@@ -237,9 +244,18 @@ module aes_control (
                     data_in_clear_i || data_out_clear_i || prng_reseed_i) ? 1'b0 : 1'b1;
         idle_we_o = 1'b1;
 
-        // Initial key and IV updates are ignored if we are not idle.
-        key_init_we_o = idle_o ? key_init_qe_i : 8'h00;
-        iv_we_o       = idle_o ? iv_qe         : 8'h00;
+        if (idle_o) begin
+          // Initial key and IV updates are ignored if we are not idle.
+          key_init_we_o  = key_init_qe_i;
+          iv_we_o        = iv_qe;
+
+          // Control register updates are only allowed if we are idle.
+          ctrl_we_o      = ctrl_qe_i;
+
+          // Control register updates clear all register status trackers.
+          key_init_clear = ctrl_we_o;
+          iv_clear       = ctrl_we_o;
+        end
 
         if (prng_reseed_i) begin
           // Request a reseed of the PRNG, perform handshake.
@@ -464,14 +480,36 @@ module aes_control (

-  // Detect new input and output read.
-  // Edge detectors are cleared by the FSM.
-  assign data_in_new_d = (data_in_load || data_in_we_o) ? '0 : (data_in_new_q | data_in_qe_i);
+  // Input and output data register status tracking detects if:
+  // - A complete new data input block is available, and
+  // - An output data block has been read completely.
+  // The status tracking needs to be cleared upon writes to the control register. The clearing is
+  // applied one cycle later here to avoid zero-latency loops. This additional delay is not

+  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin : reg_ctrl_we

   assign data_in_new   = &data_in_new_d;

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan AES IP can carry initialization-vector and counter readiness state across a write to its shadowed control register `CTRL_SHADOWED` when the block is used in automatic mode (`MANUAL_OPERATION=0`), where the engine starts as soon as it believes the required inputs are available. After one message completes, software can reconfigure the AES block while it is idle for a new message, but the new message is not always treated as requiring a fully new Counter (CTR) mode initialization vector.

## Expected Behavior
A write to `CTRL_SHADOWED` while the AES block is idle must establish a new message context for automatic mode. If the next message is configured for CTR mode, the AES block must not start encryption when input data arrives until all four 32-bit words of the new 128-bit initialization vector (IV) or counter value have been written after that control-register update.

## Actual Behavior
If software finishes an Electronic Codebook (ECB) message, waits for the AES block to return idle, rewrites `CTRL_SHADOWED` for a CTR-mode message, writes only part of the new IV/counter value, and then writes input data, the AES engine can start the CTR operation before the remaining IV words are written. The operation then uses a partially updated IV/counter, with unwritten words still coming from the earlier message state, and produces the wrong ciphertext.

## Affected Function
AES IP automatic-mode message sequencing, specifically the control logic that tracks IV/counter validity across `CTRL_SHADOWED` updates and mode changes.

## Trigger Condition
Back-to-back automatic-mode messages where the first message is ECB and the next message is CTR, with the AES unit idle between them, and software provides the second message's input block before completing all four IV/counter register writes.

resolved_issues.title: [primgen] Parameters not populated
resolved_issues.body:
It seems like if a prim module has the following parameter format
`parameter logic [Width-1:0] ResetValue`

That paramater does not get populated when it is instantiated. 

If instead I do
```
localparam int WidthSub = Width-1,
parameter logic [Width-1:0] ResetValue
```

Then parameter is correctly populated during instantiation.

I've not looked into why this is happening at all yet.. hopefully will get a chance later today / tomorrow.

problem_statement:
## Description
The Reset Manager (`rstmgr`) drives the active-low reset bundle `resets_o` for the chip's reset domains. In scan/test mode, this bundle is supposed to be controlled by the dedicated active-low scan reset input instead of the normal reset-generation path.

## Expected Behavior
After the normal reset sequence has completed, asserting `scanmode_i` should hand control of every bit in `resets_o` to `scan_rst_ni`. Driving `scan_rst_ni` low should force all reset outputs low, and driving `scan_rst_ni` high should release all reset outputs high again.

## Actual Behavior
Once `rstmgr` has left its normal reset flow, asserting `scanmode_i` does not transfer control of `resets_o` to the scan reset input. The bundle continues to reflect the normal reset path, so toggling `scan_rst_ni` does not force all reset outputs low and then release them high.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when the design first completes its normal reset sequence and then enters scan/test mode while `scan_rst_ni` is toggled.

title: [prim_arbiter*] Add more FPV fairness checks and correct tree arbiter behavior
body:
Before diving too deep in the discussion below, I should say that we did not use the `prim_arbiter_tree` arbiter in our designs just yet. I had provisioned it for cases with large amounts of requestors, since the binary tree construction scales a bit better than `prim_arbiter_ppc` in terms of timing (the latter contains sequential loops that not all tools can optimize for). One place where this could be employed is our xbar.

----------------------------------------

This PR adds more FPV assertions to our RR arbiter primitives and corrects an arbitration issue in the tree arbiter. Also, it aligns the set of assertions and parameters of both the `prim_arbiter_tree`  and  `prim_arbiter_ppc` such that they have exactly the same interface.

The two new FPV assertions check for starvation and fairness, i.e.:
1) `NoStarvation_A`: checks whether all requests will be granted eventually if they do not drop out (i.e. remain asserted until granted)
2) `Fairness_A`: checks for fairness, where fairness is defined as: given that N requests are asserted constantly and downstream is ready, each of these requests must be granted exactly once within an N cycle window (no matter in which cycle we start observing).

I ran FPV with these new properties, and found that `prim_arbiter_ppc` fulfills these without issues, but for `prim_arbiter_tree` the tool found several counter examples for the fairness check. 

This is due to the way the tree arbiter assigns priorities. I.e., the tree arbiter uses a binary tree for arbitration and muxing, and arbitration conflicts at each tree node are resolved by looking at the `i` th bit  of a counter, where `i` corresponds to the level of the binary tree. The counter is just incremented each cycle, basically toggling the priority at each node at different intervals (depending on the tree level). While this has very good timing characteristics and correct behavior when all requests are asserted, it can result in unfair arbitration behavior when only a part of all the requests are asserted.

I hence reworked the tree arbiter such that it behaves the same as the PPC arbiter and made sure that it fulfills all FPV properties, while still retaining some of the timing advantages. The main idea behind the new design is the following:
- a prefix sum of the hot-1 grant signal is computed to split the request vector into two halves via masking. say, the current grant signal is `gnt[7:0] = 0000_1000`, then the prefix mask for the next cycle will be  `gnt[7:0] = 1111_0000`.
- requests in the upper halve of that vector are assigned higher priority than the indices in the lower half. since the arbitration tree will always select the lowest index with the highest priority. requests in the upper halve will be considered first, before the requests in the lower half are considered.

Note that this is very similar to how the `prim_arbiter_ppc` implementation works - just the way we compute things is different since we use binary tree structures for this.

----------------------------------------

Last, I would like to note that the initial tree arbiter used a similar construction as some of the PULP interconnect arbiters, see [here](https://github.com/pulp-platform/cluster_interconnect/blob/f0dc98b36884b20efc7e0b3476c96be48d4ea6d2/rtl/low_latency_interco/FanInPrimitive_Req.sv#L103
) and [here](https://github.com/pulp-platform/common_cells/blob/master/src/rr_arb_tree.sv).

I believe the same arbitratuion issue has recently been uncovered and addressed by @WRoenninger via https://github.com/pulp-platform/common_cells/pull/81. @zarubaf for visibility.

commits.message:
[prim_arbiter_ppc] Add more FPV fairness checks

This moves the RoundRobin_A out of the generate loop such that it is
more generic and can be copied for other RR arbiters as well.

Further, this adds two new FPV checks:
1) NoStarvation_A: this property checks whether all requests will be
granted eventually if they do not drop out (i.e. remain asserted until
granted)
2) Fairness_A: this property checks for strict fairness, where strict
fairness is defined as: if N requests are asserted constantly and
downstream is ready, each of these requests will be granted exactly once
if we wait for N cycles.

Also, the input request stability assertion can now optionally be
disabled using the EnReqStabA parameter if needed. The arbiter works
correctly either way, but this assertion might be useful in bus
protocols where the requests must remain stable when back pressured.

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@google.com>

[prim_arbiter_tree] Fix incorrect arbitration behavior

This carries over the new FPV properties from prim_arbiter_ppc, aligns
the parameters of the design, and corrects an arbitration issue.

The arbiter should now behave the same as the PPC arbiter.

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@google.com>

[prim_arbiter_*] Propagate parameter changes

This propagates the parameter changes in prim_arbiter_* to all affected
modules.

Signed-off-by: Michael Schaffner <msf@google.com>

problem_statement:
## Description
`prim_arbiter_tree` is OpenTitan's N:1 round-robin arbiter primitive. It accepts a request vector `req_i` from multiple requesters and selects one requester to forward to a single downstream sink, whose ability to accept a transfer is indicated by `ready_i`. The bug is in this primitive's round-robin grant selection when only a subset of request ports is active.

## Expected Behavior
If some requesters keep their `req_i` bits asserted continuously until they are granted and `ready_i` stays asserted, the arbiter must rotate grants only across those active requesters. With three active requesters on a 4-port arbiter (`req_i = 4'b0111`) immediately after reset and with `ready_i = 1`, the granted index should repeat `0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, ...`. More generally, when exactly N requesters remain continuously asserted and the sink is continuously ready, each of those N requesters must be granted exactly once within every N-cycle observation window.

## Actual Behavior
`prim_arbiter_tree` can violate that round-robin fairness when not all request ports are active. Instead of serving each continuously asserted active requester once before revisiting any of them, the arbiter can favor some active inputs and revisit them early. In the 4-port case with `req_i = 4'b0111` and `ready_i` held high, the arbiter does not maintain the expected `0, 1, 2` rotation.

## Trigger Condition
The issue is triggered in `prim_arbiter_tree` when fewer than all arbiter inputs are active, the active requests stay asserted until granted, and the downstream sink remains ready. Sparse request vectors such as `req_i = 4'b0111` on a 4-port instance are sufficient to expose the incorrect arbitration behavior.

title: [prim_fifo_sync] Make FIFO output zero when empty
body:
This change makes it so that all instances of `prim_fifo_sync` present 0 on the `rdata` output when they're empty. Before, an empty FIFO would continue to output the previously read byte on `rdata` even when empty, effectively leaking stale data.

This feature is controlled by the `ReadZeroOnEmpty` parameter per FIFO (turned on by default). 

Closes issue #2315.

git reset --hard
git clean -fdx

git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at 35cef980fb929790838a9d64fba98453ff658a6c; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at 35cef980fb929790838a9d64fba98453ff658a6c"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH

  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update

problem_statement:
## Description
`prim_fifo_sync` is OpenTitan's synchronous first-in, first-out (FIFO) primitive. When an instance becomes empty after its last queued element is read, the primitive can still expose that old element on its read-data output. This behavior is externally visible in downstream users such as the UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) receive FIFO, but the underlying bug is in `prim_fifo_sync` itself.

## Expected Behavior
When a `prim_fifo_sync` instance has no valid entry available, its read interface should represent the empty state unambiguously: `rvalid_o` must be low, and `rdata_o` must be `0` rather than the value of the most recently dequeued entry. This must still hold for a one-entry FIFO configuration after its only queued byte has been read.

## Actual Behavior
After the final queued entry is dequeued, `rvalid_o` drops as expected, but `rdata_o` continues to drive the previous value instead of returning to `0`. As a result, software or logic that samples the read-data output while the FIFO is empty can observe stale data from the last entry.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the empty-state read-output behavior of the `prim_fifo_sync` primitive, including instances used on software-visible receive paths such as the UART receive FIFO.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered by writing at least one element into a `prim_fifo_sync` instance, reading until the FIFO becomes empty, and then observing the read interface before any new write occurs. The benchmarked boundary case includes a single-entry FIFO that is written once and then read once.
