problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan Alert Handler hardware block, each alert class has an accumulation counter and a per-class escalation timer. When the accumulation counter reaches its programmed threshold, the timer starts escalation for that class. Software can clear a class through the `class_clr` register. The bug is in the Alert Handler per-class escalation timer on the accumulation-trigger path: if `class_clr` is asserted in the same cycle that the accumulation counter reaches its threshold, the clear does not take priority.

## Expected Behavior
For a class whose escalation timer is currently in its idle state (`Idle`), asserting `class_clr` in the same cycle as the threshold-crossing accumulation event must cancel that escalation start. After that cycle, the timer must remain in `Idle`, the escalation count must stay at zero, and the class must not enter the first escalation phase (`Phase0`) because of that accumulation event.

## Actual Behavior
When `class_clr` and the threshold-crossing accumulation event happen in the same cycle, the accumulation counter is cleared on the following cycle, but the escalation timer still treats the event as a valid trigger and enters escalation. As a result, software can observe the class being cleared while the same class still proceeds into escalation.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs in the Alert Handler IP when all of the following are true for the same class: escalation is enabled, the escalation timer is in `Idle`, the accumulation counter reaches its programmed threshold in that cycle, and software asserts `class_clr` in that same cycle. One concrete reproducer is `classc_accum_thresh = 1`, `classc_accum_cnt` changing from 0 to 1, and `classc_clr` asserted in that same cycle.

title: [rv_plic] Change PRIO number starting from 1
body:
As discussed in #1823, this PR is to match the PRIO* registers name to
the ID read in CC register.

Previously, ID read from CC register is not matched with the offset of
PRIO0, IS, IE, IP. For example, if the software read 0x3 value from CC
register, its corresponding bit in IS is IS[2].

PLIC now generates ID w.r.t the interrupt source bit position. RISC-V
PLIC spec requires to return ID value 0 when no interrupt. So, topgen
ties bit0 of interrupt source signal to 0. By doing in this way, reggen
doesn't have to support arithmetic operation to the parameter.

resolved_issues.title: [PLIC] PLIC Interrupt IDs Off-by-one Issues
resolved_issues.body:
The PLIC interface is confusing and has some oddness which manifests as the potential for off-by-one errors in software.

This comes from the fact that the interrupt id, `i` (as read from `CC<n>`) corresponds to the priority in `PRIO<i-1>`. This is because interrupt id `0` means "no interrupt", which does not need a corresponding priority register.

It would be nice if this off-by-one issue was resolved, I can see two potential resolutions, but it would be good to understand how this affects the hardware design (and verification). I see that `rv_plic` is currently `L1D0V0`, but I think given how it's going to be verified that may not be a reflection of reality.

Possible Changes:
1. We choose a different value to represent "no interrupt", allowing interrupt id `i` to correspond to the `PRIO<i>` register. A string of all-ones (`0xFFFFFFFF`) would make sense for this other value.
2. Create a `PRIO` register for the case of "no interrupt", which is useless (and potentially not connected to anything), but means that `PRIO<i>` corresponds to interrupt id `i`.

I would be interested to hear the possibilities here from the hw side

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout ab72a5fe1b6e990e9f0a4f79db395852ef712d5c
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    if stripped == "git+https://github.com/olofk/ipyxact.git@master":
        line = "git+https://github.com/olofk/ipyxact.git@main"
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  if [ -d "$d" ]; then
    export PATH="$d:$PATH"
  fi
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's RV_PLIC (RISC-V Platform-Level Interrupt Controller) assigns an interrupt source ID to the interrupt source selected for delivery to a target, and software later observes that same numbering through the per-target Claim/Complete register `CC<n>`. In the buggy implementation, the delivered interrupt ID is off by one: if source bit `i` is the selected interrupt, the controller reports ID `i + 1` instead of `i`. This is why software can observe an ID from `CC<n>` that does not line up with the same-numbered `PRIO` (priority), `IP` (interrupt pending), and `IE` (interrupt enable) entries.

## Expected Behavior
When RV_PLIC selects interrupt source `i` for a target, the reported interrupt ID must be exactly `i`. ID `0` must remain reserved to mean "no interrupt".

## Actual Behavior
When a real interrupt source with index `i > 0` is selected, the controller reports `i + 1`. That off-by-one numbering makes the interrupt ID seen by software inconsistent with the source numbering used elsewhere in RV_PLIC.

## Affected Function
This affects the RV_PLIC target-side interrupt arbitration and interrupt ID generation logic.

## Trigger Conditions
The bug appears whenever a nonzero interrupt source is the one selected for delivery to a target, such as when that source is pending, enabled, and wins the target's interrupt selection.

commits.message:
[tlul] Add tlul_adapater_host

tlul_adapter_host was taken from rv_dv but is a generic adapter that
belongs under tlul.

It adapts an Ibex style req/gnt/addr/valid/rdata interface to TL-UL.
Basic multiple request handling has been added and some changes around
how non word size transactions have been made. See the comments within
the RTL for details.

Fixes #1860, #53

Signed-off-by: Greg Chadwick <gac@lowrisc.org>

[rv_core_ibex] Make use of tlul_adapter_host

rv_core_ibex had its own adapter logic to connect Ibex to TL-UL. This
uses the tlul_adapter_host module instead.

Signed-off-by: Greg Chadwick <gac@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [tlul] Fix handling of mask for Get and use of PutFullData vs PutPartialData in tlul_adapater_host
resolved_issues.body:
Currently tlul_adapter_host simply passes the received be_i straight out to a_mask on the TL interface.

The interface used by the debug module doesn't set any be_i when it's reading when it intends to read everything which has caused https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/1802

It's probably reasonable to say on a simple reg/grant/rvalid interface be is ignored for reads and only used for writes so tlul_adapater_host should generate a full width a_mask for reads.

There's also a subtlety around PutFullData vs PutPartialData. tlul_adapter_host always uses PutFullData as the opcode for writes. However when the be_i isn't complete with respect to the size PutPartialData must be used as per the tile-link specification:

```
On channels A and B, which carry a mask field, the mask must be LOW for all inactive byte lanes.
Furthermore, for all messages other than PutPartialData , the bits of mask for all active byte
lanes must be HIGH.
```

resolved_issues.title: Refactor TL-UL Host adapter code into common code
resolved_issues.body:
We currently two pieces of code which convert a PULP-style bus host interface to TL-UL: One is in  `hw/ip/rv_dm/tlul_adapter_host.sv` (used by the debug module), the other one is embedded in `rv_core_ibex`. We should combine this code and move it to `hw/ip/tlul`.

While doing so, we should double-check that we actually match the Protocol described here: https://ibex-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/load_store_unit.html#protocol. (The address might change as long as no grant is received. This has led to confusion in the past.)

@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+// Copyright lowRISC contributors.
+// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, see LICENSE for details.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+//
+// tlul_adapter (Host adapter) converts basic req/grant/rvalid into TL-UL interface. If
+// MAX_REQS == 1 it is purely combinational logic. If MAX_REQS > 1 flops are required.
+//
+// The host driving the adapter is responsible for ensuring it doesn't have more requests in flight
+// than the specified MAX_REQS.
+//
+// The outgoing address is always word aligned. The access size is always the word size (as
+// specified by TL_DW). For write accesses that occupy all lanes the operation is PutFullData,
+// otherwise it is PutPartialData, mask is generated from be_i. For reads all lanes are enabled as
+// required by TL-UL (every bit in mask set).
+//
+// When MAX_REQS > 1 tlul_adapter_host does not do anything to order responses from the TL-UL
+// interface which could return them out of order. It is the host's responsibility to either only have
+// outstanding requests to an address space it knows will return responses in order or to not care
+// about out of order responses (note that if read data is returned out of order there is no way to
+// determine this)
+
+`include "prim_assert.sv"
+
+module tlul_adapter_host #(
+  parameter int unsigned MAX_REQS = 2
+) (
+  input clk_i,
+  input rst_ni,
+
+  input                              req_i,
+  output logic                       gnt_o,
+  input  logic [top_pkg::TL_AW-1:0]  addr_i,
+  input  logic                       we_i,
+  input  logic [top_pkg::TL_DW-1:0]  wdata_i,
+  input  logic [top_pkg::TL_DBW-1:0] be_i,
+
+  output logic                       valid_o,
+  output logic [top_pkg::TL_DW-1:0]  rdata_o,
+  output logic                       err_o,
+
+  output tlul_pkg::tl_h2d_t          tl_o,
+  input  tlul_pkg::tl_d2h_t          tl_i
+);
+  localparam int WordSize = $clog2(top_pkg::TL_DBW);
+
+  logic [top_pkg::TL_AIW-1:0] tl_source;
+  logic [top_pkg::TL_DBW-1:0] tl_be;
+
+  if (MAX_REQS == 1) begin : g_single_req
+    assign tl_source = '0;
+  end else begin : g_multiple_reqs
+    localparam int ReqNumW  = $clog2(MAX_REQS);
+
+    logic [ReqNumW-1:0] source_d;
+    logic [ReqNumW-1:0] source_q;
+
+    always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
+      if (!rst_ni) begin
+        source_q <= '0;
+      end else begin
+        source_q <= source_d;
+      end
+    end
+
+    always_comb begin
+      source_d = source_q;
+
+      if (req_i && gnt_o) begin
+        if (source_q == MAX_REQS - 1) begin
+          source_d = '0;
+        end else  begin
+          source_d = source_q + 1;
+        end
+      end
+    end
+
+    assign tl_source = top_pkg::TL_AIW'(source_q);
+  end
+
+  // For TL-UL Get opcode all active bytes must have their mask bit set, so all reads get all tl_be
+  // bits set. For writes the supplied be_i is used as the mask.
+  assign tl_be = ~we_i ? {top_pkg::TL_DBW{1'b1}} : be_i;
+
+  assign tl_o = '{
+    a_valid:   req_i,
+    a_opcode:  (~we_i) ? tlul_pkg::Get           :
+               (&be_i) ? tlul_pkg::PutFullData   :
+                         tlul_pkg::PutPartialData,
+    a_param:   3'h0,
+    a_size:    top_pkg::TL_SZW'(WordSize),
+    a_mask:    tl_be,
+    a_source:  tl_source,
+    a_address: {addr_i[31:WordSize], {WordSize{1'b0}}},
+    a_data:    wdata_i,
+    a_user:    '{default:'0},
+
+    d_ready:   1'b1
+  };
+
+  assign gnt_o   = tl_i.a_ready & req_i;
+
+  assign valid_o = tl_i.d_valid;
+  assign rdata_o = tl_i.d_data;
+  assign err_o   = tl_i.d_error;
+
+`ifdef INC_ASSERT
+  localparam OutstandingReqCntW =
+    (MAX_REQS == 2 ** $clog2(MAX_REQS)) ? $clog2(MAX_REQS) + 1 : $clog2(MAX_REQS);
+
+  logic [OutstandingReqCntW-1:0] outstanding_reqs_q;
+  logic [OutstandingReqCntW-1:0] outstanding_reqs_d;
+
+  always_comb begin
+    outstanding_reqs_d = outstanding_reqs_q;
+
+    if ((req_i && gnt_o) && !valid_o) begin
+      outstanding_reqs_d = outstanding_reqs_q + 1;
+    end else if (!(req_i && gnt_o) && valid_o) begin
+      outstanding_reqs_d = outstanding_reqs_q - 1;
+    end
+  end
+
+  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
+    if (!rst_ni) begin
+      outstanding_reqs_q <= '0;
+    end else begin
+      outstanding_reqs_q <= outstanding_reqs_d;
+    end
+  end
+
+  `ASSERT(DontExceeedMaxReqs, req_i |-> outstanding_reqs_d <= MAX_REQS);
+`endif
+endmodule
prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 4204a8db1d6c02a747270dc029a7f1feb5720cad
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at 4204a8db1d6c02a747270dc029a7f1feb5720cad; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    if stripped == "git+https://github.com/olofk/ipyxact.git@master":
        line = "git+https://github.com/olofk/ipyxact.git@05fd1b3d577903fe47418e1090cd280094e8a49c"
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at 4204a8db1d6c02a747270dc029a7f1feb5720cad"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at 4204a8db1d6c02a747270dc029a7f1feb5720cad; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  if [ -d "$d" ]; then
    export PATH="$d:$PATH"
  fi
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) host adapter submodule `tlul_adapter_host`, which converts a simple host-side request/grant/response-valid interface into TL-UL requests, mishandles byte-enable information. The incoming `be_i` signal is the host byte-enable mask, and the outgoing `a_mask` field is the TL-UL byte-lane mask.

## Expected Behavior
For a read transaction (`Get`), `be_i` should be ignored and the adapter should drive `a_mask` to all ones for the full access width, because TL-UL reads must mark every active byte lane as enabled. For a write transaction, the adapter should emit `PutFullData` only when every byte lane in the access is enabled. If any byte lane is disabled, it should emit `PutPartialData` and preserve the partial byte mask in `a_mask`.

## Actual Behavior
The adapter currently forwards `be_i` directly into `a_mask` for reads, so a host that leaves `be_i` at zero or otherwise does not drive meaningful byte enables during a read can emit a `Get` request with an invalid zero or partial mask. It also emits `PutFullData` for writes even when `be_i` enables only a subset of the byte lanes, so the TL-UL write opcode does not match the mask.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when the host-side interface performs a read without meaningful byte enables, or when it performs a write with a partial byte-enable mask instead of a full-width mask.

title: [hmac] Drop the request prior to hash_start
body:
@jon-flatley  mentioned the case that MSG_FIFO can be back-pressured when the
software writes the message into MSG_FIFO when `hash_start` is not
asserted in issue #1869. It is not desirable behavior as it can lock the
core access. If that happens, core cannot set `hash_start` to flush out
the data.

This commit is to restrict the access from the software. It only allows
the MSG_FIFO (request to packer) from `hash_start` to `hash_process`. If
the software tries to write the message other than the time above, it
drops the request and raises an error with
`SwPushMsgWhenDisallowed(0x5)` error code.

This is related to #1869 #1871

problem_statement:
## Description
The HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) IP incorrectly accepts software writes to the `MSG_FIFO` message input window on the TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) bus before the HMAC start command (`CMD.hash_start`) has been issued.

## Expected Behavior
Before `CMD.hash_start`, a write to `MSG_FIFO` must be discarded and reported as the disallowed message-push software error (`SwPushMsgWhenDisallowed`, `0x5`). It must not consume internal message FIFO entries or block a later write to `CMD.hash_start`.

## Actual Behavior
When software writes message data while `CMD.hash_start` is still 0, the hardware can absorb those writes anyway. If enough invalid writes are issued to fill the internal message FIFO, later TL-UL accesses can be back-pressured and a `MSG_FIFO` write can hang, which can prevent software from issuing `CMD.hash_start` afterward.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the HMAC IP's software-visible `MSG_FIFO` ingress path and the logic that decides whether software is allowed to push message data before `CMD.hash_start`.

## Trigger Condition
The problem is triggered when software pushes message bytes into `MSG_FIFO` before starting a hash transaction, especially when enough invalid writes are issued to fill the message FIFO.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan I2C host controller can generate a spurious pulse on the serial clock line (SCL) immediately after a target device returns an acknowledge bit (ACK) for a transmitted byte. This happens in the transmit path when one format FIFO entry has just completed, the transfer is not ending, and another format FIFO entry is already queued for the same ongoing transaction.

## Expected Behavior
In I2C host mode, once a transmitted byte has been ACKed and the next format FIFO entry is ready to continue the transfer, the controller must keep SCL low while it pops that next entry and moves directly into the next byte transfer. It must not temporarily return to an idle bus state or generate an extra SCL high pulse between consecutive queued bytes.

## Actual Behavior
After the target ACK, the host-side state machine briefly transitions as though it were going idle while popping the next format FIFO entry. That momentarily releases SCL high, producing a visible glitch before the next byte starts.

## Affected Function
This affects the OpenTitan I2C IP host-mode transmit state machine, specifically the logic that handles format FIFO continuation after the ACK phase of a transmitted byte.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered in host mode during a multi-byte write-style transaction when a byte has just been transmitted and ACKed by the target, the transfer is supposed to continue rather than terminate with STOP, and another format FIFO entry is already queued. A representative case is a START plus device address followed immediately by additional queued bytes in the same transfer.

title: [tlul] Match tlul_adapter_sram Outstanding to value
body:
Reduce the number of Oustanding to its parameter value. Previous design
increased the request outstanding capability by one to accept next
request when it processes current request. It creates assertion error
below:

    `ASSERT(rvalidHighWhenRspFifoFull, rvalid_i |-> rspfifo_wready)

It is debatable whether the second request should be allowed or not.
This commit is to limit the request when the number of outstanding
requests reaches to its max value. Or we could revise the assertion to
consider the case.

This is related to #1489

resolved_issues.body:
Hi Eunchan, 

When I run fpv on spi_device and flash_ctrl, I found the assertion violation:
```
  `ASSERT(rvalidHighWhenRspFifoFull, rvalid_i |-> rspfifo_wready)
```
My sequence is to trigger a back to back read, and in the TL interface, set the `tl_i.a_valid` signal to low. So in `tlul_adapater_sram`, the `weady` signal is low.
However, `rvalid_i` signal seems to stay high for one more cycle, and triggers the assertion fail. 
In `u_memory_2p`:
```
 a_rvalid_sram <= a_req_q & ~a_write_q;
```
Could you help check if there is any potential protocol concerns? If not, maybe we can consider relax this assertion?

![waveform](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11466553/73890016-d43d5300-4825-11ea-8b00-57989b93deaa.png)

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/tlul/rtl/tlul_adapter_sram.sv b/hw/ip/tlul/rtl/tlul_adapter_sram.sv
index 56e0c783f5eb3..bdc6e5a3f1cbb 100644
--- a/hw/ip/tlul/rtl/tlul_adapter_sram.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/tlul/rtl/tlul_adapter_sram.sv
@@ -218,15 +218,17 @@ module tlul_adapter_sram #(
   //    responses), storing the request is necessary. And if the read entry
   //    is write op, it is safe to return the response right away. If it is
   //    read reqeust, then D response is waiting until read data arrives.
-  prim_fifo_sync #(
-    .Width  (ReqFifoWidth),
-    .Pass   (1'b0),
+
+  // Notes:
   // The oustanding+1 allows the reqfifo to absorb back to back transactions
   // without any wait states.  Alternatively, the depth can be kept as
   // oustanding as long as the outgoing ready is qualified with the acceptance
   // of the response in the same cycle.  Doing so however creates a path from
   // ready_i to ready_o, which may not be desireable.
-    .Depth  (Outstanding+1'b1)
+  prim_fifo_sync #(
+    .Width  (ReqFifoWidth),
+    .Pass   (1'b0),
+    .Depth  (Outstanding)
   ) u_reqfifo (
     .clk_i,
     .rst_ni,

problem_statement:
## Description
The TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) `tlul_adapter_sram` module does not correctly enforce its configured `Outstanding` limit for read transactions. When the module is configured with `Outstanding=1`, a back-to-back TL-UL `Get` read sequence can lead to an assertion failure because the adapter accepts a second read request before the first read response has completed.

## Affected Function
The bug is in the `tlul_adapter_sram` logic that tracks outstanding TL-UL read requests and decides whether a new read request can be accepted while a previous read is still pending.

## Expected Behavior
If `tlul_adapter_sram` is configured with `Outstanding=1`, it must allow at most one in-flight read transaction. After one TL-UL `Get` request has been accepted, a second consecutive `Get` request must not be accepted until the first read response has been accepted on the TL-UL response channel.

## Actual Behavior
When two TL-UL `Get` requests arrive in consecutive cycles, the adapter can still accept the second read even though one read is already outstanding and the configured limit is 1. This mismatch between the configured limit and the actual accepted request depth can surface as assertion failures such as `rvalidHighWhenRspFifoFull`.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when `tlul_adapter_sram` is instantiated with `Outstanding=1`, two consecutive TL-UL `Get` read requests are issued, and the first read response is temporarily blocked on the TL-UL response path.

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/opentitan || exit 1
set +e

TEST_NAME="spi_device_async_fifo_reset_no_sck"
TB_DIR="/home/opentitan/.tb_spi_device_async_reset"

rm -rf "$TB_DIR"
mkdir -p "$TB_DIR"

cat > "$TB_DIR/tb.sv" <<'EOF'
module tb;
  import tlul_pkg::*;

  logic clk = 1'b0;
  logic rst_n = 1'b0;
  tl_h2d_t tl_i;
  tl_d2h_t tl_o;
  logic cio_sck_i = 1'b0;
  logic cio_csb_i = 1'b1;
  logic cio_mosi_i = 1'b0;
  logic cio_miso_o;
  logic cio_miso_en_o;
  logic intr_rxf_o;
  logic intr_rxlvl_o;
  logic intr_txlvl_o;
  logic intr_rxerr_o;
  logic intr_rxoverflow_o;
  logic intr_txunderflow_o;

  always #5 clk = ~clk;

  spi_device dut (
    .clk_i(clk),
    .rst_ni(rst_n),
    .tl_i(tl_i),
    .tl_o(tl_o),
    .cio_sck_i(cio_sck_i),
    .cio_csb_i(cio_csb_i),
    .cio_miso_o(cio_miso_o),
    .cio_miso_en_o(cio_miso_en_o),
    .cio_mosi_i(cio_mosi_i),
    .intr_rxf_o(intr_rxf_o),
    .intr_rxlvl_o(intr_rxlvl_o),
    .intr_txlvl_o(intr_txlvl_o),
    .intr_rxerr_o(intr_rxerr_o),
    .intr_rxoverflow_o(intr_rxoverflow_o),
    .intr_txunderflow_o(intr_txunderflow_o),
    .scanmode_i(1'b0)
  );

  initial begin
    tl_i = '0;
    repeat (3) @(posedge clk);
    rst_n = 1'b1;
    repeat (6) @(posedge clk);

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan SPI Device IP, the status bits `STATUS.rxf_full` and `STATUS.txf_empty` are derived from asynchronous FIFO state sampled in the SPI serial-clock domain and synchronized into the system clock domain. After reset is released, these bits can remain unknown until the first external SPI serial clock (SCK) edge arrives.

## Expected Behavior
Immediately after reset, even if no SPI transaction has started and SCK is idle, the system-visible FIFO status must already be valid and deterministic: `STATUS.rxf_full` must indicate that the receive FIFO is not full, and `STATUS.txf_empty` must indicate that the transmit FIFO is empty. These reset values must not depend on a first SCK edge occurring after reset.

## Actual Behavior
If reset is deasserted while SCK remains idle, the synchronized FIFO status presented on the system side can stay X/unknown instead of settling to the reset values. Software or reset-time checks that read these status bits before any SCK activity can therefore observe invalid RX/TX FIFO state.

## Affected Function
This affects the SPI Device IP's asynchronous RX/TX FIFO status reporting path, specifically the logic that makes the receive-FIFO-full and transmit-FIFO-empty indicators visible in the system clock domain.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when the SPI Device leaves reset while the internal system clock is running but the external SPI serial clock (SCK) has not produced any edges yet.

resolved_issues.body:
In alert_handler tb, my regression includes an agent to drive escalation receiver pairs. I found the issue as following:
If escalation phase cycle is set to an odd number, my escalation receiver (resp signal) will drive one more cycle, which on the escalation sender side, was caught as a signal integrity error.
Tracking from the escalation receiver design side, I confirmed with Michael and found the same issue in his RTL code.
The side-effect of this issue is: if escalation phase cycle is set to an odd number, every time the alert_handler will detect an extra escalation response signal, and fire an integrity fail alert.

Since the escalation pair is planned to fully verify in FPV, we found following action items:

- [x] For cindy (@cindychip) add back the assertion to check integrity fail in this scenario.

- [x] For michael (@msfschaffner) once assertion checked in, please support the fix in RTL, and update the spec accordingly.

- [ ] Future item: discuss if FPV fully verified the model. If needed, do we need to support the pairs in simulation, or is top-level sufficient.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug affects the OpenTitan Alert Handler escalation handshake, specifically the `prim_esc_sender` primitive that checks the response returned by an escalation receiver. During an escalation phase, the sender drives a differential escalation request and the receiver returns an alternating differential response.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the response-checking path in the Alert Handler escalation sender (`prim_esc_sender`) when it is used with the Alert Handler escalation timer.

## Expected Behavior
An Alert Handler escalation phase with an odd cycle count is a valid configuration. While the sender is still actively driving the escalation request pair, `prim_esc_sender` must continue to accept the receiver's expected alternating response pattern, including the last response transition that can occur at the end of an odd-length phase. A correctly alternating response in this situation must complete without an integrity failure indication and without causing the Alert Handler to raise a false integrity-fail alert.

## Actual Behavior
When the escalation phase length is odd, the receiver may produce one additional response transition at the end of the phase. `prim_esc_sender` can treat that final valid response transition as a signal-integrity error, even though it is still part of the normal escalation handshake. This causes an integrity failure indication and makes the Alert Handler raise a false integrity-fail alert.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when the Alert Handler escalation timer runs a phase with an odd number of cycles and the paired escalation receiver continues its normal alternating response until the sender's transmitted escalation request actually stops. The final response transition at the phase boundary is then misclassified as an error.

resolved_issues.title: [hw] s0/fp/x8 register is cleared when single step debugging
resolved_issues.body:
This is a strange one.

The `s0/fp/x8` register must be working for pretty much any function call to work, so it clearly mostly works. When single step debugging the instruction is zeroed out though.

## Steps to reproduce

Get the OpenTitan board running and clone the Git repo. Apply the following diff to the OT repo and rebuild the software:

```diff
diff --git a/sw/device/examples/hello_world/hello_world.c b/sw/device/examples/hello_world/hello_world.c
index bd9aecf..0e1a393 100644
--- a/sw/device/examples/hello_world/hello_world.c
+++ b/sw/device/examples/hello_world/hello_world.c
@@ -54,6 +54,13 @@ void trap_handler(uint32_t mepc, char c) {
 int main(int argc, char **argv) {
   uart_init(UART_BAUD_RATE);
 
+  asm ("ebreak");
+
+  asm ("li t0,0xFFFF");
+  asm ("add  s0, t0, zero");
+  asm ("nop");
+  asm ("nop");
+
   pinmux_init();
   // Enable GPIO: 0-7 and 16 is input, 8-15 is output
   gpio_init(0xFF00);
```

Flash the demo application onto the board:

```shell
./sw/host/spiflash/spiflash --input=./build-fpga/sw/device/examples/hello_world/hello_world.bin
```

Then start `OpenOCD`

```shell
openocd -s util/openocd -f ./board/lowrisc-earlgrey-nexysvideo.c
```

In another terminal start GDB:

```shell
riscv32-oe-elf-gdb /home/alistair/opentitan-snapshot-20191101-2/sw/device/fpga/boot_rom/rom.elf
```

Connect to OpenOCD and restart the board:

```shell
target extended-remote :3333
monitor reset halt
```

Run until we hit the break point

```shell
c
```

You should now be stopped somewhere around here:

```
0x20000226 ? ebreak
```

with these instructions waiting to be executed

```
0x20000226 ? ebreak
0x20000228 ? lui	t0,0x10
0x2000022c ? addi	t0,t0,-1
0x20000230 ? add	s0,t0,zero
0x20000234 ? nop
0x20000236 ? nop
0x20000238 ? lui	s0,0x10
```

NOTE: We are saving a value to `s0/fp/x8` but then assembly generate by the c compiler is also saving a value to `s0` after our two `nop`s.

Print the value of `x8` and `fp` (both the same register).

```
info register x8
info register fp
```

You will see something like this

```
x8             0x0                 0x0
```

Single step GDB past the next three instructions. This should result in `s0/fp/x8` being `0x0000ffff`.

You can check with the following commands:

```
info register x8
info register fp
```

Which should give you something like:

```
x8             0xffff              0xffff
```

The next instruction waiting to be executed is now our **first** `nop` :

```
0x20000234 ? nop
```

Now take one more step. This will execute a `nop` instruction.

Now check `s0/fp/x8`

```
info register x8
info register fp
```

Notice that it is now 0

```
x8             0x0                 0x0
```

Somehow the `nop` zeroed it out!

Take two more steps until after the execution of

```
0x20000238 ? lui	s0,0x10
```

Now `s0/fp/x8` is correctly set to `0x00010000`

Take one more step, following the following jump:

```
0x2000023a ? jal	0x20000452
```

and notice that `s0/fp/x8` is back to 0!


Somehow when single step executing instructions the `s0/fp/x8` register is zeroed out after the next instruction is executed.

+Subject: [PATCH 10/11] [ROM] Restore s0 and a0 on debug exception entry
+
+As noted in lowRISC/opentitan#1035 an exception occuring during program
+buffer execution can corrupt the values of core registers (since they might
+be used by the program, but not restored due to the exception). This change
+forces the boot rom to restore its two scratch registers on exception entry.
+
+This allows the DM to recover from exceptions corrupting s0 or a0, but not
+other registers. OpenOCD currently only uses s0 in its program buffer routines.
+
+Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>
+---
+ debug_rom/debug_rom.S  | 11 +++++++++--
+ debug_rom/debug_rom.h  |  2 +-

++++ b/debug_rom/debug_rom.S
+@@ -60,11 +60,18 @@ entry_loop:
+         jal  zero, entry_loop
+ 
+ _exception:
+-        csrw CSR_DSCRATCH1, a0       // Save a0 to allow loading arbitrary DM offsets
++        // We can only get here due to an exception while in debug mode. Hence,
++        // we do not need to save a0 to a scratch register as it has already
++        // been saved on debug entry.
+         auipc a0, 0                  // Get POC
+         srli a0, a0, 12              // And throw away lower 12 bits to get the DM base
+         slli a0, a0, 12

++        // It is safe to always restore the scratch registers here as they must
++        // have been saved on debug entry. Restoring them here avoids issues
++        // with registers being overwritten by exceptions occuring during
++        // program buffer execution.

#!/bin/bash
set -e

cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 3939bae6f736dec04825261d3784e58cb41579d8
git submodule update --init --recursive

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
fi

if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
text = text.replace(
    "git+https://github.com/olofk/ipyxact.git@master",
    "git+https://github.com/olofk/ipyxact.git@main",
)

lines = []
for line in text.splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's RISC-V Debug Module (`rv_dm`) integrates the imported `pulp_riscv_dbg` debug ROM. When an external debugger single-steps code or runs other debugger-injected instructions through that ROM, re-entering debug mode after a debug exception can return with corrupted CPU register state.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the `pulp_riscv_dbg` debug ROM re-entry path used by `rv_dm` during abstract-command and program-buffer execution in OpenTitan's two-scratch-register configuration.

## Expected Behavior
Single-step debugging must not change architectural registers except for the effect of the instruction being stepped. When the debug ROM regains control after debugger-injected code re-enters debug mode, it must restore the values previously saved in the RISC-V debug scratch CSRs: `s0/fp/x8` from `dscratch0`, and `a0/x10` from `dscratch1` in OpenTitan's configuration.

## Actual Behavior
If a debug exception or breakpoint occurs while the CPU core is already in debug mode, the ROM can return control to the debugger with corrupted register state. The user-visible symptom is that single-stepping an unrelated instruction, such as a `nop`, can unexpectedly clear or otherwise alter `s0/fp/x8`; in the same re-entry path, `a0/x10` can also come back with an internal temporary value instead of the value saved on debug entry.

## Trigger Condition
This happens when the CPU core is already in debug mode and the imported debug ROM executes an abstract-command or program-buffer sequence that re-enters debug mode through its exception or breakpoint path, which is the mechanism exercised by GDB/OpenOCD single-step flows.

title: [aes] Rework register interface
body:
This PR contains a series of commits to implement the following two main changes:
- Input data and initial key registers can now be cleared using a bit in the trigger register (like the output data register). At the moment, these registers are cleared to 0. At a later point, an LFSR will be inserted to clear those registers with pseudo-random data. Previously those registers had to be cleared by software.
- Writes to the key and control registers are ignored if the AES unit is not idle. This similar to the behavior of the HMAC module changed in PR #1014 .

Hand in hand with these changes goes a restructuring/cleanup of the AES core (not the cipher, but the `aes_core.sv` file connecting the data paths with the registers).

The changes have been successfully tested using my Verilator test framework.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) IP has a control-register bug in its register interface. In manual-start mode, software starts a block by writing `TRIGGER.START`. After that block has already begun and the AES unit is no longer idle, software can still write a new value to the control register (`CTRL`), and fields such as `MODE` or `KEY_LEN` can affect the block that is already in flight.

## Expected Behavior
The control configuration for one AES block must be fixed when that block is started. Once the AES unit has left the idle state, any software write to `CTRL` must be ignored completely: it must not change the block that is currently running, and it must not become the active configuration for a later block unless software writes `CTRL` again after the AES unit returns to idle. A block started with a particular mode and key length must finish with that same mode and key length.

## Actual Behavior
A `CTRL` write performed while the AES unit is busy is not reliably ignored. If software changes `MODE` or `KEY_LEN` after `TRIGGER.START` has launched a block, the in-flight encryption or decryption can use the wrong control settings and produce output that does not match the result expected from the original configuration.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered in the AES IP `CTRL` register handling when `CTRL.MANUAL_START_TRIGGER` is enabled, a block is started through `TRIGGER.START`, the AES unit has already left the idle state, and software writes different control values before the current block completes.

title: [reggen] Remove FIFO depth when window is used
body:
Problem:

    reggen creates unintentional TL-UL buffers inside `tl_socket_1n` for
    window feature, which creates higher number of outstanding
    acceptances in the device port.

When `window` feature was implemented, `tlul_fifo_sync` doesn't have a
way to remove internal FIFO. So, when instantiating `tl_socket_1n` for
`window` requests, `ReqDepth` and `RspDepth` are set to 1h. It results
in the number of outstanding acceptances in a IP that having a window
port, to be more than or equal to 4 at least. One buffer in HReq,
another in DReq, 1 in DRsp, and 1 in DReq.

This PR is to remove the FIFO inside tlul_socket_1n, thanks to @tjaychen
added the condition of Depth == 0 and Pass == 1 case.

The IPs, for instance HMAC, still have a buffer internally. If
`tlul_adpater_sram` is used to convert TL-UL interface to the SRAM
interface, that module still has buffers internally.

The issue is discussed in #860

Signed-off-by: Eunchan Kim <eunchan@google.com>

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's register generator (`reggen`) can build a register top with a TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) window, where a sub-range of an IP block's address space is forwarded to a downstream TL-UL interface instead of the normal register bank. In that generated window path, the HMAC register top, and similarly SPI Device, can accept a window-targeted request even when the downstream window interface is stalled.

## Expected Behavior
A request that targets the TL-UL window must not be accepted at the IP's external TL-UL device port until the selected downstream window interface is ready to receive it. Back-pressure from the window side must propagate to the boundary of the register top. In HMAC, this must also hold for a request at the first address that is routed to the window, not only for later addresses inside the window range.

## Actual Behavior
The generated window route can accept the request before the downstream window interface is ready. This hidden buffering creates extra in-flight acceptance at the IP boundary, which is why HMAC and SPI Device appear to allow more outstanding TL-UL requests than intended.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the `reggen`-generated TL-UL window routing in `*_reg_top` modules that use `tl_socket_1n` to steer traffic between the normal register bank and a window interface.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when a TL-UL bus master sends a request to a window-mapped address, including the boundary where HMAC traffic first switches from the register bank to the window, while the selected downstream window interface is not ready to accept the request.

title: [prim/packer] Enhance the behavior based on FPV result
body:
Problem 1:

    `prim_packer` did not assert `valid_o` even it has enough data to
    send out on some corner case when `ready_i` is de-asserted.

Lost the previous commit message. So let it be short. `prim_packer` is
a primitive module to pack incoming data with mask into `OutW` bit-width
signal and send out to the output port.

While preparing FPV environment, a new assertion was added:

    // If input mask is greater than output width, valid should be
    // asserted
    `ASSERT(ValidOAssertedForInputGTEOutW_A,
            valid_i && ($countones(mask_i) >= OutW) |-> valid_o,
            clk_i, !rst_ni)

FPV catches a corner case based on this assertion. When the output port
lowered `ready_i`, the module stores incoming request into the internal
registers. Then it increases `pos` pointer value by `InW`. At the next
cycle, it is expected to keep asserting the `valid_o` as it has data to
send out. As `pos_next` is wrapped around in next cycle if there is more
incoming data, the `valid_next` is lowered.

Resolution:

    Now `prim_packer` considers `pos` value to assert `valid_o` prior to
    compare `pos_next`.

Problem 2:

    `ready_o` falsely asserted as `pos_next` wrapped around.

This issue is similar with the Problem 1. Problem 1 didn't cause any
functionally incorrect behavior. This problem causes an issue. As it let
the design latch the data even doesn't have sufficient storage inside.

Resolution:

    `ready_next` logic doesn't look `pos_next` but only looks at `pos`.
    If `pos` is less than `OutW`, it has enough internal storage to
    store incoming packet. Also, remind that if output port acked the
    outgoing data, it can always store incoming data.

This is related to #19

    // asserted

            valid_i && ($countones(mask_i) >= OutW) |-> valid_o,
            clk_i, !rst_ni)

FPV catches a corner case based on this assertion. When the output port

resolved_issues.title: [prim] prim_packer Testcase
resolved_issues.body: Mainly to @eunchan  for creating the testcase (or at least covergroup) for `prim_packer` module.

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_packer.sv b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_packer.sv
index 07211949bca49..5d721853d71d3 100644
--- a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_packer.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_packer.sv
@@ -59,7 +59,7 @@ module prim_packer #(
     end else if (flush_ready) begin
       pos <= '0;
     end else if (ack_out) begin
-      `ASSERT_I(pos_next_gte_outw_p, pos_next >= OutW)
+      `ASSERT_I(PosOrPosNextGTEOutW_A, (pos >= OutW) || (pos_next >= OutW))
       pos <= pos_next - OutW;
     end else if (ack_in) begin
       pos <= pos_next;
@@ -171,8 +171,28 @@ module prim_packer #(
 
   assign flush_done_o = flush_ready;
 
-  assign valid_next = (pos_next >= OutW) ? 1'b 1 : flush_ready & (pos != '0);
-  assign ready_next = ack_out ? 1'b1 : pos_next <= OutW; // New `we` needs to be hold.
+  always_comb begin
+    if (pos >= OutW) begin
+      // Pending transactions in the storage
+      valid_next = 1'b1;
+    end else if (pos_next >= OutW) begin
+      valid_next = 1'b1;
+    end else begin
+      valid_next = flush_ready & (pos != '0);
+    end
+  end
+  always_comb begin
+    if (ack_out) begin
+      // As OutW size of data can be sent out, it can accept new data always.
+      ready_next = 1'b1;
+    end else if (pos >= OutW) begin
+      // It has out data remained inside, shouldn't accept new data
+      ready_next = 1'b0;
+    end else begin
+      // Regardless of pos_next, it can store the data
+      ready_next = 1'b1;
+    end
+  end
 
   // Output request
   assign valid_o = valid_next;
@@ -182,30 +202,51 @@ module prim_packer #(
   // ready_o
   assign ready_o = ready_next;
 
-  // TODO: Implement Pipelined logic
-  //       Need to change pos logic, mask&data calculation logic too
-
-  //===========================================================================
-  // Assertions, Assumptions, and Coverpoints
-  //
-  `ifndef VERILATOR
-  //pragma translate_off
-    // Assumption: mask_i should be contiguous ones
-    // e.g: 0011100 --> OK
-    //      0100011 --> Not OK
-    property contiguous_ones_p(en, sig, clk, rst_n);
-      @(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
-        en |-> $countones(mask_i ^ {mask_i[InW-2:0],1'b0}) <= 2;
-    endproperty
-    mask_contiguous_ast: assert property (contiguous_ones_p(valid_i, mask_i, clk_i, rst_ni));
-    mask_contiguous_ass: assume property (contiguous_ones_p(valid_i, mask_i, clk_i, rst_ni));
-  //pragma translate_on
-  `endif // VERILATOR
+  //////////////////////////////////////////////
+  // Assertions, Assumptions, and Coverpoints //
+  //////////////////////////////////////////////
+  // Assumption: mask_i should be contiguous ones
+  // e.g: 0011100 --> OK
+  //      0100011 --> Not OK
+  `ASSUME(ContiguousOnesMask_M,
+          valid_i |-> $countones(mask_i ^ {mask_i[InW-2:0],1'b0}) <= 2,
+          clk_i, !rst_ni)
 
   // Flush and Write Enable cannot be asserted same time
-  `ASSERT(exclusive_flush_valid_a, flush_i |-> !valid_i, clk_i, rst_ni)
+  `ASSUME(ExFlushValid_M, flush_i |-> !valid_i, clk_i, !rst_ni)
+
   // While in flush state, new request shouldn't come
-  `ASSERT(valid_zero_while_flush_a, (flush_st == FlushWait) |-> $stable(valid_i), clk_i, rst_ni)
-  //---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  `ASSUME(ValidIDeassertedOnFlush_M,
+          flush_st == FlushWait |-> $stable(valid_i),
+          clk_i, !rst_ni)
+
+  // If not acked, input port keeps asserting valid and data
+  `ASSUME(DataIStable_M,
+          ##1 valid_i && $past(valid_i) && !$past(ready_o)
+          |-> $stable(data_i) && $stable(mask_i),
+          clk_i, !rst_ni)
+  `ASSUME(ValidIPairedWithReadyO_M,
+          valid_i && !ready_o |=> valid_i,
+          clk_i, !rst_ni)
+
+  `ASSERT(FlushFollowedByDone_A,
+          ##1 $rose(flush_i) && !flush_done_o |-> !flush_done_o [*0:$] ##1 flush_done_o,
+          clk_i, !rst_ni)
+
+  // If not acked, valid_o should keep asserting
+  `ASSERT(ValidOPairedWidthReadyI_A,
+          valid_o && !ready_i |=> valid_o,
+          clk_i, !rst_ni)
+
+  // If input mask is greater than output width, valid should be asserted
+  `ASSERT(ValidOAssertedForInputGTEOutW_A,
+          valid_i && ($countones(mask_i) >= OutW) |-> valid_o,
+          clk_i, !rst_ni)
+
+  // If output port doesn't accept the data, the data should be stable
+  `ASSERT(DataOStableWhenPending_A,
+          ##1 valid_o && $past(valid_o)
+          && !$past(ready_i) |-> $stable(data_o),
+          clk_i, !rst_ni)
 
 endmodule

problem_statement:
## Description
`prim_packer` is an OpenTitan primitive that packs masked input data into fixed-width output words and connects them with valid/ready handshakes on both its input and output sides. Its backpressure handling is incorrect when a single accepted input transfer already fills one complete output word while the downstream side is stalled.

## Expected Behavior
If an accepted input transfer causes `prim_packer` to buffer at least one complete `OutW`-bit output word, `valid_o` must assert and remain asserted until the downstream side accepts that word with `ready_i`. While that full output word is pending and `ready_i` is low, `ready_o` must deassert so the upstream side cannot send another input transfer, unless the pending output word is accepted in the same cycle.

This must also hold when one input transfer alone provides the full output word, for example when `InW == OutW` and `mask_i` selects the entire input word.

## Actual Behavior
In the current implementation, when `ready_i` is low and one accepted input transfer already provides a full output word, `prim_packer` can behave as though no complete output word is pending on the following cycle. `valid_o` can drop even though a complete output word is already buffered, and `ready_o` can remain asserted instead of applying backpressure.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the downstream interface is stalled (`ready_i` low) at the same time that an accepted input transfer makes the buffered data reach or exceed one full `OutW`-bit output word. A minimal case is `InW == OutW`, `valid_i` asserted for one input transfer, `mask_i` all ones, and `ready_i` held low until the pending output word is accepted.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the `prim_packer` primitive's output-valid generation and upstream-ready/backpressure behavior when a complete packed output word has been buffered but has not yet been acknowledged by the downstream interface.

title: [rv_plic] Latch to CC for pending interrupts
body:
This is related to #577. @GregAC reported this bug while reviewing the
RV_PLIC specification.

Error:

    RISC-V PLIC assumes the Claim/Complete register can be polled by the
    software even the interrupt pending bit (mip) isn't set. The RV_PLIC
    design only set the CC0 register when the priority is greater than
    the threshold value.

From the RISCV PLIC Spec:

> It is always legal for a hart to perform a claim even if the EIP is
> not set.  In particular, a hart could set the threshold value to
> maximum to disable interrupt notifications and instead poll for active
> interrupts using periodic claim requests, though a simpler approach to
> implement polling would be to clear the external interrupt enable in
> the corresponding xie register for privilege mode x.

https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual/blob/master/src/plic.tex#L329-L334

For instance, if the `threshold` value is set to 7h while the MAX_PRIO
is set to 7 and ID 1 interrupt is pending, the `irq_o` of the RV_PLIC IP
will never be asserted. In this case, `CC0` register of the previous
version showed value `0` always. What spec expects is to be visible of
the most highest priority pending interrupt, which is, in this case, ID
1.

Solution:

    Revise the logic not to consider threshold to calculate `irq_id` in
    the target module. But `irq` should consider the threshold value
    comparing with max priority calculated.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan RV_PLIC (RISC-V Platform-Level Interrupt Controller) does not support polling the claim/complete register correctly when a target's interrupt threshold suppresses external interrupt notification. In the buggy behavior, if an interrupt is pending and enabled for a target but its priority is not strictly greater than the target threshold, the target's claim/complete register (`CC0` in the reported case) returns `0` instead of the pending interrupt's ID.

## Expected Behavior
Polling the claim/complete register must not depend on whether the external interrupt output (`irq_o`) is asserted. When software reads a target's claim/complete register, the RV_PLIC must return the ID of the highest-priority interrupt that is both pending and enabled for that target, and it must return `0` only when no enabled pending interrupt exists. The threshold only controls whether `irq_o` is asserted. This behavior must hold regardless of which supported RV_PLIC target arbitration implementation is configured.

## Actual Behavior
When the threshold is high enough to suppress interrupt notification, the claim/complete register is also effectively suppressed. As a result, software polling the claim/complete register cannot observe a pending enabled interrupt unless that interrupt's priority is strictly greater than the threshold.

## Affected Function
This affects the RV_PLIC target-side arbitration and claim/complete selection logic that determines which pending enabled interrupt is exposed through the claim/complete register and whether the external interrupt output is raised for the target.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when at least one interrupt source is pending and enabled for a target, but all such pending interrupt priorities are less than or equal to the target threshold. A concrete reproducer is a target with `MAX_PRIO = 7`, interrupt ID 1 pending and enabled with priority `7`, and `threshold = 7`: `irq_o` should remain low, but polling the claim/complete register should still report interrupt ID 1 rather than `0`. If the threshold is then lowered below that priority, `irq_o` should assert while the reported interrupt ID remains 1.

title: [tlul/sram] Add error checker in tlul_adapter_sram
body:
Pull-request #279 adressed #236 in the register interface.
This PR is to add error checker in tlul_adapter_sram.

It adds common TL-UL protocol checker in the sram adapter too.
Also this PR slightly revises the adapter module design to increase

Previously tlul_adapter_sram forwarded the request to SRAM interface
even wrsp_error error is detected. Now the module drops the request and
handles internally (push to request fifo but req_o not asserted). Then

resolved_issues.title: [TL-UL] Error Handling
resolved_issues.body:
## Conclusion

### for Device

1. Wrong Opcode. Will always responses as `AccessAck` with Error
2. any `a_addr[1:0]`, `a_size`, `a_mask` wrong combination: Report error
  - a_address[1:0] isn't match with size: `a_size` is 1 --> `a_address[0]` should be 0. if full-word, addr[1:0] should be 0.
  - `a_size` should not be greater than 2h.
  - `a_mask` in inactive lane should be 0.
  - `PutFullData` should have `a_mask` as ones for active lanes
3. Sram with non-contiguous `a_mask` with Put*Data command: Not allowed.

### for Host

1. Discard orphant response and alert/interrupt 
2. Discard mismatched opcode (Get --> AccessAckData / Put*Data --> AccessAck) and alert/interrupt


## Description

In this issue, I would like to discuss what TL-UL spec violations should be reported to the host and what other violations should be in assertions.

There are couple of spec violations mentioned in TL-UL spec.

- Note: no combinational path from ready to valid
- Note: sender may raise valid and lower without ack
- Note: sender may change the content if not accepted
- Note: timeout within the TL network is forbidden (!)
- PutFullData should drive mask HIGH for all active lanes
  + e.g. size 1h with addr 0h. a_mask must be 4'b0011
- PutPartialData has no limitation
- Get should drive mask HIGH for active lanes
  + e.g. size 1h with addr 2h --> a_mask to be 4'b1100
- inactive byte lanes must be driven LOW
- TL-UL size should be less than or equal to the data width (a_size <= 2h)

What current register interface checks:

- Put*Data alignment: word-align
- `a_opcode`: only allow opcodes in TL-UL (Probably better to be in assertion IMO)

I personally prefer having those in assertions as it reduces the logic complexity (having more relaxed register path timing) I want to hear your opinions.

CC: @weicaiyang @sriyerg @cindychip @msfschaffner

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug affects OpenTitan's `tlul_adapter_sram`, the TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) adapter that converts TL-UL bus transactions into SRAM accesses. When the adapter receives a TL-UL request-channel (A-channel) transaction with an unsupported `a_opcode`, it can treat that beat as a real SRAM access instead of rejecting it locally as a protocol error.

## Expected Behavior
`tlul_adapter_sram` must validate each incoming TL-UL request before asserting its SRAM request output. If `a_opcode` is not one of the supported commands (`Get`, `PutFullData`, or `PutPartialData`), the adapter must not issue an SRAM request. Instead, it must complete that transaction on the TL-UL response channel (D-channel) with `AccessAck`, `d_error` asserted, and the original source ID.

## Actual Behavior
With the buggy implementation, an A-channel beat with an illegal `a_opcode` can still be forwarded onto the SRAM request interface. As a result, an invalid TL-UL transaction can reach the memory-side logic, and the host may fail to receive the required local error response for that transaction.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the `tlul_adapter_sram` request admission and error-response handling for invalid TL-UL opcodes.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when `tlul_adapter_sram` accepts a TL-UL request whose opcode is outside the legal command set while the rest of the request fields are otherwise valid and the downstream SRAM side is ready to take a request.

#!/bin/bash
set -e

cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout e15f7e52bc74713fb45c98aa3ae446434becb746
git submodule update --init --recursive

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    if stripped == "git+https://github.com/olofk/ipyxact.git@master":
        line = "git+https://github.com/olofk/ipyxact.git@05fd1b3d577903fe47418e1090cd280094e8a49c"
    elif stripped == "git+https://github.com/lowRISC/edalize.git@ot":
        line = "git+https://github.com/lowRISC/edalize.git@5ae2c3e1ca306e27d81ce5fcc769f62cb7ac42d0"
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -f -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -f
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible

  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  if [ -d "$d" ]; then
    export PATH="$d:$PATH"
  fi
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then

problem_statement:
## Description
`tlul_adapter_reg` is the device-side TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) register adapter used by OpenTitan peripherals. It accepts TL-UL requests on the A channel and returns completions on the D channel. When a host sends a request whose A-channel opcode is not one of the supported register-access operations (`Get`, `PutFullData`, or `PutPartialData`), the adapter can still treat the transaction as a normal access and return a completion that does not indicate an error.

## Expected Behavior
An unsupported TL-UL A-channel opcode must not be reported as a successful register access. `tlul_adapter_reg` should return a D-channel error response for that transaction: the response opcode should be `AccessAck`, `d_error` must be asserted, and the original source ID must be preserved so the error is attributed to the correct request.

## Actual Behavior
With an illegal A-channel opcode, the adapter can produce a normal-looking `AccessAck` response without asserting `d_error`, which makes the malformed request appear successful to the host.

## Affected Function
This bug affects the device-side request validation and D-channel error reporting logic in `tlul_adapter_reg`.

## Trigger Conditions
The bug is triggered when a host issues a TL-UL register request through `tlul_adapter_reg` with an unsupported A-channel opcode.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in OpenTitan's `prim_arbiter` primitive. If one requester has already been selected but the downstream interface keeps `arb_ready` low, a later higher-priority requester can replace the first requester before any `arb_valid && arb_ready` handshake occurs. This changes the granted requester and `arb_data` for a transfer that is still pending. The problem can appear on TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) request paths such as `tlul_socket_m1`, where the downstream side may observe request information change without a new handshake.

## Expected Behavior
After `prim_arbiter` raises `arb_valid` for a requester, that same requester and its associated `arb_data` must remain selected until the transfer is accepted with `arb_valid && arb_ready`. If another requester asserts later while the first transfer is stalled, it must wait for the next arbitration opportunity. On TL-UL paths, this means request fields carried through the arbiter, such as address or write data, must not change while `valid` remains asserted and `ready` is low.

## Actual Behavior
While a transfer is stalled by `arb_ready == 0`, asserting a later higher-priority request can change the arbiter output before the original transfer is accepted. The pending transfer can therefore appear to switch to the newer request, changing the observed grant and forwarded data without an acceptance handshake.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is `prim_arbiter`'s handling of a request that has already been selected but has not yet been accepted.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when a requester is selected, `arb_valid` remains high, the downstream interface applies backpressure with `arb_ready == 0`, and another requester with higher priority becomes active before the stalled transfer is accepted.

resolved_issues.title: [Entropy_src] repcnt watermarks not recording statistical threshold
resolved_issues.body:
DV has uncovered two challenges with the `repcnt` & `repcnts` health checks:
1. Similar to the Bucket test in issue #9757, the diagnostic being fed to the water mark is the number of failing counts, not the actual repetition counts.
2. Even though the repcnt test is continuous (i.e. has no concept of windows), the `repcnt` and `repcnts` watermarks are only being updated at the end of the health check window:
```
  entropy_src_watermark_reg #(
    .RegWidth(HalfRegWidth),
    .HighWatermark(1)
  ) u_entropy_src_watermark_reg_repcnt_bypass (
    .clk_i               (clk_i),
    .rst_ni              (rst_ni),
    .clear_i             (health_test_clr),
    .active_i            (repcnt_active),
    .event_i             (health_test_done_pulse && es_bypass_mode),
    .value_i             (repcnt_event_cnt),
    .value_o             (repcnt_event_hwm_bypass)
  );
```

The repcnt watermark should increase even if you are not at a window boundary.

problem_statement:
## Description
The Entropy Source IP has two repetition-count health checks, `repcnt` and `repcnts`, that monitor repeated incoming entropy samples and record a high-watermark value in software-visible control/status registers (CSRs). Two problems exist in this watermarking path. First, the value used for the watermark tracks post-threshold failing counts instead of the actual repetition length. Second, the watermark only updates at the end of a health-test window, even when the repeated run has already grown further inside the current window.

## Expected Behavior
For both `repcnt` and `repcnts`, the high-watermark value for the active mode must represent the largest repetition length observed so far. If a run of identical samples continues to grow after the configured repetition threshold is crossed, the recorded watermark should increase immediately to that larger repetition length; it must not wait for the health-test window boundary, and it must not report only the number of threshold violations.

## Actual Behavior
When repeated samples continue within an open health-test window, the recorded watermark can stay stale or too small because it is driven by failing-count activity and is only committed at window completion. As a result, software may read a repetition-count watermark that is lower than the true longest run already seen.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the Entropy Source IP's `repcnt` and `repcnts` repetition-count watermarking path, including the software-visible high-watermark fields for these health checks.

## Trigger Condition
A clear reproducing case is bypass mode: if identical entropy samples continue past the configured repetition threshold before the current health-test window ends, the bypass watermark for `repcnt` and `repcnts` should already reflect the full current run length, but it does not.

  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt

  else

  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {

    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)

path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"

from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)

entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):

PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"

problem_statement:
## Description
In the Earl Grey top-level `xbar_main` TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) interconnect, the RISC-V Debug Module (RV_DM) System Bus Access (SBA) path exposed over JTAG is expected to reach the control and status registers (CSRs) of both SPI Host controller instances, `spi_host0` and `spi_host1`. The affected functionality is the debug-access routing from `rv_dm.sba` to those two SPI Host IP blocks.

## Expected Behavior
A debugger-issued RV_DM SBA read to the `spi_host0` or `spi_host1` CSR address window should be accepted by the main crossbar, routed to the selected SPI Host instance, and return a normal TL-UL read response from that instance without an access error.

## Actual Behavior
`spi_host0` and `spi_host1` are not reachable through the RV_DM SBA path. A JTAG-initiated SBA read to either SPI Host CSR window is not forwarded to the selected SPI Host instance, so the read does not complete as a normal SPI Host CSR access.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the debugger uses RV_DM SBA over JTAG to access either SPI Host CSR address window, for example by performing a basic CSR read of `spi_host0` or `spi_host1`. Other RV_DM SBA targets are not the failing case described here.
