resolved_issues.title: [ entropy_src ] Bucket Health Test not including last sample
resolved_issues.body:
The Bucket health test looks for excessive correlations between RNG channels by maintaining a histogram of the RNG symbols coming and reporting an error if any symbols exceed a given threshold.

If the last RNG symbol pushes the test over the threshold, the histogram peak is recorded but not in time to register a test failure.

---

For example, in the following waveform (taken from signals within `u_entropy_src_bucket_ht`), the relevant signals are near the bottom of the screenshot.  The end of the window is shown by the last signal `window_wrap_pulse_o`.   The last input to `entropy_bit_i[3:0]` is `4'hf`, and it is the 11th instance of that value in the window.  At the very end of the test, this count (`16'000B`) is accurately reflected in the signal `test_cnt_o`, highlighted as dark blue.  Though this exceeds the threshold of 16'h000A (highlighed as light blue).  The `test_fail_pulse_o` signal remains low (highlighted as orange).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47870387/150387854-1d62d606-bfb3-42b1-9273-766bc6292510.png)

To reproduce this result, pull the branch `issue_10226`  from my fork (`git@github.com:martin-lueker/opentitan.git`) and run the following  command (from `$OT_ROOT` on WD servers):
```
./util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/entropy_src/dv/entropy_src_sim_cfg.hjson -i entropy_src_rng -r 1 -t xcelium --job-prefix="nc run -C ncsim_interactive -Il" -w=shm -s=1 --run-modes set_verbosity_comp_a_uvm_debug set_verbosity_comp_b_uvm_debug
```

---

Suggested Fix: 
The `test_fail_pulse_o` signal is drawn from the output of a secondary "Test event counter" which counts the _number_ of bins that exceed threshold, and fires an error if `test_cnt > '0`.  This however incurs a one cycle delay, and is not strictly necessary.  Instead one could look at the array `bin_cnt_exceeds_thresh`.

Written as a patch this change would look like this:

```
diff --git a/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv b/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv
index d6210ebb0..4b71cc9b2 100644
--- a/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv
@@ -94,7 +94,7 @@ module entropy_src_bucket_ht #(
     );
 
   // the pulses will be only one clock in length
-  assign test_fail_pulse_o = active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && (|bin_cnt_exceeds_thresh);
+  assign test_fail_pulse_o = active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && (test_cnt > '0);
   assign test_cnt_o = bin_max;
   assign count_err_o = test_cnt_err || (|bin_cntr_err);
```

Note: Once this change is applied, lint checks confirm that the signal test_cnt is no longer needed and the whole unit `u_prim_count_test_cnt` can be removed from the bucket test as well.

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src.sv b/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src.sv
index b109cb17db660..6067e28a74848 100644
--- a/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src.sv
@@ -298,10 +298,6 @@ module entropy_src
      alert_tx_o[1])
   end : gen_symbol_match
 
-  `ASSERT_PRIM_COUNT_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT(CntAlertCheck3_A,
-    u_entropy_src_core.u_entropy_src_bucket_ht.u_prim_count_test_cnt,
-    alert_tx_o[1])
-
   for (genvar sh = 0; sh < RngBusWidth; sh = sh+1) begin : gen_pair_cntrs
    `ASSERT_PRIM_COUNT_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT(CntAlertCheck_A,
      u_entropy_src_core.u_entropy_src_markov_ht.gen_cntrs[sh].u_prim_count_pair_cntr,
diff --git a/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv b/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv
index 7f94f8e2ece90..67e1b87a1dfea 100644
--- a/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv
@@ -31,8 +31,6 @@ module entropy_src_bucket_ht #(
   logic [NUM_BINS-1:0] bin_cnt_exceeds_thresh;
   logic [NUM_BINS - 1:0][RegWidth - 1:0] bin_cntr;

-  logic [RegWidth-1:0] test_cnt;

   // Bucket Test
@@ -77,28 +75,10 @@ module entropy_src_bucket_ht #(
     .o(bin_max)
   );
 
-  // Test event counter
-  // SEC_CM: CTR.REDUN
-  prim_count #(

-      .CntStyle(prim_count_pkg::DupCnt)

-      .set_cnt_i(RegWidth'(0)),
-      .en_i(entropy_bit_vld_i && (|bin_cnt_exceeds_thresh)),
-      .step_i(RegWidth'(1)),
-      .cnt_o(test_cnt),
-      .err_o(test_cnt_err)
-    );
-
   // the pulses will be only one clock in length
-  assign test_fail_pulse_o = active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && (test_cnt > '0);
+  assign test_fail_pulse_o = active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && (|bin_cnt_exceeds_thresh);
   assign test_cnt_o = bin_max;
-  assign count_err_o = test_cnt_err || (|bin_cntr_err);
+  assign count_err_o = |bin_cntr_err;
 
 
 endmodule
problem_statement:
## Description
The Entropy Source (`entropy_src`) IP contains a bucket health test in the `entropy_src_bucket_ht` submodule. For each observation window, this test builds a histogram of random number generator (RNG) symbols and reports a failure when any histogram bin exceeds the programmed threshold.

## Trigger Condition
The bug occurs when the symbol that first pushes a histogram bin above the threshold is also the final valid symbol of the observation window. One concrete case is a 4-bit symbol stream in which the value `0xf` appears 11 times in a single window while the threshold is 10.

## Expected Behavior
When an observation window closes, the bucket health test must evaluate the completed histogram for that window, including the last valid symbol. If any bin count is greater than the threshold, `test_fail_pulse_o` must assert for that window, and `test_cnt_o` must report the completed window's peak bin count.

## Actual Behavior
In the failing case above, the completed histogram and `test_cnt_o` reflect the final count of 11, but `test_fail_pulse_o` does not assert when the window ends. As a result, a bucket-test failure that occurs on the last sample of the window is missed.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan key manager IP's controller logic for asynchronous fatal faults while the block is idle. After the key manager completes its advance into the initialized working state and no operation is active, an asynchronous fatal fault, such as a register-file integrity error, is recorded but does not immediately force the controller out of that state.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the key manager controller's idle-time fault handling path: how it reacts to an asynchronous fatal fault when no key manager operation is currently running.

## Expected Behavior
An asynchronous fatal fault must not wait for an operation boundary. If the key manager is idle in its initialized working state when such a fault arrives, the controller must latch the fault indication and immediately enter the `Invalid` working state, rather than remaining initialized until a later command, a later operation, or some other later event.

## Actual Behavior
When the controller is idle after initialization and a register-file integrity fault is asserted, the fault indication is recorded, but the controller can remain in the initialized working state instead of promptly transitioning to `Invalid`.

## Trigger Condition
Bring the key manager to its initialized idle state by letting its advance complete, then inject an asynchronous fatal fault on the register-file integrity path while no operation is active. This idle-fault case should immediately move the controller to `Invalid`, but the buggy behavior leaves it in the pre-fault state.

title: [aes] Fix clearing of data input registers
body:
Previously, the write enable for the data input registers was set for two clock cycles when clearing the registers. This caused the
data_in_qe_i signals used for status tracking to be high during the first clock cycle when back in IDLE. As a result, the AES unit would immediately start when running in automatic operation.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#11431.

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan AES IP, automatic operation can start an encryption too early after software clears the key, initialization vector (IV), and data input registers. The issue is observed in Cipher Feedback (CFB) mode: software writes `DATA_IN_3`, clears the key/IV/data input registers, and then writes the key, IV, and only `DATA_IN_0` through `DATA_IN_2` for the next transaction. Even though the last word of the new 128-bit input block has not been rewritten, the AES block can leave `IDLE` and later produce output.

## Expected Behavior
After software clears the AES key, IV, and data input registers, automatic mode must treat the next input block as incomplete until software rewrites all four `DATA_IN` registers (`DATA_IN_0` through `DATA_IN_3`) for that block. A `DATA_IN_3` write that happened before the clear must not satisfy the start condition for the post-clear transaction. In the sequence above, the AES block should remain idle and must not produce output until `DATA_IN_3` is written again after the clear. Once all four `DATA_IN` registers have been rewritten after the clear, the new encryption may start normally.

## Actual Behavior
If `DATA_IN_3` is written before the clear, the AES block can still start a new automatic encryption after the clear once the key, IV, and only `DATA_IN_0` through `DATA_IN_2` are rewritten. That causes encryption to run even though the post-clear input block is still missing `DATA_IN_3`.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the AES IP automatic-start logic that determines whether a complete 128-bit input block has been provided after the key, IV, and data input registers are cleared.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when the AES IP is in automatic mode, configured for Cipher Feedback (CFB), `DATA_IN_3` is written, the key/IV/data input registers are cleared, and software then rewrites the key, IV, and only `DATA_IN_0` through `DATA_IN_2`. Under that sequence, the block may start before `DATA_IN_3` is rewritten after the clear.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug affects the OpenTitan SPI Host IP's `TXDATA` transmit window on the TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) bus and the `ERROR_STATUS` register bits that can change as a side effect of bad transmit-window accesses. `TXDATA` is a memory-like FIFO window with byte-write support, not a conventional word-aligned control and status register (CSR).

## Expected Behavior
Writes to `TXDATA` that enable one or more byte lanes must be accepted using window semantics, even when the TL-UL address uses nonzero low bits to select a specific byte lane. These accesses must not return an alignment or access error merely because they are not word-aligned like a normal CSR write. Separately, `ERROR_STATUS` bits that are raised by invalid transmit-window accesses or TX FIFO overflow are hardware-updated status, so CSR verification must not assume they remain equal to the last software-predicted value after such traffic.

## Actual Behavior
The SPI Host transmit window is handled like a normal CSR path. As a result, byte-enabled or sub-word writes to `TXDATA` can be rejected with a TL-UL access or alignment error when the address low bits are nonzero, even though the target is a byte-write FIFO window. In the same stress scenario, side effects from erroneous `TXDATA` writes can change `ERROR_STATUS`, which then causes false mismatches if those status bits are treated as ordinary software-controlled CSR contents.

## Trigger Condition
The failure appears during randomized concurrent CSR and memory traffic to the SPI Host, especially when partial writes reach the `TXDATA` window at nonzero byte-lane offsets and resets are injected while traffic is in flight.

resolved_issues.body:
In this waveform, EX4B(E9) is received and cfg_addr_4b_en drops for a short period then asserts again without receiving a new command.

![Screen Shot 2022-09-14 at 10 50 47 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49293026/190325000-92f70c4a-0e47-4c86-b43b-bc388588c7c3.png)

Looks like it's because the next command comes too quickly, `spi_csb_asserted_pulse_i` is asserted again but `spi_reg_cfg_addr_4b_en_sync` hasn't been updated.
```
  always_ff @(posedge spi_clk_i or negedge sys_rst_ni) begin
    if (!sys_rst_ni) begin
      spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o <= 1'b 0;
    end else if (spi_addr_4b_set_i) begin
      // This event occurs when EN4B command is received
      spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o <= 1'b 1;
    end else if (spi_addr_4b_clr_i) begin
      // EX4B command raises the clear event
      spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o <= 1'b 0;
    end else if (spi_csb_asserted_pulse_i
      && (spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o != spi_reg_cfg_addr_4b_en_sync)) begin
      // Update
      spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o <= spi_reg_cfg_addr_4b_en_sync;
    end
  end
```

Maybe we need to define the timing between 2 transactions to avoid this or try to fix it in the design.

problem_statement:
## Description
The SPI Device IP's flash-mode 4-byte address-configuration logic can lose a newly applied address-mode command when two SPI transactions are separated by little or no chip-select-bar (CSB) inactive time. In this context, EN4B enters 4-byte address mode and EX4B exits 4-byte address mode. The failure occurs in the path that keeps the flash-mode 4-byte address setting aligned between the SPI-clock-domain state and the software-visible configuration bit.

## Expected Behavior
After the SPI Device accepts EN4B, 4-byte address mode must remain enabled until a later EX4B command changes it. After the SPI Device accepts EX4B, 4-byte address mode must remain disabled until a later EN4B command changes it. A follow-up SPI transaction that is not another address-mode command, including a back-to-back status read, must not restore the previous address-width setting. Once synchronization completes, the software-readable `cfg.addr_4b_en` bit must report the same stable mode.

## Actual Behavior
If EN4B or EX4B is followed too quickly by another SPI transaction, the next CSB assertion can reapply an older mirrored value before the new state has fully propagated. This makes the 4-byte address setting transient. For example, EX4B can clear 4-byte mode briefly and then the mode becomes enabled again on the following transaction even though no new EN4B command was received.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered in SPI Device flash mode when EN4B or EX4B is immediately followed by another SPI transaction with very short or zero CSB inactive time. A concrete manifestation is an EN4B or EX4B command followed right away by a status-read transaction; repeated alternation between EN4B and EX4B under this short-idle condition exposes the stale-state overwrite.

title: [aes] Improve FI detection when OR-combining multi-rail signals
body:
This is needed for #16427.

Previously, OR-combination and error detection for multi-bit, multi-rail signals was done in a single for loop inside an always_comb block. In every loop iteration, the current combined signal was only compared to the current signal added to the combination. This is not ideal from a fault detection perspective.

For example, when faulting the last rail of the round counter to 1 when the counter is actually 0 wouldn't be detected immediately. For the first and second loop iteration, the OR-combined value was still 0. For the last rail, the OR-combined value would be 1 which is equal to the faulted counter. In practice this didn't really matter because a faulted round counter itself isn't problematic. But the faulted round counter changes the control flow of one rail which is always detected, e.g., by a register write enable signal taking on an invalid encoding as the different rails driving that get out of sync.

This minimal RTL change performs the comparison in a separate loop to effectively compare all rails with the total OR-combined value. In the example above, the final OR-combined counter value is compared against both un-faulted rails and the fault is immediately detected.

The associated area impact of this change is neglibile. With Yosys + nangate45, AES is now 110.17 kGE vs. 109.86 kGE (+0.28%). But it improves FI detection and most importantly simplifies DV as faults in the round counter are detected immediately and independent whether the AES cipher core is busy or idle.

[aes/pre_syn] Fix Yosys synthesis

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

[aes] Improve FI detection when OR-combining multi-rail signals

Previously, OR-combination and error detection for multi-bit, multi-rail
signals was done in a single for loop inside an always_comb block. In
every loop iteration, the current combined signal was only compared to
the current signal added to the combination. This is not ideal from a
fault detection perspective.

For example, when faulting the last rail of the round counter to 1 when
the counter is actually 0 wouldn't be detected immediately. For the
first and second loop iteration, the OR-combined value was still 0. For
the last rail, the OR-combined value would be 1 which is equal to the
faulted counter. In practice this didn't really matter because a faulted
round counter itself isn't problematic. But the faulted round counter
changes the control flow of one rail which is always detected, e.g., by
a register write enable signal taking on an invalid encoding as the
different rails driving that get out of sync.

This minimal RTL change performs the comparison in a separate loop to
effectively compare all rails with the total OR-combined value. In the
example above, the final OR-combined counter value is compared against
both un-faulted rails and the fault is immediately detected.

The associated area impact of this change is neglibile. With Yosys +
nangate45, AES is now 110.17 kGE vs. 109.86 kGE (+0.28%). But it
improves FI detection and most importantly simplifies DV as faults in
the round counter are detected immediately and independent whether
the AES cipher core is busy or idle.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan

RESULT_TEST_NAME="aes_cipher_ctr_redun_idle"
HWE_TEST_NAME="hwe_pr16445_aes_cipher_ctr_redun_idle"
HWE_VSEQ_NAME="${HWE_TEST_NAME}_vseq"
HWE_VSEQ_FILE="hw/ip/aes/dv/env/seq_lib/${HWE_VSEQ_NAME}.sv"
SCRATCH_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.scratch"
TMP_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tmp"

RESULT_RC=1
RESULT_PRINTED=0

print_result() {
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  if [ "${RESULT_RC}" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "TEST: ${RESULT_TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
  else
    echo "TEST: ${RESULT_TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
  fi
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  RESULT_PRINTED=1
}

cleanup() {
  local rc=$?

  if [ "${RESULT_PRINTED}" -eq 0 ]; then
    if [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ] && [ "${RESULT_RC}" -eq 0 ]; then
      RESULT_RC="${rc}"
    fi
    print_result
  fi
}

trap cleanup EXIT

mkdir -p "${TMP_ROOT}" "${SCRATCH_ROOT}"
export TMPDIR="${TMP_ROOT}"
export PATH="/tools/verible/bin:/tools/riscv/bin:${PATH}"

python3 - "${HWE_TEST_NAME}" "${HWE_VSEQ_NAME}" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import sys

test_name, vseq_name = sys.argv[1:3]


def replace_once(path_str: str, marker: str, insertion: str, guard: str) -> None:
    path = Path(path_str)
    text = path.read_text()
    if guard in text:
        return
    if marker not in text:
        raise SystemExit(f"Failed to find insertion point in {path_str}")
    path.write_text(text.replace(marker, insertion + marker, 1))


test_entry = f"""    {{
      name: {test_name}
      uvm_test: aes_fi_test
      uvm_test_seq: {vseq_name}
      reseed: 1
      run_timeout_mins: 1 // Short test; if not done within 1 min, something's wrong.
    }}
"""

replace_once(
    "hw/ip/aes/dv/aes_base_sim_cfg.hjson",
    "    {\n      name: aes_core_fi\n",
    test_entry,
    f"name: {test_name}",
)

core_entry = f"      - seq_lib/{vseq_name}.sv: {{is_include_file: true}}\n"
replace_once(
    "hw/ip/aes/dv/env/aes_env.core",
    "      - seq_lib/aes_core_fi_vseq.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n",
    core_entry,
    core_entry.strip(),
)

vseq_entry = f"`include \"{vseq_name}.sv\"\n"
replace_once(
    "hw/ip/aes/dv/env/seq_lib/aes_vseq_list.sv",
    "`include \"aes_core_fi_vseq.sv\"\n",
    vseq_entry,
    vseq_entry.strip(),
)

helper = """  function automatic int get_target_by_name(string signal_name);
    foreach (intf_array[i]) begin
      if (check_target_name(intf_array[i], signal_name)) begin
        return i;
      end
    end
    foreach (intf_mul_array[i]) begin
      if (check_target_name(intf_mul_array[i], signal_name)) begin
        return intf_array.size() + i;
      end
    end
    return -1;
  endfunction

"""

replace_once(
    "hw/ip/aes/dv/err_injection_if/fi_cipher_if.sv",
    "  // check which array we need to access and force or releae\n",
    helper,
    "function automatic int get_target_by_name(string signal_name);",
)
PY

cat > "${HWE_VSEQ_FILE}" <<EOF
// Copyright lowRISC contributors.
// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, see LICENSE for details.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

class ${HWE_VSEQ_NAME} extends aes_base_vseq;
  \`uvm_object_utils(${HWE_VSEQ_NAME})
  \`uvm_object_new

  localparam bit FORCE = 0;
  localparam bit RELEASE = 1;

  localparam int IdleFaultRail = Sp2VWidth - 1;
  localparam bit [31:0] RndCtrFaultValue = 32'h1;
  localparam string RndCtrSignalName = "rnd_ctr_o";

  task body();
    bit saw_alert = 0;
    int target;

    target = cfg.aes_cipher_control_fi_vif[IdleFaultRail].get_target_by_name(RndCtrSignalName);
    if (target < 0) begin
      \`uvm_fatal(\`gfn, \$sformatf("Failed to resolve target %s on cipher FI interface %0d",
                                  RndCtrSignalName, IdleFaultRail))
    end

    \`uvm_info(\`gfn, "Injecting a round-counter fault into the last idle cipher-control rail",
              UVM_LOW)

    wait(cfg.clk_rst_vif.rst_n);
    \`DV_WAIT(cfg.aes_cipher_control_fi_vif[IdleFaultRail].aes_cipher_ctrl_cs ==
             aes_pkg::CIPHER_CTRL_IDLE)
    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(5);

    cfg.aes_cipher_control_fi_vif[IdleFaultRail].force_signal(target, FORCE, RndCtrFaultValue);

    fork
      begin
        while (!cfg.m_alert_agent_cfg["fatal_fault"].vif.is_alert_handshaking()) begin
          cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(1);
        end
        cfg.m_alert_agent_cfg["fatal_fault"].vif.wait_ack_complete();
        saw_alert = 1;
      end
      begin
        cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(50);
      end
    join_any
    disable fork;

    if (!saw_alert) begin
      \`uvm_fatal(\`gfn, "Timed out waiting for fatal_fault after idle rnd_ctr fault injection")
    end

    apply_resets_concurrently();
    cfg.aes_cipher_control_fi_vif[IdleFaultRail].force_signal(target, RELEASE, RndCtrFaultValue);
    dut_init("HARD");
  endtask : body
endclass
EOF

set +e
timeout 1800 ./util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/aes/dv/aes_no_masking_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i "${HWE_TEST_NAME}" \
  -t vcs \
  --local \
  --max-parallel 1 \
  --scratch-root "${SCRATCH_ROOT}" \
  --purge \
  --fixed-seed 1 \
  --build-seed 1
RESULT_RC=$?
set -e

print_result
exit "${RESULT_RC}"

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)

git checkout 74c3a91499f6471910654abbd8c238f94690d995

PREP_TMP="/home/opentitan/.prepare_tmp"
rm -rf "${PREP_TMP}"
mkdir -p "${PREP_TMP}"

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt "${PREP_TMP}/apt-requirements.txt"
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' "${PREP_TMP}/apt-requirements.txt"
  if [[ -s "${PREP_TMP}/apt-requirements.txt" ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < "${PREP_TMP}/apt-requirements.txt"
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt "${PREP_TMP}/python-requirements.txt"
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/home/opentitan/.prepare_tmp/python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:

    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY

else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found"

fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's AES IP uses redundant multi-rail control values as a fault-detection mechanism. In the AES cipher-control path, the redundant round counter is OR-combined across rails and then checked for consistency. With the current logic, a fault on the last rail can escape immediate detection: if that rail is corrupted from 0 to 1 while the cipher-control state machine is idle and the true round-counter value is 0, the mismatch is not reported when it occurs.

## Expected Behavior
Whenever the AES cipher-control logic evaluates the redundant round counter, every rail must agree with the final OR-combined counter value. If any rail disagrees, including while the cipher-control state machine is idle, the AES block must treat the condition as an internal fault and raise its fatal fault alert without waiting for later control-flow divergence or for a new AES round to begin.

## Actual Behavior
A mismatch on the last round-counter rail can be missed in the idle state. When that rail is faulted from 0 to 1 while the true counter value is 0, the AES block does not immediately raise its fatal fault alert at the point of corruption. The inconsistency may only become visible later after it perturbs downstream control behavior.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the AES IP's cipher-control round-counter redundancy check (`AES_CIPHER.CTR.REDUN`), specifically the consistency check for the OR-combined multi-rail round counter.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the AES cipher-control state machine is idle, the redundant round counter's true value is 0, and the last rail of that multi-rail counter is corrupted from 0 to 1.

title: [flash_ctrl] Fix buffer enable / disable timing
body:
- fixes #16979
- In the previou design, the buffer enable was allowed to change whenever the read pipeline was idle.  This however does not account for the scenario where on the same cycle there is a new flash read request.  In the buffer enable were changed from 1->0, it would allow a new request to match a buffer entry, while disallowing that buffer from responding in subsequent cycles.
- Update the design such that when buffer enable is changed the request is back pressured during that same cycle.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug affects the OpenTitan flash controller (`flash_ctrl`) during the handoff between a controller-initiated flash read and a life cycle RMA (Return Merchandise Authorization) request. If an RMA request arrives while a controller read is still active, the controller read path can fail to retire cleanly and block forward progress of the RMA sequence.

## Trigger Condition
A controller-initiated flash read is already in progress, and an RMA request is asserted before that read operation has completed.

## Expected Behavior
When an RMA request is issued during an active controller read, the flash controller must allow the in-flight read to complete, and the RMA flow must advance into its erase phase without hanging.

## Actual Behavior
In the failing scenario, issuing an RMA request during a controller read leaves the controller read path stuck. The controller read does not complete, and the RMA sequence fails to advance into its erase phase, so the operation times out.

title: [lc_ctrl] Fix bugs in volatile unlock mechanism
body:
A few alignments are needed:
- The LC counter may already have been incremented by unsuccessful unlock operations. Hence forcing to `LcCnt1` as part of the volatile unlock could result in programming errors when further transitions are attempted. The solution is to force to `LcCnt1` only in the case when the counter is `LcCnt0`. 
- The continuous state vector sampling needs to be disabled after a volatile unlock - otherwise the LC_CTRL would revert to RAW immediately after 1 cycle. This mechanism was there before, but it had a bug that is fixed here.
- Suggested doc updates from https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/18248 are incorporated.
- An SVA inside pinmux that makes sure the straps are only sampled once is fixed.

resolved_issues.body:
This adds a volatile RAW -> TEST_UNLOCKED0 mechanism for test chips.

This solution does NOT use KMAC token hashing, hence the RTL diff is smaller. An alternative implementation with KMAC hashing is drafted in #18238 for reference. This has been discussed with @cdgori and we decided not to  pursue that since the RTL diff is too big and would add significant risk. The direct comparison without hashing is acceptable since the mechanism will not be compiled into PROD silicon.

Note that the modifications in pinmux are needed so that the hardware straps can be re-sampled in order to ungate the DFT and RISC-V TAPs.

Addresses https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/18246

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Life Cycle Controller (LC_CTRL) supports a volatile `RAW -> TEST_UNLOCKED0` transition on test-chip configurations. In this mode, LC_CTRL temporarily exposes `TEST_UNLOCKED0` without programming the One-Time Programmable (OTP) life cycle state, so software can use the unlocked state immediately after the transition succeeds.

## Expected Behavior
If the device starts in `RAW` with life cycle transition count `LcCnt0`, and software successfully requests a volatile transition to `TEST_UNLOCKED0` using the correct raw unlock token, LC_CTRL must continue reporting `TEST_UNLOCKED0` in subsequent cycles after the transition completes. In the same scenario, the reported transition count must advance to `LcCnt1` and remain `LcCnt1` while the volatile unlocked state is active; it must not fall back to the OTP-backed `RAW` / `LcCnt0` view on the next idle cycle.

## Actual Behavior
After a nominally successful volatile `RAW -> TEST_UNLOCKED0` transition, LC_CTRL resumes sampling the OTP-backed life cycle state and transition count. Because OTP still contains `RAW` and `LcCnt0`, the externally visible state can revert almost immediately after the transition, so later reads report `RAW` and `LcCnt0` instead of preserving the volatile `TEST_UNLOCKED0` state.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the LC_CTRL volatile raw unlock path for the `RAW -> TEST_UNLOCKED0` transition, specifically the logic that decides whether the post-transition life cycle state and transition count should continue to come from the volatile unlock result or from ongoing OTP sampling.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when volatile raw unlock is supported, the device is currently in `RAW` with count `LcCnt0`, software claims the LC_CTRL transition interface, enables volatile raw unlock, targets `TEST_UNLOCKED0`, provides the correct raw unlock token, and starts the transition. The failure is visible in the first later idle cycles after the transition completes.

title: [usbdev] Remove data toggle clear in suspend
body:
The link_active_i term was misplaced, and data toggles should not be cleared in suspended state. In fact, they should be retained, and usbdev will need to give software greater visibility and control, so it can save / restore state in coordination with deep sleep.

For the purposes of an ECO, leave link_active_i unused. It was intended to help prevent the packet engines from responding to packets and dirtying FIFOs before software is ready, but that is left for a later commit.

Found by @alees24 in #18940

resolved_issues.title: [usbdev] USB device clears Data Toggle flag when link inactive (Suspend-Resume)
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

When the device detects a link inactive state the OUT side clears its Data Toggle flag. The IN side leaves its flag untouched.
The result is that following Resume from the Suspended state the first _new_ data packet transmitted to a non-Control endpoint may be ACKed by the device and the data is dropped, on the assumption that this is a _re-transmission_ of the previous packet.

This is true for all endpoints, but we may assume that for Control Transfers the first thing to be transmitted will be a SETUP packet so the issue should not be seen. For Bulk Transfers such as serial port traffic, re-opening the serial port connection following a suspend-resume cycle may result in the first OUT packet (host->device) being dropped because the Linux Host Controller/driver stack still has knowledge of the previous state and the first data packet will sometimes be transmitted with a DATA1 token.

From my reading of the USB 2.0 specification the toggle state is cleared to DATA0 when the endpoint is configured but should be unaffected by device Suspend/Resume. @a-will Is this correct? What is the history of resetting in response to 'not link_active_i' please?

**RTL**:

usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv: 354
```
    end else if (link_reset_i || !link_active_i) begin
      data_toggle_q <= '0; // All endpoints
```
Suggested change for **partial mitigation**:
```
    end else if (link_reset_i) begin
      data_toggle_q <= '0; // All endpoints
```
matching the comparable logic in usb_fs_nb_in_pe.sv.

_This works for any Suspend-Resume signaling that the host performs automatically, but currently we cannot reinstate the Data Toggle states upon returning from a Sleep state. There is no register interface either for reading the current toggles or for setting them. The software is only able to clear the toggles._

Both IN and OUT traffic will suffer from this issue when returning from a Sleep state.

**Other workarounds:**

Avoid suspending, or when there is a suspicion that the host may have requested the device suspend, force a reset of the device. This can be achieved if talking to the device using libusb, but not - as far as I know - when using regular serial port traffic via open/read/write/close.

**Background**:

Streaming data test (usbdev_stream_test) normally sends PRND packets from device (IN) to host where they are checked, combined with another PRND stream and returned to the device (OUT) where they are checked against expectations. The Linux driver stack will not auto-suspend a device that has active connections, but I have modified the host-side code of this test to close its file descriptors/libusb usage, instruct the driver stack to suspend the device, and then to resume it, before re-establishing the connections to the device.

The first packet received after re-establishing the Bulk transfer connections to the device has a 50% chance of a DATA1 PID being used, in which case the logic analyzer shows the packet being transmitted to the device and ACKed, but no buffer is consumed within the device and the packet is just dropped internally. The checking code then objects to the next lump of data that is received because part of the expected PRND stream has not arrived.

This happens whether I'm using libusb or whether I'm using the 'open/read/write/close' kernel functions to access the device via /dev/ttyUSBn as regular serial ports.

My host-side code, when modified to perform Suspend-Resume signaling frequently can induce a test failure within 15-30 seconds. Introducing a bodge which sends a dummy packet when it knows the first post-Resume packet shall be sent with DATA1 allows the test to continue running for at least 45 minutes without failure. It can do this only because it can control exactly how many packets have been sent, but in so doing it is also severely limiting the bandwidth. This is not a practical fix.


@msfschaffner  @johngt @GregAC

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv b/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv
index 83aa0c5c6c0fd..dbd18e7db1c45 100644
--- a/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv
@@ -328,6 +328,11 @@ module usb_fs_nb_out_pe #(
     end
   end
 
+  // TODO(#18940): Use the link state to prevent the FSM from responding to
+  // packets until software is ready.
+  logic unused_link_active_i;
+  assign unused_link_active_i = ^link_active_i;
+
   always_ff @(posedge clk_48mhz_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
     if (!rst_ni) begin
       out_xact_state <= StIdle;
@@ -351,7 +356,7 @@ module usb_fs_nb_out_pe #(
   always_ff @(posedge clk_48mhz_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
     if (!rst_ni) begin
       data_toggle_q <= '0; // All endpoints
-    end else if (link_reset_i || !link_active_i) begin
+    end else if (link_reset_i) begin
       data_toggle_q <= '0; // All endpoints
     end else begin
       data_toggle_q <= data_toggle_d;
problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan USB device (USBDEV) IP, the receive-side data-toggle state for non-control OUT endpoints is cleared when the USB link becomes inactive during suspend. This state is used by the USB device OUT packet engine to distinguish a new packet from a retransmission. As a result, after suspend and resume, the first new OUT packet can be acknowledged but not committed to the endpoint buffer.

## Expected Behavior
Suspend and resume, without a USB bus reset, must preserve the current data-toggle value for each non-control OUT endpoint. If an endpoint successfully accepts a DATA0 packet before suspend, it must still expect DATA1 after resume. A valid DATA1 packet received after resume must be treated as new data, written into the endpoint buffer, and advance the endpoint's data-toggle state.

## Trigger Condition
The failure occurs on a non-control OUT endpoint after it has already accepted a DATA0 packet, the USB link then enters the inactive/suspended state, and the link later resumes without a bus reset. In that scenario, a host that correctly continues with DATA1 can have the first post-resume OUT packet acknowledged by the device but effectively dropped.

problem_statement:
## Description
The UART IP is intended to treat FIFO watermark interrupts as level-sensitive status conditions rather than edge-triggered events. In the failing behavior here, the transmit FIFO watermark interrupt (`tx_watermark`) still acts like an event interrupt, so the interrupt state and interrupt output do not reliably reflect the live TX FIFO watermark condition.

## Expected Behavior
`tx_watermark` should continuously reflect whether the transmit FIFO depth is below the configured transmit watermark threshold. If the TX FIFO starts empty or is cleared, `tx_watermark` should already be asserted. If software writes to clear interrupt state while the TX FIFO remains below the threshold, `tx_watermark` should stay asserted. The interrupt should deassert only after the TX FIFO depth moves back to the non-watermark side of the threshold. `tx_empty` is a separate interrupt and is not the behavior being changed here.

## Actual Behavior
`tx_watermark` behaves like a one-shot or edge/event interrupt. It can be deasserted even while the TX FIFO is still below the configured watermark threshold, and it may only assert again after another threshold crossing occurs.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the UART IP's interrupt generation and interrupt-state reporting for the transmit FIFO watermark condition (`tx_watermark`).

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when UART watermark interrupts are enabled and the TX FIFO is below the configured watermark threshold without a fresh crossing event, especially immediately after the TX FIFO is cleared or after transmission drains the FIFO back below the threshold.

The wipe secret register, in the intro of the doc (here, last paragraph: https://opentitan.org/book/hw/ip/hmac/index.html), it says that the internal variables will be reset to the written value from this register WIPE_SECRET. But the register description (https://opentitan.org/book/hw/ip/hmac/doc/registers.html#wipe_secret) is saying that a XOR is done instead. So which description should be considered?

### RTL
Within the RTL I can see that:
- hmac.sv: the secret key is replaced by the wipe_secret register value
- prim_sha2: all the internal values are XORed with the wipe_secret register value

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) IP includes a `WIPE_SECRET` register that is intended to clear sensitive internal state. The affected functionality is the secure-wipe behavior in the internal Secure Hash Algorithm 2 (SHA-2) datapath, `prim_sha2`, which is responsible for maintaining the hash state and digest value used by the HMAC IP.

## Expected Behavior
When software writes a 32-bit value to `WIPE_SECRET`, the internal values covered by the wipe operation must be overwritten with that written value. For the `prim_sha2` portion of the HMAC IP, the wiped hash or digest state must therefore become the provided wipe value and must not depend on the previous contents.

## Actual Behavior
The HMAC IP is inconsistent in how it applies `WIPE_SECRET`: the secret-key path is overwritten with the provided value, but the `prim_sha2` secure-wipe path combines the existing internal SHA-2 values with `WIPE_SECRET` using XOR. As a result, the post-wipe hash or digest state still depends on the pre-wipe contents instead of being deterministically reset to the written wipe value.

## Trigger Condition
This bug is triggered when the HMAC IP has already processed data or otherwise contains non-default SHA-2 state, and software then writes `WIPE_SECRET` to request a secure wipe. The failure is observable after a prior hash or digest value exists and the wipe is expected to clear that state.

tb_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan || exit 1

export PATH="/tools/riscv/bin:${PATH}"

TEST_NAME="manifest_address_translation"
TB_DIR="/home/opentitan/.tb_manifest_address_translation"

set +e
(
  set -euo pipefail

  rm -rf "${TB_DIR}"
  mkdir -p "${TB_DIR}"

  cat > "${TB_DIR}/min_boot.S" <<'ASM'
.section .vectors,"ax"
.globl _start_vec
_start_vec:
  j _rom_ext_start_boot

.section .crt,"ax"
.globl _crt_init
_crt_init:
  nop

.section .text,"ax"
.globl _rom_ext_start_boot
_rom_ext_start_boot:
  nop
  ret

.section .shutdown,"ax"
.globl _shutdown_stub
_shutdown_stub:
  nop

.section .static_critical.version,"aw",@nobits
.globl _static_critical_pad
_static_critical_pad:
  .space 8136
ASM

  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

tb_dir = Path("/home/opentitan/.tb_manifest_address_translation")
src = Path("/home/opentitan/sw/device/silicon_creator/lib/manifest_def.c").read_text(
    encoding="utf-8"
).splitlines()

addr_idx = None
manifest_version_idx = None
for idx, line in enumerate(src):
    if ".address_translation" in line:
        addr_idx = idx
    if ".manifest_version" in line:
        manifest_version_idx = idx

# GCC 10 accepts the repo source as C, but this minimal build uses C++ mode to
# sidestep older `_Generic` issues in hardened.h. C++20 requires designated

    "${TB_DIR}/min_boot.o" \

    -nostdlib \

    "${TB_DIR}/min_boot.o" \

    -o "${TB_DIR}/slot_virtual.elf"

module tb;
  localparam int OFFSET = 816;
  localparam int WORD_BYTES = 4;
  localparam int MIN_BYTES = OFFSET + WORD_BYTES;
  localparam int unsigned HARDENED_FALSE = 32'h0000_01d4;
  localparam int unsigned HARDENED_TRUE  = 32'h0000_0739;

  byte unsigned slot_a_data [0:2047];
  byte unsigned slot_virtual_data [0:2047];

  function automatic int unsigned read_word(input byte unsigned data [0:2047]);
    return {data[OFFSET + 3], data[OFFSET + 2], data[OFFSET + 1], data[OFFSET]};
  endfunction

  task automatic check_image(
      input string path,
      inout byte unsigned data [0:2047],
      input int unsigned expected
  );
    integer fd;
    integer bytes_read;
    int unsigned actual;
    begin
      fd = $fopen(path, "rb");
      if (fd == 0) begin
        $fatal(1, "failed to open %0s", path);
      end

      bytes_read = $fread(data, fd);
      $fclose(fd);
      if (bytes_read < MIN_BYTES) begin
        $fatal(1, "%0s too short: %0d bytes", path, bytes_read);
      end

      actual = read_word(data);
      if (actual !== expected) begin
        $fatal(1, "%0s offset %0d expected 0x%08x got 0x%08x",
               path, OFFSET, expected, actual);
      end
    end

  initial begin
    check_image("/home/opentitan/.tb_manifest_address_translation/slot_a.bin",

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 28787642672f5c080f5aad009288ef3819486862
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain and persist PATH.
# Verible is optional here because this commit pins a release tag that now 404s.
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  verible_url="https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  if curl -fILs "$verible_url" >/dev/null; then
    echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
    rm -rf /tools/verible

    tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan ROM_EXT (ROM Extension) images include a manifest field named `address_translation`. That field is not being selected from the final link address of the ROM_EXT `.text` section.

## Expected Behavior
For every ROM_EXT image, the manifest `address_translation` field must be derived from the linked address of the `.text` section. If `.text` is linked inside embedded flash (eFlash), `address_translation` must be `false`. If `.text` is linked outside eFlash, `address_translation` must be `true`.

## Actual Behavior
ROM_EXT images can be produced with an `address_translation` value that does not match where the `.text` section was linked. In particular, an image linked outside eFlash can still carry the same `address_translation` setting as an image linked inside eFlash.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the OpenTitan silicon_creator ROM_EXT manifest generation path that populates the `address_translation` field.

## Trigger Condition
The problem appears when building ROM_EXT images whose `.text` section may be linked at different locations, including at least one image linked inside eFlash and another linked outside eFlash.

title: [usbdev] Also reject OUT packet internally when STALLing
body:
The OUT packet engine was missing a signal to internal blocks about what happened to the just-received packet if it sent a STALL to the host. Fix this so the internal blocks correctly reset counters and free up resources given to the rejected packet.

Fixes #23806

resolved_issues.title: [usbdev] OUT side STALL response can leave device unable to capture next SETUP/OUT packet
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

An OUT packet that elicits a 'STALL' response is neither acknowledged nor rolled back; in `usb_fs_nb_out_pe` neither 'out_ep_acked_o' nor  'rollback_data' (= `out_ep_rollback_o`) is asserted.

This means that if the packet is 62 or more bytes in length, the byte counting logic in `usbdev_usbif` is not reset in preparation for the next OUT/SETUP packet to be received and the packet size recorded into the RX FIFO is incorrect; the true size of the packet is unknowable.

The STALLing mechanism is used within current test software to declare 'protocol stall' in response to the DEVICE_QUALIFIER requests, but this does not break anything because only the IN side receives a STALL response for that Control Transfer, I think.

To reproduce, fetch draft PR sequence #23805 and run with the following seed:
```
util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/usbdev/dv/usbdev_sim_cfg.hjson -i usbdev_setup_priority_over_stall_response --fi 71923730856705723741826963384972440023047469689158980899448095559948831305837 --wa shm --tool xcelium -v m
```
If that somehow passes, try specifying '.randomize_length(0), .num_of_bytes(64)' to the task enable 'send_prnd_out_packet(..)'

This issues needs further consideration and clarification of what else may be impacted.
To be clear, this is with ES and prod RTL; it does not relate to the draft proposed changes.

@a-will, @vogelpi, @andreaskurth

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv b/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv
index 6e116820200de..56aaff79ffbd8 100644
--- a/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv
@@ -288,6 +288,7 @@ module usb_fs_nb_out_pe #(
           // Non-isochronous OUT transactions end here
           if (out_ep_stall_i[out_ep_index]) begin
             tx_pid_o = {UsbPidStall}; // STALL
+            rollback_data = 1'b1; // Packet not accepted
           end else if (nak_out_transaction | out_ep_full_i[out_ep_index]) begin
             tx_pid_o = {UsbPidNak}; // NAK -- the endpoint could not accept the data at the moment
             rollback_data = 1'b1;
problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan USB device IP, specifically the full-speed non-isochronous OUT packet engine (`usb_fs_nb_out_pe`) and the receive-side bookkeeping in `usbdev_usbif`. When the USB device responds to a host-to-device OUT transaction with `STALL`, the rejected packet is not rolled back internally. Receive-side state from that rejected OUT transaction can remain allocated even though the USB host was told that the transfer failed.

## Expected Behavior
A `STALL` response to an OUT transaction means the packet was rejected and must not consume receive state. After a stalled OUT transaction, the USB device must discard the rejected packet's bookkeeping, reset the receive-side byte count for that packet, and be ready to accept the next receive transaction. In particular, if control endpoint 0 (EP0) stalls a long OUT transaction, the following SETUP packet must still be acknowledged and its receive FIFO (RX FIFO) entry must match the actual SETUP packet length and payload.

## Actual Behavior
If a non-isochronous OUT transaction is stalled, the receive bookkeeping is not rolled back. For OUT packets 62 bytes or longer, the byte-counting logic in `usbdev_usbif` is left uncleared before the next receive transaction arrives. As a result, the next SETUP packet, or another OUT packet, can be recorded with the wrong length in the RX FIFO and may not be captured correctly; once this happens, the true size of the affected packet cannot be recovered from the RX FIFO entry.

## Trigger Conditions
This occurs when an endpoint is configured to return `STALL` for a non-isochronous OUT transaction, the device receives a long OUT packet (reported starting at 62 bytes, including a 64-byte OUT packet), and another receive transaction follows immediately. The benchmarked case is control endpoint 0 (EP0): a 64-byte OUT packet is stalled, and the very next SETUP packet should still be accepted correctly.

title: [prim_count] Register err_o to avoid potential CDC issues downstream
body: This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#24119.

commits.message:

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#24119.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [ECO] prim_count.sv CDC
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

Reported by: @meisnere 

`sw_alert_handler_ping_ok` test fails post synthesis. 

The root cause seems to point to glitches on `err_o`. This is a CDC error as it takes time for the sum to converge here: 

https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/e439226b6c5314be12ccf5cc055f2d4b8149d0ab/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv#L140-L143

CC @andreaskurth @vogelpi

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv
index c0e77647f48f9..f70999c546bcd 100644
--- a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv
@@ -140,7 +140,18 @@ module prim_count
   // The sum of both counters must always equal the counter maximum.
   logic [Width:0] sum;
   assign sum = (cnt_q[0] + cnt_q[1]);
-  assign err_o = (sum != {1'b0, {Width{1'b1}}});
+
+  // Register the error signal to avoid potential CDC issues downstream.
+  logic err_d, err_q;
+  assign err_d = (sum != {1'b0, {Width{1'b1}}});
+  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
+    if (!rst_ni) begin
+      err_q <= 1'b0;
+    end else begin
+      err_q <= err_d;
+    end
+  end
+  assign err_o = err_q;
 
   // Output count values
   assign cnt_o              = cnt_q[0];
@@ -190,7 +201,7 @@ module prim_count
       rst_ni
       |=>
       $past(!commit_i) || (cnt_o == $past(cnt_after_commit_o)),
-      clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+      clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
 
   // Clear
   if (PossibleActions & Clr) begin : g_check_clr_fwd_a
@@ -199,7 +210,7 @@ module prim_count
             |=>
             (cnt_o == ResetValue) &&
             (cnt_q[1] == ({Width{1'b1}} - ResetValue)),
-            clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+            clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end
 
   // Set
@@ -209,7 +220,7 @@ module prim_count
         |=>
         (cnt_o == $past(set_cnt_i)) &&
         (cnt_q[1] == ({Width{1'b1}} - $past(set_cnt_i))),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end
 
   // Do not count if both increment and decrement are asserted.
@@ -218,7 +229,7 @@ module prim_count
         rst_ni && incr_en_i && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i)
         |=>
         $stable(cnt_o) && $stable(cnt_q[1]),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end
 
   // Increment
@@ -227,24 +238,24 @@ module prim_count
         rst_ni && incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) && commit_i
         |=>
         cnt_o == min($past(cnt_o) + $past({2'b0, step_i}), {2'b0, {Width{1'b1}}}),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(IncrDnCnt_A,
         rst_ni && incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) && commit_i
         |=>
         cnt_q[1] == max($past(signed'({2'b0, cnt_q[1]})) - $past({2'b0, step_i}), '0),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(UpCntIncrStable_A,
         incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) &&
         cnt_o == {Width{1'b1}}
         |=>
         $stable(cnt_o),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(DnCntIncrStable_A,
         rst_ni && incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) &&
         cnt_q[1] == '0
         |=>
         $stable(cnt_q[1]),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end
 
   // Decrement
@@ -253,24 +264,24 @@ module prim_count
         rst_ni && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) && commit_i
         |=>
         cnt_o == max($past(signed'({2'b0, cnt_o})) - $past({2'b0, step_i}), '0),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(DecrDnCnt_A,
         rst_ni && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) && commit_i
         |=>
         cnt_q[1] == min($past(cnt_q[1]) + $past({2'b0, step_i}), {2'b0, {Width{1'b1}}}),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(UpCntDecrStable_A,
         decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) &&
         cnt_o == '0
         |=>
         $stable(cnt_o),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(DnCntDecrStable_A,
         rst_ni && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) &&
         cnt_q[1] == {Width{1'b1}}
         |=>
         $stable(cnt_q[1]),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end
 
   // A backwards check for count changes. This asserts that the count only changes if one of the
@@ -279,12 +290,12 @@ module prim_count
           rst_ni ##1 $changed(cnt_o) && $changed(cnt_q[1])
           |->
           $past(clr_i || set_i || (commit_i && (incr_en_i || decr_en_i))),
-          clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+          clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
 
-  // Check that count errors are reported properly in err_o
-  `ASSERT(CntErrReported_A, ((cnt_q[1] + cnt_q[0]) != {Width{1'b1}}) == err_o)
+  // Check that count errors are reported properly in err_d
+  `ASSERT(CntErrReported_A, ((cnt_q[1] + cnt_q[0]) != {Width{1'b1}}) == err_d)
  `ifdef PrimCountFpv
-  `COVER(CntErr_C, err_o)
+  `COVER(CntErr_C, err_d)
  `endif
 
   // This logic that will be assign to one, when user adds macro

    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
toolchain_version=""
verible_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
command -v vcs >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
`prim_count` is OpenTitan's hardened counter primitive. It stores the count in two redundant internal shares whose sum should remain all ones (`2**Width - 1`). The affected behavior is the primitive's integrity indicator, `err_o`, which is intended to report that the stored redundant state is invalid.

## Expected Behavior
When `prim_count` performs a legal count update from one valid redundant state to another, `err_o` must remain low. In particular, a normal increment that updates the counter must not create a transient `err_o` pulse. `err_o` should assert only if the stored redundant shares are actually inconsistent after the update has settled.

## Actual Behavior
`err_o` can glitch high during a normal count update even though the counter starts and ends in a valid redundant state. This false pulse can appear in post-synthesis timing and can be interpreted downstream as a false Clock Domain Crossing (CDC) or integrity error.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a legal increment updates both redundant shares in the same cycle and the two shares do not settle at exactly the same time. During that convergence window, the sum check can temporarily observe an invalid total and pulse `err_o` even though no real counter corruption occurred.
